questions.question: What data formats can IntegrationHub parse?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Both XML and JSON responses
• Correct because IntegrationHub is designed to handle multiple data formats when integrating with external systems.
• It can parse XML (commonly used in SOAP APIs and legacy systems) and JSON (standard for REST APIs and modern applications).
• Supporting both ensures flexibility and compatibility across diverse integrations.
Incorrect
Option A. Only XML responses
• Incorrect because limiting parsing to XML ignores JSON, which is the most widely used format in modern APIs.
• This would restrict IntegrationHub’s ability to integrate with RESTful services.
Option C. Only JSON responses
• Incorrect because while JSON is common, many enterprise and legacy systems still rely on XML.
• IntegrationHub must support both formats to meet broad integration requirements.

questions.question: Task table is a “___” table. Fill in the blank with the right option.
questions.explanation: Task [task] is one of the core tables provided with the base system. It provides a series of standard fields used on each of the tables that extend it, such as the Incident [incident] and Problem [problem] tables.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a formatter in ServiceNow instance? Select one of the following.
options: Formatter allows you to populate fields automatically
Formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record
A formatter allows you to configure applications on your instance
Formatter is a set of conditions applied to a table to help find and work with data
questions.explanation:
A formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record. Add formatters to a form by configuring the form.
Documentation – https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/orlando-platform-administration/page/administer/form-administration/concept/c_Formatters.html

questions.question: On the ServiceNow instance. where does the global text search appear?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Banner
• The global text search in ServiceNow appears in the banner frame at the top of the interface.
• This allows users to search across the entire instance (records, knowledge, catalog items, etc.) from a single location.
• It is a key navigation feature designed for quick access.
Incorrect
Option A. Content Area
• The content area displays forms, lists, and dashboards.
• It does not host the global text search bar.
Option B. Left Navigation Pane
• The left navigation pane contains the Application Navigator for modules and applications.
• While you can search for applications/modules here, this is not the global text search.

questions.question: Which of the below is not a list interface element?
questions.explanation: Gauges is not a list interface element but container for holding graphical content on dashboards and homepages in ServiceNow, but gauges are no longer supported.

questions.question: Which of the following is a best example of Contextual Security in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation: Contextual security is securing your data and record using create, read, write, delete functionality using Access Control List. Contextual security gives you controlling access on every level.

questions.question: Which protocol is used to send outbound emails from Service-now?
questions.explanation:
The ServiceNow application uses the ServiceNow SMTP server to process outbound email messages to users ([email protected]). These messages are sent from the ServiceNow datacenter, routed as standard SMTP traffic to your primary mail exchanger (MX) server, and processed internally within the organization.
Documentation – https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/orlando-servicenow-platform/page/administer/reference-pages/concept/c_EmailConfiguration.html

questions.question: A variable Set is a modular unit of variables that “CAN BE” shared between catalog items. True or False?
questions.explanation: Variable sets allow you to create a collection of structured variables that can be reused across multiple catalog items and order guides. Using variable sets saves time because you do not have to create the same variables individually for many catalog items.

questions.question: Which one of the statement below describes the relationship between the incident table and task table?
options: The incident table is the parent of the task
The incident table extends the task table
The task table extends the incident table
The task table is the child of the incident table
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. The incident table extends the task table
• In ServiceNow, the task table is a base table that contains common fields used by all task-based records (e.g., assignment, state, priority).
• The incident table is a child table that extends the task table, inheriting all its fields and adding incident-specific fields.
• This means incidents are specialized tasks, and the incident table builds upon the task table’s structure.
Incorrect
Option A. The incident table is the parent of the task
• Incorrect because the task table is the parent, not the incident table.
• The incident table is a child that extends task.
Option C. The task table extends the incident table
• Incorrect because the relationship is the opposite.
• The incident table extends the task table, not the other way around.
Option D. The task table is the child of the incident table
• Incorrect because the task table is the base/parent table.
• The incident table is the child, not the parent.

questions.question: Which module in service catalog application is responsible for creating items?
questions.explanation: Maintain items is an application module that list few types of request items like catalog item, record producer, standard change templates, software catalog, hardware catalog etc. All of these are extended from the base sc_cat_item table and used for request fulfillment from your service catalog.

questions.question: Which OOB support will help you to avoid creating duplicates while importing data?
questions.explanation:
The coalesce option allows you to update existing target table records when transforming import data.
If an existing record with a matching value in the target table is found, that record is updated. If no matching record is found, then a new record is created in the target table.

questions.question: Which of the below components runs on server side on ServiceNow instance? Select all that apply.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Script Include
• Correct because Script Includes are reusable server‑side scripts.
• They run on the server and can be invoked by other server‑side logic (like Business Rules) or client‑side code via GlideAjax.
Option C. Business Rule
• Correct because Business Rules execute on the server when records are inserted, updated, deleted, or queried.
• They enforce logic and automation at the database level.
Option F. Data Policy
• Correct because Data Policies run on the server to enforce field requirements and rules regardless of how data is entered (UI, import, API).
• They ensure consistency and compliance across the platform.
Incorrect
Option A. UI
• Incorrect because UI components (like forms, lists, and layouts) are client‑side.
• They control how data is displayed but do not execute server‑side logic.
Option D. UI Policy
• Incorrect because UI Policies run on the client side in the browser.
• They dynamically change form behavior (like making fields mandatory or visible) but do not enforce rules on the server.
Option E. Client Script
• Incorrect because Client Scripts run in the user’s browser.
• They handle client‑side validation and interactivity, not server‑side processing.

questions.question: Which technique is used to get information from a series of referenced fields from different tables?
questions.explanation: Refer to https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/orlando-platform-user-interface/page/use/navigation/reference/dot-walking-examples.html

questions.question: Which table stores information about CI relationship existing on a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: The CI Relationship table in a ServiceNow instance is “cmdb_rel_ci”

questions.question: From the below options, please choose the correct definition of “inactivity monitor” in ServiceNow instance.
options: It is used to enhance the system logs. It provides more information on the duration of transactions between the client and the server.
It triggers an event for a task record if the task is inactive for a certain period of time. If the task remains inactive, the monitor repeats at regular intervals.
questions.explanation:
The correct definition of an “inactivity monitor” in a ServiceNow instance is:
• It triggers an event for a task record if the task is inactive for a certain period of time. If the task remains inactive, the monitor repeats at regular intervals.
Here’s why:
• Inactivity monitors are designed to track and act upon tasks that haven’t been updated or changed within a specified timeframe. This helps ensure that tasks don’t get lost or forgotten.

questions.question: Can we coalesce multiple fields in a table for given transform map?
options: No. Only 1 field per table can be coalesced
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow allows you to coalesce against multiple fields, and use multiple transform maps against a single data source.
If multiple fields are set to coalesce, all coalesce values are used to match an existing record. If two fields are set for coalescing and a matching value is found on one of the coalescing fields but not on the other, a new record is inserted.

questions.question: Does ServiceNow support table rotation?
questions.explanation: Table rotation preserves instance performance and averts risk associated with querying growing data sets by using the External Communication Channel (ECC) Queue and the sys_created_on field to separate data sets into multiple tables based on date.

questions.question: Which of the following statements holds true for Service Catalog categories?
options: Users with the admin or catalog_admin roles can view categories only if there is an active item in the category and Availability is set to either Desktop or Both.
Users with the admin or cat_admin roles can view categories only if there is an active item in the category and Availability is set to either Desktop or Both.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Users with the admin or catalog_admin roles can view categories only if there is an active item in the category and Availability is set to either Desktop or Both.
• Correct because in ServiceNow, Service Catalog categories are visible to users with the admin or catalog_admin roles only when:
• The category contains at least one active item.
• The Availability setting is configured to Desktop or Both.
• This ensures that categories without active items or those restricted to mobile-only availability are not displayed to these roles.
Incorrect
Option B. Users with the admin or cat_admin roles can view categories only if there is an active item in the category and Availability is set to either Desktop or Both.
• Incorrect because the role name cat_admin is not valid in ServiceNow.
• The correct role is catalog_admin. Using cat_admin would not grant the intended permissions, making this statement false.

questions.question: Which of the following is not an example of a UI action?
questions.explanation:
UI actions include the buttons, links, and context menu items on forms and lists. Configure UI actions to make the UI more interactive, customized, and specific to user activities.
Administrators and users with the ui_action_admin role can define UI actions.

questions.question: Which is the parent table for incident, problem, change in an ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: Tables Incident, Problem, Change are extended from Task table in ServiceNow. Task is the parent table in ServiceNow, so most of the fields on this forms are derived from the parent Task table itself.

questions.question: What is the master table that contains a record for each table in the database?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option C. sys_db_object table
• Correct: The sys_db_object table is the master table in ServiceNow.
• It contains a record for every table in the database, including custom tables and extensions of base tables.
• This table defines metadata such as table name, label, and whether the table extends another.
Incorrect
• Option A. sys_master_db table
• Incorrect: No such table exists in ServiceNow. This is a distractor option.
• Option B. sys_master_object table
• Incorrect: Again, this table does not exist in ServiceNow. It is a misleading option.

questions.question: How are users related to roles or groups in an ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation: Users can have multiple roles or be part of different groups so it is many to many relationship.

questions.question: _______ is used to join two tables. Fill in the blank with the correct option.
questions.explanation:
A database view defines table joins for reporting purposes.
A number of useful database views are installed with the Database View plugin and the Database Views for Service Management plugin. These database views cover most metric reporting needs and greatly reduce the need to define new ones.
For example, a database view can join the Incident table to the Metric Definition and Metric Instance tables.

questions.question: Where are customizations done on a ServiceNow instance stored?
questions.explanation:
Update sets store both new
Correct
Option A. sys_update_xml
• Correct because all customizations made in a ServiceNow instance are stored in the sys_update_xml table.
• This table captures the XML records of changes (such as new fields, forms, scripts, or configurations) and is used when creating or applying update sets.
• It ensures that customizations can be tracked, migrated, and managed across different instances.
Incorrect
Option B. sys_update
• Incorrect because there is no table named sys_update in ServiceNow for storing customizations.
• This option is a distractor and does not exist in the platform.
Option C. sys_update_set
• Incorrect because sys_update_set stores metadata about update sets themselves, not the actual customization records.
• It defines the container for a group of changes but does not hold the detailed XML records of the customizations.
and updated choice options as separate records in the Update Version [sys_update_version] and Customer Update [sys_update_xml] tables.

questions.question: Is it true that a variable set can be used in multiple catalog Items?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. TRUE
• Correct because variable sets in ServiceNow are designed to be reusable across multiple catalog items.
• A variable set is essentially a container of variables that can be applied to different catalog items, reducing duplication and ensuring consistency.
• For example, a variable set for “User Information” (Name, Email, Department) can be reused across multiple catalog items like hardware requests, software requests, or access requests.
Incorrect
Option A. FALSE
• Incorrect because variable sets are not limited to a single catalog item.
• Saying “FALSE” would imply that each catalog item requires its own unique set of variables, which is not true.
• This would contradict the purpose of variable sets, which is to promote reusability and efficiency.

questions.question: What defines conditions that are evaluated against users to determine which users can access Service Catalog items?
questions.explanation: You can apply several user criteria records to a single catalog item or category. In this situation, users match only one of these criteria records to have access.

questions.question: What is the sequence of conditions in a ServiceNow SLA definition?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Start, Pause, Stop
• In ServiceNow, an SLA (Service Level Agreement) definition includes conditions that determine when the SLA starts, when it is paused, and when it stops.
• These three conditions define the lifecycle of the SLA and ensure accurate tracking of service commitments.
• This is the correct sequence used in SLA definitions.
Incorrect
Option A. Start, Hold, Halt
• “Hold” and “Halt” are not valid SLA condition names in ServiceNow.
• The platform uses Pause and Stop instead.
Option B. Start, In Progress, Stop
• “In Progress” is a task state, not an SLA condition.
• SLA definitions do not use “In Progress” as part of their lifecycle.
Option C. Begin, Hold, Halt
• “Begin” is not the correct terminology (ServiceNow uses Start).
• Similarly, “Hold” and “Halt” are not valid SLA condition names.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct when referring to UI Actions?
options: UI Actions on the Task Table are not available to its extended tables.
UI Actions are only executed on the server.
Conditions can be specified to determine when a UI Action appears
UI Actions cannot use scripts or be scripted.
questions.explanation:
Correct:
Option C.
Conditions can be specified to determine when a UI Action appears.
UI Actions in ServiceNow support condition fields and scripts that control their visibility and availability based on record state, user role, or other criteria. This allows administrators to show or hide UI Actions dynamically.
Incorrect:
Option A.
UI Actions on the Task table are not available to its extended tables.
This is incorrect because UI Actions created on the Task table are inherited by tables that extend Task (such as Incident, Problem, and Change), unless explicitly restricted.
Option B.
UI Actions are only executed on the server.
UI Actions can run client-side scripts, server-side scripts, or a combination of both, depending on how they are configured.
Option D.
UI Actions cannot use scripts or be scripted.
This is incorrect because UI Actions can contain scripted logic, including client scripts and server-side scripts, to perform actions when triggered.

questions.question: Which of the below role is required to manage UI policies?
questions.explanation:
With role “ui_policy_admin”, you can use UI policies to make the number field on a form read-only, make the short description field mandatory, and hide other fields. Basic UI policies do not require any scripting, however for more advanced actions, use the Run scripts option.
You can also use client scripts to perform all of these actions, but for faster load times use UI policies when possible.

questions.question: For UI policy to be applied on all views, which among the following should be checked?
questions.explanation: A UI policy needs to be global to be applied on all views.

questions.question: Which role will a user require to initiate the setup of Agent Intelligence?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Admin or ml_admin
• Correct because to initiate the setup of Agent Intelligence (ServiceNow’s machine learning framework), a user must have either the admin role or the ml_admin role.
• These roles provide the necessary permissions to configure predictive intelligence models, manage training data, and enable the feature in the instance.
Incorrect
Option A. security_admin
• Incorrect because the security_admin role is used for managing security‑related configurations such as access controls and encryption keys.
• It does not grant permissions to set up Agent Intelligence.
Option C. agent_admin
• Incorrect because there is no standard agent_admin role in ServiceNow related to Agent Intelligence setup.
• This option is misleading and not valid for enabling predictive intelligence.

questions.question: What CMDB table stores the basic attributes of all the configuration items?
questions.explanation:
Configuration Item [cmdb_ci] table stores the basic attributes of all the configuration items.
Base Configuration Item [cmdb] is the base CMDB table for non-IT CIs.
CI Relationship [cmdb_rel_ci] contains CI relationship data.
Configuration File [cmdb_ci_config_file] is one of the CI types.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: Is it true that any user can have multiple roles but can only be part of a single assignment group on ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. FALSE
• Correct. In ServiceNow, a user can indeed have multiple roles (e.g., itil, admin, catalog_admin).
• However, a user can also belong to multiple assignment groups. Assignment groups are used to route tasks (like incidents, changes, or requests) to the right team. A single user may be part of several groups (e.g., “Network Support,” “Database Team,” “Help Desk”).
• Therefore, the statement that a user can only be part of a single assignment group is incorrect.
Incorrect
Option A. TRUE
• Incorrect. While the first part of the statement (users can have multiple roles) is true, the second part (only one assignment group) is false. ServiceNow allows users to be members of multiple assignment groups simultaneously.

questions.question: What information does the System Dictionary contain?
options: The human-readable labels and language settings
The definition for each table and column
The language dictionary used for spell checking
The information on how tables relate to each other
questions.explanation:
The system dictionary is a table, called Dictionary Entry [sys_dictionary], that contains details for each table and the definition for every column on each table in an instance.
Each row in the system dictionary represents either a table or a column in one of the tables. The system dictionary provides options for administrators to modify tables and fields, which in turn define lists and forms.
Reference: System Dictionary

questions.question: An IT manager is responsible for the network and hardware assignment groups, each group contains 5 team members. These team members are working on many tasks, but the manager cannot see any tasks on the Service Desk > My Groups Work List. What could explain this?
options: The manager is not a member of the network and hardware groups
The manager is not a member of the service desk group
The assignment group manager field is empty
The manager does not have the ITIL role
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A: The manager is not a member of the network and hardware groups
• Correct because the My Groups Work List only shows tasks assigned to groups that the logged-in user is a member of.
• Even though the manager oversees the groups, if they are not explicitly added as a member of those groups, they will not see the tasks.
Incorrect
Option B: The manager is not a member of the service desk group
• Incorrect because being part of the service desk group is not required to view tasks in My Groups Work List.
• What matters is membership in the specific assignment groups (network and hardware), not the service desk group.
Option C: The assignment group manager field is empty
• Incorrect because the assignment group manager field is for administrative purposes and does not control visibility in My Groups Work List.
• Group managers do not automatically see tasks unless they are also group members.
Option D: The manager does not have the ITIL role
• Incorrect because while the ITIL role is required to work with incidents and tasks, the issue here is group membership, not role assignment.
• Even with ITIL, the manager would not see tasks unless they belong to the groups.

questions.question: Which of the following is true of Service Catalog Items in relation to the Service Catalog?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. They are the building blocks
• Correct because:
• In ServiceNow, the Service Catalog is made up of Catalog Items.
• Catalog Items are the fundamental building blocks that represent services or goods offered to users (e.g., request a laptop, reset a password, order software).
• Without Catalog Items, the Service Catalog cannot function, making this the true statement.
Incorrect
Option A. They provide options
• Incorrect because Catalog Items themselves are not “options.” Instead, they contain variables that provide options to users (like color, size, or configuration).
Option B. They run behind the scenes
• Incorrect because Catalog Items are visible to end users in the Service Catalog. Behind‑the‑scenes processes are handled by workflows, approvals, and scripts, not the items themselves.
Option C. They are optional
• Incorrect because Catalog Items are not optional; they are required to define what services or products are available in the Service Catalog.

questions.question: What is the path an Administrator could take to view the fulfillment stage task list for an order placed by a user?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
Within a request, there can be one or more request items. For each request item, it takes one or more tasks to fulfill it.
a) Request ticket starts with REQ
b) Request item ticket starts with RITM
c) Task ticket starts with TASK

questions.question: The MID Server enables communication and the movement of data between ServiceNow instance and external applications, data sources, and services. Which table stores all related communication records in this regard?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. ECC Queue (ecc_queue) table
• The ECC Queue (ecc_queue) table is the central table that stores all communication records between the ServiceNow instance and the MID Server.
• It contains input and output messages, ensuring proper orchestration of requests and responses.
• Correct answer.
Incorrect
Option A. ECC Queue (cmdb_ci_queue) table
• This is not a valid table for MID Server communication.
• The prefix cmdb_ci refers to configuration items in the CMDB, not ECC Queue records.
• Incorrect.
Option C. ECC Queue (cmdb_ecc_queue) table
• Similarly, this is not a valid table name in ServiceNow.
• The ECC Queue table is specifically ecc_queue, without CMDB prefixes.
• Incorrect.

questions.question: When adding a variable to a catalog item, what does an order field determine?
options: The order field displays the fulfillment priority value in calculating and presenting an expected delivery date
The order field value is used to display the variable by price. The order is moreexpensive to less expensive
The order field establishes the display order of the variables. Variables are listed by ascending order values.
The order field sets the availability of the variable item by graying the item if it is not available to, he ordered
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. The order field establishes the display order of the variables. Variables are listed by ascending order values
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the order field determines the sequence in which variables appear on the catalog item form.
• Lower order values are displayed first, and higher values follow.
• This is purely a UI display control, not related to fulfillment, pricing, or availability.
Incorrect
Option A. Fulfillment priority / delivery date
• Incorrect because the order field does not affect fulfillment or delivery calculations.
• Fulfillment priority is managed through workflows and SLA definitions, not variable order fields.
Option B. Display by price (expensive to less expensive)
• Incorrect because the order field is not tied to pricing.
• Pricing is managed through catalog item configuration and variable pricing rules, not the order field.
Option D. Availability control (graying out items)
• Incorrect because availability is controlled by UI policies, catalog client scripts, or ACLs, not the order field.
• The order field only controls display sequence, not availability.

questions.question: Any ServiceNow user can impersonate other user on ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. FALSE
This is correct because not all ServiceNow users can impersonate other users. The impersonation feature is restricted to users with the admin role or specific elevated privileges. It is a powerful capability used for troubleshooting and testing, but it is not available to every user for security reasons.
Incorrect
Option A. TRUE
• Incorrect because allowing all users to impersonate others would be a major security risk. Impersonation could expose sensitive data or allow unauthorized actions. ServiceNow limits this functionality to administrators or users with explicit permissions.

questions.question: You can limit Service Now instance access by IP ranges?
questions.explanation: You can limit Service Now instance access by IP ranges that can be defined in white listed IP fields.

questions.question: Two departments (HR onboarding and facilities) have come to you, asking for a way for employees to request event room setup services. The requirements are the same for the form and the task routing to the facilities assignment group. 1) For HR, the item will be used primarily for the onboarding condition, for employees orientation sessions. 2) for facilities, the item will be used for anyone in the company who needs room setup services. However, both departments have their own service catalogs. what do you do, to support these requirements?
options: create one catalog item for HR event room setup and one for facilities even room setup; then publish each to the appropriate catalog
create one catalog item for event room setup; then publish to the parent catalogue, which is accessible to both HR and facilities
create one catalog item for event room setup; then use ACLs to control access
create one catalogue item for event room setup; then publish to both catalogs
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Create one catalogue item for event room setup; then publish to both catalogs
• Correct because you only need one catalog item since the requirements (form and routing) are identical.
• ServiceNow allows publishing the same catalog item to multiple catalogs.
• This minimizes duplication, reduces maintenance overhead, and ensures consistency across HR and Facilities.
Incorrect
Option A. Create one catalog item for HR event room setup and one for Facilities event room setup; then publish each to the appropriate catalog
• Incorrect because this duplicates the catalog item unnecessarily.
• It increases maintenance overhead since any change would need to be updated in two separate items.
Option B. Create one catalog item for event room setup; then publish to the parent catalogue, which is accessible to both HR and Facilities
• Incorrect because ServiceNow does not use a “parent catalog” concept in this way.
• Catalogs are independent, and items must be explicitly published to each catalog.
Option C. Create one catalog item for event room setup; then use ACLs to control access
• Incorrect because ACLs control security and access, not catalog publishing.
• This approach would complicate access unnecessarily when the requirement is simply to publish to both catalogs.

questions.question: What do you use in CMDB Workspace to verify the existence of actual IT infrastructure and applications that you own, systematically and in bulk?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. CI Attestation
• Correct because CI Attestation in CMDB Workspace is specifically designed to verify the existence of actual IT infrastructure and applications.
• It allows owners to systematically confirm and validate CIs in bulk, ensuring that the CMDB reflects reality.
• This process improves CMDB accuracy and trustworthiness by requiring attestation from responsible stakeholders.
Incorrect
Option A. Multisource Report Builder
• Incorrect because this tool is used to create reports from multiple data sources, not to verify infrastructure existence.
• It helps with reporting and analytics, but not attestation.
Option B. Service Graph Connectors
• Incorrect because Service Graph Connectors are used to integrate external data sources into the CMDB.
• They help populate and enrich CMDB data but do not verify ownership or existence of infrastructure.
Option C. Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE)
• Incorrect because IRE ensures data consistency and avoids duplicates when importing data into the CMDB.
• It reconciles attributes but does not perform attestation or verification of infrastructure existence.
Option E. IntegrationHub ETL
• Incorrect because IntegrationHub ETL is used for extract, transform, and load operations to bring external data into ServiceNow.
• It is a data integration tool, not a verification mechanism.

questions.question: Which module displays a list of tasks assigned to a user’s group but not yet assigned to an individual user?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
By default, the ITIL Homepage includes the following reports.
Users by location: a pie chart displaying users divided by location.
Open Items by Escalation: tasks with an open state, grouped by escalation.
My Groups Work: outstanding work for your group (not yet assigned to individual user)
My Work: your outstanding work.
ITIL Summary Counts: tasks that are critical, overdue, and over a week old.
These reports link directly to the appropriate records and tables. Use the work queues and the reports on critical tasks to manage your work directly from the homepage.

questions.question: Is it true that you cannot revert update set versions?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. FALSE
• In ServiceNow, update sets can be reverted to previous versions.
• Administrators have the ability to rollback changes if needed.
• Therefore, the statement “you cannot revert update set versions” is false.
Incorrect
Option B. TRUE
• Suggests that update set versions cannot be reverted.
• This is incorrect because ServiceNow provides the option to revert update set versions.
• Misrepresents the platform’s functionality.

questions.question: What can agents do with the Sidebar feature in the Next Experience UI? (Choose 2)
options: Integrate with other Workspaces to display related records.
Create, open and search for discussions about their work
Have real-time collaboration with others from a Workspace interaction-based record
Broadcast a text message or initiate a conference call with other agents
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Create, open and search for discussions about their work
• Correct because the Sidebar allows agents to collaborate and communicate by creating or joining discussions directly related to their tasks.
• This feature helps agents stay aligned with team activities without leaving the Workspace.
Option D. Have real-time collaboration with others from a Workspace interaction-based record
• Correct because the Sidebar provides real-time collaboration tools.
• Agents can interact with colleagues while working on records, ensuring context is shared instantly and improving efficiency.
Incorrect
Option A. Integrate with other Workspaces to display related records
• Incorrect because the Sidebar is not designed to integrate or display records from other Workspaces. Its purpose is collaboration and communication, not record integration.
Option C. Communicate with the caller/requester directly
• Incorrect because communication with callers or requesters is handled through channels like Virtual Agent or case comments, not the Sidebar.
Option E. Broadcast a text message or initiate a conference call with other agents
• Incorrect because the Sidebar does not provide broadcasting or conferencing capabilities. It focuses on collaboration within Workspace records, not mass communication.

questions.question: Which of the following operation is a record-type access control list that restricts access to reports based on a role?
questions.explanation:
The report_view operation is a record-type access control list (ACL) that restricts access to reports. Only users with one of the required roles can view reports containing the restricted resource.
There are two kinds of report_view access control lists (ACLs):
1. report_view table ACLs, and
2. report_view field ACLs.
Report_view table ACLs prevent users from viewing report content based on the table specified in the ACL.
Report_view field ACLs prevent users from viewing reports that use the field specified in the ACL in the group by, row, column or aggregation.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is a recommendation from ServiceNow about Update Sets?
options: Use the Baseline Update Set to store the contents of items after they are changed the first time
Before moving customizations from instance to instance with Update Sets, ensure that both instances are different versions
Once an Update Set is closed as “Complete“, change it back to “In Progress“ until it is applied to another instance
Avoid using the Default Update set as an Update Set for moving customization from instance to instance
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Avoid using the Default Update Set as an Update Set for moving customization from instance to instance
• Correct because ServiceNow strongly recommends not using the Default Update Set for migration.
• The Default Update Set is intended only for capturing changes when no other Update Set is selected.
• Using it for migration can cause confusion, incomplete transfers, and difficulty in tracking changes.
• Best practice is to create named Update Sets for each customization effort and use those for moving changes between instances.
Incorrect
Option A. Use the Baseline Update Set to store the contents of items after they are changed the first time
• Incorrect because the Baseline Update Set is automatically created by ServiceNow to capture the original state of items before customization.
• It is not meant to store changes after they are made, nor is it used for migration.
Option B. Before moving customizations from instance to instance with Update Sets, ensure that both instances are different versions
• Incorrect because ServiceNow recommends that instances be on the same version when migrating Update Sets.
• Moving Update Sets between different versions can cause compatibility issues and errors.
Option C. Once an Update Set is closed as “Complete”, change it back to “In Progress” until it is applied to another instance
• Incorrect because once an Update Set is marked Complete, it should not be reopened.
• Reopening can corrupt the migration process. Instead, you should export/import the completed Update Set to the target instance.

questions.question: What details can you find in the import set record after running an import? (Choose 3)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Import Log
• Correct because the Import Log provides detailed information about the import execution, including errors, warnings, and success messages.
• This helps administrators troubleshoot and validate the import process.
Option D. Import Set Runs
• Correct because Import Set Runs track each execution of an import set, showing when it was run, its status, and the results.
• This is essential for auditing and monitoring import activity.
Option F. Import Set Rows
• Correct because Import Set Rows contain the actual data records that were imported.
• Each row represents a piece of source data that has been staged in the import set table before being transformed into the target table.
Incorrect
Option A. Import Maps
• Incorrect because Import Maps define how source data maps to target tables, but they are not part of the import set record itself.
• They are configuration objects used before or during the import, not details stored in the record after execution.
Option B. Import Set API
• Incorrect because the Import Set API is a mechanism for programmatic imports, not a detail stored in the import set record.
• It is used externally to push data into ServiceNow.
Option E. Concurrent Import Sets
• Incorrect because this refers to multiple imports running simultaneously, not a detail of a single import set record.
• It is more about system behavior than record-level information.

questions.question: Which of the following statement describes the purpose of an Order Guide?
options: Order Guide provides a list of guidelines for Administrators on how to set up item variables
Order Guides take the user directly to the checkout without prompting for information
Order Guide restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request
Order Guide provides the ability to order multiple, related items as one request
questions.explanation:
Order guide submits a single service catalog request that generates several items.
Order guides determine which catalog items to order by evaluating order guide rule conditions. Information the customer enters within the order guide can be passed as cascading variables to the ordered items, allowing common information to be reused across multiple items.
Reference: Order Guide

questions.question: Which one of the following statements describes the purpose of a Service Catalog workflow?
options: A Service Catalog workflow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and notifications
A Service Catalog workflow generates three basic components. item variable types, tasks, and approvals
Although a Service Catalog workflow cannot send notifications, the workflow drives complex fulfillment processes
A Service Catalog workflow is used to drive complex fulfillment processes and sends notifications to defined users or groups
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. A Service Catalog workflow is used to drive complex fulfillment processes and sends notifications to defined users or groups
• Correct because the primary purpose of a Service Catalog workflow is to manage the fulfillment process of catalog requests.
• It can include tasks, approvals, and notifications, ensuring that requests are processed efficiently and stakeholders are informed.
• This aligns with the CSA exam expectation: workflows automate fulfillment and communication.
Incorrect
• Option A. A Service Catalog workflow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and notifications
• Incorrect because item variable types are not generated by workflows; they are defined at the catalog item level.
• Workflows handle fulfillment, not variable creation.
• Option B. A Service Catalog workflow generates three basic components: item variable types, tasks, and approvals
• Incorrect for the same reason as Option A: workflows do not generate variable types.
• Approvals and tasks are valid, but variable types are not part of workflow generation.
• Option C. Although a Service Catalog workflow cannot send notifications, the workflow drives complex fulfillment processes
• Incorrect because workflows can send notifications.
• This option is misleading and contradicts ServiceNow functionality.

questions.question: Which technique is used to get information from a series of referenced fields from different tables?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option C. Dot-Walking This is correct because Dot-Walking is the ServiceNow technique that allows you to access information from referenced fields across related tables. For example, if you have an Incident record referencing a User, you can “dot walk” into the User table to pull fields like user.email. It is the standard method used in ServiceNow to traverse relationships between tables.
Incorrect
• Option A. Table-Walking Incorrect because “Table-Walking” is not a valid ServiceNow term or technique. It is a distractor that sounds similar but does not exist in the platform.
• Option B. Sys ID Pulling Incorrect because while Sys IDs uniquely identify records, pulling Sys IDs does not provide field-level information across tables. It is not a technique for accessing referenced fields.
• Option D. Record-Hopping Incorrect because “Record-Hopping” is not a recognized ServiceNow technique. Like Table-Walking, it is a distractor term with no actual functionality in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Which knowledge feedback option CANNOT be disabled at the knowledge base level?
options: All of them can be disabled
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. All of them can be disabled
• Correct because in ServiceNow, knowledge feedback options such as marking as helpful, commenting, flagging, and rating can all be controlled at the knowledge base level.
• Administrators can configure whether these feedback mechanisms are enabled or disabled for each knowledge base.
• Therefore, none of the listed options are permanently enforced — they can all be disabled.
Incorrect
Option A. Marking as helpful
• Incorrect because this option can be disabled at the knowledge base level.
• It is not mandatory to keep it enabled.
Option B. Commenting
• Incorrect because commenting can also be disabled at the knowledge base level.
• Admins can restrict user feedback through comments if desired.
Option D. Flagging
• Incorrect because flagging inappropriate or incorrect articles can also be disabled.
• It is configurable per knowledge base.
Option E. Rating
• Incorrect because rating (e.g., star ratings) can also be disabled at the knowledge base level.
• It is not a mandatory feedback option.

questions.question: Buttons, form links and context menu items are example of what type of functionality?
questions.explanation:
UI actions include the buttons, links, and context menu items on forms and lists. Configure UI actions to make the UI more interactive, customized, and specific to user activities.
Administrators and users with the ui_action_admin role can define UI actions.

questions.question: What is the name of the conversational bot platform that provides assistance to help users obtain information, make decisions, and perform common tasks?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow Virtual Agent is a platform for providing user assistance through conversations within a messaging interface. Use ServiceNow Virtual Agent to design and build automated conversations that help your users quickly obtain information, make decisions, and perform common work tasks.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: For Administrators creating new Service Catalog items, what is the characteristic they should know about Service Catalog variables?
options: Service Catalog variables can only be used in Record Producers
Service Catalog variables cannot affect the order price
Service Catalog variables can only be used in Order Guides
Service Catalog variables are global by default
questions.explanation:
Global : An option to show the variable in all catalog tasks within service catalog workflows or execution plans by default. The variable must be attached to individual catalog tasks if this option is not selected.
Reference: Service Catalog variable

questions.question: When using the Load Data and Transform Map process, what is the Mapping Assist used for?
options: Mapping fields using the Import Log
Mapping fields using a Field Map
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Mapping fields using a Field Map
• Correct because Mapping Assist in ServiceNow helps administrators quickly align source fields (from the import set table) with target fields (in the destination table).
• It leverages Field Maps to suggest or apply mappings, reducing manual effort and ensuring consistency.
• This is the intended functionality of Mapping Assist during the Load Data and Transform Map process.
Incorrect
Option A. Mapping fields using Transform History
• Incorrect because Transform History is used to track past transform events and results, not to assist in mapping fields.
Option B. Mapping fields using the Import Log
• Incorrect because the Import Log records the status of imported data (success, errors, etc.), but it does not provide field mapping assistance.
Option C. Mapping fields using an SLA
• Incorrect because SLAs (Service Level Agreements) are unrelated to data import or field mapping. They measure performance against defined service targets, not data transformation.

questions.question: Which of the following can be customized through the Basic Configuration UI 16 module? (Choose three)
questions.explanation:
CORRECT
Option B. System Date Format
Explanation:
• The Basic Configuration UI 16 module allows administrators to configure system-wide date and time formats.
• This ensures consistency across forms, lists, and reports.
Option C. Banner Image
Explanation:
• You can customize the banner image (the logo or branding at the top of the ServiceNow interface).
• This is commonly used to apply corporate branding.
Option D. Browser Tab Title
Explanation:
• The browser tab title can be customized to reflect the organization’s name or environment (e.g., “ServiceNow – Production”).
• This helps users distinguish between multiple ServiceNow instances.
INCORRECT
Option A. Record Number Format
Explanation:
• Record number format (e.g., INC0001 for incidents) is configured through Number Maintenance, not the Basic Configuration UI 16 module.
• Therefore, this option is incorrect.
Option E. Form Header Size
Explanation:
• Form header size is not configurable through Basic Configuration UI 16.
• UI 16 focuses on branding and general system settings, not layout-specific adjustments like header sizing.

questions.question: Which term best describes something that is created, has worked performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a state of closed?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. task
• In ServiceNow, a task is the fundamental record type that represents work to be performed.
• Tasks are created, worked on, and eventually moved to a closed state once completed.
• Examples include incidents, problems, changes, and service requests—all of which extend the task table.
• This is the correct answer because it directly matches the definition in the question.
Incorrect
Option A. workflow
• A workflow is a process automation tool that defines how tasks move through states.
• It is not itself something that is “created and closed”; instead, it orchestrates the lifecycle of tasks.
Option B. report
• A report is used to visualize and analyze data in ServiceNow.
• Reports are not created, worked on, and closed in the same sense as tasks.
Option C. event
• An event is a system notification mechanism used for triggers and responses.
• Events are not worked on by users and do not follow a “created → worked → closed” lifecycle.

questions.question: A knowledge article must be which of the following states to display
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Published
• Correct because only Published knowledge articles are visible to end users in the Knowledge Base.
• The Published state indicates the article has passed review/approval and is ready for consumption.
• Drafted, Reviewed, or Retired articles remain hidden from general display.
Incorrect
Option A. Drafted
• Incorrect because Drafted articles are still being created or edited.
• They are not visible to end users until they are published.
Option C. Retired
• Incorrect because Retired articles are intentionally removed from active use.
• They remain in the system for reference but are not displayed to users.
Option D. Reviewed
• Incorrect because Reviewed is an intermediate state where the article has been checked but not yet published.
• It cannot be displayed until it transitions to Published.

questions.question: What allows agents to initiate a group discussion from a Workspace task‑based or interaction‑based record?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Sidebar
• Correct because in ServiceNow Agent Workspace, the Sidebar provides collaboration features.
• Agents can initiate group discussions directly from task‑based or interaction‑based records using the Sidebar.
• This enables real‑time communication and collaboration without leaving the Workspace context.
Incorrect
Option A. Help menu
• Incorrect because the Help menu provides documentation, guided tours, and support resources.
• It does not allow agents to start group discussions.
Option C. Connect Hub
• Incorrect because Connect is ServiceNow’s older chat framework.
• In Workspace, group discussions are initiated via the Sidebar, not Connect Hub.
Option D. Virtual Agent
• Incorrect because Virtual Agent is a conversational bot for self‑service and automation.
• It does not initiate group discussions among human agents.
Option E. Chatbot
• Incorrect because “Chatbot” is a generic term, not a ServiceNow Workspace feature.
• Group discussions are specifically tied to the Sidebar functionality.

questions.question: What will happen if you make the short description field on task table as mandatory at the dictionary level?
options: Short description will be mandated on incident table only
Short description will be mandated on all the tables which are extending task table
questions.explanation:
Child classes derive fields from parent classes. For example, the Incident table derives fields from the Task table. Hence, short description will be mandated on all the tables which are extending task table.
Ref – https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/orlando-platform-administration/page/administer/table-administration/concept/table-extension-and-classes.html

questions.question: Which of the following allows a user to edit field values in a list without opening the form?
questions.explanation: The list editor allows you to edit field values directly from a list without navigating to a form.

questions.question: IntegrationHub enables execution of third-party APIs as a part of a flow. These integrations are referred to as:
questions.explanation:
A spoke is a scoped application that includes Flow Designer or IntegrationHub actions or subflows. A spoke is a logical grouping of related actions, subflows, and supporting application files. Developers and Process Designers can reuse spoke logic in their own applications. IntegrationHub includes baseline spokes. Developers can obtain additional spokes from the ServiceNow Store, Share, or create their own.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: Which of the following statements is true when a new table is created by extending another table?
options: The new table archives the parent table and assumed its roles in the database
The new table inherits all of the Business Rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table, but none of the existing fields
The new table inherits all of the fields, but does not inherit Access Control rules, Client Scripts, and UI Policies of the parent table
The new table inherits all of the fields of the parent table and can also contain new fields unique to itself
questions.explanation: When you add new field to parent, that field will automatically be inherited by all child tables.

questions.question: A REQ number in the Service Catalog represents.
options: the individual item in the order
questions.explanation: Reference: Track a request

questions.question: What are the different Schema relationship types that are supported for tables? (Choose 4)
questions.explanation:
The four different Schema relationship types supported for tables are:
1. Referenced by,
2. Referencing,
3. Extended by, and
4. Extending.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: Which term refers to application menus and modules which you may want to access quickly and often?
questions.explanation:
Items you add as favourites appear in the favourites tab of the application navigator, which is represented by a star icon.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: How are Workflows moved between instances?
options: Workflows are moved using Application Sets
Workflow cannot be moved between instances
Workflows are moved using Update Sets
Workflows are moved using Transform Maps
questions.explanation:
The system tracks workflows in update sets differently than other records because workflow information is stored across multiple tables.
Changes made to a workflow version are not added to the update set until the workflow is published, at which point the entire workflow is added into the update set.

questions.question: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to which of the following components?
options: Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Workflows
Order Guides, Item Variables, and Workflows
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
Record Producers, Order Guides, and tem Variables
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
• Correct because the baseline Service Catalog homepage in ServiceNow provides links to:
• Record Producers → used to create records in tables (e.g., incident, change request) through a simplified form.
• Order Guides → help users order multiple related items in a single request.
• Catalog Items → represent the actual goods or services offered (e.g., request a laptop, software, or password reset).
• These three are the core components accessible from the Service Catalog homepage.
Incorrect
Option A. Order Guides, Catalog Items, and Workflows
• Incorrect because workflows are behind-the-scenes automation tied to catalog items, not directly linked from the homepage.
Option B. Order Guides, Item Variables, and Workflows
• Incorrect because item variables are part of catalog items but not standalone links on the homepage.
• Workflows again are not directly accessible from the homepage.
Option D. Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables
• Incorrect because while record producers and order guides are correct, item variables are not listed separately on the homepage.
• Variables are embedded within catalog items, not independent links.

questions.question: There is a business requirement to restrict incident reporting to specific roles for better governance. The Development team decided to add a new access control (ACL), so only those roles can view the contents of the reports on the incident table. What access control operation should they use to allow this access on the incident table?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. report_view
• Correct because the report_view ACL operation is specifically designed to control access to viewing reports on a table.
• By applying this ACL to the incident table, only users with the specified roles will be able to view the report contents, meeting the governance requirement.
Incorrect
Option A. report_on
• Incorrect because report_on controls whether a user can create reports on a table, not view them.
• This does not meet the requirement of restricting report viewing.
Option B. add_to_list
• Incorrect because add_to_list controls whether a user can add records to a list, not related to report viewing.
Option C. execute
• Incorrect because execute is used for running scripts or functions, not for report access.
Option E. read
• Incorrect because read ACLs control access to records and fields, not specifically to reports.
• While read is important for general data access, the requirement is about restricting report viewing, which is handled by report_view.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is correct when referring to UI Actions?
options: UI Action on the task table are not available to its extended tables
UI Actions cannot use scripts or be scripted
UI Actions are only executed on the server
Conditions can be specified to be determined when a UI Action appears
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Conditions can be specified to be determined when a UI Action appears
• Correct because UI Actions in ServiceNow can be configured with conditions that control their visibility.
• For example, a button or link can be set to appear only when a record meets certain criteria (such as state = “Open”).
• This makes UI Actions flexible and context‑aware, ensuring they only appear when relevant.
Incorrect
Option A. UI Action on the task table are not available to its extended tables
• Incorrect because UI Actions defined on the task table are inherited by extended tables (like Incident, Problem, Change).
• This inheritance is a fundamental feature of ServiceNow’s table hierarchy.
Option B. UI Actions cannot use scripts or be scripted
• Incorrect because UI Actions often rely on scripts to perform actions such as redirecting users, updating records, or triggering workflows.
• Scripting is a core capability of UI Actions.
Option C. UI Actions are only executed on the server
• Incorrect because UI Actions can run client‑side scripts (executed in the browser) or server‑side scripts (executed on the server).
• They are not limited to server execution.

questions.question: Which feature enables you to add related entries for Identification and Reconciliation Engine (IRE) identification rules?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. CI Class Manager
• This is correct.
• The CI Class Manager feature allows administrators to configure CI classes and manage identification rules.
• It specifically enables adding related entries for IRE identification rules, ensuring that configuration items are properly identified and reconciled in the CMDB.
• This is the required feature for extending and managing IRE rules.
Incorrect
Option A. IntegrationHub ETL
• Incorrect because IntegrationHub ETL is used for extracting, transforming, and loading external data into ServiceNow.
• It does not provide functionality for adding related entries to IRE identification rules.
Option B. CMDB Data Manager
• Incorrect because CMDB Data Manager is used for lifecycle management and governance of CI data.
• It does not directly handle adding related entries for IRE identification rules.
Option D. Service Graph connectors
• Incorrect because Service Graph connectors are used to integrate external systems and bring data into the CMDB.
• They help populate the CMDB but do not provide the feature to add related entries for IRE identification rules.

questions.question: Which feature enables you to maintain a unified content categorization across different content types, such as catalogue items, knowledge articles, and community posts?
questions.explanation:
The taxonomy feature enables you to link an article to one or more topics from multiple taxonomies. It also helps you maintain a unified content categorisation across content types such as catalogue items, knowledge articles, and community posts.
Content Taxonomy is the application that provides the data model or the topic hierarchy and the taxonomy management (content authoring) capabilities for the unified taxonomy. The content types mapped by default are requests, articles, quick links, and employee communications. Once the plugin is downloaded, this mapping will be visible as part of the content taxonomy app in the platform.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: Which one of the following phrases completes the statement: “The purpose of transform map is to“
options: Create a set of new tables before any data is imported during the load data process.
Determine the relationship between fields displaying in an import set table to the fields in an existing ServiceNow table.
Encrypt data within the instance for higher security.
It adds a dummy record to align fields in a table before an administrator runs transform.
questions.explanation:
A transform map is a set of field maps that determine the relationships between fields in an import set and fields in an existing ServiceNow table, such as Incident [incident] or User [sys_user].
The Transform Maps module enables an administrator to define destinations for imported data on any tables. Transform mapping can be as simple as a drag and drop operation to specify linking between source fields on an import set table and destination fields on any table. Use transform mapping to map source and destination fields dynamically.

questions.question: Which of the following describes the purpose of an order guide?
options: Order guides provide a list of guidelines for administrators on how to set up item variables
Order guides provide me ability to order multiple related items as one request
Order guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request
Order guides take the user directly to the checkout without prompting for information
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option B. Order guides provide the ability to order multiple related items as one request
• Correct because the purpose of an order guide in ServiceNow is to help users order multiple related catalog items together in a single request.
• For example, when onboarding a new employee, an order guide can group items like a laptop, software licenses, and access badges into one guided request.
• This improves efficiency and ensures consistency in fulfilling related service catalog items.
Incorrect
• Option A. Order guides provide a list of guidelines for administrators on how to set up item variables
• Incorrect because order guides are not documentation tools for administrators. They are designed for end‑users to request multiple items, not for admin guidance.
• Option C. Order guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request
• Incorrect because order guides do the opposite — they allow multiple items to be ordered together, not restrict to one.
• Option D. Order guides take the user directly to the checkout without prompting for information
• Incorrect because order guides are interactive. They prompt users with questions to determine which items should be included in the request before checkout.

questions.question: How to manage record numbering (like INC0000777)?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. System Definition > Number maintenance
• Correct because ServiceNow uses the Number Maintenance module to manage record numbering for tables such as Incident (INC), Problem (PRB), Change (CHG), etc.
• Administrators can configure prefixes, number length, and the next available number from this module.
• Example: Setting the incident prefix to INC and defining the number format ensures records are created as INC0000777.
Incorrect
Option B. Number field > Number
• Incorrect because the numbering is not managed directly at the field level.
• The “Number” field simply stores the generated value, but the logic for numbering is controlled through Number Maintenance, not the field itself.
Option C. System Definition > Numbers
• Incorrect because there is no module named “Numbers” under System Definition.
• This is a distractor option.
Option D. None of the above
• Incorrect because Option A is valid.
• Record numbering is indeed managed through System Definition > Number Maintenance.

questions.question: What is contextual security in ServiceNow?
options: The contextual security manager profile incredible flexibility and power to perfect information by controlling read/write authorization.
It doesn‘t apply the security rules to any level in the object hierarchy.
In platform security Settings, High automatically activities the contextual security plugin if is already active.
Protects a record based on its contents and table location, data is acted upon based on the position of the information in the table hierarchy. Defines access control rules to any level.
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. Protects a record based on its contents and table location
• Correct: Contextual security in ServiceNow means that records are protected based on their context (contents and table hierarchy).
• Access control rules can be defined at any level in the hierarchy (table, field, or record).
• This ensures fine‑grained security, allowing administrators to enforce rules depending on where the data resides and its context.
Incorrect
• Option A. Flexibility to control read/write authorization
• Incorrect: While ACLs do provide read/write control, this description is vague and does not capture the contextual nature of ServiceNow security.
• Option B. Doesn’t apply security rules to any level
• Incorrect: This is the opposite of contextual security. In fact, contextual security does apply rules at multiple levels in the hierarchy.
• Option C. High automatically activates contextual security plugin
• Incorrect: This statement is inaccurate and misleading. Contextual security is not about automatic activation of plugins; it is about hierarchical ACL enforcement.

questions.question: What are the three components of a filter condition?
questions.explanation: Condition builder format works in Field > Operator > Value fashion.

questions.question: What is the primary application used to load data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
To load data from a data source into a staging table, use the Application Navigator in the main ServiceNow browser window to open System Import Sets > Load Data. The configuration options vary depending on the Data Source. In the example, the Data Source is an Excel file. The staging table, x_snc_employee_spe_occasions_staging, is created dynamically.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: Which statement of the following is correct when referring to UI actions?
options: UI actions are only executed on the server.
UI Actions cannot use scripts or be scripted.
Conditions can be specified to determine when a UI Action appears.
UI Actions on the task table are not available to its extended tables.
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option C. Conditions can be specified to determine when a UI Action appears.
• Correct because UI Actions in ServiceNow can be configured with conditions that control their visibility.
• For example, you can set conditions so that a button or link only appears when a record meets certain criteria.
• This is a key feature of UI Actions, allowing administrators to tailor the user interface dynamically.
Incorrect
• Option A. UI actions are only executed on the server.
• Incorrect because UI Actions can run client‑side scripts (executed in the browser) or server‑side scripts (executed on the server). They are not limited to server execution.
• Option B. UI Actions cannot use scripts or be scripted.
• Incorrect because UI Actions often rely on scripts to perform actions such as redirecting users, updating records, or triggering workflows.
• Option D. UI Actions on the task table are not available to its extended tables.
• Incorrect because UI Actions defined on the task table are inherited by its extended tables (e.g., Incident, Problem, Change). This inheritance is a core feature of ServiceNow’s table hierarchy.

questions.question: Which of the following can be configured by all users in the Next Experience instances?
questions.explanation:
Users have a new user preference that enables them to specify the page that appears when they login to the Next Experience user interface.
You can configure a user-selected/personalised start page, other than the default landing page, to appear when you log in to your Next Experience instances.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: Which one of the following is a list of what the Service Catalog contains?
options: Record Producer, Order Guide, and Catalog Items.
Catalog Items, Asset Contracts, Task Surveys.
Order Guide, Catalog Items and Interceptors.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Record Producer, Order Guide, and Catalog Items
• Correct because the Service Catalog in ServiceNow is designed to provide users with a structured way to request services.
• It contains:
• Record Producers → Forms that create records in tables (e.g., incident, request).
• Order Guides → Help users order multiple related items in a single request.
• Catalog Items → Individual services or products that users can request.
• This is the accurate list of what the Service Catalog contains.
Incorrect
Option B. Order Axles, Exchange Rates, Calendar
• Incorrect because these are not Service Catalog components.
• They represent unrelated business concepts, not catalog structures in ServiceNow.
Option C. Catalog Items, Asset Contracts, Task Surveys
• Incorrect because while Catalog Items are valid, Asset Contracts and Task Surveys are not part of the Service Catalog.
• Asset contracts belong to Asset Management, and surveys are part of Feedback/Assessment modules.
Option D. Order Guide, Catalog Items and Interceptors
• Incorrect because Interceptors are not part of the Service Catalog.
• The correct trio is Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items.

questions.question: Which field (or fields) is used as a unique key during imports?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option C. Coalesce Fields Correct because in ServiceNow imports, Coalesce Fields are used to determine whether an incoming record should update an existing record or create a new one. When a field is marked as coalesce, ServiceNow uses it as a unique key to match records during the import process. This ensures proper deduplication and accurate updates.
Incorrect
• Option A. Sys IDs Incorrect because Sys IDs are unique identifiers for records in ServiceNow, but they are not typically used as the matching key during imports. Sys IDs are system-generated and not practical for external data matching.
• Option B. Match Fields Incorrect because “Match Fields” is not a formal concept in ServiceNow imports. The correct terminology is Coalesce Fields, which serve the matching purpose.
• Option D. Key Fields Incorrect because “Key Fields” is a generic term and not specifically tied to ServiceNow’s import process. The platform explicitly uses Coalesce Fields for unique key matching.

questions.question: Which component of a table contains a piece of data for one record?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Field
• In ServiceNow, a field is the component of a table that stores a single piece of data for one record.
• Each record in a table is made up of multiple fields, and each field corresponds to a column in the database.
• For example, in an Incident table, fields might include Number, Short Description, Priority, etc.
Incorrect
Option B. Factor
• “Factor” is not a recognized component of a ServiceNow table. It is unrelated to how data is stored in records.
Option C. Datapoint
• While “datapoint” is a general term in data analysis, it is not the formal ServiceNow terminology. ServiceNow uses fields to represent data values.
Option D. Item
• “Item” refers to catalog items or other ServiceNow objects, not table components. It does not represent a single piece of data in a record.
Option E. Elements
• “Elements” is not the correct term in ServiceNow for table components. The precise term is field.

questions.question: You can add human-readable keywords to the URLs of portal pages to improve search engine optimization (SEO) and click-through rates and help users understand what to expect on the page. What can be added as human-readable keywords to help with SEO? (Select 2)

Correct:
Option A. Dynamic page variables
Dynamic page variables can be included in Service Portal URLs to create meaningful, human-readable keywords. These variables help describe the content of the page, improving SEO, increasing click-through rates, and making URLs easier for users to understand.
Option D. Static content
Static content such as fixed, descriptive words in the URL path provides clear context about the page purpose. Search engines can easily index these keywords, which improves SEO and helps users know what to expect before opening the page.
Incorrect:
Option B. Page parameters
Page parameters are mainly used to pass values internally to a page. They are not optimized for readability or SEO and usually appear as query strings, which are less effective for search engine indexing.
Option C. Sys ID
Sys IDs are system-generated identifiers that are not human-readable. Including them in URLs does not improve SEO and makes links harder for users to interpret.
Option E. Page ID
Page IDs are internal identifiers used by ServiceNow to reference portal pages. They are not descriptive keywords and do not contribute to search engine optimization or user understanding.

questions.question: Why is it recommended that you limit update sets to a maximum of 100 records? (Choose 2 answers)
options: Smaller update sets can be imported to production during business hours
Improve ability to troubleshoot issues with default update set
Make it easier to identify and review changes
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Reduce potential conflicts
• Correct because smaller update sets reduce the chance of overlapping changes or conflicts when merging into production.
• Large update sets make it harder to identify which specific record caused an issue, increasing risk during deployment.
Option E. Make it easier to identify and review changes
• Correct because limiting update sets to fewer records makes them easier to review, test, and validate before moving to production.
• Smaller sets improve visibility and control, ensuring that only intended changes are deployed.
Incorrect
Option A. Comply with ISO audit requirements
• Incorrect because ISO audits are not directly tied to the number of records in update sets.
• Limiting update sets is about practical deployment management, not compliance.
Option B. Smaller update sets can be imported to production during business hours
• Incorrect because update sets should generally be imported during planned maintenance windows, not business hours.
• The recommendation is not based on timing but on minimizing risk and complexity.
Option D. Improve ability to troubleshoot issues with default update set
• Incorrect because the default update set is not intended for production migration.
• Troubleshooting is improved by smaller, well‑defined update sets, not by relying on the default.
Option F. Keeps update set logs shorter
• Incorrect because log length is not the primary concern.
• The focus is on conflict reduction and reviewability, not log size.
