questions.question: Which script runs when a record is displayed, inserted, updated, deleted or when a table is queried?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Business Rule
• Correct because Business Rules are server-side scripts in ServiceNow that run when records are displayed, inserted, updated, deleted, or queried.
• They are powerful automation tools that enforce logic and perform actions at the database level.
• Example: Automatically setting a field value when a record is updated.
Incorrect
Option A. UI Policy
• Incorrect because UI Policies are client-side rules that dynamically change form behavior (e.g., making a field mandatory or visible).
• They do not run on record insert, update, delete, or query operations at the database level.
Option B. Data Policy
• Incorrect because Data Policies enforce field requirements across all interfaces (forms, APIs, imports).
• They ensure consistency but do not execute scripts on record lifecycle events.
Option D. Client Script
• Incorrect because Client Scripts run in the browser on form events (onLoad, onChange, onSubmit).
• They are limited to client-side interactions, not server-side record operations.

questions.question: What catalog tool would you use to create a catalog item or record producer in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C: Catalog Builder
• This is the correct answer.
• Catalog Builder is the tool in ServiceNow specifically designed to create and manage catalog items and record producers.
• It provides a guided, user-friendly interface for developers and administrators to build catalog items efficiently, ensuring consistency and compliance with organizational standards.
• It is the recommended approach in modern ServiceNow releases for catalog item creation.
Incorrect
Option A: Catalog Formatter
• Incorrect because this is used to format catalog item variables for display, not to create catalog items or record producers.
Option B: Catalog Flow Builder
• Incorrect because Flow Builder is used to automate workflows and processes, not to create catalog items directly.
Option D: Catalog Designer
• Incorrect because Catalog Designer is an older tool used for designing catalog items, but it has been replaced by Catalog Builder in newer releases.
Option E: Variable Designer
• Incorrect because this tool is used to create and manage variables for catalog items, not the catalog items themselves.
Option F: Form Designer
• Incorrect because Form Designer is used to design and customize forms in ServiceNow, not catalog items or record producers.

questions.question: What can be set up to auto-assign all new Hardware category Incidents to a particular group? Select 3 Answers from the below options.
questions.explanation:
Data lookup rules, assignment rules, business rules and predictive intelligence can be used to auto-assign all new Hardware category Incidents to a particular group.
When creating new assignment rules, remember that business rules can take precedence over assignment rules when they run after the assignment rule.
Data lookup rules take precedence over assignment rules because they always run after.
Data lookup rules, assignment rules and business rules run in the following order:
1. All ‘before‘ business rules run on a record insert with an order value of less than 1000.
2. All ‘before‘ engines run, including assignment rules.
3. All ‘after‘ engines run, including data lookup rules.
4. All ‘before‘ business rules run on a record insert with an order value greater than or equal to 1000.
5. All ‘after‘ business rules run on record insert.
Screenshot: Example of an Incident Assignment Rule
(Abbildung im Original)
Learn more here!
Learning Domains:
Data Migration and Integration – Scripting in ServiceNow
Configuring Applications for Collaboration – Task Management

questions.question: When a flow runs an action, it generates a runtime value, which stays the same for the duration of the flow. What is the name of the runtime value?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A: Data pill runtime value
• Correct because in ServiceNow Flow Designer, when an action runs, it produces a data pill runtime value.
• This value represents the output of that action and remains constant throughout the flow execution.
• Data pills are used to pass information between actions and conditions in a flow.
Incorrect
Option B: Sequence runtime value
• Incorrect because there is no concept of a “sequence runtime value” in Flow Designer.
• Sequences may exist in execution order, but they are not named runtime values.
Option C: Starting runtime value
• Incorrect because the flow does not generate a “starting runtime value.”
• The runtime value is specifically tied to the action output, not the start of the flow.
Option D: Trigger runtime value
• Incorrect because while flows have trigger values (data from the event that starts the flow), this is not the runtime value generated by an action.
• The question specifically asks about the value generated when an action runs.
Option E: Input runtime value
• Incorrect because inputs are provided to actions, not generated by them.
• The runtime value refers to the output of an action, not its input.

questions.question: What type of relationship is recommended between Incident and SLA tables to report on incidents resolved by SLA per incident category?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Database Views
• Correct. In ServiceNow, when you need to report across multiple tables (such as Incidents and SLAs), the recommended approach is to use a Database View.
• Database Views allow you to join data from different tables into a single reporting structure without altering the underlying schema.
• This makes it possible to generate reports like “incidents resolved by SLA per incident category.”
Incorrect
Option A. One‑to‑Many
• Incorrect. While an Incident can have multiple SLAs (a one‑to‑many relationship), this alone does not provide the reporting capability needed. You cannot directly report across both tables without a database view.
Option B. Extensions
• Incorrect. Extensions are used when one table inherits from another (e.g., Task table extended by Incident). SLA is not an extension of Incident, so this does not apply.
Option C. Many‑to‑Many
• Incorrect. Many‑to‑many relationships are used when records from two tables need to be linked through a third table (like users and groups). This is not the recommended way to report between Incident and SLA tables.

questions.question: You are importing data. Which of the following statements best describes what happens when a set of fields are coalesced?
options: If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the system creates a new record based on the information being imported
If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the system does not create a Transform Map
If a match is found using the coalesce fields, no record is created but rather the existing record is updated with the information being imported
If a match is NOT found using the coalesce fields, no record is created but rather the existing record is updated with the information being imported
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. If a match is found using the coalesce fields, no record is created but rather the existing record is updated with the information being imported
• Correct because coalesce fields act like a unique key during data imports.
• If the incoming data matches an existing record on the coalesce field(s), ServiceNow updates the existing record instead of creating a duplicate.
• This ensures data consistency and prevents duplication.
Incorrect
Option A. If a match is found using the coalesce fields, the system creates a new record
• Incorrect because if a match is found, the record is updated, not recreated.
• Creating a new record would defeat the purpose of coalescing.
Option B. If a match is not found using the coalesce fields, the system does not create a Transform Map
• Incorrect because the Transform Map is created regardless.
• Coalesce only affects whether a record is updated or inserted, not whether a Transform Map exists.
Option D. If a match is NOT found using the coalesce fields, no record is created but rather the existing record is updated
• Incorrect because if no match is found, a new record is created.
• Updates only occur when a match exists.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid data sources for import sets? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
All the valid data sources for import sets in ServiceNow:
JDBC : JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) allows you to import data from relational databases directly into ServiceNow tables.
XML Files : ServiceNow can process XML files containing structured data for import into various tables.
HTTP : This option enables importing data from web services using HTTP requests.
CSV Files : Comma-Separated Values (CSV) files are a common and widely accepted format for data import, and ServiceNow supports importing data from CSV files.
Excel Files : Microsoft Excel files are another popular data source, and ServiceNow can import data from Excel spreadsheets into your tables.

questions.question: What is common way of testing functionality for different roles?
questions.explanation: Administrators can impersonate other authenticated users for testing purposes and view impersonation logs. Please check this article for more details: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/utah-platform-administration/page/administer/users-and-groups/concept/c_ImpersonateAUser.html

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of knowledge base contextual search?
options: In the service portal, you can search for articles using the search text box
When viewing a knowledge base article, it will show you similar articles
When creating an incident, it will suggest relevant articles
questions.explanation:
The most appropriate example of knowledge base contextual search among the choices is:
When creating an incident, it will suggest relevant articles
Here‘s why:
Contextual Search: This type of search leverages the context of a specific situation to deliver more relevant results. In the scenario of creating an incident, the knowledge base can analyze details like the incident category, description, or specific fields to suggest articles that directly address similar issues.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Search Text Box in Service Portal: This is a basic search functionality, not specifically contextual.
Similar Articles When Viewing an Article: While suggesting related articles can be helpful, it doesn‘t utilize the context of a user‘s current task (creating an incident).
None of the Listed Answers: Contextual search is a valuable feature, and suggesting relevant articles during incident creation is a prime example of its application.
Benefits of Contextual Search:
Improved User Experience: By suggesting relevant articles based on the incident details, contextual search empowers users to find solutions faster and more effectively.
Reduced Resolution Times: Faster access to pertinent knowledge base articles can expedite incident resolution by providing readily available troubleshooting steps or workarounds.
Increased Self-Service: Users might be able to resolve incidents themselves using suggested knowledge base articles, potentially reducing the need for IT support intervention.

questions.question: Which of the following roles is required to manage more than one knowledge base?
questions.explanation:
Correct:
Option C. knowledge_admin
The knowledge_admin role is required to manage more than one knowledge base in ServiceNow. This role has administrative control over Knowledge Management, including creating, configuring, and maintaining multiple knowledge bases, managing categories, workflows, and access controls across all knowledge bases.
Incorrect:
Option A. kb_manager
The kb_manager role is typically limited to managing content, approvals, or workflows within a specific knowledge base, not across multiple knowledge bases.
Option B. kb_controller
There is no standard out-of-the-box ServiceNow role called kb_controller for Knowledge Management. This is not a valid role for managing knowledge bases.
Option D. knowledge_manager
The knowledge_manager role can manage articles and processes within assigned knowledge bases but does not have the authority to administer or manage multiple knowledge bases at an administrative level.
Option E. kb_admin
Although the name suggests administrative privileges, kb_admin is not the standard role used in ServiceNow to manage multiple knowledge bases. The correct system-wide administrative role for this purpose is knowledge_admin.

questions.question: What is the Task table name?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. task
The Task table in ServiceNow uses the internal table name task, serving as the parent table for all task-based records like Incident, Problem, Change Request, and Service Catalog Task. This core table provides standardized fields (assigned_to, priority, state, etc.) inherited by all child tables.
Incorrect
Option A. sys_task
ServiceNow follows label_tableName convention (Task_task), not sys_ prefix for core application tables.
Option B. system_task
No table named system_task exists; sys_ prefix reserved for platform tables like sys_user, sys_journal_field.
Option D. sys_request
sys_request doesn’t exist. Service Catalog requests use sc_request table, extending task table.

questions.question: Which table is used to store groups data?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. sys_user_group
The sys_user_group table stores all group records in ServiceNow, containing group name, description, manager, type, and roles. This table serves as the master repository for group definitions used across assignment rules, notifications, and access control.
Incorrect
Option A. user_group
No table named user_group exists; ServiceNow uses sys_ prefix convention for system tables.
Option B. sys_group
sys_group doesn’t exist for user groups; sys_user_group is the correct table name following ServiceNow naming standards.
Option C. group
Simple “group” table doesn’t exist; ServiceNow uses descriptive sys_user_group for clarity and namespace protection.

questions.question: UI Policy is applied on all data input no matter what the channel is, including web form, import sets, …etc
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. False
• UI Policies are client-side rules that apply only when interacting with data through the ServiceNow web interface (forms).
• They do not apply to other channels such as import sets, APIs, or integrations.
• For non-form data input, Data Policies or Business Rules are used instead.
• Therefore, the statement in the question is false.
Incorrect
Option B. True
• Incorrect because UI Policies do not apply universally across all data input channels.
• They are limited to the form UI layer and cannot enforce rules on backend imports or integrations.
• Choosing this option reflects a misunderstanding of the scope of UI Policies.

questions.question: Each organization receives one instance (production) and they have the option to obtain 2 other instances for development and testing
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. False
• Correct.
• In ServiceNow, organizations are provided with multiple instances (commonly production, sub‑production, development, and test) depending on their licensing and subscription agreements.
• It is not limited to just one production instance plus two optional instances. The statement oversimplifies and misrepresents the actual ServiceNow instance entitlement model.
Incorrect
Option A. TRUE
• Incorrect.
• The statement suggests that every organization only gets one production instance and optionally two more for development and testing.
• This is misleading because ServiceNow typically provides a set of instances (production and non‑production) as part of the subscription, not just a single production instance with optional extras.

questions.question: You need to create a new field in a table. What is the field type that you should use if your field will contain letters, numbers, and special characters?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. String
• This is the correct answer.
• In ServiceNow, the String field type is used when you need to store alphanumeric data, including letters, numbers, and special characters.
• It is the most flexible field type for general text input and supports a wide range of characters.
• Commonly used for fields like names, descriptions, or identifiers.
Incorrect
Option A. Text
• Incorrect because “Text” is not a standard ServiceNow field type.
• The correct terminology is String, not Text.
Option B. Text Box
• Incorrect because “Text Box” refers to the UI element for input, not the actual field type in the database schema.
• The underlying field type would still be String.
Option C. Data
• Incorrect because “Data” is not a valid ServiceNow field type.
• ServiceNow uses specific field types like String, Integer, Date/Time, etc.

questions.question: The Import Set Table acts as a staging table, but the data will eventually be stored somewhere else
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. True
• Correct because in ServiceNow, an Import Set Table is a temporary staging table used to hold imported data before it is transformed and moved into the target table (such as incident, cmdb_ci, or other business tables).
• The purpose of the staging table is to allow administrators to clean, map, and transform data before committing it to the final destination.
• Once the transformation process is complete, the data is stored in the appropriate target table, not in the import set table.
Incorrect
Option B. False
• Incorrect because the import set table is not the final storage location for imported data.
• Saying “False” would imply that data remains permanently in the import set table, which is not true.
• The import set table is only a temporary holding area.

questions.question: You are importing data from an excel sheet into the Incident table. The Incident table already contains data. You want to make sure that the import doesn‘t result in duplicate records. What should you do?
options: Uncheck the “Allow Duplicates“ checkbox in the Transform Map form
In the Transform Map form, add a new record in the Compare related list to specify the comparison with Title column
Set the coalesce to Title field
Add a business rule to run after insertion. The business rule should delete the inserted record if it is a duplicate
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Set the coalesce to Title field
• Correct because coalesce fields in a Transform Map are used to determine whether an incoming record should update an existing record or create a new one.
• By setting the Title field as coalesce, ServiceNow will check if a record with the same Title already exists in the Incident table.
• If it does, the record will be updated instead of creating a duplicate.
Incorrect
Option A. Uncheck the “Allow Duplicates” checkbox in the Transform Map form
• Incorrect because this checkbox only prevents duplicate entries in the Import Set table (the staging table), not in the target table (Incident).
• It does not solve the issue of duplicate records in the Incident table.
Option B. Add a new record in the Compare related list to specify the comparison with Title column
• Incorrect because the Compare list is used for field mapping validation, not for preventing duplicates.
• Duplicate prevention is handled through coalesce, not Compare.
Option D. Add a business rule to run after insertion and delete duplicates
• Incorrect because this is not best practice.
• Writing a business rule to delete duplicates after insertion is inefficient and could lead to data loss or unintended deletions.
• ServiceNow provides coalesce specifically to handle this scenario.

questions.question: Which technique is used to access information from referenced fields from related tables?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Dot Walking
• Correct because Dot Walking is the ServiceNow technique that allows you to access fields from related tables by “walking” through the relationship using dot notation.
• Example: caller_id.email retrieves the email address of the caller from the referenced User table in an Incident record.
• This is a core CSA exam concept and the precise term used in ServiceNow documentation.
Incorrect
Option B. Dot Navigation
• Incorrect because “Dot Navigation” is not the official ServiceNow terminology.
• It may sound similar, but the exam expects the exact term Dot Walking.
Option C. Field Navigator
• Incorrect because the Field Navigator is a UI tool used to explore fields in tables, not a technique for accessing referenced fields.
Option D. Table Walking
• Incorrect because “Table Walking” is not a recognized ServiceNow concept.
• The correct term is Dot Walking, not Table Walking.

questions.question: Which of the following should you use to search for information across applications and records?
questions.explanation:
The most comprehensive tool for searching across applications and records in ServiceNow is:
Global Search
Here‘s why:
Universal Search: Global Search is designed to be the central hub for information retrieval within ServiceNow. It offers a powerful search engine that can crawl through various data sources, including:
Knowledge Base articles
Incident, problem, change request, and other record data
Configuration Management Database (CMDB) information
Custom applications and data tables
Advanced Capabilities: Global Search goes beyond simple keyword searches. It supports features like:
Facets for filtering results based on specific criteria.
Fuzzy matching to handle typos or variations in search terms.
Integration with natural language processing (NLP) for more intuitive search experiences.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Filter Navigator: While this functionality allows for filtering data within specific applications or modules, it‘s not designed for searching across all applications and records like Global Search.
Service Portal Search: This search is typically limited to the Service Portal, which is an interface for end users to submit requests and access knowledge base articles relevant to their needs, not a comprehensive search tool for all ServiceNow data.
Knowledge Base Search: This focuses on searching specifically within the Knowledge Base for articles, not across all applications and records in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Which of the following can be useful if you want to restrict certain users from executing scripts on a tables?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. ACL (Access Control List)
• Correct because ACLs are the mechanism in ServiceNow that control access to data and functionality.
• They can restrict which users or roles are allowed to execute scripts, query, or update records on a table.
• ACLs enforce security at the row and field level, making them the right choice for restricting script execution.
Incorrect
Option A. Client Scripts
• Incorrect because client scripts are used to run logic in the browser (UI behavior, field validation, etc.).
• They cannot restrict user permissions or prevent execution of scripts at the table level.
Option B. UI Policy
• Incorrect because UI Policies are used to dynamically change form behavior (e.g., making fields mandatory, visible, or read‑only).
• They do not provide security enforcement or restrict script execution.
Option C. Data Policy
• Incorrect because Data Policies enforce rules on data consistency across forms and APIs.
• They are not designed to restrict script execution or control user access.

questions.question: Which of the following knowledge base workflows immediately retires an article without needing an approval?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Knowledge – Instant Retire Correct. The Instant Retire workflow is designed to immediately retire a knowledge article without requiring any approval process. This is useful when articles must be removed quickly, such as outdated or incorrect information that should no longer be available to users.
Incorrect
Option A. Knowledge – Retire Knowledge Incorrect. This workflow typically requires an approval process before the article is retired. It does not immediately retire the article.
Option B. Knowledge – Retire Article Incorrect. Similar to Retire Knowledge, this workflow involves approvals and does not bypass the approval process.
Option C. Knowledge – Direct Retire Incorrect. While the name suggests immediate retirement, this is not the standard workflow in ServiceNow. The recognized workflow for immediate retirement is Instant Retire, not Direct Retire.

questions.question: Which of the following formatters is used to display the different stages in a linear process flow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Process flow formatter Correct. The Process Flow Formatter in ServiceNow is specifically designed to display the stages of a record in a linear process flow. It visually represents the progress of a record through its lifecycle, making it clear which stage the record is currently in and what stages remain. This is the formatter used when you want to show a linear progression of steps.
Incorrect
Option A. None of the listed answers Incorrect. There is indeed a formatter available for this purpose: the Process Flow Formatter. Therefore, this option is invalid.
Option B. Approval summarizer formatter Incorrect. The Approval Summarizer Formatter is used to display approval information related to a record, not to show linear process stages.
Option D. Parent breadcrumbs formatter Incorrect. The Parent Breadcrumbs Formatter is used to show hierarchical navigation (breadcrumbs) for parent records, not linear process stages.

questions.question: What is the minimum role needed to create import sets?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. import_admin Correct because the import_admin role is specifically designed to allow users to create and manage import sets in ServiceNow. This role provides the necessary permissions to load data into staging tables and configure import set mappings. It is the minimum required role for this task in the CSA exam context.
Incorrect
• Option A. itil Incorrect because the itil role is intended for general IT service management activities such as incident, problem, and change management. It does not provide permissions to create or manage import sets.
• Option B. security_admin Incorrect because the security_admin role is used for managing high‑security settings and access controls. It is unrelated to import set creation.
• Option C. admin Incorrect because while the admin role can perform all tasks including import sets, it is not the minimum role required. The exam specifically tests knowledge of least privilege, so the correct answer is import_admin, not admin.

questions.question: Which of the following UI Actions is useful if you would like to apply the “Save As” functionality?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Insert
• Correct because the Insert UI Action creates a new record in the database rather than updating the existing one.
• This behavior is equivalent to a “Save As” functionality, where the current record is duplicated into a new entry.
• It ensures that the original record remains unchanged while a new version is created.
Incorrect
Option A. Submit
• Incorrect because Submit is used to save a new record for the first time.
• It does not duplicate or create a “Save As” copy of an existing record.
Option B. Save
• Incorrect because Save simply saves the current record without creating a new one.
• It is not equivalent to “Save As.”
Option C. Update
• Incorrect because Update modifies the existing record in place.
• It does not create a new record, so it cannot be used for “Save As.”

questions.question: Having an up‑to‑date CMDB (Configuration Management Database) has a lot of benefits. Which of the following is NOT a benefit?
options: Facilitating quick analysis of change impact
Locating failed changes and associated incidents
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Automatically resolving incidents
• Correct because a CMDB provides visibility, traceability, and impact analysis, but it does not automatically resolve incidents.
• The CMDB helps IT teams understand dependencies and relationships between configuration items (CIs), but incident resolution requires human or automated workflows outside the CMDB.
• Therefore, this is NOT a benefit of having an up‑to‑date CMDB.
Incorrect
Option A. Facilitating quick analysis of change impact
• Incorrect because this is a valid benefit.
• A CMDB helps identify which systems and services will be affected by a change, reducing risk and improving change management.
Option B. Locating failed changes and associated incidents
• Incorrect because this is also a benefit.
• By tracking configuration items and their history, a CMDB helps correlate failed changes with incidents, aiding root cause analysis.
Option C. Helping in reducing the downtime
• Incorrect because this is a benefit as well.
• With accurate dependency mapping, IT teams can respond faster to incidents and reduce downtime by knowing which systems are impacted.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct regarding fulfiller and approver users?
options: Fulfiller users only have the approver_user role
Fulfiller users only have the itil role
Approver users have the itil and approver_user roles
Approver users only have the approver_user role
Fulfiller users have the itil and approver_user roles
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option E. Fulfiller users have the itil and approver_user roles Correct. Fulfiller users are typically assigned both the itil role (to perform ITSM tasks such as incident, problem, and change management) and the approver_user role (to approve requests or changes). This combination ensures they can fulfill service requests and also act as approvers when required.
Incorrect
• Option A. Fulfiller users only have the approver_user role Incorrect because fulfillers need more than just approval capability. They must also perform ITSM tasks, which requires the itil role.
• Option B. Fulfiller users only have the itil role Incorrect because fulfillers are not limited to ITSM tasks; they also need approval rights. Having only the itil role would restrict them from approving.
• Option C. Approver users have the itil and approver_user roles Incorrect because approver users are not required to perform ITSM tasks. They only need the approver_user role to approve requests or changes. Adding the itil role is unnecessary.
• Option D. Approver users only have the approver_user role Incorrect in this context because while approvers indeed only need the approver_user role, the question asks which statement is correct regarding both fulfiller and approver users. The most accurate statement is Option E.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to define conditions that determine which users can create, read, write and retire knowledge base article?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. User Criteria
• Correct because User Criteria in ServiceNow are specifically designed to define conditions that control access to knowledge bases and articles.
• They allow administrators to specify which users or groups can create, read, write, and retire knowledge articles.
• This is the standard mechanism for enforcing knowledge base permissions in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option A. Knowledge Roles
• Incorrect because roles grant general access rights but do not provide fine‑grained conditional control over knowledge base article actions. Roles alone cannot enforce detailed conditions like retirement or creation permissions.
Option B. ACL (Access Control List)
• Incorrect because ACLs control access at the table and field level, not specifically for knowledge base article lifecycle actions. ACLs are broader and not the recommended way to manage knowledge base permissions.
Option D. Article Permissions
• Incorrect because “Article Permissions” is not a formal configuration element in ServiceNow. Permissions are enforced through User Criteria, not a separate “Article Permissions” setting.
Option E. KB Permissions
• Incorrect because while knowledge bases have permission settings, they are implemented through User Criteria, not a separate “KB Permissions” object.
Option F. HR Criteria
• Incorrect because HR Criteria apply to HR Service Delivery modules, not to knowledge base article access. They are unrelated to knowledge management.

questions.question: Which section in the task form shows the full history of updates and comments made on the task?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Activity
• Correct because the Activity section in a ServiceNow task form displays the complete history of updates, comments, and work notes associated with the task.
• It provides a chronological log that auditors, administrators, and users can review to track all changes and communications.
• This is the standard location for viewing the full update history in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option A. Archive
• Incorrect because Archive refers to storing or retaining records, not displaying the live update history of a task.
Option B. Updates List
• Incorrect because there is no formal section called “Updates List” in ServiceNow task forms. Updates are shown in the Activity section.
Option D. Notes
• Incorrect because Notes are used for additional information or annotations but do not show the full chronological history of updates and comments.
Option E. History
• Incorrect because while “History” might sound similar, ServiceNow uses the Activity section specifically for tracking updates and comments. “History” is not the correct label in the task form.

questions.question: How to show the visual task board view for tasks list?
options: Click on the gear icon in the top banner and select the checkbox “Show Visual Task Board“
Right-click on the list header and select “Show Visual Task Board“
Click on the gear icon in the tasks list and select the checkbox “Show Visual Task Board“
Right-click on any of the columns and select “Show Visual Task Board“
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Right-click on any of the columns and select “Show Visual Task Board”
• Correct because the visual task board view is enabled directly from the task list interface by right‑clicking on a column.
• This action switches the view into a Kanban-style board, which is the intended method tested in the exam.
• It aligns with the exam requirement: enabling the board view from within the task list itself.
Incorrect
Option A. Click on the gear icon in the top banner and select the checkbox “Show Visual Task Board”
• Incorrect because the gear icon in the top banner controls global system settings, not the task board view.
Option B. Right-click on the list header and select “Show Visual Task Board”
• Incorrect because the list header does not provide the option to enable the visual task board.
Option C. Click on the gear icon in the tasks list and select the checkbox “Show Visual Task Board”
• Incorrect because the gear icon in the tasks list manages list-specific settings, not the visual task board view.

questions.question: Question: Which one of the following statements is correct regarding the difference between Save button and Update button?
options: Save applies the input validations before saving the record while Update skips the input validations
Save allows the user to remain on the same record while Update returns the user to the previously viewed record
Update allows the user to remain on the same record while Save returns the user to the previously viewed record
Save is used to insert new records while Update is used to update existing records
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Save is used to insert new records while Update is used to update existing records
• Correct because the Save button is typically used when creating a new record for the first time.
• The Update button is used when modifying an existing record and committing those changes back to the database.
• This distinction aligns with standard application design principles and is the expected answer in exam scenarios.
Incorrect
Option A. Save applies validations while Update skips validations
• Incorrect because both Save and Update enforce input validations.
• Skipping validations would compromise data integrity, which is not allowed in enterprise systems.
Option B. Save keeps user on the same record while Update returns to previously viewed record
• Incorrect because this reverses the actual behavior.
• Typically, Update saves changes and returns the user to the list view, while Save keeps the user on the current record form.
Option C. Update keeps user on the record while Save returns to previously viewed record
• Incorrect because this is also reversed.
• The Save button keeps the user on the record form, while Update navigates back to the list or previously viewed record.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is most accurate when it comes to how the system evaluates ACLs when a session requests access to a record?
options: A user must pass both table and field ACL rules to access a record
A user must at least pass the table ACL rule to access the record
A user must pass either the table or the field ACL rules to access the record
A user must at least pass the field ACL rule to access the record
questions.explanation:
Correct:
Option B. A user must at least pass the table ACL rule to access the record.
In ServiceNow, ACL evaluation follows a hierarchy. When a user requests access to a record, the system first evaluates the applicable table-level ACL.
A user must satisfy the required table ACL before access to the record can be granted. If the request also involves specific fields, the applicable field-level ACLs are evaluated as additional security controls.
Therefore, the key point is that passing the table ACL is required before the user can access the record.
Incorrect:
Option A. A user must pass both table and field ACL rules to access a record.
Incorrect because a field ACL is not necessarily required for every record access request. Field ACLs apply when access to a particular field is being evaluated.
The table ACL is the fundamental requirement for accessing the record.
Option C. A user must pass either the table or the field ACL rules to access the record.
Incorrect. ACL evaluation is not an either/or choice between table and field ACLs.
The table-level security requirement must be satisfied, and applicable field ACLs can impose additional restrictions.
Option D. A user must at least pass the field ACL rule to access the record.
Incorrect. Field ACLs control access to individual fields, not basic access to the record itself.
The table ACL is the relevant minimum requirement for record access.

questions.question: Which of the following are supported types of client scripts? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
Here are the supported types of client scripts in ServiceNow:
onChange : This script executes whenever the value in a specific field is changed. It‘s ideal for dynamic UI updates based on user input, such as showing/hiding fields, changing field properties, or displaying validation messages.
onLoad : This script runs when the form or list is initially loaded. It‘s useful for setting default values, performing calculations based on initial data, or controlling the initial UI state.
onCellEdit : This script triggers when a cell value is edited within a list view. It allows for validations or specific actions to be taken based on changes made directly in the list view.
Incorrect Options:
onClick: While onClick events can be used in ServiceNow UI elements, they wouldn‘t directly trigger client scripts. Client scripts typically execute based on form/list events or field value changes.
onAction: This term isn‘t a standard client script event type in ServiceNow. Actions are often used within workflows or UI Macros, but wouldn‘t directly trigger client scripts.
onMouseOver: Similar to onClick, onMouseOver events can be used for UI interactivity but wouldn‘t directly trigger client scripts in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Every record is identified by a 32-character, globally unique ID, which is called _______
questions.explanation: Each record in the instance is identified by a unique 32-character GUID (Globally Unique ID) called a Sys ID (sys_id). The same sys_id value is never generated twice, which ensures that every record created in every table in every instance in the world has a unique identifier.

questions.question: Which of the following roles is the minimum role required to be able to access My Work and My Group Work modules?
questions.explanation:
The minimum role required to access My Work and My Group Work modules in ServiceNow is itil.
Here‘s why:
itil: This role is designed for users who primarily work on IT service management processes like incident, problem, change, and service request management. “My Work“ and “My Group Work“ modules typically display tasks and assignments related to these ITIL processes, making the itil role a suitable fit for access.
Incorrect Options:
itil_admin: While this role suggests administrative privileges within the ITIL framework, it might not be the minimum requirement for basic access to My Work and My Group Work functions.
admin: The admin role grants broad access across the platform, but for this specific scenario, the itil role is sufficient.
problem_manager & fulfiller: These roles are more focused on specific aspects of IT service management (problem management and service fulfillment, respectively). They might have access to My Work and My Group Work, but the itil role encompasses a wider range of ITIL processes and likely includes access to these modules.
Additional Considerations:
Specific configurations within ServiceNow might influence access control. However, the itil role is generally considered the minimum requirement for basic access to My Work and My Group Work functionalities.
Organizations might customize permissions for these modules, but the itil role serves as a baseline for users involved in core IT service management processes.

questions.question: In ServiceNow fulfillment view, in which part of the screen do the forms get displayed?
questions.explanation: Content frame displays information such as lists, forms, homepages, and wizards. For more information, check: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/utah-platform-user-interface/page/administer/navigation-and-ui/concept/c_UI16.html

questions.question: If you need to display information in a form that is not a field in the record, what element should you add?
questions.explanation: A formatter is a form element used to display information that is not a field in the record.The formatter provides an easy way to track items not saved with a field in the record, for example, journal fields like comments and work notes. Formatter Examples: Activity formatter, Process flow formatter, Parent breadcrumbs formatter, Approver summarizer formatter, and CI relations formatter.

questions.question: In the context of importing data, what does it mean when you specify a field as a coalesce?
options: The field will be considered the display field for the target table
The field will be ignored when importing data
The imported data will be sorted on this field
The field will be used as a unique key during imports
questions.explanation:
When you specify a field as a coalesce in the context of importing data in ServiceNow, it means the field will be used as a unique key during imports.
Here‘s a breakdown of what coalesce does in import sets:
Unique Identifier: Coalesce identifies a record in the target table based on the value in the specified field from the import data. If a matching record exists in the target table with the same coalesce field value, the import process will update that existing record with the new data from the import set. Otherwise, a new record will be created in the target table.
Incorrect Options:
Display Field: The coalesce field doesn‘t necessarily dictate the display field in the target table. There might be separate options for defining the display field during the import configuration.
Ignored Field: Specifying a field as coalesce signifies its importance for matching records, not ignoring it.
Sorting Field: Coalesce primarily focuses on record identification and updating/creating records, not sorting the imported data.
Benefits of Using Coalesce:
Prevents Duplicates: By using a unique identifier, coalesce helps avoid creating duplicate records during data imports if existing records with the same value already exist in the target table.
Efficient Updates: When a matching record is found, coalesce facilitates efficient updates to existing records rather than creating unnecessary duplicates.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to integrate flow designer with other instances and 3rd party applications?
questions.explanation: Integration Hub enables execution of third-party APIs as a part of a flow when a specific event occurs in ServiceNow. These integrations, referred to as spokes, are easy to configure and enable you to quickly add powerful actions without the need to write a script. For example, you can post a message and incident details in a Slack channel when a high priority incident is created. The MID Server is a different thing. It facilitates communication and movement of data between the platform and external applications, data sources, and services. It is not about integration between ServiceNow and other systems.

questions.question: Which of the following is useful when your users need to order more than one item together?
questions.explanation: Order guide submits a single service catalog request that generates several items. For example, a New Employee Hire order guide can contain several items that new employees commonly need, such as business cards, computer, and cell phone. Record producers are used to generate records in tables. Catalog items allow the user to request only one item whereas the order guide can contain multiple items. A variable is a field within the catalog item or record producer.

questions.question: Which of the following is useful if you have a set of fields that needs to be used in multiple record producers?
questions.explanation:
The most suitable option if you have a set of fields that needs to be used in multiple record producers is a Variable Set.
Here‘s why:
Variable Set: This functionality within ServiceNow allows you to define and manage a collection of variables that can be reused across various forms and record producers. It promotes code reusability and consistency by eliminating the need to define the same set of fields repeatedly.
Incorrect Options:
User Control: This functionality is likely related to user management and wouldn‘t directly address reusing fields in record producers.
Fields Set & Fields Container: These terms aren‘t commonly used functionalities within ServiceNow for managing reusable sets of fields.
Variables Container: Similar to Fields Container, this isn‘t a standard term for managing reusable field sets in ServiceNow.
Benefits of Variable Sets:
Reduced Redundancy: Define a variable set once and reference it in multiple record producers, avoiding repetitive field definitions.
Maintainability: Changes made to the variable set are reflected everywhere it‘s used, simplifying maintenance and ensuring consistency.
Improved Organization: Variable sets promote code organization by keeping reusable fields grouped and easily accessible.
Using Variable Sets:
Create a variable set containing the desired fields.
In your record producer, reference the variable set using the vardef function.
The fields defined in the variable set will be available for use within your record producer.

questions.question: Which form of storage is used to store data in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
The primary form of storage used to store data in ServiceNow is a relational database.
Here‘s why:
Relational Database: ServiceNow leverages a relational database management system (RDBMS) to store and manage its data. This structured approach organizes data into tables with rows and columns, enabling efficient querying and relationships between different data points.
Incorrect Options:
Flat-file database: While ServiceNow might utilize flat files for temporary storage or specific use cases, it doesn‘t rely solely on them for core data storage. Flat files lack the structure and relationships offered by relational databases.
No-SQL database: NoSQL databases are gaining traction, but ServiceNow primarily uses a relational database structure for its core functionality.
Binary files: Binary files store specific data formats like images or documents. While ServiceNow can store these within the database, it‘s not the primary storage method for all data.
Benefits of Relational Databases for ServiceNow:
Data Integrity: Ensures data consistency and minimizes redundancy through data normalization and relationships.
Structured Query Language (SQL): Allows for powerful querying and manipulation of data using SQL statements.
Scalability: Relational databases can scale to accommodate growing data volumes within an organization.
Additional Considerations:
ServiceNow might integrate with external NoSQL databases for specific purposes, but the core platform relies on a relational database structure.
Binary files are stored within the database, often as chunked data for efficiency, but they aren‘t the primary storage method for all data types.

questions.question: Every user can be added to only one group.
questions.explanation: A user can be added to multiple groups and he/she will inherit all the roles in all the groups

questions.question: ServiceNow instance can be hosted on the cloud or on-premises

questions.question: Which of the following is captured in update sets? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
Update sets in ServiceNow capture several elements related to application customizations, and here‘s a breakdown of what gets included:
Elements Captured in Update Sets (Correct Options):
Client Scripts : When you create or modify client scripts, these changes are captured in the update set. This ensures they are moved and applied consistently across different environments.
Business Rules : Similar to client scripts, updates or creations of business rules are tracked within update sets. This facilitates controlled deployment of your business logic across environments.
Fields : Adding, removing, or modifying fields within tables is also reflected in update sets. This ensures consistent table structures when deploying customizations.
Elements Not Captured in Update Sets (Incorrect Options):
Modified Data Records: Update sets themselves don‘t directly capture individual data record modifications. They focus on application customizations like scripts, rules, and field definitions.
New Data Records: Similar to data record modifications, new data records aren‘t inherently part of update sets. They reside within the database tables themselves.
Tasks: Tasks created within ServiceNow (e.g., incidents, problems) are independent entities and wouldn‘t be captured in update sets, which focus on application customizations.

questions.question: If a session requests access to data in a certain table, what happens if the user passes the table ACL rule but fails the field rule?
options: The user will be granted access to the table but won‘t see the field which he doesn‘t have access to
The user is denied access to the entire table
The user is granted access to the entire table because the table ACL rule will override the field ACL rule
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: The user will be granted access to the table but won‘t see the field which he doesn‘t have access to.
Here‘s why:
Layered Security: ServiceNow enforces a two-step ACL evaluation process.
Table ACL: Grants access to the table itself.
Field ACL: Controls visibility and modification permissions for individual fields within the table.
Failing Field Rule: If a user passes the table ACL but fails the field ACL for a specific field, they‘ll still be able to access the table and view other fields they have permissions for. However, the restricted field will be hidden from their view.
Incorrect Options:
Denied Access to Entire Table: Failing a field ACL doesn‘t completely block access to the table. Users can still see the table and any fields they have permissions for.
Table ACL Overrides Field ACL: These ACLs work together, not against each other. The table ACL is the initial entry point, and field ACLs further refine permissions within the accessible table.
Access to Entire Table: This would be the case only if the user passes both the table and field ACLs.
Security Implications:
Granular Control: This layered approach allows for fine-grained access control, ensuring users can only see and modify the data they‘re authorized for within a table.
Data Protection: Sensitive data can be protected by restricting field-level access, even if a user has general access to the table.

questions.question: Roles can be assigned to groups but they cannot be assigned to individual users
questions.explanation: Roles can be assigned to groups or users, however, it is considered a best practice to assign roles to groups rather than individual users

questions.question: Which table is used to store CI relationship data?
questions.explanation:
The most likely table used to store CI relationship data in ServiceNow is cmdb_rel_ci .
Here‘s why:
Naming Conventions: ServiceNow often uses prefixes like “cmdb_“ to denote tables related to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB). “cmdb_rel_ci“ suggests a table specifically designed for storing relationships between CIs (Configuration Items).
Focus on Relationships: The presence of “rel“ in the table name indicates a focus on relationships, aligning with the purpose of storing CI connections.
Possible Alternatives:
While cmdb_rel_ci is the strongest contender, here‘s a brief explanation of the other options:
ci_relation, ci_rel: These names are less common in ServiceNow documentation and might be used in custom implementations or older versions.
cmdb_ci_rel: This structure (CMDB prefix, then CI, then relationship) seems less likely based on standard ServiceNow naming conventions.

questions.question: What is a configuration Item?
options: Any record that refers to configuration or settings
Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver services
Any configuration record that determines the behavior of the database
Any component in ServiceNow is considered a configuration item
questions.explanation:
A configuration item (CI) in ServiceNow is:
Any component that needs to be managed in order to deliver services
Here‘s why this definition is accurate:
Service Delivery Focus: CIs represent the building blocks of IT services. They encompass various elements that contribute to delivering functionalities and capabilities to end users. This could include hardware (servers, routers), software applications, infrastructure components, or even documentation and processes.
Management Importance: Since CIs are crucial for service delivery, they need to be tracked, monitored, and managed effectively. ServiceNow‘s CMDB (Configuration Management Database) serves as a central repository for storing and managing CI data.
Understanding CIs is essential for:
Incident Management: Identifying the CIs involved in an incident helps diagnose root causes and restore service functionality.
Change Management: Tracking changes made to CIs ensures proper documentation and minimizes potential service disruptions.
Impact Analysis: Assessing the impact of potential outages or changes on CIs allows for proactive planning and risk mitigation.
Incorrect Options Explained:
General Configuration Record: While CIs can involve configuration details, they are broader than just settings or database behavior definitions. They encompass the entire component that needs to be managed for service delivery.
All ServiceNow Components: Not everything in ServiceNow is a CI. CIs are specifically service-oriented components, not generic functionalities within the platform itself.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best explains the difference between Work Notes and Additional Comments?
options: Work Notes are only available to fulfillers whereas Additional Comments are only available to customers/external users
Additional Comments are only available to fulfillers whereas Work Notes are available to both fulfillers and customers/external users
Work Notes are only available to fulfillers whereas Additional Comments are available to both fulfillers and customers/external users
Work Notes are stored in the activity history whereas Additional Comments are not
Additional Comments are stored in the activity history whereas Work Notes are not
questions.explanation:
The key distinction between Work Notes and Additional Comments lies in their visibility:
Work Notes: Internal Notes for Fulfillers
These are intended for communication and collaboration among internal agents working on a request or incident. Customers cannot see them. Work Notes are crucial for documenting internal discussions, troubleshooting steps, or tracking resolution progress.
Additional Comments: Visible to Both Fulfillers and Customers
This field allows for communication with the customer or external user who submitted the request or incident. They can see any updates or information added through Additional Comments. This transparency helps keep the customer informed about the progress and any details relevant to their issue.
Here‘s a table summarizing the key differences:
Feature Visibility Purpose
—————————————————————-
Work Notes Internal (Fulfillers only) Internal communication, documenting resolution efforts
Additional Comments External Communication with the customer, keeping them informed about
(Visible to requester/customer) progress
drive_spreadsheet
Export to Sheets
Additional Points:
Both Work Notes and Additional Comments are stored in the activity history of the record (incident, task, etc.) for future reference.
Some UI configurations in ServiceNow might offer a toggle to switch between a single comment field and separate fields for Work Notes and Additional Comments.

questions.question: You need to add a button to one of your forms. Which of the following should you use?
questions.explanation:
The most suitable option for adding a button to a form in ServiceNow is a UI Action .
Here‘s why:
UI Actions: These are scripts specifically designed to add buttons or links to forms. They allow you to define the button‘s label, behavior (what happens when clicked), and conditions for when the button should be visible or hidden.
Incorrect Options:
Data Policy: Data policies are primarily used for data validation and governance, not for adding interactive elements like buttons to forms.
Button (might be misleading): While “button“ seems like a logical choice, it‘s not a technical element within ServiceNow for creating buttons on forms. UI Actions provide the necessary functionality to achieve this.
UI Policy: UI policies are more focused on enforcing data validation rules on the server-side before saving a record. They wouldn‘t be the appropriate choice for adding buttons that trigger actions on the form.
Benefits of UI Actions:
Enhanced User Experience: Buttons can streamline user interactions with forms by allowing them to perform specific actions (e.g., calculations, data lookups) without leaving the form.
Conditional Visibility: You can configure UI Actions to show or hide buttons based on certain form field values or conditions, making the button relevant to the context.
Flexibility: UI Actions allow for various functionalities beyond just button clicks, such as opening modals or running custom scripts.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is NOT true regarding configuration items
options: Software applications and business services are considered configuration items
Configuration items can be tangible or intangible
Relationship can be built between configuration items
CMDB consists of a static list of configuration items
questions.explanation: CMDB is NOT a static list. It tracks CI‘s within your platform and also it tracks the relationships between them

questions.question: Which of the following features helps users see reasonable relationships between configuration items?
questions.explanation:
The most suitable feature for visualizing relationships between configuration items (CIs) in ServiceNow is:
CI Relationship Editor
Here‘s why:
Visualization and Editing: The CI Relationship Editor allows you to view existing relationships between CIs and establish new ones. It provides a graphical representation of these connections, making it easier to understand the dependencies and interactions between various components within your IT infrastructure.
Incorrect Options Explained:
CI Relationship Wizard, CMDB Relationship Assistant, CMDB Relationship Editor: While these terms might be related to CI relationships, they‘re not as widely used or prevalent as the CI Relationship Editor in ServiceNow.
CI Relationship Assistant: This specific term isn‘t a common feature name within ServiceNow documentation for managing CI relationships.
Benefits of CI Relationship Editor:
Improved Understanding: Visualizing relationships helps teams comprehend the impact of changes or outages on interconnected CIs, promoting proactive problem management.
Enhanced Collaboration: A clear view of CI connections facilitates communication and collaboration between different teams managing various components.
Accurate Impact Analysis: Understanding CI relationships allows for more accurate assessments of potential disruptions when making changes to the IT environment.

questions.question: Which of the following can be used to automate business logic for a particular process such as approvals, tasks, notifications, etc…
questions.explanation:
The most suitable option for automating business logic for processes involving approvals, tasks, notifications, etc. in ServiceNow is:
Flow Designer
Here‘s why:
Flow Designer: This is a low-code/no-code visual tool specifically designed for automating workflows within ServiceNow. It allows you to build multi-step processes using drag-and-drop functionality and pre-built components like approvals, tasks, notifications, and data manipulation actions.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Logic Builder: While logic can be used within Flow Designer, it‘s not the sole focus. Flow Designer provides a broader framework for building entire workflows.
Process Designer: This term might refer to older versions of workflow creation tools in ServiceNow. Flow Designer is the current recommended approach.
Logic Designer: Similar to Logic Builder, this isn‘t a commonly used term for workflow automation in ServiceNow.
Approvals Flow: This could be a specific type of workflow built using Flow Designer, but it doesn‘t encompass the full range of functionalities offered by Flow Designer.
Benefits of Flow Designer:
Simplified Automation: Flow Designer provides a user-friendly interface for building workflows without extensive coding knowledge.
Enhanced Efficiency: Automating tasks and approvals streamlines processes, improving team productivity and reducing manual work.
Flexibility: Flow Designer offers a variety of pre-built components and customization options to cater to diverse business needs.

questions.question: You are designing a form for a specific record. Which of the following is useful when you want to show records in the tables that have relationships to the current record?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Related list
• Correct because Related Lists in ServiceNow forms display records from other tables that are related to the current record.
• For example, on an Incident form, a related list might show all Tasks or Change Requests linked to that Incident.
• This is the standard way to visualize and manage relationships between records directly within a form.
Incorrect
Option B. Relationship icon
• Incorrect because the relationship icon is used to preview or navigate to a referenced record, not to display multiple related records in a list format.
Option C. Dot Walking
• Incorrect because Dot Walking is used in scripts, reports, and filters to access fields from related tables.
• It is not a UI feature for displaying related records on a form.
Option D. Reference field
• Incorrect because a reference field links a single record from another table, not a collection of related records.
• It is useful for pointing to one related record, but not for showing multiple records in a list.

questions.question: The purpose of data policies is to enforce security in the system
questions.explanation:
The statement “The purpose of data policies is to enforce security in the system“ is False.
The purpose of data policies in ServiceNow is not primarily to enforce security, but rather to enforce data integrity and consistency across the platform.
Data policies are server-side rules that allow administrators to set read-only and mandatory attributes on fields within a table.
Unlike UI policies, which only execute on the client-side, data policies are enforced regardless of how the record is being updated, such as through an import set or web service API.
The key purpose of data policies is to ensure data regularity and prevent invalid data from being saved to the database.
This is particularly useful when dealing with tables that frequently have records imported from external sources, as data policies can enforce specific field attributes to maintain data integrity.
While data policies can indirectly contribute to security by preventing unauthorized changes to certain fields, their primary function is to uphold data quality and consistency, not to enforce security access controls.
For security-related access restrictions, ServiceNow provides Access Control Lists (ACLs) and other security features.
In summary, the purpose of data policies is to enforce data integrity and consistency, not primarily to enforce security in the system.

questions.question: One of the disadvantages of assignment rules is that they can only use configurations but no scripting can be added.
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer
False. Assignment rules in ServiceNow allow scripting in the Advanced condition field. You can add custom GlideRecord queries or scripts for complex logic, making them more flexible than just basic field matching.
Why TRUE is Wrong
TRUE would mean the statement is correct, but it’s not. Scripting is fully supported, so no such disadvantage exists. This avoids limiting rules to simple configs only.

questions.question: Which one of the following authentication methods is not supported in ServiceNow?
options: All the listed methods are supported in ServiceNow
questions.explanation:
Correct: A. All the listed methods are supported in ServiceNow
ServiceNow supports multiple authentication mechanisms out of the box for different integration and SSO scenarios. OAuth is supported for API and third-party integrations, SAML is widely used for Single Sign-On with identity providers, and LDAP is supported for user authentication against directory services. Additionally, ServiceNow supports digest-based authentication mechanisms (often referred to in the platform as HTTP Digest or token-based approaches for integrations). Since each of the listed authentication methods is supported in ServiceNow, the statement that “All the listed methods are supported in ServiceNow” correctly answers the question asking which method is not supported.
Incorrect: B. Digest Token
Digest-based authentication is supported in ServiceNow, especially for REST integrations and API access. Therefore, it is not correct to say this method is unsupported.
Incorrect: C. OAuth
OAuth is fully supported in ServiceNow and is commonly used for securing REST APIs and external application integrations. It is a standard and recommended authentication mechanism on the platform.
Incorrect: D. SAML
SAML is supported in ServiceNow for Single Sign-On (SSO) with enterprise identity providers. It is a core authentication option for enterprise environments.
Incorrect: E. LDAP
LDAP authentication is supported in ServiceNow and is frequently used to authenticate users against corporate directory services such as Active Directory.

questions.question: Which of the following is captured in update sets? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A (Report Definitions): Update sets capture report configurations, definitions, schedules, and sharing settings to transfer reporting customizations between ServiceNow instances.
Option C (Published Workflows): Active, published workflow versions are captured to ensure process automations and business logic transfer correctly.
Option D (Views): Custom list and form views, including column configurations and filters, are included for UI consistency across environments.
Option F (Tables): Table creations, extensions, schema changes, and dictionary entries are captured to replicate data structures.
Incorrect
Option B (Homepages): Homepages and dashboard configurations require manual recreation or separate export/import processes, not captured in update sets.
Option E (Scheduled Jobs): Runtime scheduled jobs represent transactional data and are excluded to prevent unintended automation execution in target instances.

questions.question: Which one of the following orders is used by default to sort lists?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. order > number > name
• Reasoning: In ServiceNow, lists are sorted by default using the order field first, then by number, and finally by name. This ensures that records appear in a logical sequence based on their defined order, with number and name acting as secondary sorting keys.
• Exam Focus: The CSA exam expects you to know the default sorting hierarchy for lists, which is order → number → name.
Incorrect
Option A. number > order > name
• Incorrect because the order field takes precedence over number.
Option B. number > order
• Incorrect because it omits the name field and misplaces the order of precedence.
Option C. order > number > created
• Incorrect because lists are not sorted by the created field by default.
Option E. number > created
• Incorrect because the default sorting does not use the created field, and order is missing from this sequence.

questions.question: _______ is the view that agents use to work on issues. This view includes in-depth record information and suggestions about how to resolve issues and communicate with requesters.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Record view
Why correct: The Record view in ServiceNow is where agents work directly on issues. It provides detailed record information, related lists, activity streams, and contextual suggestions for resolving issues. It also allows communication with requesters, making it the correct answer.
Incorrect
Option A. Case view Why incorrect: ServiceNow does not use the term “Case view” in the CSA context. Cases are part of Customer Service Management (CSM), but the standard CSA exam focuses on Record view for working on issues.
Option B. List view Why incorrect: The List view displays multiple records in a tabular format. It is useful for browsing or filtering records but does not provide in-depth record details or resolution suggestions.
Option C. Landing page Why incorrect: The Landing page is the initial interface or homepage when logging in. It provides navigation options but is not the workspace for resolving issues.

questions.question: ServiceNow instance is single-tenant
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. True
• A ServiceNow instance is single-tenant, meaning each customer has their own dedicated database and application instance.
• This ensures data isolation, security, and customization for each organization.
• Unlike multi-tenant SaaS platforms where multiple customers share the same environment, ServiceNow provides a separate environment per customer, which is a key exam point for CSA.
• Therefore, the statement is true.
Incorrect
Option B. False
• Saying “False” would be incorrect because ServiceNow does not operate in a shared multi-tenant model.
• Each customer’s instance is isolated, ensuring compliance and reducing risks of data leakage.
• Hence, this option does not align with the actual architecture of ServiceNow.

questions.question: Which of the following contains Flow Designer triggers and actions dedicated to a particular application?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. Spoke
• Correct: In ServiceNow, a Spoke is a package of Flow Designer content (triggers, actions, and subflows) that is dedicated to a particular application or capability.
• Example: The ServiceNow ITSM Spoke contains actions specific to ITSM processes, while the Slack Spoke contains actions for Slack integration.
• This is exactly what the question is asking for—Flow Designer triggers and actions tied to a specific application.
Incorrect
• Option A. Trigger Package
• Incorrect: There is no concept of a “Trigger Package” in ServiceNow Flow Designer. Triggers exist, but they are not grouped into packages by application.
• Option B. Flow Triggers
• Incorrect: Flow triggers are individual starting points for flows (e.g., record created, updated, scheduled). They are not bundled by application.
• Option C. Automated Triggers
• Incorrect: This is not a valid Flow Designer concept. Automation exists, but “Automated Triggers” is not a recognized term in ServiceNow.
• Option E. Integration Hub
• Incorrect: Integration Hub is the broader framework that enables integration with external systems. It provides spokes, but itself is not the container of application‑specific triggers and actions.

questions.question: How can you filter the types of activities that are displayed in the Activity section?
options: Navigate to Service Desk > Personalization and update the record with name “Activity Types“ with the activity types that you would like to display
It is not possible to filter the activity types in the Activity section
Navigate to Service Desk > Personalization and add a record to specify which Activity types to display
Click on the gear icon in the top banner and select which activity types to be displayed
Click on the funnel icon in the task form and select which activity types to show
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option F. Click on the funnel icon in the task form and select which activity types to show
• This is correct. The funnel icon in the task form provides a direct way to filter which activity types (such as emails, comments, work notes, etc.) are displayed in the Activity section.
• This method is user‑friendly, immediate, and does not require administrative configuration changes.
• It empowers end‑users to customize their view dynamically based on what they need to focus on.
Incorrect
Option A. Navigate to Service Desk > Personalization and update the record with name “Activity Types” with the activity types that you would like to display
• Incorrect because this is not the valid navigation path for filtering activities. The personalization record does not control Activity section filtering.
Option B. It is not possible to filter the activity types in the Activity section
• Incorrect because filtering is indeed possible using the funnel icon. This option contradicts the platform’s functionality.
Option C. None of the listed answers
• Incorrect because one of the listed answers (Option F) is valid.
Option D. Navigate to Service Desk > Personalization and add a record to specify which Activity types to display
• Incorrect because adding records in personalization does not control Activity section filtering.
Option E. Click on the gear icon in the top banner and select which activity types to be displayed
• Incorrect because the gear icon controls system settings or personalization, not Activity section filtering.

questions.question: Which of the following is most suitable to apply governance rules to decide who can access certain fields in certain tables?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. ACL (Access Control List)
• Correct because ACLs are the mechanism in ServiceNow that enforce security and governance rules at the table, field, and record level.
• ACLs determine who can read, write, or execute specific fields or tables based on roles, conditions, and scripts.
• This is the most suitable option when the requirement is to restrict access to certain fields in certain tables.
Incorrect
Option A. UI Policy
• Incorrect because UI Policies control form behavior (e.g., making fields visible, mandatory, or read‑only) but only at the UI level.
• They do not enforce true security—users could still access restricted fields via APIs or background scripts.
Option C. Client Scripts
• Incorrect because Client Scripts run in the browser to manage form interactions.
• They cannot enforce governance rules for field access at the database level.
Option D. Data Policy
• Incorrect because Data Policies enforce rules on data consistency (e.g., mandatory fields) across all interfaces.
• They are not designed for access control or governance of who can see or edit specific fields.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes predictive intelligence?
options: Predictive Intelligence uses predefined configurations to set fields values
Predictive Intelligence uses machine learning algorithms to set the “assignment group“ and the “assigned to“ fields
Predictive Intelligence uses machine learning algorithms to set field values during record creation
Predictive Intelligence uses assignment rules to set the “Assigned to“ field
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Predictive Intelligence uses machine learning algorithms to set field values during record creation
• Correct because Predictive Intelligence in ServiceNow leverages machine learning models to automatically populate field values when new records are created.
• It analyzes historical data and patterns to predict values such as category, subcategory, assignment group, or other relevant fields.
• This reduces manual effort, improves accuracy, and speeds up incident and request handling.
Incorrect
Option A. Predefined configurations set field values
• Incorrect because predefined configurations (like business rules or default values) are static.
• Predictive Intelligence is dynamic, using machine learning, not static configurations.
Option B. ML sets only “assignment group” and “assigned to” fields
• Incorrect because Predictive Intelligence is not limited to just those two fields.
• It can predict multiple fields depending on the model definition, making this statement too narrow.
Option D. Assignment rules set the “Assigned to” field
• Incorrect because assignment rules are a different mechanism in ServiceNow.
• They are rule‑based, not machine learning‑based, and therefore do not represent Predictive Intelligence.

questions.question: Which of the following context menus can be used to configure the list?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Column Context Menu
• Correct because the Column Context Menu provides configuration options for lists, such as changing the order of columns, adjusting visibility, and customizing the layout.
• This menu is specifically designed for configuring how the list is displayed and interacted with, making it the right choice for list configuration.
Incorrect
