Option A. Record Context Menu
• Incorrect because the Record Context Menu applies to individual records, allowing actions like opening, editing, or deleting a record. It does not configure the list itself.
Option B. None of the listed answers
• Incorrect because the Column Context Menu is indeed a valid option for configuring lists. Therefore, this statement is false.
Option C. List Context Menu
• Incorrect because the List Context Menu provides actions related to the list as a whole (such as filtering or exporting), but it does not configure the structure or layout of the list.

questions.question: Data policies can be applied to a table and can be enforced on both the form and the list
questions.explanation:
True.
Data policies in ServiceNow can be applied to a table and enforced on both the form and the list.
These policies are used to implement data regularity by setting field attributes based on specific conditions, ensuring data integrity and consistency within the platform.
Unlike UI policies that execute on the client side, data policies run on the server side, making them effective in controlling field attributes and behaviors regardless of how a record is changed or updated.
Data policies are versatile and can be applied to various data sources within ServiceNow, including data imported from external sources like import sets and web services.
They play a crucial role in maintaining data quality and enforcing business rules across different types of data interactions within the platform.

questions.question: The _______ provide(s) the Platform Analytics Workspace with a single page for all the dashboards, visualizations, analytics answers, and insights on your instance.
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. Analytics Center Correct because the Analytics Center is specifically designed to serve as the unified entry point within the Platform Analytics Workspace. It consolidates dashboards, visualizations, analytics answers, and insights into a single page, making it the central hub for analytics on the instance.
Incorrect
• Option A. Agent Workspace Incorrect because Agent Workspace is tailored for customer service agents to manage cases and interactions. It is not intended to provide a consolidated analytics view.
• Option B. Performance Analytics Incorrect because Performance Analytics provides KPIs, scorecards, and trend analysis, but it does not serve as the single consolidated page for all dashboards and insights.
• Option C. Dashboards Incorrect because dashboards are individual visualization containers. While they display analytics, they do not provide the unified workspace view across all dashboards and insights.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to initiate flows?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Triggers This is correct because in Flow Designer, flows are initiated by triggers. A trigger defines the condition or event that starts a flow, such as a record being created, updated, or deleted, or an application‑based event. Without a trigger, a flow cannot begin execution.
Incorrect
Option A. Record Producers Incorrect because record producers are used to create records (commonly in the Service Catalog), not to initiate flows directly. They can indirectly cause flows to run if the record creation matches a trigger, but they are not the mechanism themselves.
Option B. Actions Incorrect because actions are the building blocks inside a flow. They define what happens after a flow is triggered, but they do not initiate the flow.
Option D. Scheduled Jobs Incorrect because scheduled jobs are part of the platform’s job scheduling system. They can run scripts or tasks at defined times, but they are not the native mechanism for initiating flows in Flow Designer.
Option E. Events Incorrect because events are part of the Event Registry and can be used in legacy workflows or scripts. In Flow Designer, flows are initiated by triggers, not directly by events.

questions.question: The ServiceNow platform uses a single system of record and a common data model
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. True
• Correct because:
• ServiceNow is built on a single system of record, meaning all applications share the same underlying data architecture.
• This ensures consistency, eliminates data silos, and allows seamless integration across ITSM, HR, Security Operations, and other modules.
• The common data model standardizes how information is stored and accessed, making reporting and automation more reliable.
• This is a foundational principle of the ServiceNow platform and is a key exam concept.
Incorrect
Option B. False
• Incorrect because:
• Choosing False would imply that ServiceNow uses multiple systems of record or lacks a common data model.
• That is not true—ServiceNow’s strength lies in its unified architecture.
• Without a single system of record, ServiceNow would not be able to provide consistent workflows, dashboards, and analytics across different applications.

questions.question: The field name is a user‑friendly term which allows people to identify the field in the user interface.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. False
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the field label is the user‑friendly term shown in the user interface.
• The field name is the backend reference used in scripts, configurations, and database queries.
• Therefore, the statement is false: the field name is not the user‑friendly identifier; the field label is.
Incorrect
Option A. TRUE
• Incorrect because this confuses field name with field label.
• While the label is what users see in the UI, the field name is a technical identifier used internally.
• Saying TRUE would misrepresent how ServiceNow distinguishes between backend references and user‑friendly terms.

questions.question: Every list can have only one view.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. False
• Correct because in ServiceNow, a list can have multiple views.
• Views allow different configurations of columns and filters to be displayed depending on the user’s role or preference.
• For example, administrators may have a detailed view with more fields, while end users may have a simplified view.
• Therefore, the statement that every list can have only one view is incorrect.
Incorrect
Option B. TRUE
• Incorrect because this assumes that lists are restricted to a single view.
• In reality, ServiceNow supports multiple views per list, enabling flexibility and customization for different user needs.
• Saying TRUE would contradict the platform’s functionality.

questions.question: The impersonate feature is not recommended because there is no way to know what actions the impersonator took on behalf of the impersonated user.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. False
• Correct because ServiceNow does track actions performed while impersonating another user.
• The system logs activities in the audit records, so administrators can review what was done during impersonation.
• Therefore, the impersonate feature is safe to use for troubleshooting and testing, and the statement in the question is incorrect.
Incorrect
Option B. TRUE
• Incorrect because this assumes impersonation is untraceable.
• In reality, ServiceNow provides audit trails and logs that capture impersonated actions, making it possible to monitor and review them.
• Saying TRUE would misrepresent the platform’s built‑in tracking capabilities.

questions.question: A data policy defined for a table will only run when data is inserted through the form, but it will not run when the data is inserted via import set.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. False
• Correct because data policies in ServiceNow apply regardless of how the data is entered — whether through forms, web services, or import sets.
• The purpose of a data policy is to enforce rules consistently across all data entry methods, ensuring compliance and data integrity.
• Therefore, the statement is incorrect: data policies are not limited to form entries only.
Incorrect
Option B. TRUE
• Incorrect because this assumes data policies only apply when using forms.
• In reality, ServiceNow enforces data policies across multiple entry points, including import sets and APIs.
• Saying TRUE would misrepresent the platform’s functionality and lead to misunderstanding of how data policies work.

questions.question: The benefit of the activity stream inline editor is that you can add comments to tasks without opening them.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. True
• Correct because the activity stream inline editor allows users to quickly add comments directly from the list view or activity stream.
• This improves productivity by eliminating the need to open each task record individually.
• It is especially useful for updating multiple tasks or providing quick feedback.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE
• Incorrect because the inline editor is specifically designed to let users add comments without opening the task.
• Saying “FALSE” contradicts the actual functionality of ServiceNow’s activity stream inline editor.

questions.question: Every task can be assigned to an assignment group and to a specific user at the same time.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. True
• Correct because in ServiceNow, every task record (such as incidents, problems, changes, etc.) has both an Assignment Group field and an Assigned To field.
• The Assignment Group ensures accountability at the group level, while the Assigned To field specifies the individual user responsible for execution.
• This dual assignment model allows flexibility: tasks can be tracked at the group level while also being delegated to a specific person.
Incorrect
Option A. FALSE
• Incorrect because saying “FALSE” would imply that tasks cannot be assigned to both a group and a user simultaneously.
• In reality, ServiceNow supports both fields, and it is common practice to assign tasks to a group for accountability and to a user for execution.

questions.question: The disadvantage of enabling the virtual agent is that some users would prefer to speak to a human agent
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. False
• Correct because enabling the Virtual Agent in ServiceNow is not considered a disadvantage.
• The Virtual Agent is designed to augment support, providing automated responses and self‑service for common issues.
• If users prefer human interaction, the system can be configured to escalate to live agents.
• Therefore, the exam expects you to recognize that Virtual Agent is a benefit, not a drawback.
Incorrect
Option B. TRUE
• Incorrect because while it is true that some users may prefer speaking to human agents, this does not make Virtual Agent a disadvantage.
• The feature is optional, configurable, and provides value by reducing wait times and handling repetitive queries.
• Saying TRUE misrepresents the Virtual Agent’s role in improving efficiency and user experience.

questions.question: The Activity Stream is an example of a formatter
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. True
• Correct because the Activity Stream in ServiceNow is indeed a formatter.
• A formatter is a UI element that provides a specific visualization or interaction on a form.
• The Activity Stream formatter allows users to view and add journal entries (like comments and work notes) directly on a record without opening it separately.
• This makes collaboration and tracking changes easier, aligning with ServiceNow’s design principles.
Incorrect
Option A. FALSE
• Incorrect because denying that the Activity Stream is a formatter ignores its actual role in ServiceNow.
• The Activity Stream is not just a widget or a field—it is explicitly categorized as a formatter in the platform.
• Choosing FALSE would contradict ServiceNow CSA exam knowledge requirements.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the Dependency View?
options: Dependency Views display all the configuration items that can be impacted by a change
Dependency Views display all the incidents that are linked to a change
Dependency views display a list of all configuration items in a CMDB
Dependency Views display the configuration items and the business services that it is part of and that it supports
questions.explanation:
The most accurate description of a Dependency View in ServiceNow:
Dependency Views Display CIs, Services Supported and Impacted : A Dependency View graphically depicts the relationships between configuration items (CIs) within your IT infrastructure. It showcases:
CIs themselves (e.g., servers, applications, network devices)
The business services that a CI is part of (e.g., the server is part of the email service)
The services that a CI supports (e.g., the network device supports the HR application)
This visual representation helps you understand the potential impact of a change to a specific CI. By seeing the connected services, you can anticipate how other parts of your IT environment might be affected.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Display All Impacted CIs from a Change: While Dependency Views can be helpful in understanding potential impact, they don‘t directly show all CIs that might be impacted by a specific change. A formal Change Management process might utilize Dependency Views for impact assessment.
Display Incidents Linked to a Change: Dependency Views focus on configuration items and their relationships, not incidents. Incidents might be linked to specific CIs within a Dependency View, but the primary purpose isn‘t to display incidents.
List of All CIs in CMDB: A Dependency View is a more targeted visualization compared to just listing all CIs in the CMDB. It highlights the connections and dependencies between CIs, providing a more contextual view.

questions.question: You are designing a record producer. You need to add questions to the form to solicit information from customers. Which of the following should you use?
questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow record producers, the correct way to define the questions displayed on the form to collect information from customers is by using:
Variables
Here‘s why:
Variables and Record Producers: Record producers are essentially scripts that generate forms for users to input data. These forms leverage variables to define the questions or prompts displayed to users. Each variable corresponds to a specific field on the form, capturing the user‘s input.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Attributes: Attributes are properties associated with a record itself, not directly used for defining questions on a form.
Fields: Fields represent the data elements stored within a table. While record producers utilize fields to store the collected data, they don‘t directly define the form questions themselves.
Properties: Properties can be associated with various elements in ServiceNow, but for record producer forms, variables are the primary mechanism for defining the questions presented to users.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to display a set of records?
questions.explanation: The correct answer is “List“ because lists are used to show records from a table. Tables are used to store data. Form is used to represent data for a single record rather than a set of records. A moudle is a container of a group of relevant links

questions.question: Which of the following chart types can be used to represent individual values as bars and the cumulative total as line?
questions.explanation:
The most suitable chart type to represent individual values as bars and the cumulative total as a line is:
Pareto chart
Here‘s why:
Pareto Chart Functionality: A Pareto chart is specifically designed to visually depict the 80/20 rule (Pareto principle). It combines bars and a line graph to effectively represent this principle.
The bars represent the individual values of each category, typically in descending order of magnitude.
The line graph overlays the bars, showcasing the cumulative total as a percentage or another relevant unit.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Pivot Table: Pivot tables are for data summarization and manipulation, not for visualizing data with bars and lines.
Bar Chart: A standard bar chart only displays individual values as bars.
Trend Line: A trend line is a statistical line superimposed on a scatter plot to show a general tendency, not cumulative totals.
Heatmap: Heatmaps use color gradients to represent data intensity within a matrix, not individual bars and a cumulative line.

questions.question: Which of the following are the 3 key attributes for a field?
questions.explanation:
The three key attributes for a field in ServiceNow are:
Label : This is the user-friendly name displayed for the field on forms and list views. It helps users understand the purpose of the field and the kind of data it holds.
Name : This is the internal identifier used within the system to reference the field. It should be unique and follow ServiceNow naming conventions for consistency.
Value : This represents the actual data stored within the field for each record. The value type depends on how the field is defined (e.g., string, number, date, reference).
Other Important Field Attributes:
While not part of the core three, here are some other noteworthy field attributes in ServiceNow:
Data Type: Defines the kind of data the field can hold (e.g., string, integer, date).
Mandatory: Specifies whether a value must be entered in the field before a record can be saved.
Read-Only: Controls whether users can modify the value in the field.
Default Value: Sets a pre-populated value that automatically appears in the field for new records.

questions.question: What defines which fields appear in a list and order of fields?
questions.explanation: A view defines the elements that appear when a user opens a form or a list, and you can switch the view from the default for lists and forms. Check this article for more details: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/tokyo-platform-user-interface/page/administer/navigation-and-ui/concept/view-management-overview.html

questions.question: In the context of Flow designer, which of the following are examples of ServiceNow core actions? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
Several core actions available within ServiceNow Flow Designer:
Wait for Condition : This action pauses the workflow execution until a specified condition is met, allowing for conditional branching and process automation based on dynamic criteria.
Delete Record : This action removes a record from a ServiceNow table, enabling workflows to automate data deletion tasks based on certain conditions.
Ask for Approval : This action introduces an approval step into the workflow, routing the request to designated approvers and pausing execution until a decision (approve/reject) is made.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Schedule job: While scheduling jobs can be integrated with workflows, it‘s not a core ServiceNow Flow Designer action directly available within the flow canvas. You might need to use a custom script or integration to achieve job scheduling within a flow.
Repeat: The “Repeat“ functionality might not be a core action available in all versions of Flow Designer. It‘s recommended to consult your specific ServiceNow documentation for confirmation.
Activate Plugin: Activating plugins typically involves administrative tasks or code execution outside the flow canvas itself. Core ServiceNow Flow Designer actions focus on building workflows using pre-defined functionalities.

questions.question: You are designing an email notification that will be sent to the manager of the “Assigned to“ user once an incident is created. Which of the following features will be useful to specify the recipient field?
questions.explanation: Dot-Walking gathers information from a series of tables through reference fields. If the current table contains a reference to another table, any field on the referenced table can be accessed using dot-walking. Dot-walking references a field by building a chain of field names separated by dots (periods). For instance, incident.assigned_to.company references the company of the user assigned to an incident. The recommended limit for chain length is three levels.

questions.question: You are designing a form for a specific record. Which of the following is useful if you need to allow fields to be populated automatically?
questions.explanation: Templates allow fields to be populated automatically, simplifying the process of submitting new records

questions.question: What is the limit of Templates that can be made for a form?
questions.explanation: There is no limit to the number of templates a user can create or access

questions.question: What does it mean if the “Match all“ checkbox is checked in the User Criteria form?
options: This user criteria includes all the users with any roles
Any users in the users list of the user criteria is granted permission
All the elements of the user criteria form are mandatory and should be defined by the user criteria creator
The user must meet at least one element of the criteria to be granted permission
The user must meet all criteria to be granted permission
questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow User Criteria forms, the “Match all“ checkbox indeed signifies a specific requirement for users to be granted permission. Here‘s the correct explanation:
Match All = All Criteria Must Be Met : When the “Match all“ checkbox is selected, a user will only be granted permission if they satisfy all the conditions defined within the User Criteria form. This means they must meet the criteria for users, groups, roles, companies, locations, departments, and any advanced criteria (scripts) specified in the form.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Includes All Users with Any Roles: This isn‘t the case. With “Match all“ checked, even if a user has a matching role, they wouldn‘t qualify if other criteria aren‘t met.
Any User in List Granted Permission: The user list is just one element of the criteria. With “Match all“ enabled, all criteria must be satisfied for permission.
All Elements Mandatory: While some fields might be mandatory individually, checking “Match all“ doesn‘t automatically make all fields mandatory. It emphasizes that all defined criteria need to be met.
Meet At Least One Criterion: This is the opposite of “Match all.“ When “Match all“ is checked, users need to meet every criterion, not just one.

questions.question: Which of the following are valid options in the “When“ field in the business rule form? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
All the valid options for the “When“ field in the business rule form in ServiceNow:
Before : This option executes the business rule logic before the record is saved to the database. It‘s commonly used for data validation, setting default values, or modifying data before it‘s persisted.
After : This option executes the business rule logic after the record is saved to the database. It‘s suitable for tasks like sending notifications, updating related records, or performing post-save actions.
Display : This option executes the business rule logic whenever the form is displayed for the record. It‘s useful for dynamically modifying the form based on certain conditions or pre-populating fields with relevant data.
Async : This option is similar to “After“ but allows the business rule to run asynchronously in the background. This can improve the performance of the user interface by not blocking the user while the business rule executes complex tasks.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Sync: There‘s no “Sync“ option specifically for the “When“ field in business rules. The options focus on timing relative to database interactions (Before, After) or form display (Display). Async execution provides a type of asynchronous behavior within the “After“ execution context.
In Parallel: Similar to “Sync,“ there‘s no “In Parallel“ option for business rule execution timing. Business rules typically run sequentially based on the chosen “When“ option.

questions.question: You need to move your work from development instance to production instance. Which of the following can you use to move your work?
questions.explanation:
The most suitable method for moving your work (customizations and configurations) from a development instance to a production instance in ServiceNow is:
Update Sets
Here‘s why:
Version Controlled Deployments: Update sets are designed for this specific purpose. They allow you to group your customizations (e.g., changes to forms, workflows, scripts) into logical units, test them in a development environment, and then deploy them to a production environment in a controlled manner. Update sets provide version control, enabling you to track changes and revert if necessary.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Deployment Sets: While deployment sets are a related concept, they are typically used for large-scale deployments involving multiple applications or updates. Update sets are better suited for moving individual customizations or smaller sets of changes.
Data Migration: Data migration tools are primarily for transferring data itself (e.g., incident records, user data) between instances, not customizations or configurations.
Application Scope: Application scope defines the boundary of your customizations within a scoped application. It doesn‘t directly facilitate moving work between instances.
Integration Hub: The Integration Hub is used for integrating ServiceNow with external systems, not for managing deployments within ServiceNow itself.
How Update Sets Work:
In your development instance, create an update set and group your desired customizations within it.
Make your changes (e.g., modify forms, workflows, scripts).
Test the update set thoroughly in the development environment.
Once testing is complete, commit the update set, marking it ready for deployment.
In your production instance, import the update set and review the changes.
You can then choose to activate the update set, applying the customizations to your production environment.

questions.question: How to make a notification subscribable?
options: Select the checkbox “Allow personalization“ in the notification form.
Select the “Subscribable“ checkbox in the notification form
All members of groups that is specified in the “Who will receive“ can subscribe to the notifications
Change the notification privacy type to “Public“
There is nothing that you need to do. All notifications are subscribable by default.
questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow, you can make a notification subscribable by selecting the “Subscribable“ checkbox in the notification form .
Here‘s why the other options are incorrect:
“Allow personalization“ checkbox: This checkbox allows users to personalize the notification by changing the subject line or adding comments. While personalization can be helpful for subscribers, it‘s not directly related to enabling subscriptions.
Group members can subscribe: While specifying groups in “Who will receive“ can ensure certain groups get notified, it doesn‘t inherently allow individual users to subscribe or unsubscribe.
Notification privacy type: The privacy type (public, private, or group) determines who can see the notification by default, but it doesn‘t directly control subscriptions.
All notifications subscribable by default: This is not the case. By default, notifications are not subscribable unless you enable it with the “Subscribable“ checkbox.

questions.question: Which table is used to store Roles?
questions.explanation: Roles control access to features and capabilities in applications and modules. The admin role provides access to all features and capabilities. Roles control access to features and capabilities in applications and modules. The admin role provides access to all features and capabilities. Check this article for more details: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/utah-platform-administration/page/administer/roles/concept/c_Roles.html

questions.question: You need to create a new field in a table. What is the field type that you should use if your field needs to display records from another table?
questions.explanation: A reference field stores a reference to a field on another table. For example, the Caller field on the Incident table is a reference to the User [sys_user] table. Check this article for more details: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/vancouver-platform-administration/page/administer/field-administration/concept/c_ReferenceField.html

questions.question: You are trying to import some data and you would like to map the fields in the source with the fields in the target table. Which of the following features provides visually intuitive environment for specifying mapping between Import Set fields and Target table fields?
questions.explanation:
While Transform Maps play a role in the import process, for visual field mapping within ServiceNow:
Mapping Assist Utility is the ideal feature.
Here‘s a breakdown of the options:
Automatic Mapping Utility: This option might attempt to automatically match source and target fields based on similar names, but it doesn‘t provide a visual environment for manual adjustments.
Mapping Assist Utility : This is the graphical user interface (GUI) specifically designed for mapping import set fields to target table fields. It allows you to see both sides of the mapping (source and target) and visually drag-and-drop or select the appropriate corresponding fields.
Visual Mapping Utility: While there might not be a specific feature named “Visual Mapping Utility“ within ServiceNow, Mapping Assist Utility fulfills the role of providing a visual interface for field mapping.
Transform Map: A Transform Map is a broader concept that encompasses the entire data transformation process during import. It might include field mapping defined through the Mapping Assist Utility but also involves defining transformations like data formatting or calculations before loading data into the target table.

questions.question: Which prefix is used for custom tables in the global application?
questions.explanation:
The correct prefix used for custom tables in the global application of ServiceNow is:
“u_“
Here‘s why:
Standardized Prefix: “u_“ is the recognized prefix within ServiceNow to denote custom tables created by users or customizations on top of the platform.
Avoiding Conflicts: Using a prefix helps differentiate custom tables from system tables (which have no prefix) and prevents naming conflicts.
Incorrect Options Explained:
“_“ (underscore): While an underscore can be used in table names, it‘s not a specific prefix for custom tables.
“e_“ or “c_“* : There are no standard prefixes like “e_“ or “c_“ specifically designated for custom tables in ServiceNow.
No Prefix: Not using a prefix can lead to naming conflicts with system tables or other custom tables.

questions.question: Which of the following chart types can be created directly by right-clicking a list? (select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
When you right-click on a list in ServiceNow, you can directly create several chart types to visualize the data within that list. Here are the ones you can create:
Bar chart : This is a common choice for depicting data in categories using rectangular bars proportional to the values they represent.
Pie chart : This circular chart displays data as slices, where each slice corresponds to a category and its size reflects its proportional value.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Line chart: While line charts are valuable for visualizing trends over time, they cannot be directly created by right-clicking a list. You‘d need to leverage reporting tools or widgets for line charts.
Area chart: Similar to line charts, area charts require reporting tools or widgets and cannot be directly generated from a list right-click menu.
Donut chart: Donut charts are a variation of pie charts and typically require reporting tools or widgets for creation, not directly available through a list right-click.
Bubble chart: Bubble charts use circles of varying sizes and positions to represent data with three dimensions (X, Y, and bubble size). They are not directly available through a list right-click menu in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Which of the following is a set of tables containing assets and business services controlled by a company?
questions.explanation:
The most accurate answer for a set of tables containing assets and business services controlled by a company in ServiceNow is:
CMDB
Here‘s why CMDB stands out:
Configuration Management Database: The Configuration Management Database (CMDB) is the core repository within ServiceNow that stores information about all the configuration items (CIs) within an organization‘s IT environment.
Assets and Business Services: CIs in the CMDB encompass various IT and business components, including hardware assets (servers, network devices), software applications, and business services.
Comprehensive View: The CMDB provides a centralized and holistic view of all these assets and services, enabling effective IT asset management, service delivery, and incident resolution.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Servers List: While a servers list might capture specific server assets, it wouldn‘t include the broader range of CIs (software, services) typically found in a CMDB.
CI: CI (Configuration Item) itself is a concept, not a specific table. The CMDB is the collection of tables that house data for all CIs.
CI List: Similar to “Servers List,“ a CI list might be a basic view, but the CMDB offers a more comprehensive structure for managing CI data.
Assets List: An asset list might focus primarily on hardware assets, whereas the CMDB encompasses a wider range of CIs including hardware, software, and services.

questions.question: You are importing data from an excel sheet into the Incident table. Which of the following features should be used to map the columns in the excel sheet with the columns in the Incident table?
questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow, you‘ll use a Transform Map to map the columns in your Excel sheet to the corresponding fields in the Incident table during an import.
Here‘s why the other options are less likely:
Matching Rules: Matching rules are a broader concept used for data reconciliation or matching records based on specific criteria. While they might be involved in the import process, they wouldn‘t directly define the field mapping between the source and target.
Columns Map: “Columns Map“ might be a general term, but ServiceNow uses “Transform Map“ as the specific feature for defining field mappings during data import.
Columns Sheets: This term likely refers to the sheets within your Excel spreadsheet and wouldn‘t be used for field mapping.
Transform Matrix: While “Transform Matrix“ might sound similar, “Transform Map“ is the established terminology within ServiceNow for data import field mapping.

questions.question: Which of the following statements best describes the formatter?
options: A formatter is used to define the format used to display special fields like date and currency
A formatter is used to define the theme used in the service portal
Any field that is added in the form is called a formatter
A formatter is an element used to display information that is not a field in the record
questions.explanation: The formatter provides an easy way to track items not saved with a field in the record, for example, journal fields like comments and work notes. Formatter Examples: Activity formatter, Process flow formatter, Parent breadcrumbs formatter, Approver summarizer formatter, and CI relations formatter

questions.question: Which of the following elements is used to store data in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow, the primary element used to store data is:
Tables
Here‘s why tables are the foundation for data storage in ServiceNow:
Structured Data Storage: Tables are relational databases that store data in a structured format with rows and columns. Each row represents a record, and each column represents a specific field or attribute of that record.
Foundation for Applications: ServiceNow applications rely on tables to store information about incidents, problems, changes, assets, configuration items (CIs), and various other entities.
Relationships and Queries: Tables can be linked to each other to represent relationships between data. This allows you to query and retrieve data efficiently based on your specific needs.
Incorrect Options Explained:
Sheets: While ServiceNow might have functionalities for displaying data in sheets, these sheets typically represent temporary views or reports based on underlying tables. The data itself resides in the tables.
Lists: Similar to sheets, lists are often ways to view and interact with data stored in tables. They don‘t represent the core storage mechanism.
Forms: Forms are user interfaces for creating, editing, and displaying data stored in tables. They provide a way to interact with the data, but the data itself resides within the tables.

questions.question: Incident and Problem tables extend the Task table?
questions.explanation:
True.
The Incident and Problem tables in ServiceNow extend the Task table.
This means that the Incident and Problem tables inherit attributes and behaviors from the Task table, which is a core table that other tables like Incident, Change, and Problem use to track work within ServiceNow.
The Task table is the parent class of many other tables in ServiceNow, and it is one of the most important tables in the platform.

questions.question: Giving roles to groups considered best practices when it comes to assigning roles.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. TRUE Explanation: This is correct. In ServiceNow, assigning roles to groups rather than directly to individual users is considered a best practice. It simplifies administration, ensures consistency, and makes role management more scalable. When a user is added to a group, they automatically inherit the group’s roles, reducing manual effort and minimizing errors.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE Incorrect. Marking this as false would contradict ServiceNow best practices. Directly assigning roles to individual users is discouraged because it becomes difficult to manage at scale and increases the risk of misconfiguration.

questions.question: What can you do if the Homepage is slow?
options: Remove some gauges or change the refresh page
Set the refresh page to sooner
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Remove some gauges or change the refresh page
• Correct because in ServiceNow, a Homepage can become slow if it contains too many gauges or if gauges refresh too frequently.
• Removing unnecessary gauges or adjusting the refresh interval reduces the load on the system and improves performance.
• This is the recommended best practice for optimizing Homepage speed.
Incorrect
Option A. Do not Refresh the page
• Incorrect because simply avoiding refresh does not solve the underlying performance issue.
• The Homepage will still remain slow due to heavy gauges or frequent refresh cycles.
Option C. Set the refresh page to sooner
• Incorrect because setting the refresh interval to sooner (more frequent) would increase system load and make the Homepage even slower.
• The correct approach is to increase the refresh interval or reduce gauges.
Option D. Just be patient
• Incorrect because waiting does not address the root cause of the slowness.
• ServiceNow administrators are expected to optimize performance, not ignore issues.

questions.question: What are the type of SLAs?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: All of the above (Correct).
In ServiceNow, there are three main types of SLAs (Service Level Agreements) that define the expected quality of service delivery:
Service Level Agreement (SLA): This is the most common type, typically established between a service provider (IT department) and its internal customers (end-users within the organization). The SLA outlines the agreed-upon response times, resolution times, and other service expectations for various IT services.
Operational Level Agreement (OLA): An OLA focuses on internal agreements between different IT service providers within an organization. It defines the level of service that one internal department (e.g., network operations) agrees to deliver to another (e.g., application support) to ensure smooth overall service delivery to end-users.
Underpinning Contract (UC): A UC is an agreement between an external service provider and your organization. It outlines the expected service standards from the external vendor for services they deliver to your organization.
Understanding these different SLA types is essential for effective service management within ServiceNow. Each type plays a specific role in ensuring that IT services meet the agreed-upon quality standards.

questions.question: Where would you create the order guide choices/questions (e.g., department)?
options: Go to the order guide and go to the variables section.
Go to social it > feed administration
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Go to the order guide and go to the variables section. (Correct)
Here’s why:
• Order guides in ServiceNow allow you to group related catalog items and potentially define additional options or questions for users when requesting those items.
• Variables within an order guide provide a way to capture user input during the service catalog request process. These variables can be used to collect additional information from the user that might be needed to fulfill the request.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• Go to social it > feed administration: This section likely deals with social IT functionalities and wouldn’t be related to order guide configuration.
• System properties > css: System properties manage various system-wide settings, and CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) defines the visual presentation of web pages. Neither of these areas is relevant to order guide variables.
• None of the above: While the other options are incorrect, defining order guide choices/questions is indeed done through variables within the order guide itself.

questions.question: Transform maps can only be used once.
questions.explanation:
The statement is FALSE. Transform maps in ServiceNow can be reused multiple times.
Transform maps are a crucial component of the import set functionality in ServiceNow. They define how data is mapped and transformed during the import process from a source file (like Excel or CSV) to a target table within the platform.
Here’s why transform maps can be reused:
• Efficiency: By creating reusable transform maps, you can avoid the need to redefine mapping rules for every import that uses a similar data structure. This saves time and effort, especially for recurring imports.
• Consistency: Reusing transform maps helps ensure consistency in how data is mapped and transformed across different import sets. This reduces the risk of errors or inconsistencies in the imported data.
Here’s how to reuse transform maps:
• When creating a new import set, you can select an existing transform map during the configuration process.
• The chosen transform map will define the field mappings and any data manipulation rules to be applied during the import.
Overall, the ability to reuse transform maps is a valuable feature that streamlines the import process and promotes data consistency within ServiceNow.

questions.question: How to capture workflow in update sets?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B: Publish
• In ServiceNow, workflows must be published before they are captured in update sets.
• Only published versions of workflows are included in update sets for migration between instances.
• This ensures consistency and that the correct workflow logic is transferred.
Incorrect
Option A: Create
• Simply creating a workflow does not capture it in update sets.
• The workflow must be published; otherwise, it remains in draft and is not included.
Option C: Checkout
• Checkout is used for editing workflows, not for capturing them in update sets.
• A checked-out workflow is considered a draft and will not be migrated.
Option D: Validate
• Validation checks for errors in the workflow but does not capture it in update sets.
• It is a quality check step, not a migration step.

questions.question: What is an access control?
options: It is a security rule defined and set at the row level and the column level, and it is executed when attempting to access any ServiceNow table
It is a security rule defined and set on field level, and it is executed when attempting to access any ServiceNow record
Access control is a role provided out of the box in ServiceNow.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. It is a security rule defined and set at the row level and the column level, and it is executed when attempting to access any ServiceNow table
• This is correct because in ServiceNow, Access Control Rules (ACLs) are security rules that determine whether a user can access a particular row (record) or column (field) in a table.
• They are evaluated whenever a user attempts to access data, ensuring proper enforcement of security at both the record and field levels.
Incorrect
Option B. It is a security rule defined and set on field level, and it is executed when attempting to access any ServiceNow record
• Incorrect because while ACLs can apply at the field level, they are not limited to that. They also apply at the row (record) level. This option is incomplete and misleading.
Option C. Access control is a role provided out of the box in ServiceNow.
• Incorrect because access control is not a role. Roles are separate entities that can be assigned to users, while access controls are rules that check conditions (often involving roles) to determine access.
Option D. All of the above
• Incorrect because not all statements are true. Only Option A correctly defines access control.

questions.question: Inbound action can be used to: (Select all that Apply)
questions.explanation:
Here’s a breakdown of how inbound actions can be used in ServiceNow:
• Parse Email (Correct): Inbound actions are a powerful tool for processing incoming emails. They can extract information from the email content (sender, recipient, subject, body, etc.) and use it to perform various actions.
• Modify Records (Correct): Inbound actions can update existing records within ServiceNow based on the information extracted from an email. This allows for automation of tasks like updating incident details or adding comments based on email content.
• Create Records (Correct): Inbound emails can trigger the creation of new records in ServiceNow. For example, an email might automatically generate a new incident record with relevant details parsed from the email content.
• Schedule a job (Incorrect): While inbound actions can’t directly schedule jobs, they can potentially initiate workflows that might include a scheduled job as a later step. The core functionalities of inbound actions revolve around processing emails and taking immediate actions based on the extracted information.

questions.question: What is a data policy?
options: Enables admins to set mandatory and read only states for fields and can enforce data consistency across applications. You can set import data as read only, e.g., user info
It's the control record of the table and determines whether the table will be audited, default sorting, attributes of table and how it will behave when it is a reference field
It's a series of tables that contain all the assets and business services controlled by your company as well as their configuration
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is:
Enables admins to set mandatory and read-only states for fields and can enforce data consistency across applications. You can set import data as read-only, e.g., user info.
Here’s why this answer best describes a data policy:
• Data policies in ServiceNow allow administrators to define rules that govern how data is entered and managed within the platform. These rules can:
• Set mandatory fields: Ensure specific fields are filled in by users when creating or editing records.
• Set read-only fields: Restrict users from modifying certain fields, potentially for security reasons or to prevent accidental changes.
• Enforce data consistency: Maintain consistent data formats and values across different applications within ServiceNow.
Here’s why the other options are not as accurate:
• Control record of the table: While data policies might interact with table properties, they are not the same as the control record that defines the overall structure and behavior of a table.
• Series of tables for assets and services: This description refers more to the Configuration Management Database (CMDB) functionality within ServiceNow, not data policies.
• All of the above: While data policies do influence data consistency and potentially interact with table properties, they are not a direct replacement for control records or the CMDB.
In summary, data policies provide a mechanism for administrators to enforce specific data management practices within ServiceNow, promoting data integrity and consistency across the platform.

questions.question: What is a UI policy?
options: Its a required field that requires a value
It's a rule that applies to a form to dynamically change the ways the fields behave in a form
It's a script that applies to a form to dynamically change form information or the form itself
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. It’s a rule that applies to a form to dynamically change the ways the fields behave in a form
• Correct because a UI policy in ServiceNow is a declarative rule that controls form behavior dynamically.
• It can make fields mandatory, visible, or read-only based on conditions, without requiring custom scripting.
• This is the standard definition tested in the CSA exam.
Incorrect
Option A. Required field that requires a value
• Incorrect because this describes a field property or a data policy, not a UI policy.
• UI policies can make fields required, but they are broader than just enforcing required values.
Option C. Script that applies to a form
• Incorrect because this describes a Client Script, not a UI policy.
• Client scripts use JavaScript to manipulate form data and behavior, while UI policies are rule-based and simpler to configure.

questions.question: Where would you go to start an import set?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. System Import Sets > Load Data
• Correct: To start an import set in ServiceNow, you go to System Import Sets > Load Data. This is where you upload a data file (such as CSV, Excel, or XML) into a staging table. From there, you can transform and map the data into target tables.
• This is the entry point for initiating an import set process.
Incorrect
• Option A. System Import Sets > Import Sets
• Incorrect: This menu shows existing import set tables and records but does not initiate a new import.
• Option B. System Definition > Import Sets
• Incorrect: Import sets are not managed under System Definition. That menu is for defining tables, fields, and schema.
• Option C. System Properties > Import Sets
• Incorrect: System Properties is for configuring global settings, not for starting import sets.

questions.question: What gets skipped during a major upgrade?
options: Read only data of a form that is not editable
All system features, applications, functions, and data
Any record that has been altered from the base state. The upgrade app looks at the customer update table (e.g,, sys_update_xml)
questions.explanation:
During a major ServiceNow upgrade, C. Any record that has been altered from the base state. The upgrade app looks at the customer update table (e.g., sys_update_xml) is skipped.
The upgrade process relies on the customer update table (e.g., sys_update_xml) to identify records that have been customized from their original state. These customized records are then skipped during the upgrade to prevent any potential conflicts or data loss.
During a major ServiceNow upgrade, the system will not overwrite any changes you have made to your instance. Instead, it will identify these customized records and “skip” them, meaning they will not be updated as part of the upgrade process.
The key reasons for this are:
• Record Inserts – New records you have created, such as ACLs, business rules, and fields
• Record Updates – Changes you have made to the out-of-the-box records provided by ServiceNow
• Deletes – Deletion of out-of-the-box records
The upgrade process evaluates each record in your instance and compares it to the base version to determine if a “skipped change” needs to be generated. This allows you to review the changes and decide whether to revert to the base version, merge the changes, or retain your customizations.
The quantity of skipped changes and the time required to review them depends on factors like the number of customizations in your instance and the extent of changes made by ServiceNow in the new release. Reviewing and addressing skipped changes is a critical part of the upgrade process.
Here’s a breakdown of the other answer choices:
• A. Read only data of a form that is not editable: This type of data is typically included in the upgrade as it forms the base configuration of the system.
• B. All system features, applications, functions, and data: While some features might be deprecated during an upgrade, most core functionalities and data are carried over.
• D. All the above: This is incorrect as customized records are specifically skipped during the upgrade process.
References:
https://www.servicenow.com/content/dam/servicenow-assets/public/en-us/doc-type/success/quick-answer/skipped-changes-review.pdf
https://www.servicenow.com/community/developer-articles/helpful-enhancement-for-reviewing-skipped-updates-during/ta-p/2322874

questions.question: Which of the following can be an example of Out Of The Box table?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is incident.
Here’s why:
• Out-of-the-box (OOTB) tables come pre-configured with ServiceNow and provide core functionalities. They are designed to support common IT service management (ITSM) processes.
• incident is a fundamental OOTB table used for logging and managing user-reported issues.
• u_incident and x_u123_incident start with “u_” or “x_” prefixes, which typically indicate custom tables created by users or specific instances.
• u_movie also follows the custom table naming convention.
Understanding OOTB tables is crucial for a ServiceNow CSA, as they form the foundation of the platform.

questions.question: What is an Order Guide?
options: An order guide provides the ability to order multiple related items as one request
A documentation guide which helps in ordering items
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. An order guide provides the ability to order multiple related items as one request
• Correct because the purpose of an Order Guide in ServiceNow is to allow users to request multiple related catalog items together in a single request.
• Example: For onboarding a new employee, an order guide can group items such as a laptop, software licenses, and an access badge into one guided request.
• This ensures consistency, efficiency, and reduces the chance of missing required items.
Incorrect
Option A. A type of catalog item
• Incorrect because an order guide is not a catalog item itself. It is a container or grouping mechanism that helps users order multiple catalog items at once.
Option C. A documentation guide which helps in ordering items
• Incorrect because an order guide is not documentation. It is an interactive tool within the Service Catalog that guides users through ordering related items, not a written manual.

questions.question: Which among the following is true regarding UI Policies?
options: They run only on server side
All the UI Policies of task table are not extended by the incident table
Based on the condition, it can be decided when to make it visible/hidden
They run on the cloud side
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C (Based on the condition, it can be decided when to make it visible/hidden): UI Policies in ServiceNow dynamically control field visibility, mandatory status, and read-only state based on conditional logic, providing immediate client-side form behavior changes.
Incorrect
Option A (They run only on server side): UI Policies execute client-side in the browser for responsive UI updates; server-side equivalents are Data Policies.
Option B (All the UI Policies of task table are not extended by the incident table): Incident table inherits UI Policies from its parent Task table through table extension.
Option D (They run on the cloud side): UI Policies run client-side; “cloud side” isn’t valid ServiceNow terminology for execution context.

questions.question: ACLs can be defined in how many ways?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D: All of the above
• Correct.
• In ServiceNow, Access Control Lists (ACLs) can be defined in multiple ways:
• Conditional Expressions → Logical conditions that must be met for access to be granted.
• Scripts → JavaScript-based rules for more complex access logic.
• Roles → Role-based security that grants or restricts access depending on user roles.
• Since ACLs can be defined using all three methods, the correct answer is All of the above.
Incorrect
Option A: Conditional Expressions
• Incorrect as a standalone answer.
• While ACLs can be defined using conditional expressions, this is only one method. The question asks for all ways, so this option alone is incomplete.
Option B: Scripts
• Incorrect as a standalone answer.
• Scripts are another valid method, but ACLs are not limited to scripts only.
Option C: Roles
• Incorrect as a standalone answer.
• Roles are a key part of ACLs, but ACLs also rely on conditions and scripts.

questions.question: Which feature helps you in testing what another user sees in the instance without logging in with the user credentials?
questions.explanation:
Impersonate is the feature that allows you to see what another user sees in the ServiceNow instance without needing their credentials.
Impersonation is a valuable tool for administrators for various purposes, including:
• Testing user permissions and access: By impersonating a user, admins can verify if the user has the correct access rights to perform specific tasks.
• Troubleshooting user issues: Impersonation can help admins replicate problems faced by users and diagnose the root cause.
• Providing user support: By seeing the user’s interface, admins can offer more targeted and effective assistance.
The other options you provided are not directly related to impersonating users:
• Escalate: This function increases the priority of an existing incident or request.
• Elevate Role: This grants temporary access to a higher privilege level for a specific task. While it might involve seeing a broader user interface, it’s not focused on mimicking another user’s view.
• None: There is indeed a feature for impersonation in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Like business rules, notifications can be created when a record is inserted or updated.
questions.explanation:
TRUE, notifications can be triggered just like business rules when a record is inserted or updated.
Both notifications and business rules are functionalities within ServiceNow that react to events on the platform. Here’s a quick comparison:
• Notifications: Their primary purpose is to send alerts or messages (emails, SMS, etc.) based on specific criteria. They can be configured to trigger upon record insert/update and notify relevant users or groups.
• Business Rules: They offer a broader range of actions. They can trigger notifications, update fields, manipulate data, or even execute scripts based on record insert/update events. They provide more flexibility for automating tasks and data manipulation.
So, while both can react to record changes, they serve slightly different purposes.

questions.question: What is SLM?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Service Level Management (SLM).
SLM stands for Service Level Management and it’s a core functionality within ServiceNow that helps organizations define, track, and report on the quality of IT services delivered to users. It focuses on establishing agreements (SLAs) that outline the expected performance of these services.

questions.question: Unique ID is stored in which field of table
questions.explanation:
The unique identifier in ServiceNow tables is stored in the sys_id field.
Here’s why:
• sys_id is a standard field present in all ServiceNow tables. It’s a 32-character alphanumeric string (GUID) that uniquely identifies each record in the instance.
• global_number and unique_id are not standard fields in ServiceNow. While some custom tables might utilize these names, they wouldn’t be guaranteed to hold unique identifiers across the platform.
• 32_id isn’t a common field name either. While the length (32 characters) might suggest a connection to the unique identifier, it’s not a standard way to reference it.
So, remember, sys_id is the go-to field for unique record identification within ServiceNow.

questions.question: Where would you go to create an order guide?
options: Service catalog > catalog definition > order guides and click new
Go to system definition > choice list
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Service catalog > catalog definition > order guides and click new.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• System properties > css: This section is for managing system properties and Cascading Style Sheets (CSS) used for customizing the platform’s appearance. It’s not related to creating order guides.
• Go to system definition > choice list: Choice lists are used to define pre-defined options for users to select from within forms. While order guides may utilize choice lists, creating them happens within the service catalog.

questions.question: Multiple Choice, Single Text, and select Box are what type of elements in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Variable Types.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• Related Lists: Related lists display records associated with a specific record on a form. They are not elements used to define user input or selection options.
• Request Types: Request types categorize service catalog offerings based on the type of service being requested. They are not specific elements used for user input.
• Order Guides: Order guides allow users to request multiple related items as a single service offering within the service catalog. They are not specific elements used for user input.
Multiple Choice, Single Text, and Select Box are all Variable Types. These define the type of information users can provide when submitting a request through the service catalog. They allow for capturing various details like selecting options from a predefined list, entering text, or making choices between multiple options.

questions.question: An ACL is _ type of security.
questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow, an ACL is a Contextual (Correct) security measure.
Here’s why:
• Physical: Physical security refers to tangible measures like locks and security guards, not software-based controls like ACLs.
• Barrier: While ACLs restrict access, they are more than a simple barrier. They offer granular control based on user roles, conditions, and specific actions (read, write, etc.).
• Compliance: Compliance refers to adhering to regulations. ACLs can help enforce compliance by restricting access to sensitive data based on compliance requirements. However, they are a tool for achieving compliance, not the compliance itself.
• Contextual (Correct): Contextual security is a perfect fit for ACLs. ACLs consider the context of a user, record, and action when determining access permissions. They can be configured to grant or deny access based on various factors, making them highly adaptable to different security needs.
So, ACLs are a form of contextual security that allows for fine-grained access control within ServiceNow.

questions.question: What is the correct sequence of the steps of a Knowledge article?
questions.explanation:
The correct sequence for a ServiceNow Knowledge Article is:
Draft, Review, Publish, Retire (Correct)
Here’s the breakdown of each stage:
• Draft: In this initial phase, the author creates the content of the knowledge article. This includes adding details, formatting, and ensuring clarity.
• Review: Once drafted, the article undergoes a review process. This might involve subject matter experts, editors, or internal stakeholders verifying the information’s accuracy and completeness.
• Publish: After successful review, the article gets published and becomes accessible to users based on its visibility settings (public, private, etc.).
• Retire: Over time, knowledge articles might become outdated due to changes in processes or technology. When an article is no longer relevant, it can be retired. This archives the article and prevents users from encountering potentially inaccurate information.
The other options you provided don’t follow the best practice for knowledge article lifecycle management:
• Review, Draft, Publish: While review is important, it typically happens after the initial content is drafted.
• Draft, Publish, Delete: Deleting an article can lead to data loss. Retiring it maintains a record while preventing its active use.
• Draft, Publish, Retire: This skips the crucial review step, which helps ensure quality and accuracy before publishing.

questions.question: Where do UI Policies run?
options: On record stored in the sys_user_group table
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. On client side
• Correct because UI Policies in ServiceNow are client-side rules.
• They dynamically control form behavior in the browser (e.g., making fields mandatory, visible, or read-only) based on conditions.
• They do not execute on the server or database level; instead, they run in the user’s browser session to provide real-time interaction.
Incorrect
Option A. On server side
• Incorrect because server-side logic is handled by Business Rules or Server-side scripts, not UI Policies.
• UI Policies are specifically designed for client-side execution.
Option C. On record stored in the sys_user_group table
• Incorrect because UI Policies are not tied to specific database tables like sys_user_group.
• They apply to forms and fields, not directly to stored records.
Option D. All of the above
• Incorrect because UI Policies do not run on both client and server sides, nor on database records.
• They are strictly client-side only.

questions.question: To see the relationship between tables in a graphical view, what is used?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Schema Map.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• Business Service Map: Business Service Maps show how Configuration Items (CIs) relate to Services offered by your organization. While they can involve tables indirectly, they don’t directly depict table relationships.
• Tables and Columns: This module provides a list of all tables and their associated columns, but it doesn’t offer a visual representation of how tables relate to each other.
• Tables Map: There’s no standard term like “Tables Map” within ServiceNow. Schema Map is the specific tool used for this purpose.
A Schema Map is a valuable tool for ServiceNow administrators as it allows you to visualize the relationships between different tables in the platform. It displays:
• Tables: All the tables involved in the schema.
• Relationships: The connections between tables, typically represented by arrows or lines. These can be one-to-one, one-to-many, or many-to-many relationships.
• Fields: Sometimes, schema maps may also depict relevant fields within the tables to illustrate the connection points.
By understanding these relationships, you can better manage data flow, identify potential issues, and ensure data consistency across your ServiceNow instance.

questions.question: The upgrade history module helps an admin locate and resolve upgrade conflicts by reverting customization to the base version if necessary.
questions.explanation:
The statement is TRUE. The Upgrade History module in ServiceNow is a valuable tool for admins to track upgrades and troubleshoot any issues that may arise. Here’s how it helps with upgrade conflicts:
• Records Upgrade Details: It maintains a history of all upgrades performed on the instance, including the versions involved, timestamps, and any relevant logs.
• Identifies Conflicts: By reviewing the upgrade history, admins can pinpoint potential conflicts that might have occurred during the upgrade process. These conflicts can stem from customizations made to the instance that are incompatible with the new version.
• Revert Option: The Upgrade History module may provide the ability to revert specific customizations back to their base versions. This allows admins to isolate and address conflicts, potentially restoring functionality or preventing errors.
While reverting customizations isn’t always the ideal solution, it can be a helpful first step in resolving conflicts and ensuring a smooth upgrade process.
Here’s why the other option is incorrect:
• FALSE: If the Upgrade History module couldn’t help with reverting customizations, it would lose a significant part of its usefulness in resolving upgrade conflicts.

questions.question: How do you change the sort sequence of fields or tasks?
options: Make changes by clicking on the gear icon
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. Modify the order field
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the Order field determines the sort sequence of fields or tasks.
• By adjusting the numeric value in the Order field, administrators can control the display sequence.
• This is the standard CSA exam answer because it directly addresses how sorting is managed in forms and lists.
• Option B. Make changes by clicking on the gear icon
• Also correct because the gear icon (Personalize List Layout) allows users to configure how fields are displayed and sorted in a list view.
• While this is more of a user‑level customization than a system‑wide configuration, it is still a valid way to change sort order for tasks or fields in a list.
Incorrect
• Option C. None of the above
• Incorrect because both modifying the Order field and using the gear icon are valid methods.
• Therefore, “None of the above” is not correct.

questions.question: What are update sets?
options: Customization that can be moved from 1 instance to another
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Customization that can be moved from 1 instance to another
• Correct because update sets in ServiceNow are containers that capture customizations and configuration changes (like forms, fields, scripts, workflows) made in one instance.
• They allow administrators to move these changes to another instance (e.g., from development → test → production).
• This is the primary purpose of update sets and is a critical exam concept.
Incorrect
Option A. History of upgrades
• Incorrect because update sets do not track upgrade history.
• Upgrade history is managed separately in ServiceNow, while update sets specifically capture customizations, not upgrade logs.
Option C. Groups items together
• Incorrect because while update sets do group captured changes, this description is too vague and does not reflect their actual purpose.
• The exam expects recognition of update sets as migration tools for customizations, not just grouping mechanisms.
Option D. All the above
• Incorrect because not all the listed statements are true.
• Only Option B correctly defines update sets, so “All the above” is misleading.

questions.question: In service catalog application, which module is used for creating items?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Maintain Items.
In the Service Catalog application within ServiceNow, the Maintain Items module is specifically designed for creating new catalog items. These catalog items represent the services or products users can request through the service catalog.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• Items: “Items” might be a general term encompassing all catalog items within the service catalog. It doesn’t denote the specific module for creating new ones.
• Maintain Category: This module is likely used for managing categories within the service catalog, which helps organize catalog items for easier browsing by users. While creating categories is important, it’s separate from creating the actual catalog items themselves.
• Maintain Dynamic Categories: Dynamic categories might be a specific feature for managing categories that adjust based on user selections or other criteria. Similar to “Maintain Category”, it focuses on category management and not directly on creating catalog items.

questions.question: All users can manage and setup import sets.
questions.explanation:
The statement is FALSE. Only users with specific permissions can manage and set up import sets in ServiceNow.
Here’s why:
• Import sets are a powerful tool for importing data into ServiceNow tables. Due to the potential impact on data integrity, access to managing and setting them up is restricted.
• Users require the import_set role or be a member of a group that has this role to perform these actions.
By limiting access, ServiceNow ensures that only authorized users can import data, minimizing the risk of errors or unauthorized modifications.

questions.question: How to get security_admin role / elevated privilege for a user session?
options: Select the Elevate Role option in the security admin
Add security role to the user from Roles related list in user record
Select the security_admin option in the Elevate Roles section
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Select the security_admin option in the Elevate Roles section
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the security_admin role is not permanently assigned to users by default.
• Instead, administrators must elevate roles during a session by selecting security_admin in the Elevate Roles dialog.
• This provides temporary elevated privileges to perform sensitive security operations such as modifying Access Control Lists (ACLs) or High Security Settings.
Incorrect
Option A. Select the Elevate Role option in the security admin
• Incorrect because the phrasing is misleading. You don’t elevate “in the security admin”; you elevate roles via the Elevate Roles section in the user session.
Option B. Add security role to the user from Roles related list in user record
• Incorrect because the security_admin role cannot be permanently assigned through the Roles related list.
• It must be elevated per session for security reasons.

questions.question: Task table is a _ table.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Base
Explanation:
• In ServiceNow, the Task table is a base table.
• It is one of the core tables in the ServiceNow platform and provides common fields (such as number, assigned_to, state, priority) that are inherited by many other tables.
• Examples of tables that extend from Task include Incident, Problem, Change Request, and Service Request.
• Because Task is a base table, it serves as the foundation for multiple extended tables.
Incorrect
Option A. Custom
• Incorrect because the Task table is not custom; it is a standard, out‑of‑the‑box table provided by ServiceNow.
Option C. Extended
• Incorrect because Task is the parent/base table, not an extended table. Extended tables (like Incident or Problem) inherit from Task.
Option D. Child
• Incorrect because Task is the parent table, not a child. Child tables (like Incident) derive from Task.

questions.question: A Business rule can be set before or after the database action has occurred.
questions.explanation:
The statement is TRUE.
Business rules in ServiceNow offer flexibility by allowing them to be set to run either before or after a database operation occurs on a record.
Here’s a breakdown of the two main types of business rules:
• Before: These rules execute before the data is saved to the database. This allows you to manipulate or validate data before it’s committed to the system. For instance, a before business rule might ensure a specific field is filled in before allowing the record to be saved.
• After: These rules execute after the data is saved to the database. This is useful for actions that rely on the record already existing, like sending notifications or updating related records.
By choosing the appropriate timing for a business rule, you can achieve a wide range of functionalities within ServiceNow.

questions.question: Types of SLA (SLA, OLA & UC) are defined in which field?
questions.explanation:
The type of SLA (Service Level Agreement), OLA (Operational Level Agreement), and UC (Underpinning Contract) is defined in the Type Field (Correct) within ServiceNow.
Here’s why:
Type Field: This field explicitly captures the specific agreement type (SLA, OLA, or UC). It allows the system to differentiate between different agreements and apply relevant rules or calculations.
Retroactive Start: This field, while relevant to SLAs, doesn’t specify the agreement type. It determines whether the SLA timer starts when the record is created or when a specific condition is met.
Condition Field: This field defines the conditions that trigger the start or stop of an SLA timer. It’s independent of the agreement type.
Duration: This field specifies the timeframe associated with the agreement (e.g., response time in hours). While it’s an important SLA element, it doesn’t indicate the type of agreement.
By defining the agreement type in the “Type Field,” ServiceNow can manage different agreements (SLA, OLA, UC) with appropriate configurations and tracking mechanisms.

questions.question: What are the out of box progress stages for a Service Request?
questions.explanation:
All of the above (Correct) is the answer. ServiceNow offers the following out-of-the-box progress stages for a Service Request:
• Waiting for Approval: This stage indicates the request is pending approval from a designated person or group before proceeding.
• Fulfillment: This stage signifies that the request is being actively worked on by the assigned personnel.
• Delivery: This stage marks the completion of the requested service and its delivery to the user.
These stages provide a basic framework for tracking the lifecycle of a Service Request within ServiceNow.
It’s important to note that organizations can customize these progress stages or add additional stages to better reflect their specific service request workflows.

questions.question: What is true about deleting tables?
options: An ESS user can delete any table
Deleting a table doesnot delete associated elements like views
only tables beginning with "u_" can be permanently deleted
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Only tables beginning with “u_” can be permanently deleted
• In ServiceNow, custom tables created by users (which always begin with the prefix "u_") can be permanently deleted.
• System tables and baseline tables provided by ServiceNow cannot be deleted to protect platform integrity.
• This ensures administrators can remove their own customizations but not core functionality.
Incorrect
Option A. An ESS user can delete any table
• Incorrect because ESS (Employee Self‑Service) users have very limited permissions.
• They cannot delete tables; only administrators with the right roles can manage table deletion.
Option B. Deleting a table does not delete associated elements like views
• Incorrect because when a table is deleted, all associated elements (views, forms, lists, fields, etc.) are also deleted.
• ServiceNow enforces this to maintain consistency and avoid orphaned metadata.

questions.question: Where can you view a series of customizations?
