questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Update set.
Here’s why:
• Update sets are specifically designed to bundle and track customizations made within a ServiceNow instance. They act as containers that group together various changes, including:
• Custom scripts and workflows
• Field and table modifications
• UI customizations
By reviewing the contents of an update set, you can view a series of customizations made to the instance. Update sets also provide information about who made the changes, when they were made, and a brief description of the modifications.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• System Log: The system log primarily records system events and activities, not necessarily user-made customizations.
• History: While history logs might exist for specific modules or configurations, there isn’t a central “History” location for viewing all customizations within ServiceNow.
• None of the above: Update sets are indeed the primary way to view and manage a series of customizations in ServiceNow.

questions.question: What are the main tools you can use to automate servicenow?
options: Ui policy, data policies, ui actions and scripts
Lists, global text search, navigation filter, live feed
questions.explanation:
Out of the choices provided, the main tools for automating ServiceNow are:
Ui policy, data policies, UI actions and scripts (Correct)
Here’s why these options are strong contenders for automation:
• UI Policy: These dynamically control the user interface based on conditions. They can hide/show fields, set mandatory fields, and manipulate field behavior, automating specific UI interactions.
• Data Policies: These automate data validation and manipulation during record creation or update. They can enforce data quality and consistency, reducing manual data entry tasks.
• UI Actions: These are buttons or links on forms that trigger scripts when clicked. These scripts can automate various tasks like creating new records, sending notifications, or updating data based on user actions.
• Scripts: These are custom programs written in ServiceNow’s scripting language (mostly JavaScript). They offer extensive automation capabilities, interacting with data, integrating with external systems, and orchestrating complex workflows.
The other options you listed are not directly related to automation:
• System properties > css: System properties are for configuring various system settings, while CSS styles define the visual appearance of the user interface. Neither directly contributes to automation.
• Lists, global text search, navigation filter, live feed: These are user interface elements for searching, filtering, and displaying information. While they can improve efficiency, they aren’t core automation tools.
By effectively combining these ServiceNow automation tools (UI policies, data policies, UI actions, and scripts), you can streamline processes, reduce manual effort, and improve overall platform efficiency.

questions.question: You cannot revert update set versions.
questions.explanation:
The statement is FALSE.
You can revert update set versions in ServiceNow.
Update sets are a valuable tool for managing customizations, but they can sometimes introduce unintended consequences. Reverting an update set allows you to undo those changes and go back to a previous state.
Here’s how reverting update sets works:
• Identify the Version: You need to determine the specific version of the update set you want to revert to. Update sets maintain version history, allowing you to choose the desired point in time.
• Revert Option: Within the update set record, there’s usually a “Revert” or “Rollback” option that, when activated, initiates the reversion process.
• Impact: The reversion process essentially removes the changes introduced by the later versions of the update set, restoring the instance to the state it was in at the chosen version.
It’s important to note that reverting update sets can have downstream impacts on other customizations or functionalities that may have relied on the changes being reverted. A well-defined rollback strategy and testing procedures are recommended before reverting an update set.

questions.question: Which one is used to group related fields together?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Sections
• Correct because Sections in ServiceNow forms are specifically designed to group related fields together.
• They provide logical organization within a form, making it easier for users to navigate and understand related data.
• For example, in an Incident form, you might have separate sections for Caller Information, Incident Details, and Resolution Information.
Incorrect
Option A. Form Layout
• Incorrect because Form Layout defines the overall arrangement of fields and sections on a form.
• It controls placement but does not itself group related fields — that is the role of Sections.
Option C. List Layout
• Incorrect because List Layout determines how records are displayed in a list view (columns, sorting, etc.).
• It does not group related fields inside a form.
Option D. View
• Incorrect because a View defines a specific arrangement of fields for a form or list, often tailored for different roles or use cases.
• While views can include sections, they are not the mechanism for grouping fields — they are higher‑level configurations.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements describes the purpose of an update set?
options: Move customizations from Production to Development
Create a standard process for moving customizations from instance to instance
Load incidents data from one instance to other instance
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B: Create a standard process for moving customizations from instance to instance
• Correct.
• An update set in ServiceNow is used to capture configuration changes (customizations such as forms, fields, business rules, workflows) made in one instance and move them to another instance.
• This ensures a consistent and controlled process for migrating changes between environments (e.g., from development → test → production).
• Update sets do not move data records like incidents or users, only configuration/customization changes.
Incorrect
Option A: Move customizations from Production to Development
• Incorrect.
• Best practice is to move changes from Development to Production, not the other way around.
• Update sets are not designed for reverse migration from production to development.
Option C: Load incidents data from one instance to other instance
• Incorrect.
• Update sets do not transfer data records (like incidents, problems, or tasks).
• They only move configuration changes. Data migration requires other methods such as import sets or integration tools.

questions.question: What database kept all the customization that you made on your instance?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Sys_update_XML
• The Sys_update_XML table stores all customizations made in a ServiceNow instance.
• This includes changes to forms, fields, scripts, and configurations.
• It is the key table used for tracking updates and is essential for update sets and migration between instances.
• Therefore, this is the correct answer.
Incorrect
Option B. Sys_update_HTML
• No such table exists in ServiceNow.
• HTML is used in UI pages and widgets, but customizations are not tracked in a Sys_update_HTML table.
Option C. Sys_update_SAML
• SAML relates to authentication and single sign‑on (SSO).
• It is not used to store customizations.
• This option is invalid.
Option D. Sys_update_CSS
• CSS is used for styling UI elements.
• There is no Sys_update_CSS table in ServiceNow.
• Customizations are not stored here.

questions.question: What does a dictionary override do?
options: It updates the db fields and brings you back to a list
Set fields on a form from to visible or hidden; editable or read only; optional or mandatory
It provides the ability to override several aspects of a field in extended tables
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: It provides the ability to override several aspects of a field in extended tables (Correct).
Here’s why:
• A dictionary override allows you to customize the behavior and appearance of fields within extended tables in ServiceNow. It doesn’t directly update database fields or navigate you back to a list after making changes.
• While dictionary overrides can affect how a field is displayed on a form (visibility, editability), their core function goes beyond just those aspects. They offer a broader range of customization options.
Here are some of the key things you can do with dictionary overrides:
• Change field labels and descriptions: This improves user understanding of the field’s purpose.
• Modify field behavior: You can define default values, set mandatory requirements, or control how the field interacts with other parts of the system.
• Define field choices: For choice-based fields, you can edit the available options or even create new choices based on specific needs.
• Set field validation rules: You can define rules that data entered into the field must comply with, ensuring data accuracy and consistency.
In essence, dictionary overrides empower administrators to tailor extended tables’ fields to their specific requirements, enhancing the functionality and user experience within ServiceNow.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• It updates the db fields and brings you back to a list: While dictionary overrides can indirectly affect database fields by modifying field behavior, they don’t directly update the database themselves. Additionally, navigating back to a list isn’t a core function of dictionary overrides.
• Display information from a record: This is more aligned with what a field itself does. Dictionary overrides focus on customizing how fields function and appear, not just displaying information.

questions.question: To create two columns in a form, how many splits should be used
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: One (Correct).
Here’s why:
• In ServiceNow forms, you don’t necessarily need to split the form layout to create multiple columns. The form layout itself can be configured to have multiple columns within a single section.
• Splitting the form (using the “Split” option) might be used to create entirely separate sections within the form, but it’s not the primary method for creating columns to display fields side-by-side.
Here’s how you can achieve two columns in a ServiceNow form:
• Access the form in “Form Layout” mode.
• Drag and drop the desired fields onto the form layout.
• Use the layout options to arrange the fields side-by-side. This might involve adjusting the width of each field or using the “Column Layout” option (if available) to define a two-column structure within the form section.
By following these steps, you can create a form with two columns without needing to split the form layout itself.

questions.question: What does a patch release fix in ServiceNow?
options: It allows you to update the record without having to into a form
Combines hot fixes from last feature release and does other fixes
Define the questions to ask from the end user ordering the catalog item
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Combines hot fixes from last feature release and does other fixes
• Correct because a patch release in ServiceNow is specifically intended to fix issues (bugs, hotfixes, and minor improvements) that were discovered after a feature release.
• It does not introduce new major functionality but ensures stability and reliability by bundling fixes.
Incorrect
Option A. Update the record without going into a form
• Incorrect because this describes list editing or inline editing, not patch releases.
Option C. Define questions for catalog item ordering
• Incorrect because this refers to variables in Service Catalog items, not patch releases.
Option D. None of the above
• Incorrect because Option B correctly describes what a patch release fixes.

questions.question: What is a healthy total response time for Network, browser & server?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. 3 seconds, On Average
• Correct: In ServiceNow performance guidelines, a healthy total response time (network + browser + server combined) should average around 3 seconds.
• This ensures good user experience and aligns with industry standards for web application responsiveness.
Incorrect
• Option B. 60 seconds, On Average
• Incorrect: A 60‑second response time is far too slow and would indicate severe performance issues.
• Option C. 10 seconds, On Average
• Incorrect: While better than 60 seconds, 10 seconds is still considered poor performance and not “healthy.”
• Option D. 1 Minute, On Average
• Incorrect: Same as Option B, 1 minute is unacceptable for normal ServiceNow operations.

questions.question: What does SAAS stands for?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is: Software as a service.
SAAS stands for Software as a Service. It’s a cloud-based software delivery model where users access applications over the internet instead of installing and maintaining them on their local computers.

questions.question: If a row level and a field level rule are in conflict, both rules must be met before an operation is allowed.
questions.explanation:
The statement is TRUE.
In ServiceNow, if a row level rule and a field level rule are in conflict, both rules must be met before an operation is allowed.
Here’s how these rule types interact:
• Row Level Rules: These rules evaluate the entire record and determine access permissions based on various criteria. A record might be restricted from specific operations (like edit or delete) if the row level rule doesn’t grant permission.
• Field Level Rules: These rules focus on individual fields within a record. They can dictate field behavior, such as visibility, editability, or mandatory requirements.
For an operation to be successful, both the row level rule and any relevant field level rules must be satisfied. Here’s an example:
• A row level rule might restrict edit access to a record for users without a specific role.
• A field level rule on a specific field within that record might make the field read-only for everyone.
In this scenario, even if a user has edit permissions based on other factors, they wouldn’t be able to edit the record because the field level rule makes the specific field read-only. Both rules (row level and field level) must be met for a successful edit operation.

questions.question: A group can contain a nested group.
questions.explanation:
True.
A group can indeed contain a nested group. This allows for a hierarchical structure, where groups can be organized into smaller, more specific subgroups. This is a common feature in various systems and applications, such as email clients, file managers, and project management tools.

questions.question: What records can be created when placing an order in the Service Catalog? Select 3 answers
questions.explanation:
The records that can be created when placing an order in the Service Catalog are:
• Requested Item [sc_req_item]: This record represents the specific item or service requested by the user.
• Catalog Task [sc_task]: This record represents the tasks that need to be completed to fulfill the requested item.
• Request [sc_request]: This record represents the overall request or order placed by the user.
Therefore, the correct answers are Requested Item [sc_req_item], Catalog Task [sc_task], and Request [sc_request].
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: What are the major workflow activities?
options: Approvals, Conditions, Notifications, Tasks, Timers, Utilities
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Approvals, Conditions, Notifications, Tasks, Timers, Utilities This is correct because these are the major workflow activities in ServiceNow. They represent the building blocks used to automate processes:
• Approvals – manage authorization steps.
• Conditions – define logic for branching workflows.
• Notifications – send alerts or updates.
• Tasks – assign work items to users or groups.
• Timers – control time-based actions.
• Utilities – provide supporting functions like logging or variable manipulation.
Incorrect
Option A. Approvals, Conditions, Notifications Incorrect because while these are valid workflow activities, the list is incomplete. It omits Tasks, Timers, and Utilities, which are also major activities.
Option B. Approval conditions, Notification, Tasks Incorrect because “Approval conditions” is not a distinct workflow activity. The correct term is Approvals. This option also misses Timers and Utilities.
Option D. None of the above Incorrect because option C correctly lists all major workflow activities.

questions.question: The problem_task table extends which table?
options: There is no table such as problem_task
It does not extend any table
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
In ServiceNow, the problem_task table is a child table of the task table.
Task table is the base table for many process-specific tables such as incident, change_request, problem, and problem_task.
Therefore, problem_task extends the task table, not the other way around.
The original explanation may have implied that problem_task extends nothing or extends problem.
In reality:
problem_task is a child table
Parent = task table`

questions.question: How is it possible for a non-administrator to develop and deploy applications on the Now Platform?
options: Ask the administrators to do it since only administrators have this level of access.
It is not possible to develop or deploy applications in ServiceNow.
It is not necessary for a non-administrator to develop or deploy applications.
Use delegated development and deployment application.
questions.explanation:
The ServiceNow Delegated development and deployment application enables non-administrators to develop and deploy applications.
(Abbildung im Original)
Use delegated development and deployment application.
In ServiceNow, delegated development and deployment applications can be used to grant non-administrators specific permissions to create, modify, and deploy applications. These applications can be configured to restrict access to certain areas of the platform, ensuring that non-administrators only have the necessary permissions to perform their tasks.
Here’s a breakdown of the other options:
• Ask the administrators to do it since only administrators have this level of access: While this is a possible solution, it can be inefficient and time-consuming, especially if there are many non-administrators who need to develop and deploy applications.
• It is not possible to develop or deploy applications in ServiceNow: This is incorrect. ServiceNow provides a platform for developing and deploying applications.
• It is not necessary for a non-administrator to develop or deploy applications: This may be true in some cases, but it’s not always the case. In many organizations, non-administrators are responsible for developing and deploying custom applications to meet specific business needs.
Therefore, using delegated development and deployment applications is the most effective way for non-administrators to develop and deploy applications on the Now Platform while maintaining appropriate security and control.

questions.question: Who can access schema maps, tables, and column module?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Administrator
• Only Administrators have access to schema maps, tables, and column modules in ServiceNow.
• These modules are part of the system configuration and data model, which require elevated privileges.
• Administrators can view and manage the schema map, table structures, and column definitions.
Incorrect
Option A. ITIL User
• ITIL users have access to incident, problem, change, and other ITSM processes.
• They do not have access to schema maps or table/column modules.
Option B. End User
• End users interact with the Service Portal or standard forms to submit requests or incidents.
• They do not have access to backend schema maps or table structures.
Option C. Approver
• Approvers can approve requests or changes but do not have access to schema maps or table/column modules.

questions.question: What are the workflow activities?
options: Waiting for approval, fulfillment, delivery, completed
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Waiting for approval, fulfillment, delivery, completed
• Correct because these represent the core workflow activities in ServiceNow workflows.
• Workflow activities are the building blocks that define the actions and transitions in a process, such as approvals, task fulfillment, delivery, and marking completion.
• They ensure automation of processes like request handling, incident resolution, and change management.
Incorrect
Option A. Start, Pause, Reset, Complete
• Incorrect because these are workflow states, not activities.
• They describe the status of a workflow instance rather than the activities performed within it.
Option B. Draft, Review, Publish, Retire
• Incorrect because these are knowledge management lifecycle stages, not workflow activities.
• They apply to knowledge articles, not to workflow processes.
Option D. Start, Pause, Reset
• Incorrect because, like option A, these are workflow states.
• They do not represent the actual activities that drive workflow execution.

questions.question: When you have subject filled on email notification as well as on the notification template, which one will appear on the sent email?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option B. Subject from Email Notification Correct. In ServiceNow, when both the email notification record and the notification template contain a subject, the subject defined in the email notification takes precedence. This ensures that the administrator’s explicit subject choice in the notification record is what appears in the sent email.
Incorrect
• Option A. Both the subjects are concatenated Incorrect because ServiceNow does not merge or concatenate subjects from both sources. Only one subject line is used, and it comes from the notification record.
• Option C. Subject from Template Incorrect because the template subject is overridden if the notification record itself has a subject defined. The template subject is only used when the notification record does not specify one.
• Option D. Blank Incorrect because the email will not be sent with a blank subject if one is defined in either the notification or the template. ServiceNow ensures a subject is always populated.

questions.question: What does the attachment functionality in a kb article do?
options: It will take you to a blank incident form
Read only data that is not editable on this form
It provides a choice of adding documents as attachments
Allow you to attach any other existing record in ServiceNow
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: C. It provides a choice of adding documents as attachments
The attachment functionality in a Knowledge Base (KB) article allows you to add documents, such as PDFs, Word documents, images, or other file types, to enrich the article’s content. These attachments can be helpful for providing additional information, examples, or visual aids to users.
Incorrect Options:
• A. It will take you to a blank incident form: This is not related to the attachment functionality of a KB article.
• B. Read only data that is not editable on this form: This is not accurate. Attachments can be added and removed from a KB article.
• D. Allow you to attach any other existing record in ServiceNow: While you can reference other records in a KB article, the attachment functionality is specifically for adding documents.

questions.question: What is the purpose of the import set table?
options: Used to import users data only
It acts as a staging area for records imported
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: B. It acts as a staging area for records imported
The Import Set table in ServiceNow serves as a temporary storage area for records that are being imported into the system. It acts as a staging area where the imported data is temporarily stored before being processed and inserted into the target tables.
This staging area allows administrators to review and validate the imported data before it’s committed to the ServiceNow database. It also provides flexibility for data transformation and mapping during the import process.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Used to import users data only: While Import Sets can be used to import user data, they are not limited to that. They can be used to import various types of data, such as incidents, change requests, or custom records.
• C. A new application in ServiceNow: Import Sets are not a standalone application. They are a core component of ServiceNow’s data import and integration capabilities.

questions.question: Which of the following is possible via an inbound action? choose two options
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Sends an email notification
• Inbound actions can be configured to send email notifications when specific conditions are met.
• This is a common use case, for example, notifying users when an inbound email triggers a record update.
Option D. Modifying existing records
• Inbound actions can also modify existing records in ServiceNow.
• For example, an inbound email can update an incident record or change its state.
• This is a core function of inbound actions.
Incorrect
Option A. Schedule a job
• Scheduling jobs is handled by Scheduled Jobs or Scheduled Script Executions, not inbound actions.
• Inbound actions respond to inbound email triggers, not job scheduling.
Option C. Change main banner
• Changing the main banner is a UI customization task, not something inbound actions can perform.
• Inbound actions are focused on email processing and record manipulation, not UI changes.

questions.question: How are users and groups related?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Many to Many
• Correct because in ServiceNow, users and groups have a many‑to‑many relationship.
• A single user can belong to multiple groups, and a single group can contain multiple users.
• This relationship is managed through the sys_user_grmember table, which maps users to groups.
• This design allows flexible role assignment and access control, ensuring scalability in large organizations.
Incorrect
Option B. One to One
• Incorrect because this would mean each user belongs to exactly one group, and each group has exactly one user.
• ServiceNow does not restrict users or groups in this way; it would be too limiting for real‑world scenarios.
Option C. One to Many
• Incorrect because this implies one user can belong to only one group, but a group can contain many users.
• In ServiceNow, users can belong to multiple groups, so this does not reflect the actual relationship.
Option D. All to All
• Incorrect because “All to All” is not a valid relationship type in ServiceNow or in database terminology.
• It is simply a distractor option with no technical meaning.

questions.question: What is a Service Now event?
options: Business rules, client scripts, fields, forms and form sections, reports, tables, views and workflows
Create a new table and fill out he extend table field
It is an indication to the ServiceNow processes that something notable has occurred, e.g., approving a request, workflow, etc.
Semaphores, which control the number of user transactions that can be run in parallel. It makes sure there aren't too many things running at once.
questions.explanation:
A ServiceNow event is an indication to the ServiceNow processes that something notable has occurred, e.g., approving a request, workflow, etc.
It acts as a trigger for various actions within the platform, such as executing business rules, client scripts, workflows, and other automated processes. Events can be generated by user actions, system processes, or external integrations.

questions.question: When can SLAs include actions be triggered on ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Anytime
• SLA actions can be configured to trigger at any point in the SLA lifecycle.
• Examples: when SLA starts, while in progress, at warning thresholds, on breach, or on completion.
• This flexibility allows administrators to design notifications, escalations, or task updates based on business needs.
Incorrect
Option A. Breached
• Too narrow. Actions are not limited to breach events. Breach is just one possible trigger.
Option B. Completed
• Partial truth. Actions can occur at completion, but not only then. Limiting to “Completed” misses other valid triggers.
Option C. In Progress
• Again, only one stage. SLAs can trigger actions during progress, but also at start, breach, or completion.

questions.question: What are the ways you can bring users into your ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: D. All the above
ServiceNow offers multiple methods to bring users into your instance:
• SSO (Single Sign-On): This method allows users to authenticate with a centralized identity provider and access ServiceNow without requiring a separate login.
• LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol): This protocol allows ServiceNow to synchronize user information from an external directory service, such as Active Directory.
• Manual Import: Users can be manually created and imported into ServiceNow using import sets or the user interface.

questions.question: What’s a module and application in the example … Incident > create new
options: Incident is an application and create new is the module
Incident is a module and create new is an application
Incident and create new both are applications
Incident and create new both are modules
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: A. Incident is an application and create new is a module
In ServiceNow, an application is a self-contained suite of modules that provides specific functionality. For example, the “Incident” application is a complete application that allows users to manage incidents, from creation to resolution.
Modules are the individual components within an application that provide specific features or functionalities. The “Create New” module is a specific module within the Incident application that allows users to create new incident records.
So, in the example “Incident > Create New,” “Incident” is the application, and “Create New” is the module within that application.

questions.question: Difference between Business Rule & Client Script?
options: Business rule works on before insert, update and delete in a database & client script works only on Submit.
Business rule works on before or after Insert, update and delete in a database & client script works on Submit, on change, on Cell Edit & on Load.
Business Rule works on Browser side and client scripts works on Server side.
There is no difference b/w the two.
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: B. Business rule works on before or after Insert, update and delete in a database & client script works on Submit, on change, on Cell Edit & on Load.
Business Rules operate on the server-side and are triggered by specific events like:
• Before Insert: Before a record is inserted into the database.
• After Insert: After a record is inserted into the database.
• Before Update: Before a record is updated in the database.
• After Update: After a record is updated in the database.
• Before Delete: Before a record is deleted from the database.
• After Delete: After a record is deleted from the database.
Client Scripts execute on the client-side (browser) and are triggered by events like:
• onSubmit: When a form is submitted.
• onChange: When a field value changes.
• onCellEdit: When a cell in a list view is edited.
• onLoad: When a form or list view loads.
Key Differences:
• Execution Environment: Business Rules run on the server, while Client Scripts run on the client.
• Timing: Business Rules can be triggered before or after database operations, while Client Scripts are triggered by user interactions.
• Performance: Business Rules can potentially impact performance more than Client Scripts, especially if they perform complex calculations or database operations.
It’s important to choose the right tool for the job based on the specific requirements of the task. For example, if you need to validate data before it’s saved to the database, a Business Rule is the appropriate choice. If you want to enhance the user experience by providing real-time feedback or dynamic UI elements, a Client Script is more suitable.

questions.question: Which of the following concepts are associated with the ServiceNow CMDB? (Choose four)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Service Processes
✅ CMDB powers ITSM processes (Incident, Problem, Change Management) by providing CI relationship data for impact analysis.
Option B. Tables and Fields
✅ CMDB built on hierarchical table structure (cmdb_ci, cmdb_ci_server, cmdb_ci_service) with CI class extensions.
Option C. A Database
✅ CMDB is a centralized database storing all Configuration Items (CIs), relationships, and attributes.
Option E. The Dependency View
✅ Visual mapping tool showing CI relationships, service dependencies, and impact analysis.
Incorrect
Option D. User Permissions
❌ Access control mechanism, not a CMDB concept. Managed via ACLs, not core CMDB functionality.

questions.question: Question: Access to tables and fields are governed by Access Control.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A: TRUE
• Correct.
• In ServiceNow, Access Control Rules (ACLs) govern access to tables, records, and fields.
• They determine whether a user can read, write, create, or delete data based on roles, conditions, and scripts.
• Without ACLs, users would have unrestricted access, so ACLs are essential for enforcing data security and compliance.
Incorrect
Option B: FALSE
• Incorrect.
• This statement is wrong because access is indeed governed by ACLs.
• If ACLs were not in place, ServiceNow would not be able to enforce role-based security at the table and field level.

questions.question: What Details does a knowledge article hold? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
A. Known errors
This option is correct. Knowledge articles can contain information about known errors, which helps users understand issues that have been identified and documented within the system. This aligns with the purpose of knowledge management to capture and share information about problems and their resolutions.
B. User Solutions
This option is correct. Knowledge articles often include solutions that users can apply to resolve issues they encounter. These solutions are typically derived from past incidents or queries and are documented for easy access by users seeking help
C. Troubleshooting tips
This option is correct. Knowledge articles frequently provide troubleshooting tips that guide users through resolving common issues or errors they may face. This information is valuable for self-service support and enhances user experience
D. User information
This option is incorrect. While knowledge articles may reference user roles or groups in terms of access control, they do not typically contain personal user information. The focus of knowledge articles is on general information and solutions rather than specific user data, which is protected under privacy policies
E. All of the above
This option is incorrect because it implies that all listed items are applicable, including “User information,” which is not typically part of a knowledge article’s content.

questions.question: What is an Access Control List (ACL)?
options: It's a bunch of access controls for a table
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. It’s a bunch of access controls for a table
• Correct because in ServiceNow, an Access Control List (ACL) is a collection of rules that define what data users can access within a table, record, or field.
• ACLs enforce contextual security by checking roles, conditions, and scripts before allowing access.
• They are not standalone objects like tables or update sets, but rather a set of access control entries applied to tables and fields.
Incorrect
Option A. Database Table
• Incorrect because a database table stores records and fields.
• ACLs are security rules applied to tables, not the tables themselves.
Option B. Update Set
• Incorrect because update sets are used to capture and move customizations between ServiceNow instances.
• They have nothing to do with access control security.
Option D. None of the above
• Incorrect because Option C correctly defines ACLs.
• Saying “None of the above” ignores the valid description provided.

questions.question: How do you change the sort sequence of fields or tasks?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Modify the order field
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the Order field determines the sequence in which fields, variables, or tasks are displayed.
• By editing the Order field value, administrators can explicitly control the sort order rather than relying on default alphabetical or type‑based arrangements.
• This is the standard CSA exam answer for controlling sort sequence.
Incorrect
Option A. Variable Set
• Incorrect because variable sets are used to group variables for reuse across catalog items.
• They do not control the sort order of fields or tasks.
Option B. Arrange in Alphabetical Order
• Incorrect because alphabetical arrangement is not a configurable option in ServiceNow.
• Sorting is explicitly controlled by the Order field, not by automatic alphabetical sorting.
Option C. Modify Field Types
• Incorrect because changing a field type (e.g., string, integer, choice) does not affect its display order.
• Field type impacts data handling, not sort sequence.

questions.question: What are the three basic elements of a workflow?
options: SLA definition, Task SLA, SLA workflow
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Approval, notification and task
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the three basic elements of a workflow are approvals, notifications, and tasks.
• These represent the core building blocks of automated processes:
• Approval: Ensures required authorization before proceeding.
• Notification: Keeps stakeholders informed of progress or required actions.
• Task: Defines work items that need to be completed as part of the process.
• Together, they form the foundation of ServiceNow workflows, aligning with CSA exam expectations.
Incorrect
Option A. SLA definition, Task SLA, SLA workflow
• Incorrect because these are components of Service Level Agreements (SLAs), not the basic elements of a workflow.
• SLAs measure performance but are not workflow building blocks.
Option C. Task, Table and Fields
• Incorrect because while tasks are part of workflows, tables and fields are database elements, not workflow components.
Option D. None of the above
• Incorrect because Option B correctly identifies the three basic workflow elements.

questions.question: End Users can personalize the list layouts for themselves.
questions.explanation:
TRUE
End users in ServiceNow have the ability to personalize list layouts to suit their individual preferences. They can customize the displayed columns, sort order, and other settings to improve their productivity and efficiency. This personalization feature empowers users to tailor their ServiceNow experience to their specific needs.

questions.question: Is it true that System upgrade schedule auto‑updates an existing MID server to the latest build on a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. FALSE
• Correct because MID Servers are not automatically updated when a ServiceNow instance undergoes a system upgrade.
• The system upgrade schedule applies only to the ServiceNow instance itself, not external components like MID Servers.
• Administrators must manually download and install the updated MID Server package to ensure compatibility with the upgraded instance.
• This is a key exam concept: MID Servers require manual maintenance.
Incorrect
Option B. TRUE
• Incorrect because this implies that MID Servers are automatically upgraded during a system upgrade schedule, which is not the case.
• Believing this could lead to compatibility issues if administrators fail to manually upgrade the MID Server after an instance upgrade.

questions.question: What related tables does the schema map show?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C: Class extension or reference
• Correct.
• The schema map in ServiceNow visually shows how tables are related through class extensions (inheritance) and references (relationships).
• Example: The Task table is extended by Incident, Problem, and Change tables. Reference fields (like assigned_to pointing to sys_user) are also displayed.
• This is the intended purpose of the schema map: to provide a clear view of table relationships.
Incorrect
Option A: Sys_user
• Incorrect.
• While the schema map may show a reference to sys_user if a table has a field pointing to it, the schema map does not specifically show “Sys_user” as a default related table.
• It shows relationships in general, not one fixed table.
Option B: Cmdb_ci_computers
• Incorrect.
• Similar to sys_user, the schema map does not specifically show cmdb_ci_computers unless a table has a defined relationship to it.
• The schema map is not limited to CMDB tables; it applies across the platform.
Option D: All of the above
• Incorrect.
• Not all listed tables (sys_user, cmdb_ci_computers) are always shown. The schema map shows relationships (extensions and references), not every table by default.

questions.question: Resetting the list layout globally will over ride personal preferences.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. TRUE Correct because when the list layout is reset globally, it applies to all users and overrides any personal preferences they may have set. This enforces a standardized view across the system, ensuring consistency but removing individual customizations.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE Incorrect because global resets do not preserve personal preferences. Once the global reset is applied, personal layouts are overridden, so this option does not reflect the actual behavior.

questions.question: Form Context Menu provides a graphical representation of other tables related to a specific table?
questions.explanation:
The statement is FALSE. While the Form Context Menu provides various actions and options related to the current form, it does not offer a graphical representation of related tables.
To visualize relationships between tables, you can use tools like the ServiceNow Application Navigator or custom-built visualizations.

questions.question: ESS users have access to only self service portal.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. TRUE
• Correct because ESS (Employee Self‑Service) users in ServiceNow are limited to the self‑service portal.
• They do not have access to administrative modules or advanced functionality.
• Their role is designed for basic interactions such as submitting requests, checking knowledge articles, and tracking incidents.
• This restriction ensures security and prevents unauthorized access to system configurations.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE
• Incorrect because ESS users are not granted access beyond the self‑service portal.
• They cannot access core modules like incident management, change management, or configuration management.
• Saying FALSE would imply they have broader access, which contradicts the CSA exam’s expected understanding of ESS role limitations.

questions.question: What is a CI (Configuration Item) in ServiceNow?
options: CI is a menu of any application in ServiceNow
CI is a table in serviceNow
CI is a tangible device or intangible dedicated software in CMDB
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. CI is a tangible device or intangible dedicated software in CMDB
Reasoning: In ServiceNow, a Configuration Item (CI) is any component that needs to be managed to deliver an IT service. This can include hardware (servers, laptops, routers), software (applications, services), or intangible items (licenses, documentation). All CIs are stored and tracked in the Configuration Management Database (CMDB), which helps organizations understand relationships and dependencies between IT assets and services.
Incorrect
Option A. CI is a menu of any application in ServiceNow
Reasoning: A CI is not a menu item. Menus are part of the UI navigation, while CIs are actual assets or components managed within the CMDB.
Option B. CI is a table in ServiceNow
Reasoning: While CIs are stored in tables (like cmdb_ci), a CI itself is not defined as a table. It is an instance (record) representing a specific asset or service component.
Option D. None of the above
Reasoning: This is incorrect because Option C correctly defines what a CI is.

questions.question: Example of Contextual Security
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: C. ACL
Contextual Security in ServiceNow refers to the ability to control access to records based on specific conditions or context. Access Control Lists (ACLs) are a key mechanism for implementing contextual security.
How ACLs Implement Contextual Security:
ACLs can be configured to restrict access to records based on various factors, such as:
• User Roles: Limiting access to specific roles or groups of users.
• Record Owner: Restricting access to the record owner or specific teams.
• Record State: Controlling access based on the record’s lifecycle stage (e.g., open, closed).
• Other Record Fields: Using specific field values to determine access permissions.
By leveraging ACLs, administrators can ensure that sensitive information is protected and that users only have access to the data they need to perform their job functions.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Data Policy: Data policies are used to enforce data privacy and security rules, but they don’t directly control access to specific records based on context.
• B. Business Rules: Business rules are used to automate business processes and enforce data integrity, but they are not primarily used for access control.

questions.question: When relating to Task SLA Time-Based Fields, The Breach time is the same as Planned end time.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. FALSE
• Correct because in ServiceNow, Breach time and Planned end time are distinct SLA time‑based fields.
• Breach time represents the exact point when the SLA will be violated if the task is not completed.
• Planned end time is calculated based on the SLA schedule and pause conditions, and may differ depending on business rules or SLA configuration.
• Therefore, they are not the same, making FALSE the correct answer.
Incorrect
Option A. TRUE
• Incorrect because it assumes Breach time and Planned end time are identical.
• While they may sometimes align under specific SLA configurations, they are conceptually different fields and should not be treated as the same in exam contexts.

questions.question: What is the significance of the Order field on Catalog Item variables?
options: It established the display order of variables - Listed in ascending order values
It displays the number to the left side of the variable
It provides the order in which data will be parsed
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. It established the display order of variables – Listed in ascending order values
• Correct because the Order field determines how variables are displayed on the catalog item form.
• Variables are shown in ascending numerical order based on the value in the Order field.
• This ensures a predictable and user-friendly layout when multiple variables exist.
Incorrect
Option B. It displays the number to the left side of the variable
• Incorrect because the Order field is not visually displayed to end users.
• It is a backend property used for sorting, not for showing numbers beside variables.
Option C. It provides the order in which data will be parsed
• Incorrect because parsing order is not controlled by the Order field.
• The field only affects display sequence, not how ServiceNow processes or parses variable data.

questions.question: What is a sys_id?
options: It is a unique 16 character globally unique id used to identify a record
It is a unique 24 character globally unique id used to identify a record
It is a unique 32 character globally unique id used to identify a record
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
C. It is a unique 32 character globally unique id used to identify a record:
• In ServiceNow, a sys_id is a unique 32-character globally unique identifier used to uniquely identify each record in the database. This sys_id ensures that every record can be distinctly recognized and referenced across the platform, allowing for consistent data management and operations.
Incorrect Options:
A. It is a unique 16 character globally unique id used to identify a record:
• Incorrect. The sys_id in ServiceNow is not 16 characters long. It is specifically a 32-character identifier.
B. It is a unique 24 character globally unique id used to identify a record:
• Incorrect. The sys_id in ServiceNow is not 24 characters long. It is defined as a 32-character globally unique identifier.

questions.question: Which is the correct role that allows you personalising a list view on a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
The role that allows you to personalize a list view on a ServiceNow instance is personalize_list.
This role grants users the ability to customize list views by adding, removing, and reordering columns, as well as adjusting the layout and filters.

questions.question: What is retroactive start in SLA?
options: A: It is used for attaching SLA from a particularly created date & time without attaching SLA on the opened time.
This is used for calculating duration of SLA.
Through this field we can stop SLA on any condition.
This field is not there on SLA Definition page.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A: It is used for attaching SLA from a particularly created date & time without attaching SLA on the opened time.
• Correct because retroactive start allows an SLA to begin at a specific condition or timestamp rather than the record’s creation time.
• This is useful when the SLA should reflect a business rule or milestone (e.g., approval date) instead of the initial record open time.
Incorrect
Option B: This is used for calculating duration of SLA.
• Incorrect because SLA duration is calculated based on start and stop conditions, not by retroactive start.
• Retroactive start only changes the point in time when the SLA is considered to have begun.
Option C: Through this field we can stop SLA on any condition.
• Incorrect because stopping an SLA is controlled by stop conditions, not retroactive start.
• Retroactive start does not terminate SLAs; it only adjusts their starting point.
Option D: This field is not there on SLA Definition page.
• Incorrect because retroactive start is available on the SLA Definition page as a configuration option.
• It is a recognized field used to fine-tune SLA behavior.

questions.question: Which is not Related to UI Action?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Search
• In ServiceNow, UI Actions are elements like buttons, links, and context menu items that trigger scripts or actions.
• Examples include Form Buttons, Form Links, and List Links.
• Search is not a UI Action; it is a separate functionality used to query records in the system.
• Therefore, “Search” is the correct answer as it is not related to UI Actions.
Incorrect
Option A. List Link
• A List Link is a valid UI Action that appears on list views and can trigger scripts or actions.
Option B. Form Link
• A Form Link is also a UI Action that appears on forms and can execute logic when clicked.
Option D. Form Button
• A Form Button is a common UI Action that appears on forms and allows users to perform specific actions.

questions.question: Can you change the number prefix from “INC” to “IN” for the incident table?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. System definition – Number maintenance table (sys_number)
• Correct because the Number Maintenance module (stored in the sys_number table) is where administrators configure prefixes, number lengths, and next available numbers for records in ServiceNow.
• For the Incident table, you can change the prefix from INC to IN by editing the entry in Number Maintenance.
• This ensures that new incident records will be generated with the updated prefix (e.g., IN0001234).
Incorrect
Option A. System definition – Data dictionary
• Incorrect because the Data Dictionary defines field properties and table schema, not record numbering.
• Changing prefixes cannot be done here.
Option B. System definition – Auto number
• Incorrect because there is no module named “Auto number” in ServiceNow. This is a distractor option.
Option D. No. It is not possible
• Incorrect because it is possible to change the prefix using Number Maintenance. ServiceNow allows customization of record numbering formats.

questions.question: SSO abbreviation is
questions.explanation:
SSO stands for Single Sign On. In ServiceNow, and many other software applications, SSO allows a user to log in once and access multiple applications or systems with those same credentials.
This improves user experience and security by reducing the need to remember and enter multiple passwords.

questions.question: What is an order guide?
options: It defines every table and field in the system. It contains information about a field's data type, character limit, default value, dependency and other attributes
It allows user to order everything they need for one particular request
It's a bunch of access controls for a table, i.e., show me all access controls for table
questions.explanation:
An order guide in ServiceNow is:
• It allows users to order everything they need for one particular request (Correct)
Here’s why the other options aren’t what an order guide does:
• Defines every table and field: This describes the Field Dictionary, which provides information about data structure within ServiceNow.
• Bunch of access controls for a table: This describes Access Controls, which manage user permissions for specific tables and fields.
• None of the above: While the other options are functionalities within ServiceNow, option B accurately describes the purpose of an order guide.
An order guide essentially acts as a bundle or a pre-configured set of catalog items that a user can request together in a single transaction.
This streamlines the process for users who need multiple related items, improving efficiency. For example, a “New Hire” order guide might include catalog items for setting up a user account, provisioning a laptop, and assigning access to specific applications.

questions.question: Where does the global text search appear?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Banner
• Correct because the global text search in ServiceNow appears in the banner frame at the top of the interface.
• This allows users to search across the entire instance (records, knowledge, catalog items, etc.) from a single location.
• It is a key navigation feature designed for quick access to information across applications.
Incorrect
Option B. Left Navigation Pane
• Incorrect because the Left Navigation Pane contains the Application Navigator, which is used to search for modules and applications.
• While you can search for apps/modules here, this is not the global text search.
Option C. Content Area
• Incorrect because the Content Area displays forms, lists, and dashboards.
• It does not host the global text search bar.

questions.question: You can limit Service Now access by IP ranges.
questions.explanation:
The statement is TRUE (Correct). ServiceNow allows you to limit access based on IP ranges.
Here’s how IP range-based access control works in ServiceNow:
• Configuration: You can define allowed IP ranges within the System Security > IP Address Access Control section.
• Functionality: Users attempting to access ServiceNow from IP addresses outside the allowed ranges will be denied access. This can be a useful security measure to restrict access to your ServiceNow instance from unauthorized locations.
It’s important to note that IP range-based access control might not be suitable for all scenarios. For example, it wouldn’t be ideal for users who need to access ServiceNow remotely from various locations.
Here are some additional points to consider:
• Alternative Security Measures: ServiceNow offers other security features like multi-factor authentication (MFA) that can be combined with IP range restrictions for a more robust security posture.
• Dynamic IP Addresses: Some users might have dynamic IP addresses that change frequently. IP range-based control might not be feasible in such cases.
Overall, IP range-based access control is a valuable tool for enhancing ServiceNow security, but it should be implemented strategically considering your specific requirements and user base.

questions.question: Enhanced notification preferences enable you to easily change your preferences and choose which notifications you prefer, where and when you want to be notified. What options are available for users when setting their notification preferences in Next Experience? (Select 3)
options: Set global notification preferences for all active users in the system.
Enable or disable a particular channel for receiving notifications.
Create, edit, or delete notification channels for instant messages, email, SMS, and voice.
Create, edit, or delete system notifications for a particular channel.
Create custom notifications by subscribing to system notifications and applying desired conditions.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B: Enable or disable a particular channel for receiving notifications
• Correct.
• Users can choose whether to receive notifications via specific channels such as email, SMS, push, or in-app.
• This gives flexibility to control how they are notified.
Option C: Create, edit, or delete notification channels for instant messages, email, SMS, and voice
• Correct.
• Users can manage their notification channels directly, adding or removing them as needed.
• This ensures they only use the channels they prefer.
Option E: Create custom notifications by subscribing to system notifications and applying desired conditions
• Correct.
• Users can subscribe to system notifications and configure conditions (e.g., only notify for high-priority incidents).
• This allows personalization and relevance of notifications.
Incorrect
Option A: Set global notification preferences for all active users in the system
• Incorrect.
• Users cannot set global preferences for everyone; they can only manage their own notification settings.
• Global settings are controlled by administrators.
Option D: Create, edit, or delete system notifications for a particular channel
• Incorrect.
• System notifications are predefined and managed by administrators.
• End users cannot create or delete system-level notifications; they can only subscribe or adjust preferences.

questions.question: Scenario: Question: What provides a guide for moving data from import sets?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B: Transform Maps
• Correct.
• Transform Maps in ServiceNow define the relationship between fields in an import set table and fields in a target table.
• They provide the guide for how imported data is moved, transformed, and stored into the correct ServiceNow tables.
• Example: Mapping “Caller” in the import set to “Opened by” in the Incident table.
Incorrect
Option A: Data Source
• Incorrect.
• A Data Source defines where the data is coming from (CSV, JDBC, Excel, etc.), not how it is moved into target tables.
• It is about input, not transformation.
Option C: Coalesce Fields
• Incorrect.
• Coalesce fields are part of a transform map configuration. They help determine whether to update an existing record or insert a new one.
• They are not the overall “guide” for moving data; they are just a rule within the transform map.
Option D: Business Rules
• Incorrect.
• Business Rules are server-side scripts that run when records are inserted, updated, or deleted.
• They can automate actions but do not guide the movement of data from import sets.

questions.question: Update sets cannot be merged.
questions.explanation:
The statement is FALSE (Correct). Update sets in ServiceNow can be merged.
Here’s how merging update sets works:
• You can combine multiple update sets into a single new update set.
• During the merge process, ServiceNow prioritizes the latest changes from each source update set. This helps avoid conflicts and ensures the merged update set reflects the most recent customizations.
• Merging update sets can be beneficial for consolidating changes from different development branches or environments before deploying them to a target environment.
Here are some additional points to consider:
• Merge Conflicts: In some cases, merging update sets might encounter conflicts, especially if the same fields or configurations were modified differently in the source update sets. You’ll need to resolve these conflicts manually before proceeding with the merge.
• Alternative Approach: Instead of merging, you can also choose to “rollback” update sets. This essentially removes the changes introduced by an update set from your instance.
Overall, merging update sets is a valuable technique for managing configuration changes and streamlining deployments within ServiceNow.

questions.question: Incident, Problem tables inherit which table
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Task Table
Explanation:
In ServiceNow, the task table is a foundational table from which many other tables inherit properties and behaviors. This inheritance structure helps to maintain consistency and efficiency in managing various types of work items.
Both the incident and problem tables extend from the task table. This means they inherit common fields like assigned_to, state, due_date, and other properties, providing a unified framework for tracking and managing incidents and problems.

questions.question: To access knowledge articles without login, the knowledge article must be?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. Set to public This is correct because knowledge articles must be explicitly marked as public in ServiceNow to be accessible without requiring a user login. Public articles are intended for external audiences and bypass authentication.
Incorrect
• Option B. Set to review Incorrect because “review” is a workflow state used for internal validation before publishing. Articles in review are not accessible externally.
• Option C. Set to private Incorrect because private articles are restricted to authenticated users with specific roles or permissions. They cannot be accessed without login.
• Option D. Set to retire Incorrect because retired articles are archived and no longer available for use. They cannot be accessed by any user, logged in or not.

questions.question: What can you do with a service catalog item once it’s built?
options: Publish it in the service catalog
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D) All of the above
This is correct because once a service catalog item is built in ServiceNow, you can:
• Publish it in the service catalog so users can request it.
• Group it in an order guide to bundle related items together for easier requests.
• Show users questions and choices to capture input and customize the request.
All of these actions are valid and supported, so the correct answer is “All of the above.”
Incorrect
Option A) Publish it in the service catalog Incorrect because while this is true, it is only one of the possible actions. The question asks what can be done overall, so this option alone is incomplete.
Option B) Group in an order guide Incorrect because this is also true, but it represents only one of the available actions. It does not cover the full scope of what can be done.
Option C) Show users questions and choices Incorrect because this is valid functionality, but again, it is only part of the complete set of actions.

questions.question: What are variables in regards with Service Catalog?
options: They define the items in service catalog
They define the questions to ask to end user while ordering catalog items
They define the rules of order guide
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. They define the questions to ask to end user while ordering catalog items
In ServiceNow’s Service Catalog, variables are used to capture specific information from the user when they order a service. They act as placeholders for data that needs to be collected to fulfill the request. This information can be used to customize the service delivery, generate reports, or trigger automated workflows.
Incorrect Options:
• A. They define the items in service catalog: Catalog items themselves are defined separately from variables. Variables are used to gather additional information about the item being requested.
• C. They define the rules of order guide: Order guides define the flow and logic of the ordering process, but they don’t directly define the variables themselves.
• D. None of the above: Option B accurately describes the purpose of variables in Service Catalog.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a field?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B: Split
• Correct because:
• In ServiceNow, Split is not a standard field type.
• Common field types include Duration, Script, and Suggestion, but “Split” is not recognized as a field in the platform.
• Therefore, this option correctly identifies something that is not a field.
Incorrect
Option A: Duration
• Incorrect because Duration is a valid field type in ServiceNow, often used to calculate elapsed time between two date/time values.
Option C: Script
• Incorrect because Script fields exist in ServiceNow, typically used for scripting logic in business rules or client scripts.
Option D: Suggestion
• Incorrect because Suggestion is a valid field type used in ServiceNow for providing recommended values or auto-complete functionality.

questions.question: What do requesters see when they go to the service catalog?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Self-service items
When requesters access the Service Catalog, they typically see a list of self-service items or catalog items. These are the services, products, or requests that they can submit.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Homepage: While the Service Catalog might be accessible from the homepage, the primary content for requesters is the self-service items.
• B. Record: This is a general term for any record in ServiceNow. It doesn’t specifically relate to the Service Catalog.
• D. News: News articles are typically related to announcements and updates, not the services offered through the Service Catalog.

questions.question: Where do you change the banner of the application?
options: System Properties and in CSS Properties
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. System Properties and in CSS Properties
To change the banner of your ServiceNow application, you’ll need to modify the CSS styles and potentially some system properties.
Here’s a general approach:
CSS Customization:
• Create a custom CSS file or modify an existing one.
• Target the specific CSS selectors for the banner elements you want to change (e.g., background color, font, logo).
• Apply the desired CSS styles to these elements.
• Deploy the CSS file to your ServiceNow instance.
System Properties:
• In some cases, you might need to adjust system properties to control certain aspects of the banner, such as the logo URL or branding.
Note: The exact steps and CSS properties may vary depending on your specific ServiceNow version and theme. It’s recommended to consult the ServiceNow documentation or seek assistance from a ServiceNow expert for tailored guidance.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Order it from Service Catalog: Service Catalog is used to order services, not customize the application’s appearance.
• B. cmn_location: While cmn_location is a system property, it’s not directly related to the banner customization.
• C. Application Navigator: The Application Navigator is used to navigate between different applications and modules within ServiceNow. It doesn’t control the banner’s appearance.

questions.question: If the Default update set is marked complete:
options: The changes are tracked in the user's current update set.
The system creates another update set named Default1 and uses it as the default update set.
The default update set cannot be marked completed.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. The system creates another update set named Default1 and uses it as the default update set.
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the Default update set is always required to capture changes.
• When the current Default update set is marked complete, the system automatically creates a new update set (e.g., Default1) and designates it as the new default.
• This ensures that configuration changes continue to be tracked without interruption.
Incorrect
Option A. The changes are tracked in the user’s current update set.
• Incorrect because once the Default update set is marked complete, it cannot continue tracking changes.
• A new Default update set is created instead.
Option C. The instance fails.
• Incorrect because marking the Default update set complete does not cause the instance to fail.
• ServiceNow handles this gracefully by creating a new Default update set.
Option D. The default update set cannot be marked completed.
• Incorrect because the Default update set can be marked complete.
• The system simply creates a new one automatically to replace it.

questions.question: Regarding update sets, Customer updates/payload is stored in _ table?
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. sys_update_xml
In ServiceNow, the sys_update_xml table stores the XML payload of customer updates. This table contains the changes made to ServiceNow configurations, such as table definitions, script includes, and workflows. When a customer update is applied, the XML data in this table is processed to update the ServiceNow instance.
Incorrect Options:
• A. update_set: The update_set table tracks the overall state of an update set, including its version, scope, and deployment status.
• C. sys_customer_update: This table doesn’t exist in ServiceNow.

questions.question: ACL is part of which security?
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Contextual Security
An Access Control List (ACL) is a type of contextual security in ServiceNow. It provides granular control over access to specific records or fields within a table, based on the user’s role, group membership, or other criteria. This allows you to define specific access permissions for different users, ensuring that sensitive information is protected and only accessible to authorized individuals.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Physical Security: Physical security refers to measures taken to protect physical assets, such as hardware and data centers.
• B. General Security: General security is a broad term that encompasses various security measures, but it doesn’t specifically refer to the fine-grained access control provided by ACLs.
• C. Compliance Security: Compliance security focuses on meeting specific regulatory requirements and industry standards. While ACLs can help enforce compliance, they are not exclusively related to compliance.

questions.question: _ can be used to join two tables.
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
B. Database Views:
• Database Views in ServiceNow are used to join two or more tables. They provide a way to define and display data from multiple tables as if it were in a single table, which can be very useful for reporting and data analysis.
Incorrect Options:
A. Link Tables:
• Incorrect. While “Link Tables” sounds like a method to connect tables, it is not a recognized term or feature in ServiceNow for joining tables.
C. Views:
• Incorrect. While “Views” might sound similar to “Database Views,” the specific term and functionality in ServiceNow for joining tables is “Database Views.” Regular views in ServiceNow typically refer to how data is presented in the UI, not the underlying table joins.

questions.question: Which of the following gets automatically captured in an update set?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Tables, forms, views
Update sets in ServiceNow are designed to capture configuration changes, not data. They primarily capture changes to the structure and behavior of the ServiceNow instance, including:
• Tables: Changes to table definitions, fields, and relationships.
• Forms: Modifications to form layouts, field placements, and UI policies.
• Views: Changes to list views and related configurations.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Table, forms, data: While tables and forms are captured, data itself is not captured in update sets.
• B. Table, schedules, forms: Schedules are not typically captured in update sets.
• D. Tables, lists, data: Data is not captured in update sets.

questions.question: Which of the following modules are available to ITIL users by default?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. Incident, Problem, Change, Service Catalog
• Correct because ITIL users in ServiceNow are granted access to the core ITSM modules by default. These include:
• Incident Management (to log and resolve issues)
• Problem Management (to identify root causes)
• Change Management (to manage changes in a controlled manner)
• Service Catalog (to request services and items)
• This aligns with ITIL best practices and ensures ITIL users can perform standard IT service management tasks.
Incorrect
• Option A. Incident, Problem, Change
• Incorrect because while these modules are available, Service Catalog is also included by default. Leaving it out makes this option incomplete.
• Option B. Self‑Service, Knowledge, Change
• Incorrect because ITIL users are not limited to self‑service and knowledge modules. They require access to Incident and Problem Management, which are missing here.
• Option C. Time Cards, Reports, Knowledge
• Incorrect because these are not the default ITIL modules. Time Cards and Reports are separate functionalities, not part of the ITIL role’s default access.

questions.question: How do you get to the categories on an incident and other table?
options: Go to system definition > choice list
Go to social it > feed administration > messages
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Go to System Definition > Choice List
• Correct because categories in ServiceNow (such as those on the Incident table) are stored as choice list values for specific fields.
• Administrators can navigate to System Definition > Choice List to view and manage these values.
• This is the proper way to access and configure categories across tables like Incident, Problem, and Change.
Incorrect
Option B. In the Task SLA form
• Incorrect because the Task SLA form is used to define and manage Service Level Agreements for tasks.
• It does not provide access to incident categories or other table categories.
Option C. Base Class
• Incorrect because the Base Class refers to the underlying table structure (like task), not the categories themselves.
• Categories are field values, not part of the base class definition.
Option D. Social IT > Feed Administration > Messages
• Incorrect because this module is related to social feeds and collaboration, not incident categories.
• It manages messages and feeds, not choice list values for categories.

questions.question: A new group has been created to access service catalog requests however the group members are not able to access it. What is the BEST practice that should be followed to make sure the group members are able to access the requests?
options: Assign catalog role to the group and then add users to the group
Assign catalog role to individual users and then add them to the group
Assign catalog role to individual users
Assign catalog role to individual users and to the group
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Assign catalog role to the group and then add users to the group
Assigning the catalog role to the group and then adding users to the group is the most efficient and secure approach. This ensures that all members of the group have the necessary permissions to access and utilize the Service Catalog.
Incorrect Options:
• B. Assign catalog role to individual users and then add them to the group: This approach is less efficient, especially if there are many users in the group. It requires manually assigning the role to each individual user.
• C. Assign catalog role to individual users: This approach is even less efficient and can be tedious, especially for large groups. It also doesn’t provide a centralized way to manage permissions for the group.
• D. Assign catalog role to individual users and to the group: This is redundant and unnecessary. Assigning the role to the group is sufficient to grant access to all group members.

questions.question: What is a piece of JavaScript configured to run when a record is displayed, inserted, updated, deleted, or when a table is queried?
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Business Rule
A Business Rule is a piece of JavaScript code that executes server-side when specific events occur, such as:
• Record operations: Insert, update, or delete
• Table queries: When records are queried from a table
Business Rules can be used to automate tasks, validate data, and modify records based on predefined conditions. They are a powerful tool for customizing ServiceNow’s behavior and enforcing business logic.
Incorrect Options:
• B. UI Policy: UI Policies are used to dynamically modify the user interface of a form based on specific conditions. They do not execute on record operations or table queries.
• C. Notifications: Notifications are used to send alerts and messages to users. They are not directly related to executing JavaScript code.
• D. Access Controls Lists: ACLs are used to control access to records and fields. They do not involve executing JavaScript code.

questions.question: UI Policy runs on
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
A. Client Side:
• Client Side: UI Policies in ServiceNow are designed to run on the client side. They are used to dynamically change form fields based on certain conditions without the need to reload the page or interact with the server. UI Policies can show/hide fields, make fields read-only, or require fields based on the user interactions on the form.
Incorrect Options:
B. Server Side:
• Incorrect. UI Policies do not run on the server side. Server-side logic is handled by Business Rules, Script Includes, and other server-side scripts.
C. Server and Client Side:
• Incorrect. UI Policies specifically operate on the client side to provide immediate feedback and changes to the form without server interaction. They do not run on both the server and client side.

questions.question: What is SLM
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Service Level Management
SLM stands for Service Level Management. It’s a set of processes and tools used to ensure that IT services are delivered to agreed-upon service levels. This involves defining, measuring, monitoring, and managing service levels, such as response times, availability, and performance.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Service Line Management: While related to service delivery, SLM is specifically focused on managing service levels.
• B. Server Limit Management: This term is not commonly used in IT service management.
• D. None: SLM is a well-established concept in IT service management.

questions.question: In Knowledge Base, articles are grouped by
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. Categories
In ServiceNow’s Knowledge Base, articles are typically organized into categories. This hierarchical structure helps users easily find relevant information by browsing through different categories. Each category can contain multiple articles, and articles can be assigned to multiple categories as needed.
Incorrect Options:
