• A. Contents: While “contents” might refer to the actual text of an article, it’s not the primary way to group articles.
• C. Catalogs: Catalogs are related to the Service Catalog, which is a different feature for offering services to users.
• D. None: Categories are a fundamental way to organize Knowledge Base articles in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Each record in a table corresponds to:
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Row
In a ServiceNow table, each record represents a row of data. A row contains specific values for each field in the table. For example, in an Incident table, a single row might represent a specific incident with information about its number, priority, assigned to, and other relevant details.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Column: Columns define the structure of the table, but they don’t represent individual records.
• B. Fields: Fields are the individual data elements within a record.
• C. List: A list is a view of multiple records from a table.

questions.question: The base table of “Change” table is:
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. Task Table
In ServiceNow, the task table is a foundational table from which many other tables inherit properties and behaviors. The change_request table is one such table that extends from the task table. This inheritance structure provides a consistent framework for managing various types of work items, including changes.
By inheriting from the task table, the change_request table gains common fields and functionalities, such as assigned_to, state, due_date, and more. This simplifies the management of change requests and ensures consistency across different types of records.

questions.question: A Schema Map displays which of the following? (Select three)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Extended Tables Why correct: A Schema Map shows the hierarchy of tables that extend from a parent table. For example, the Task table has extended tables like Incident, Problem, and Change Request.
Option D. Extending Tables Why correct: The Schema Map also shows which tables extend a given table, helping administrators understand inheritance and relationships.
Option F. Reference Table Why correct: Schema Maps display reference tables, which are tables linked through reference fields. This helps visualize dependencies and relationships across the data model.
Incorrect
Option A. Incidents Why incorrect: While the Incident table is an example of a table that extends Task, the Schema Map does not specifically display “Incidents” as a standalone feature. It shows tables in general, not individual records or modules.
Option C. Task Table Why incorrect: The Task table itself is a parent table, but the Schema Map is not limited to showing only the Task table. It shows all extended and extending tables in relation to the selected table.
Option E. Workflows Why incorrect: Workflows are process automation tools and are not part of the Schema Map. Schema Maps focus on table relationships, not workflow logic.

questions.question: Where can we create SLAs, OLAs and Underpinning Contracts?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Service Level Management
Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Operational Level Agreements (OLAs), and Underpinning Contracts are all related to Service Level Management in ServiceNow. This module provides the tools and processes to define, measure, and manage service levels. You can create and configure SLAs, OLAs, and Underpinning Contracts within the Service Level Management module.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Incident: Incident management is a separate module focused on tracking and resolving incidents.
• B. Service Catalog: The Service Catalog is used to offer services to users. While it may reference SLAs, it’s not the primary location for creating and managing them.
• D. Configuration Management: Configuration Management is focused on managing IT assets and their configurations. It’s not directly related to SLAs, OLAs, and Underpinning Contracts.

questions.question: How can we avoid creating duplicates while importing data
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
C. Coalesce Field:
• Coalesce Fields are used during data imports to avoid creating duplicates in ServiceNow. When you configure a field as a coalesce field, the import set will use this field to determine whether a record already exists. If a match is found, the existing record will be updated; otherwise, a new record will be created. This ensures that data is not duplicated in the system.
Incorrect Options:
A. sys_id:
• Incorrect. The sys_id is a unique identifier for each record in ServiceNow, but it is not used to avoid duplicates during data import. sys_id is used internally by the system to track records.
B. Transform Script:
• Incorrect. Transform Scripts are used to manipulate data during the transformation process, but they are not specifically designed to prevent duplicates. They can be used for data validation and transformation logic.
D. Transform Field:
• Incorrect. Transform Fields map the data from the import set to the target table fields but do not inherently prevent duplicates. Coalesce fields are specifically used for this purpose during the import process.

questions.question: Which among the following is correct regarding access control list (ACL)?
options: Rule which have more roles will get the precedence
The row level and field level rule both should be active before required operation should takes place
For more than one rule, older one runs first
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. The row level and field level rule both should be active before required operation should take place
• Correct because ACL evaluation in ServiceNow requires that both the row-level (table/record) rule and the field-level rule must evaluate to true for access to be granted.
• If either fails, the operation (read, write, create, delete) is denied.
• This is the fundamental principle of ACL enforcement in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option A. Rule which have more roles will get the precedence
• Incorrect because ACL precedence is not determined by the number of roles.
• Precedence is based on specificity (field > table > record) and order of evaluation, not role count.
Option C. For more than one rule, older one runs first
• Incorrect because ACLs are not evaluated based on age or creation date.
• They are evaluated by specificity and type of access (record-level first, then field-level).

questions.question: Users cannot read, write, create, or delete data unless access controls are in place to explicitly allow those actions.
questions.explanation:
TRUE
In ServiceNow, users cannot perform any actions on data unless they have been granted explicit permissions through access controls. This principle ensures data security and integrity. Access controls are implemented using roles, ACLs (Access Control Lists), and other security mechanisms to regulate user access to specific records and fields.

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of custom table?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: D. u_incident
In ServiceNow, custom tables are created to store specific data that is not natively supported by standard tables. They are often prefixed with “u_” to differentiate them from standard tables.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Project: This is a standard table in ServiceNow used for project management.
• B. Custom: This is not a specific table name. “Custom” refers to the category of tables that are created by administrators.
• C. sys_scripts: This is a system table used to store scripts and other system-level configurations. It’s not a custom table.

questions.question: Which application menu is used in capturing and moving changes from one instance to other?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: A. Update Set
Update Sets are the primary mechanism for capturing and moving changes between ServiceNow instances. They allow you to package changes, such as configurations, scripts, and records, and deploy them to other instances.
Incorrect Options:
• B. Import Set: Import Sets are used to import data from external sources into ServiceNow. They are not used for moving changes between instances.
• C. Change: The Change application is used to manage changes to the IT infrastructure. It’s not directly related to moving changes between instances.
• D. None: This is incorrect, as Update Sets are specifically designed for this purpose.

questions.question: What does the banner frame contain?
options: It is one set of table fields
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: A. Logo and global navigation control
The banner frame in ServiceNow is the topmost section of the user interface. It typically contains:
• Logo: The company or organization’s logo.
• Global Navigation: A navigation bar that provides access to different applications and modules within ServiceNow.
This frame provides a consistent user experience across different parts of the platform.
Incorrect Options:
• B. Task [task] and configuration item: These are specific types of records in ServiceNow, not elements of the banner frame.
• C. Self-service items: Self-service items are typically displayed in portals or service catalogs, not in the banner frame.
• D. It is one set of table fields: The banner frame is a visual component of the user interface and doesn’t directly relate to specific table fields.

questions.question: All workflows absolutely must have a beginning and an end.
questions.explanation:
TRUE
In ServiceNow, all workflows must have a defined start and end point. This ensures that workflows execute as intended and don’t run indefinitely. The starting point is typically triggered by an event, such as a record creation or update, while the end point can be reached through various conditions, such as task completion or timeouts.

questions.question: Where can you find the response time indicator?
options: Any form that has the know icon: Ess self-service; itil users can get it through self-service and service desk; admins and knowledge managers have additional ability with other modules
In the right hand corner of forms and lists
It's the filter views (i.e., when you run a report); the more you add the longer it gets
What is being secured (row or table) and the rights to it
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. In the right‑hand corner of forms and lists
• Correct because the response time indicator in ServiceNow is displayed in the top‑right corner of forms and lists.
• It shows how long the system took to respond to the user’s request, helping administrators and developers monitor performance.
• This is the official location where the indicator is visible in the ServiceNow UI.
Incorrect
Option A. Any form that has the knowledge icon: ESS self‑service; ITIL users can get it through self‑service and service desk; admins and knowledge managers have additional ability with other modules
• Incorrect because this description refers to knowledge management access and roles, not the response time indicator.
• The indicator is not tied to knowledge icons or role‑based access.
Option C. It’s the filter views (i.e., when you run a report); the more you add the longer it gets
• Incorrect because filter views and reports affect query performance but do not display the response time indicator.
• The indicator is specifically tied to forms and lists, not reports.
Option D. What is being secured (row or table) and the rights to it
• Incorrect because this refers to Access Control Lists (ACLs) and security rights.
• ACLs determine data access, not response time visibility.

questions.question: What provides a guide for moving data from import sets?
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Transform Maps
Transform Maps are the primary tool for guiding the movement of data from import sets into ServiceNow tables. They define how incoming data should be transformed, cleaned, and mapped to specific fields in the target table.
Incorrect Options:
• B. Coalesce Fields: Coalesce fields are used to merge multiple fields into a single field during the import process. They don’t provide a comprehensive guide for the entire data transformation process.
• C. Data Source: The data source is the external system or file from which the data is being imported. It doesn’t provide instructions for transforming the data.
• D. Business Rules: Business Rules are used to automate actions based on specific conditions. While they can be used to manipulate data after it’s imported, they are not directly involved in the import process itself.

questions.question: Which of the following are captured in update set: (Select all that Apply)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Field Creation
• Correct because when you create new fields (customizations to tables), these are configuration changes.
• Update sets capture configuration changes so they can be moved between instances.
Option D. Table Creation
• Correct because creating new tables is also a configuration change.
• Update sets capture table schema changes, ensuring they can be migrated to other ServiceNow instances.
Incorrect
Option A. Group Creation
• Incorrect because creating groups is data, not configuration.
• Update sets do not capture data records like groups, users, or roles.
Option B. Incident Creation
• Incorrect because incidents are transactional data, not configuration.
• Update sets are designed to move configuration changes, not business records.

questions.question: Only _ update sets can be exported
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Completed
Only Completed update sets can be exported in ServiceNow. This is because a completed update set represents a stable and finalized set of changes that are ready to be deployed to another instance. By exporting a completed update set, you can share the changes with other teams or instances.
Incorrect Options:
• A. In Progress: An in-progress update set is still being modified and may not be stable enough for export.
• B. Full: The “Full” option is not relevant to exporting update sets.
• C. Ignore: The “Ignore” option is used to exclude specific changes from an update set during deployment. It’s not related to exporting update sets.

questions.question: Basic Knowledge publishing workflow stages are?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option C. Draft > Review > Published > Retire
• Correct because the Basic Knowledge publishing workflow in ServiceNow follows these stages.
• Articles begin in Draft, move to Review for approval, then become Published for end-user visibility, and finally can be Retired when outdated or no longer relevant.
• This is the standard lifecycle for knowledge articles in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
• Option A. Start > Process > End
• Incorrect because this is a generic workflow description, not specific to ServiceNow Knowledge publishing.
• Option B. Created > Reviewed > Deployed
• Incorrect because while it resembles a workflow, ServiceNow Knowledge articles do not use “Deployed” as a stage. The correct terminology is Published and Retire.
• Option D. None
• Incorrect because ServiceNow does indeed have a defined publishing workflow for Knowledge articles.

questions.question: Which among the following tables cannot be deleted?
options: Semaphores control the number of user transactions that can be run in parallel. It makes sure there aren't too many things running at once
Approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers, utilities
To automate a sequence of activities
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D: Base tables, e.g., task, cmdb_ci
• Correct because:
• In ServiceNow, base tables are foundational system tables that other tables extend from.
• Examples include task (used by incident, problem, change, etc.) and cmdb_ci (used by configuration items).
• These tables are critical to the platform’s functionality and cannot be deleted.
• Deleting them would break core functionality across the system.
Incorrect
Option A: Semaphores control the number of user transactions that can be run in parallel. It makes sure there aren’t too many things running at once.
• Incorrect because:
• This describes semaphores, which are not related to ServiceNow tables.
• It is a concept in concurrency control, not a ServiceNow table restriction.
Option B: Approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers, utilities
• Incorrect because:
• These are functional components or application features in ServiceNow.
• While they may rely on tables, they are not inherently undeletable tables.
• The exam specifically asks about tables that cannot be deleted, which refers to base tables, not functional modules.
Option C: To automate a sequence of activities
• Incorrect because:
• This describes workflows or flow designer automation, not tables.
• Workflows use tables but are not themselves undeletable tables.

questions.question: Select Correct statements: (Select all that Apply)
options: Metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of ITSM process
Metric can gather data as the data is updated
Metric measures data over time to show past history
Metric definition provides a declarative way of defining metrics and once defined, the data for the metric is gathered and occurences of the metric are calculated and stored
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A: Metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of ITSM process
• Correct.
• Metrics in ServiceNow are designed to track and evaluate ITSM processes (e.g., incident resolution time, SLA compliance).
• They provide quantitative insight into process performance.
Option B: Metric can gather data as the data is updated
• Correct.
• Metrics dynamically collect data when records are created or updated.
• This allows real-time tracking of process performance.
Option C: Metric measures data over time to show past history
• Correct.
• Metrics are historical in nature; they capture values over time to show trends and past performance.
• This helps in analyzing whether processes are improving or degrading.
Option D: Metric definition provides a declarative way of defining metrics and once defined, the data for the metric is gathered and occurrences of the metric are calculated and stored
• Correct.
• ServiceNow allows administrators to define metrics declaratively.
• Once defined, the platform automatically gathers data and stores metric occurrences for reporting and analysis.

questions.question: What is the sequence of conditions in an SLA definition?
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Start, Pause, Stop
In ServiceNow, an SLA definition typically involves three main conditions:
• Start: This condition defines when the SLA timer starts. It can be triggered by various events, such as record creation, assignment, or other specific criteria.
• Pause: This condition specifies when the SLA timer should be paused. This might occur during specific periods, such as weekends or holidays, or when the incident is waiting for external input.
• Stop: This condition defines when the SLA timer should stop. This usually happens when the incident is resolved or closed.
By understanding these conditions, you can effectively configure SLAs to meet specific service level objectives and track performance metrics.

questions.question: How to manage record numbering (like INC0000001)
questions.explanation:
A. System Definition > Number maintenance
This option is correct. The “Number Maintenance” feature in ServiceNow allows administrators to manage and configure the number series for various records, including incidents. Through this interface, you can define how numbers are generated, set prefixes, and manage the incrementing of numbers, ensuring that each new record receives a unique identifier in the specified format.
B. Number field > Number
This option is incorrect. While the number field itself holds the generated number for records (like INC0000001), it does not provide a method for managing or configuring how those numbers are generated or maintained. This option lacks the context of management; it simply refers to the field that stores the number rather than a method of controlling or configuring it.
C. System Definition > Numbers
This option is incorrect. Although “System Definition” is a valid section in ServiceNow, there is no specific module titled “Numbers” that directly pertains to managing record numbering. The correct area for managing numbering is specifically “Number Maintenance,” making this option misleading as it does not accurately describe the functionality available in ServiceNow.
D. None
This option is incorrect. Since there are valid methods available for managing record numbering (specifically through “System Definition > Number maintenance”), stating “None” would not accurately reflect the capabilities of ServiceNow regarding record numbering management.
Summary
• Correct Option: A (System Definition > Number maintenance)
• Incorrect Options: B (Number field > Number), C (System Definition > Numbers), D (None)

questions.question: A role cannot contain any other role?
questions.explanation:
FALSE
In ServiceNow, roles can indeed contain other roles. This concept is known as role inheritance. By assigning one role to another, you can effectively grant the permissions and privileges of the contained role to users who have the containing role.
This feature is useful for creating hierarchical role structures and managing complex access control scenarios. For example, you might create a role called “IT Manager” and assign it to the “itil” role. This would grant IT Managers all the permissions of the itil role, plus any additional permissions specifically assigned to the “IT Manager” role.

questions.question: What is related to High Security Plugin in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: B. security_admin role for elevated privilege
The security_admin role in ServiceNow is often associated with the High Security Plugin. This role grants elevated privileges, allowing users to perform sensitive administrative tasks, such as:
• Modifying system properties: Changing core system settings.
• Accessing system logs: Reviewing detailed system logs.
• Managing user roles and permissions: Controlling access to various parts of the ServiceNow instance.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Impersonation feature: Impersonation allows users to temporarily assume the identity of another user, but it’s not directly related to the High Security Plugin.
• C. ACL: Access Control Lists (ACLs) are used to control access to specific records and fields within ServiceNow, but they are not directly related to the High Security Plugin.

questions.question: Banner Color can be personalized from?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: B. Themes section
The banner color in ServiceNow can be customized using Themes. Themes allow you to change the overall look and feel of your ServiceNow instance, including the banner color, font, and other visual elements.
By creating and applying custom themes, you can tailor the appearance of your ServiceNow instance to your organization’s branding and preferences.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Not Possible: This is incorrect, as ServiceNow provides the flexibility to customize the banner color through themes.
• C. Navigation Pane: The Navigation Pane is used to navigate between different applications and modules within ServiceNow. It doesn’t control the banner color.
• D. Developer Section: While the Developer section provides tools for advanced customizations, it’s not directly used to change the banner color. Themes are the primary mechanism for customizing the visual appearance of ServiceNow.

questions.question: What is the search engine used while doing the global search in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: A. Zing
Zing is the internal search engine used by ServiceNow to power global search functionality. It efficiently indexes and searches through vast amounts of data within the platform, enabling users to quickly find relevant information, records, and knowledge articles.
Incorrect Options:
• B. Zenn: This is not a search engine used by ServiceNow.
• C. Google Search: While Google Search can be integrated with ServiceNow for external search, it’s not the primary search engine used for internal searches within the platform.
• D. TRX: This is not related to ServiceNow’s search functionality.

questions.question: ServiceNow automatically provides numbers for which tables?
questions.explanation:
Correct Answer: D. All of the above
ServiceNow automatically generates unique numbers for various record types, including:
• Incident: Each incident record is assigned a unique incident number (e.g., INC0000001).
• Problem: Each problem record is assigned a unique problem number (e.g., PRB0000001).
• Change Request: Each change request is assigned a unique change request number (e.g., CHG0000001).
• Knowledge Article: Each knowledge article is assigned a unique knowledge article number (e.g., KB0000001).

questions.question: What is a Workflow?
options: Can manage all form and list Changes
It's a virtual representation of activities consisting of connected steps planned out in a sequential manner
Its a static representation of activities of connected steps planned out in a chronological manner, which cannot be change or modified
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. It’s a virtual representation of activities consisting of connected steps planned out in a sequential manner
A Workflow in ServiceNow is a dynamic process that automates business tasks. It consists of a series of steps, each with specific actions and conditions. These steps can be configured to execute in a sequential or parallel manner, allowing for flexibility in process design. Workflows can be triggered by various events, such as record creation, update, or closure.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Can manage all form and list Changes: While Workflows can trigger actions based on form and list changes, they are not the sole tool for managing all such changes.
• C. Its a static representation of activities of connected steps planned out in a chronological manner, which cannot be change or modified: Workflows are highly customizable and can be modified to adapt to changing business needs.
• D. None of the above: Option B accurately describes the concept of a Workflow in ServiceNow.

questions.question: What’s an example of a CI?
options: Computer, Software Contract, Business Service (tangible and intangible)
Service Catalog records (an alternative to lists and forms)
an automation block such as approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers and utilities
A role with special permissions during the logon session.
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Computer, Software Contract, Business Service (tangible and intangible)
A Configuration Item (CI) in ServiceNow is a representation of a tangible or intangible asset that needs to be managed. Examples of CIs include:
• Tangible Assets: Hardware (computers, servers, routers), network devices, and physical infrastructure.
• Intangible Assets: Software applications, licenses, databases, and business services.
By managing CIs in ServiceNow, organizations can gain better visibility into their IT infrastructure, track asset lifecycles, and improve overall IT service management.
The other options are not accurate representations of CIs:
• B. Service Catalog records: While Service Catalog records are important for offering services, they are not considered CIs.
• C. An automation block such as approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers and utilities: These are components used to build workflows and automation, but they are not CIs.
• D. A role with special permissions during the logon session: Roles define user access and permissions, not physical or logical assets.

questions.question: How are referenced fields identified in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. From Reference lookup Icon
• Correct because referenced fields in ServiceNow are identified by the reference lookup icon (magnifying glass) that appears next to the field.
• This icon allows users to search and select values from the referenced table.
• For example, in the Incident table, the “Assigned to” field references the User table, and the lookup icon helps identify and select the correct user record.
Incorrect
Option A. From Base Class
• Incorrect because the base class defines inheritance in ServiceNow tables, not how referenced fields are identified.
• Referenced fields are not identified by base class relationships.
Option B. From Blue Book
• Incorrect because there is no concept of a “Blue Book” in ServiceNow related to referenced fields.
• This is a distractor option.
Option D. None of the above
• Incorrect because option C is indeed correct.
• Referenced fields are clearly identified by the lookup icon, so “None of the above” is not valid.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to Service Catalog? (Select all that Apply)
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Catalog Items, B. Record Producers, C. Variables
These three components are fundamental to the Service Catalog in ServiceNow:
• Catalog Items: These are the products or services offered through the Service Catalog. They can be simple items like software licenses or complex offerings involving multiple steps and approvals.
• Record Producers: These are scripts that automate the creation of records, such as incidents, change requests, or problem records, when a catalog item is ordered.
• Variables: These are used to collect information from the requester during the ordering process. They can be of various types, such as text, number, date, or reference.
Incorrect Option:
• D. Change Tasks: Change tasks are part of the Change Management module and are not directly related to the Service Catalog.

questions.question: What is a schema map?
options: It's JavaScript configured to run when a record is displayed, inserted, updated, deleted, or when a table is queried
It's a gear icon located in top left hand side every list. It allows you to add columns (via slush bucket) to the current list you are on
Graphical representation that shows the referenced, referencing, extended, and extending tables
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Graphical representation that shows the referenced, referencing, extended, and extending tables
A schema map in ServiceNow is a visual representation of the relationships between different tables. It helps you understand how tables are connected through references, extensions, and other relationships. This visual tool is invaluable for system administrators to design and maintain complex data models.
Incorrect Options:
• A. It’s JavaScript configured to run when a record is displayed, inserted, updated, deleted, or when a table is queried: This describes a Business Rule, not a schema map.
• B. It’s a gear icon located in top left hand side every list. It allows you to add columns (via slush bucket) to the current list you are on: This describes the List Layout configuration, not a schema map.
• D. None of the above: Option C accurately defines a schema map.

questions.question: Which of the following are captured in update set
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. Changes to Form Layout
Update Sets in ServiceNow are used to package and transport configuration changes between instances. They capture changes to various aspects of the ServiceNow configuration, including:
• Forms: Changes to form layouts, form scripts, and UI policies are captured in update sets.
• Tables: Changes to table structures, fields, and ACLs are also included.
• Business Rules: Modifications to business rules and script includes are captured.
• Workflows: Changes to workflow definitions, activities, and conditions are tracked.
• Reports: New reports and modifications to existing reports are captured.
Why not A and C?
• A. Changes to Incident Record: Changes to individual records, like incidents, are not captured in update sets. Update sets primarily focus on configuration changes, not data changes.
• C. Changes to Group Members: Changes to group membership are typically managed through the user interface and are not directly captured in update sets.

questions.question: Use _________ to categorize, flag, and locate your records
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Tags
Tags are a powerful tool in ServiceNow to categorize and organize records. They allow you to:
• Categorize: Assign relevant tags to records to group them based on specific criteria.
• Flag: Use tags to highlight important records or those requiring attention.
• Locate: Easily search for records using specific tags as filters.
Here’s why the other options aren’t suitable:
• A. Search: Search is a broader function used to find records based on various criteria, including tags. However, it doesn’t specifically categorize or flag records.
• B. Favourites: Favourites are used to bookmark specific records for quick access but don’t provide categorization or flagging capabilities.
• D. Bookmarks: Similar to favourites, bookmarks are used to save links to specific records or pages, not to categorize or flag them.

questions.question: Can we coalesce multiple fields?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. TRUE
• Correct because in ServiceNow, when configuring Import Sets and Transform Maps, you can coalesce multiple fields.
• Coalescing means using one or more fields to determine whether an incoming record should update an existing record or create a new one.
• By coalescing on multiple fields, ServiceNow checks the combination of those fields to find a match in the target table.
• This is useful when a single field (like email or employee ID) is not unique enough, and you need a composite key to ensure proper record matching.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE
• Incorrect because ServiceNow does allow coalescing on multiple fields.
• Choosing FALSE would imply that only one field can be coalesced, which is not accurate.

questions.question: Banner Color can be personalized from which section in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Themes section Correct because personalization of the banner color in ServiceNow is done through the Themes section. Themes allow users to customize the look and feel of the interface, including banner colors, to improve usability and align with organizational branding.
Incorrect
Option A. Developer Section Incorrect because the Developer Section is used for building and customizing applications, scripts, and configurations. It does not provide options for personalizing banner colors.
Option C. Navigation Pane Incorrect because the Navigation Pane is used for accessing modules and applications. It does not control banner color personalization.
Option D. Not Possible Incorrect because banner color personalization is indeed possible through the Themes section, so this option is invalid.

questions.question: Personalizing form doesn’t allow users to hide __________ fields
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. Mandatory
While ServiceNow’s form personalization feature allows users to customize their form layouts, it does not allow them to hide mandatory fields. Mandatory fields are essential for data integrity and cannot be hidden, as they must be filled out before a record can be saved.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. Reference: Users can hide reference fields if they are not necessary for their specific workflow or task.
• C. Pre-populated: Pre-populated fields can be hidden if they don’t add value to the user’s experience or if their values are not relevant to the current task.
• D. Read-only: Read-only fields can also be hidden if they don’t provide necessary information or if their values are already displayed elsewhere on the form.

questions.question: A _ is a cell in a table which holds an individual piece of data
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Field
• Correct because in ServiceNow (and relational database terminology), a field is the smallest unit of data storage in a table.
• Each field corresponds to a column in the table, and each cell in that column holds one piece of data for a record.
• Example: In the Incident table, the “Priority” field holds the priority value for each incident record.
Incorrect
Option B. Data
• Incorrect because “data” is a general term referring to information stored in the system.
• It does not specifically describe the structure of a table cell.
Option C. List
• Incorrect because a list in ServiceNow refers to a view of multiple records in a table.
• It is not the individual cell that holds a single piece of data.
Option D. Record
• Incorrect because a record is a row in a table, which consists of multiple fields (cells).
• A record represents a complete entity, not a single piece of data.

questions.question: At which location are the records saved?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Table
This is the correct choice because in ServiceNow, records are saved in tables. A table is the underlying data structure where all records are stored. Each record corresponds to a row in the table, and fields correspond to columns. This is fundamental to the CSA exam: forms and lists are just views of the data, but the actual storage location is the table.
Incorrect
Option B: Form Incorrect because a form is simply a user interface used to view or edit a single record. It does not store the record itself.
Option C: List Incorrect because a list is a representation of multiple records from a table. It is a way to display data but not where records are saved.
Option D: All Incorrect because records are not saved in multiple places. They are stored only in the table. Forms and lists are views, not storage locations.

questions.question: What defines and monitors the guarantees established with an outside supplier and is a tool for supplier management?
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. Underpinning contract (UC)
An Underpinning Contract (UC) in ServiceNow is a formal agreement between an organization and an external service provider. It defines the specific service level expectations, performance metrics, and other contractual terms. UCs are used to manage relationships with third-party suppliers and ensure that they meet the agreed-upon service levels.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Variables: Variables are used to collect information from users during the ordering process in the Service Catalog.
• C. Catalog Item Designer: This tool is used to create and manage Service Catalog items.
• D. systems, CI, caller: These are components of ServiceNow configuration management and incident management, not related to supplier management.
By effectively managing UCs, organizations can maintain high-quality service delivery, reduce risks, and improve overall supplier performance.

questions.question: What displays the details of tables and their relationships?
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Schema Map
A Schema Map in ServiceNow provides a visual representation of the relationships between different tables. It helps you understand how tables are connected through references, extensions, and other relationships. This visual tool is invaluable for system administrators to design and maintain complex data models.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Base Class: Base Classes define the structure of tables and fields, but they don’t provide a visual representation of relationships.
• B. cmdb_ci: This is a specific table used to store information about Configuration Items (CIs). It doesn’t provide a visual overview of table relationships.
• C. BSM Icon: BSM (Business Service Management) is a broader concept related to managing IT services. The BSM icon might represent various elements within the BSM framework, but it doesn’t specifically show table relationships.

questions.question: How are users related to roles or groups?
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Many to many relationships
In ServiceNow, a many-to-many relationship exists between users and roles or groups. This means:
• One user can belong to multiple groups. A user can be a member of multiple teams or departments, each represented by a different group.
• One group can contain multiple users. A group can consist of many users who share common permissions and access rights.

questions.question: onCellEdit client script is executed when
options: A particular field is modified on Form
A particular field is modified on List
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
C. A particular field is modified on List:
• onCellEdit client scripts in ServiceNow are specifically designed to run when a particular field in a list (table view) is modified and then saved. This allows administrators to execute specific logic when data in list cells is edited directly from the list view.
Incorrect Options:
A. A particular field is modified on Form:
• Incorrect. onCellEdit client scripts do not run on form fields. They are meant for list views, not for individual form fields where form-related client scripts like onChange would be more appropriate.
B. Any field is modified:
• Incorrect. The onCellEdit script is triggered by modifications in list view cells, not by any field changes in general. This option is too broad and doesn’t specify the context of list editing.

questions.question: If a workflow is not published, it will be captured in update set.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. FALSE
• Correct because only published workflows are captured in update sets.
• Unpublished workflows remain in draft state and are not included in update sets.
• This ensures that only finalized, deployable versions of workflows are moved between instances.
Incorrect
Option A. TRUE
• Incorrect because saying “True” would imply that even unpublished workflows are captured in update sets.
• In reality, unpublished workflows are excluded, so this option does not meet the stated behavior.

questions.question: We can draw multiple transition from a single activity in workflow
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. TRUE
• Reason: In ServiceNow workflows, an activity can have multiple outgoing transitions.
• This allows branching logic (e.g., approvals, conditions, or decision points) where different paths are followed depending on outcomes.
• For example, an Approval activity can transition to “Approved” or “Rejected,” enabling flexible workflow design.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE
• Incorrect because ServiceNow workflows are designed to support multiple transitions from a single activity.
• Limiting to one transition would prevent branching logic and conditional flows, which are essential in workflow automation.

questions.question: After high security plugin is activated, a security_admin privilege is created. What is an elevated privilege?
options: Used to enable the ITIL role to have an Admin type access
Elevated privilege is used to promote extension tables
A role that has special permissions for the duration of the log in session
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. A role that has special permissions for the duration of the log in session
An elevated privilege in ServiceNow is a temporary role that grants a user additional permissions for a specific session. This allows users to perform actions that they wouldn’t normally be authorized to do, such as modifying system properties or accessing sensitive data.
Elevated privileges are often used for troubleshooting issues, performing system maintenance, or making configuration changes. Once the elevated session ends, the user’s permissions revert to their normal role.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Used to enable the ITIL role to have an Admin type access: This is not the purpose of elevated privileges.
• B. Users with the Admin role: Users with the Admin role already have extensive permissions and do not need elevated privileges.
• C. Elevated privilege is used to promote extension tables: Promoting extension tables is a different process that involves using the ServiceNow Update Sets.

questions.question: Out of the below listed applications which will not run natively on smartphones?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Workflow
• Correct because the Workflow application is designed for administrators and developers to build and manage process automation.
• It is not supported natively on smartphones, as mobile interfaces are optimized for end‑user tasks like approvals, catalog requests, and self‑service actions.
• Workflow design and management requires the full web interface, not the mobile app.
Incorrect
Option B. Service Catalog
• Incorrect because the Service Catalog is accessible on mobile devices.
• End users can request services, submit forms, and track approvals natively through the ServiceNow mobile app.
Option C. Self‑Service
• Incorrect because Self‑Service is specifically designed for mobile and web access.
• Users can search for knowledge articles, submit incidents, and interact with the portal directly from smartphones.
Option D. User Administration
• Incorrect because basic User Administration tasks (like profile updates or approvals) can be performed through mobile interfaces.
• While advanced administration is better suited for desktop, the application itself is not blocked from mobile use.

questions.question: In ServiceNow, Multiple Choice, Single Text, and Select Box are examples of what type of elements?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Variable Types Correct because Multiple Choice, Single Text, and Select Box are all variable types used in Service Catalog items and record producers. Variables capture user input and allow customization of requests, making them essential for gathering information from users.
Incorrect
Option A. Related Lists Incorrect because Related Lists display records related to the current record (e.g., tasks related to an incident). They are not input elements.
Option B. Order Guides Incorrect because Order Guides group multiple catalog items together in a single request. They are not individual input fields.
Option C. Request Types Incorrect because Request Types categorize service requests (e.g., incident, change, catalog request). They are not specific input elements like variables.

questions.question: What process does the Knowledge Base manage?
options: Document review cycle, which includes submission, feedback from SME, and publishing
Weekly and monitoring operations reports done on archived and current data
Ordering and billing cycle initiated when items are purchased using the service catalog
System asset reassignment accomplished as the real-time tracking of hardware and software assets
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Document review cycle, which includes submission, feedback from SME, and publishing
The Knowledge Base in ServiceNow is primarily used to manage and share knowledge articles. It facilitates a document review cycle where:
• Submission: Knowledge articles are created and submitted by subject matter experts (SMEs).
• Feedback from SME: Articles can be reviewed and edited by SMEs to ensure accuracy and completeness.
• Publishing: Once approved, articles are published to the Knowledge Base, making them accessible to users.
This process helps to maintain a high-quality knowledge base and ensures that users have access to accurate and up-to-date information.
Incorrect Options:
• B. Weekly and monitoring operations reports done on archived and current data: While the Knowledge Base can be used to store historical information, it’s not specifically designed for generating reports.
• C. Ordering and billing cycle initiated when items are purchased using the service catalog: This is related to Service Catalog and Order Management, not the Knowledge Base.
• D. System asset reassignment accomplished as the real-time tracking of hardware and software assets: This is related to Configuration Management Database (CMDB) and asset management, not the Knowledge Base.

questions.question: When is a workflow complete?
options: When the workflow runs out of activities.
When the workflow reached to Delivery stage.
When the workflow reached to End Activity
When the workflow reached to Complete stage.
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. When the workflow reached to End Activity
A workflow in ServiceNow is considered complete when it reaches an End Activity. This signifies the conclusion of the workflow process, indicating that all necessary tasks and conditions have been fulfilled.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. When the workflow runs out of activities: This is not sufficient. A workflow can have multiple activities, and it’s the final End Activity that determines completion.
• B. When the workflow reached to Delivery stage: A Delivery stage might be part of a workflow, but it doesn’t necessarily indicate completion. There could be further steps or conditions to be met after delivery.
• D. When the workflow reached to Complete stage: While a “Complete” stage might be used in certain workflow designs, it’s not the definitive indicator of completion. The End Activity is the standard way to signify the end of a workflow.

questions.question: What are the components of a condition:
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Field, Operator, Value
A condition in ServiceNow typically consists of three components:
• Field: The specific field in a table that you want to evaluate.
• Operator: The logical operator used to compare the field value, such as “equals,” “greater than,” “contains,” etc.
• Value: The value to compare the field against.
By combining these components, you can create complex conditions to control the behavior of workflows, business rules, and other ServiceNow features.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Variable, Operator, Value: Variables are used to store values, but they are not directly used in conditions.
• B. Variable, Condition, Script: Conditions do not involve scripts.
• D. Field, Condition, Script: Conditions do not involve scripts.

questions.question: Which of the components are visible on Workflow welcome screen?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. New Workflow Button Correct. The Workflow welcome screen provides a New Workflow button that allows administrators to start creating a new workflow directly from the interface.
• Option B. Pallete Tabs Correct. The Palette Tabs are visible on the Workflow welcome screen, giving access to workflow activities and logic elements that can be dragged into the workflow canvas.
• Option D. List of published workflows Correct. The welcome screen also shows a list of published workflows, allowing administrators to quickly view and manage existing workflows.
Incorrect
• Option C. Catalog form Incorrect because the Catalog form is part of Service Catalog management, not the Workflow welcome screen. It is used for catalog items and requests, not workflow design.

questions.question: How does ServiceNow decide which application should be visible when a user login to ServiceNow?
options: Everybody can see all the applications
Defined on the basis of roles assigned to the user
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Defined on the basis of roles assigned to the user
ServiceNow determines which applications are visible to a user based on the roles assigned to that user. Roles define the permissions and access rights for users, including which applications they can see and use.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. UI Policies: UI Policies are used to control the visibility and behavior of fields on forms and lists, not entire applications.
• B. Everybody can see all the applications: This is not the default behavior. ServiceNow allows for granular control over application visibility based on roles.
• D. Defined through Managers permission: While managers can assign roles to users, the actual visibility of applications is determined by the roles themselves, not by direct manager permissions.

questions.question: In workflow, what is an activity?
options: Waiting for Approval, Approved, Pending, Fulfilled, Completed
creates Service Catalog records (an alternative to lists and forms)
Defines unique key for record. If record found, import will update the record. If not found, import will create a new record.
An automation block such as approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers and utilities
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. An automation block such as approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers and utilities
• Reason: In ServiceNow workflows, an activity is a reusable automation block that performs a specific function.
• Examples include approval activities, task creation, notifications, timers, and utility functions.
• Activities are the building blocks of workflows, enabling automation of business processes.
Incorrect
Option A. Waiting for Approval, Approved, Pending, Fulfilled, Completed
• Incorrect because these are workflow states, not activities.
• States represent the status of a workflow or task, not the automation blocks themselves.
Option B. Creates Service Catalog records (an alternative to lists and forms)
• Incorrect because this describes Service Catalog functionality, not workflow activities.
• Activities are broader automation components, not catalog record creation.
Option C. Defines unique key for record. If record found, import will update the record. If not found, import will create a new record.
• Incorrect because this describes transform maps in data imports, not workflow activities.
• Import sets and transform maps handle record creation/update logic, unrelated to workflow automation blocks.

questions.question: Which module contains SLA, OLA, and UC (Underpinning Contracts) in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Service Level Management Correct because the Service Level Management (SLM) module in ServiceNow is specifically designed to manage Service Level Agreements (SLAs), Operational Level Agreements (OLAs), and Underpinning Contracts (UCs). It ensures that commitments made to customers and internal teams are tracked, measured, and reported.
Incorrect
Option A. Service Catalog Incorrect because the Service Catalog is used to provide users with a structured list of services and items they can request. It does not manage SLAs, OLAs, or UCs.
Option B. Content Management Incorrect because Content Management is related to managing and publishing content (like knowledge articles or web content), not service-level agreements.
Option C. Asset Contract Incorrect because Asset Contract deals with managing contracts related to assets (like hardware or software), not SLAs, OLAs, or UCs.

questions.question: Context Menus, List Buttons, Form buttons are
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. UI Actions
UI Actions are used to create buttons and links that trigger specific actions within ServiceNow. They can be displayed in various locations, including:
• Context Menus: These are the menus that appear when you right-click on a record.
• List Buttons: These are buttons displayed on list views that allow you to perform actions on multiple records at once.
• Form Buttons: These are buttons displayed on forms that allow you to perform actions on a single record.
By creating UI Actions, you can customize the user interface and provide additional functionality to users, such as:
• Opening related records
• Running workflows
• Sending emails
• Executing scripts
The other options are not relevant to creating buttons and links:
• A. Buttons: Buttons are a visual component of UI Actions, but they are not the underlying mechanism.
• B. Business Rules: Business Rules are used to automate processes and enforce data integrity, but they don’t directly create buttons or links.
• D. UI Pages: UI Pages are used to create custom web pages within ServiceNow, but they are not used to create buttons or links in the context of forms and lists.

questions.question: Which role is required for creating ACL?
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
B. security_admin:
• security_admin: The security_admin role in ServiceNow is required to create, modify, or delete Access Control Lists (ACLs). This role grants the necessary permissions to manage security rules, ensuring that only authorized users can access specific data and perform certain actions.
Incorrect Options:
A. approval_admin:
• Incorrect. The approval_admin role is typically used for managing approval processes and does not have the permissions needed to create ACLs.
C. itil_admin:
• Incorrect. The itil_admin role is focused on ITIL processes and administration but does not include the specialized permissions required for managing ACLs.
D. admin:
• Incorrect. While the admin role has broad administrative privileges, creating ACLs specifically requires the security_admin role due to the sensitive nature of access control configurations.

questions.question: The ________ protects application by identifying and restricting access to available files and data.
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
D. Application scope:
• Application scope: In ServiceNow, the application scope is a security boundary that protects an application by identifying and restricting access to its files and data. Each application has its own scope, which ensures that the components of the application are insulated from other applications. This scope helps maintain the integrity and security of the application by controlling access to scripts, tables, and other resources within the application.
Incorrect Options:
A. Application configuration:
• Incorrect. Application configuration refers to the settings and customization of an application, but it does not inherently protect the application by restricting access to its files and data.
B. Verbose log:
• Incorrect. Verbose logging provides detailed logging information for debugging purposes but does not have a role in restricting access to files and data within an application.
C. Access control rule:
• Incorrect. While access control rules (ACLs) are used to restrict access to specific records and fields, they are not the mechanism that defines the overall security boundary of an application. ACLs operate within the context of the application scope.

questions.question: In the smart filter condition builder, what are the three elements of a filter?
options: Application Service Response, network latency and browser rendering
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Field, Operator, Value
• Correct because in ServiceNow’s smart filter condition builder, every filter is defined by three essential elements:
• Field → the database column or attribute being filtered (e.g., “State”, “Priority”).
• Operator → the condition applied (e.g., “is”, “greater than”, “contains”).
• Value → the specific data being matched (e.g., “Open”, “High”).
• These three together form the logical condition that drives queries and reports.
Incorrect
Option B. Social IT > Feed administration > Messages
• Incorrect because this refers to a navigation path in ServiceNow, not filter elements.
• It is unrelated to how filters are constructed.
Option C. Application Service Response, network latency and browser rendering
• Incorrect because these are performance metrics, not filter components.
• They may be monitored in ServiceNow but are not part of the filter condition builder.
Option D. They are the same
• Incorrect because filters are not defined as “the same.”
• This option is vague and does not identify the three required elements.

questions.question: Which of the following options is an example of a UI Policy?
options: Creating a new field on form.
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. To make priority field mandatory
A UI Policy is a rule that controls the behavior of UI elements on ServiceNow forms and lists. It can be used to:
• Hide or show fields based on certain conditions.
• Make fields mandatory or read-only under specific circumstances.
• Set default values for fields.
• Change the appearance of fields (e.g., color, font size).
In this case, making a priority field mandatory is a common use case for a UI Policy. By setting up a UI Policy to make the priority field mandatory, you can ensure that users always fill out this important field when creating or updating records.
The other options are not directly related to UI Policies:
• A. Creating a new field on form: This is done through table configuration.
• C. Increasing width of field: This can be done through form layout customization or CSS.
• D. None of these: Option B is the correct answer.

questions.question: What will be the name in ServiceNow for a newly created table?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. u_abc Correct because in ServiceNow, when you create a custom table, the system automatically prefixes the table name with u_ to indicate it is a user‑defined table. For example, if you name the table abc, the actual system name becomes u_abc. This ensures that custom tables are distinguishable from system tables (which typically start with sys_).
Incorrect
Option B. sys_a Incorrect because the sys_ prefix is reserved for system tables created by ServiceNow itself (e.g., sys_user, sys_db_object). Custom tables do not use this prefix.
Option C. abc_sys Incorrect because ServiceNow does not append _sys to custom table names. This format is invalid for newly created tables.
Option D. a_abc Incorrect because the prefix a_ is not used in ServiceNow naming conventions. Custom tables always start with u_.

questions.question: On an Application Menu, if the role field is left blank, then
options: Only ITIL and Admins can see the appliaction menu
Only admins can see the Application menu
All users can see the application menu
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. All users can see the application menu
If the Role field on an Application Menu is left blank, it means that all users in the ServiceNow instance, regardless of their specific roles, will be able to see the application menu.
This is the default behavior when no specific role is assigned to an application menu.
Therefore, if you want to restrict access to an application menu to specific roles, you must explicitly assign the appropriate roles to the menu record.

questions.question: Which of the following client script works on list view?
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
C. OnCellEdit:
• OnCellEdit: This type of client script is designed to work on list views in ServiceNow. It triggers when a cell in a list is edited and then saved. This script allows you to execute custom logic whenever a cell’s content is changed directly within the list view.
Incorrect Options:
A. OnSubmit:
• Incorrect. OnSubmit client scripts are used to execute code when a form is submitted. These scripts do not operate on list views but are instead used to validate or process data when a user submits a form.
B. OnChange:
• Incorrect. OnChange client scripts are triggered when a specific field’s value changes on a form. They do not apply to list views, as they are intended for use with individual form fields.
D. OnLoad:
• Incorrect. OnLoad client scripts run when a form is loaded, allowing you to perform actions when a form initially appears. These scripts are also not applicable to list views, as they are specifically tied to form loading events.

questions.question: Which among the following is an example of Contextual Security in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. ACL Correct because Access Control Lists (ACLs) are the primary example of contextual security in ServiceNow. They define who can access specific data and under what conditions, ensuring that security is enforced based on context such as roles, conditions, and record values.
Incorrect
Option A. Business rules Incorrect because Business rules are server-side scripts used to automate processes, not enforce contextual security.
Option C. Data Policy Incorrect because Data Policies enforce consistency of data across platforms (e.g., enforcing mandatory fields), but they are not considered contextual security.
Option D. None Incorrect because ACLs are indeed an example of contextual security, so “None” is not valid.

questions.question: _ is used to grant access to application menus and modules
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. User Roles
User Roles are used to grant access to specific applications, modules, and records within ServiceNow. By assigning appropriate roles to users, you can control their permissions and ensure that they can only access the features and data they need to perform their tasks.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. ACL (Access Control List): ACLs are used to control access to individual records and fields within a table. They don’t directly grant access to applications and modules.
• B. User Rules: User Rules are used to automate user creation and assignment processes, but they don’t control access to applications and modules.
• C. Assignment Rules: Assignment Rules are used to automatically assign records to specific users or groups. They don’t control access to applications and modules.

questions.question: Where can Pause condition be used in SLA?
options: It can be put on any desired field
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. It can be put on any desired field
• Correct because in ServiceNow, Pause conditions in SLAs can be configured on any field of the task record (e.g., incident, problem, change).
• This allows administrators to define when the SLA timer should pause, such as when a ticket is in a specific state (like Pending Vendor or Awaiting User).
• Flexibility is key: the pause condition is not limited to predefined states, but can be applied to any field value that matches the business requirement.
Incorrect
Option A. When putting Pending State
• Incorrect because while Pending is a common state used for pausing SLAs, it is not the only option.
• The exam emphasizes that pause conditions are configurable on any field, not restricted to a single state.
Option B. When putting Resolved State
• Incorrect because once a record is in Resolved, the SLA is typically stopped or completed, not paused.
• Pause conditions are meant for temporary suspension, not for states that indicate closure.
Option D. None
• Incorrect because ServiceNow does support pause conditions.
• Saying “None” ignores the SLA configuration capability that allows administrators to define pause rules.

questions.question: Which one of the following contains text search options?
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. All of the above
ServiceNow provides text search functionality across various areas of the platform, including:
• Knowledge: You can search for specific articles or keywords within the Knowledge Base.
• Homepage: You can search for records, articles, and other content from the homepage search bar.
• Lists: You can use the built-in search functionality to filter and find specific records within a list view.

questions.question: Which among the following is true for UI actions?
options: They run only on server side.
All the UI actions of task table are not extended by the incident table.
List choices do not contain any UI action.
Based on the condition, it can be decided when to make it visible.
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. Based on the condition, it can be decided when to make it visible
• Correct because UI Actions in ServiceNow can be configured with conditions that determine when they should be visible or active. This allows administrators to control the availability of buttons, links, or context menu items depending on record state or user role.
Incorrect
• Option A. They run only on server side
• Incorrect because UI Actions can run on both client side (using scripts) and server side (executing scripts or actions). They are not limited to server-side execution.
• Option B. All the UI actions of task table are not extended by the incident table
• Incorrect because UI Actions defined on the task table are extended to child tables such as incident, unless explicitly restricted.
• Option C. List choices do not contain any UI action
• Incorrect because UI Actions can be added to lists (e.g., list buttons, list context menu actions). They are not limited to forms only.

questions.question: What are the different components of an SLA in ServiceNow?
options: SLA Definition, Task SLA, SLA Workflow, SLA Automation, SLA Conditions
SLA Definition, SLA Workflow, SLA Conditions
SLA Workflow, SLA Automation, SLA Conditions
SLA Definition, SLA Workflow, Task SLA, SLA Conditions
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. SLA Definition, Task SLA, SLA Workflow, SLA Automation, SLA Conditions
• Correct because these represent the full set of SLA components in ServiceNow:
• SLA Definition: Defines the rules and targets for SLAs.
• Task SLA: Tracks SLA progress on individual tasks.
• SLA Workflow: Automates actions when SLA conditions are met or breached.
• SLA Automation: Handles triggering and managing SLA events automatically.
• SLA Conditions: Define when an SLA applies (e.g., priority, assignment group).
Incorrect
Option B. SLA Definition, SLA Workflow, SLA Conditions
• Incorrect because it omits Task SLA and SLA Automation, which are essential components for tracking and managing SLAs.
Option C. SLA Workflow, SLA Automation, SLA Conditions
• Incorrect because it leaves out SLA Definition and Task SLA, both of which are fundamental to SLA configuration.
Option D. SLA Definition, SLA Workflow, Task SLA, SLA Conditions
• Incorrect because it excludes SLA Automation, which is necessary for automated SLA handling.

questions.question: In ServiceNow, which of the following statements about Metrics are correct?
options: Metric can gather data as the data is updated
Metric measures data over time to show past history
Metric definition provides a declarative way of defining metrics and once defined, the data for the metric is gathered and occurences of the metric are calculated and stored
Metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of ITSM process
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. Metric can gather data as the data is updated
• Option B. Metric measures data over time to show past history
• Option C. Metric definition provides a declarative way of defining metrics and once defined, the data for the metric is gathered and occurrences of the metric are calculated and stored
• Option D. Metric is used to measure and evaluate the effectiveness of ITSM process
All four statements are correct because ServiceNow metrics track changes in data, measure performance historically, provide declarative definitions for automated tracking, and evaluate ITSM process effectiveness.

questions.question: Multiple Choice, Single Line Texts and Select Box are what type of elements in Service Now?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Variable Types
Correct because in ServiceNow, Multiple Choice, Single Line Texts, and Select Box are examples of variable types used in catalog items and record producers. Variables capture user input and allow customization of requests. They are fundamental building blocks in the Service Catalog for gathering information from users.
Incorrect
Option A. Order Guides Incorrect because Order Guides are used to group multiple catalog items together in a single request. They are not input elements like variables.
Option C. Request Types Incorrect because Request Types refer to categories of service requests (e.g., incident, change, catalog request). They are not specific input elements in forms.
Option D. Related Lists Incorrect because Related Lists display records related to the current record (e.g., tasks related to an incident). They are not input fields or variable types.

questions.question: Changes made to a workflow version are not added to the update set until the workflow is published
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. TRUE
• Correct because in ServiceNow, changes made to a workflow version are only captured in the update set once the workflow is published.
• Draft or unpublished versions do not get recorded in the update set, ensuring that only finalized workflows are tracked for migration between instances.
• This behavior prevents incomplete or experimental workflow changes from being unintentionally moved to other environments.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE
• Incorrect because unpublished workflow changes are not automatically added to update sets.
• Selecting FALSE would imply that all changes, even drafts, are tracked in update sets, which is not the case.

questions.question: Which of the following helps in finding the records from tables?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Global text search icon
The global text search icon in ServiceNow allows you to search for records across various tables based on specific keywords or phrases. This powerful tool helps you quickly find the information you need, regardless of where it’s stored in the instance.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Impersonate user: This feature allows you to temporarily assume the identity of another user to see the system from their perspective.
• B. Elevate roles: This feature grants you additional permissions for a specific session.
• D. Connect sidebar icon: This feature is used for real-time communication with other users.

questions.question: Incident extends which table?
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Task
In ServiceNow, the incident table is a child table that extends the task table. This means that incident records inherit properties and behaviors from the task table, such as:
• Assignment: Assigning incidents to specific users or groups.
• State: Tracking the status of incidents (e.g., open, in progress, closed).
• Due Date: Setting deadlines for resolving incidents.
• Work Notes: Adding comments and updates to incident records.
By inheriting from the task table, incident records benefit from a common framework for managing work items, ensuring consistency and efficiency in incident management processes.

questions.question: What does ‘Coalesce’ field mean?
options: Field/s will bind with target table
Field/s will be set a unique key
Field/s will be set a reference key
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Field(s) will be set a unique key
• This is correct because in ServiceNow Coalesce is used during data imports (via Transform Maps).
• When a field is marked as Coalesce, ServiceNow treats it as a unique key to determine whether to update an existing record or insert a new one.
• If a matching record exists based on the coalesce field(s), the record is updated; if not, a new record is created.
• This ensures data integrity and prevents duplicate records during imports.
Incorrect
Option A. Field(s) will bind with target table
• Incorrect because coalesce does not “bind” fields to a table.
• Binding is not a ServiceNow concept in this context; coalesce specifically defines uniqueness for update/insert logic.
Option C. Field(s) will be set a reference key
• Incorrect because coalesce does not set reference keys.
• Reference keys are used to link records between tables (e.g., sys_id references), but coalesce is about uniqueness in data import.

questions.question: Searches are available in (select three options)
questions.explanation:
Correct:
Option A. Navigation Filter
The Navigation Filter provides a search capability that allows users to quickly find applications, modules, and menus within the ServiceNow application navigator. This is a core and commonly tested search feature in the CSA exam.
Option C. Knowledge Base
The Knowledge Base includes a search function that allows users to search for knowledge articles using keywords. This enables users to quickly locate relevant documentation and solutions.
Option D. Lists
Lists support searching through records using the list search bar. Users can search for specific records based on field values, making lists a key searchable interface in ServiceNow.
Incorrect:
Option B. Forms
Forms themselves do not provide a general search feature. While users can search for reference field values within a form, forms are primarily used for viewing and editing individual records, not for performing searches across records.

questions.question: Which application is visible to all the users
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Self-Service
The Self-Service application is typically visible to all users in a ServiceNow instance, regardless of their specific roles or permissions. It provides a user-friendly interface for end-users to submit requests, check the status of their requests, and access knowledge articles. This promotes self-service and reduces the burden on IT support teams.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Incident, B. Problem, D. Clone: These applications are primarily used by IT support teams and other authorized users to manage incidents, problems, and changes. They are not typically visible to all users.

questions.question: How to make a fields madatory at data base level, before updating or inserting?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Data Policy
• Correct because Data Policies enforce rules at the server/database level.
• They ensure that fields are mandatory or read‑only regardless of how the data is entered (via UI, import sets, web services, or APIs).
• This guarantees consistency and compliance across all data entry methods, not just the UI.
• Example: If a field like Serial Number must always be filled in before insert/update, a Data Policy enforces this rule universally.
Incorrect
Option A. UI Policy
• Incorrect because UI Policies only apply at the form/UI level.
• They can make fields mandatory or read‑only in the interface, but they do not enforce rules at the database level.
• If data is inserted via imports or APIs, UI Policies will not apply.
Option B. Client Scripts
• Incorrect because Client Scripts run in the browser and apply only to the user interface.
• They can validate input or make fields mandatory in the form, but they cannot enforce rules at the database level.
• Like UI Policies, they do not affect imports or integrations.

questions.question: ServiceNow consists of standard integration with LDAP
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. True
• Correct because ServiceNow provides out‑of‑the‑box (standard) integration with LDAP.
• This integration allows ServiceNow to authenticate users against an LDAP directory and import user/group information directly.
• It is a widely used feature for enterprises that rely on Active Directory or other LDAP‑based systems for identity management.
Incorrect
Option A. FALSE
• Incorrect because saying “FALSE” would imply ServiceNow does not support LDAP integration.
• In reality, LDAP integration is a native, standard capability of ServiceNow and is commonly implemented for user authentication and synchronization.

questions.question: How are Workflows moved between instances?
options: Workflows cannot be moved between instances
Workflows are moved using Application Sets
Workflows are moved using XML only
Workflows are moved using Update Sets
questions.explanation:
Update Sets are used to move customizations and configurations from one ServiceNow instance to another. Workflows, being a type of customization, can be moved between instances using Update Sets. When you create an Update Set, you can add workflows to it, along with any related components such as tables, fields, business rules, and UI pages. Once you have created an Update Set, you can then export it from the source instance and import it into the target instance. This allows you to move workflows and other customizations between instances as needed.
The system tracks workflows in update sets differently than other records because workflow information is stored across multiple tables.
Changes made to a workflow version are not added to the update set until the workflow is published, at which point the entire workflow is added into the update set. Update sets store workflows as a single Workflow [wf_workflow] record and only retain the latest version with the update type of Workflow.

questions.question: Which term best describes something that is created, has worked performed upon it, and is eventually moved to a state of closed?
