questions.question: What is the definition of a group?
options: A collection of subject matter experts
questions.explanation:
Manage the individuals who can access your instance by defining them as users in the system. Create user groups, and assign users to them. Use roles to specify what different users and user groups can see and do.
A group is a set of users who share a common purpose. Members of groups perform tasks such as approving change requests, resolving incidents, receiving email notifications, or performing change request tasks. Assign every user to at least one group.
A good practice is to assign roles to groups rather than to users. Administrators can assign roles quickly to multiple users by adding the users to the group. If a user moves to another group, the role assigned to the new group is applied automatically.

questions.question: What Service Catalog feature do you use to organize catalog items into logical groups?
questions.explanation:
Categories organize service catalog items into logical groups. Administrators and catalog administrators can create and configure categories, defining their characteristics and adding content such as catalog items to them.
Categories can have a parent-child relationship, for example, IT and Laptops. A child category is a subcategory of its parent category. Each catalog item, order guide, record producer, content item, and subcategory appears as a single item within the category. A catalog item can exist in multiple categories, giving you the flexibility to offer the same service from multiple places within your catalog.

questions.question: For Administrators creating new Service Catalog items, what is a characteristic they should know about Service Catalog variables?
options: Service Catalog variables are global by default
Service Catalog variables cannot affect the order price
Service Catalog variables can only be used in Record Producers
Service Catalog variables can only be used in Order Guides
questions.explanation: Service Catalog variables are global by default, display in all the tasks of a Requested Item, and provide options to tailor a catalog item to the customer‘s needs. For example, a computer might be available with different operating systems. The Service Catalog lets you attach variables either to a catalog item or to an execution plan. Question choices can define the available options and might affect the order price.

questions.question: Which ServiceNow capability allows you to provide knowledge articles, via a conversational messaging interface?
questions.explanation: The ServiceNow® Virtual Agent application provides user assistance through a conversational messaging interface so that you can design and build automated conversations that help users quickly obtain information and perform common work tasks. Virtual Agent was enhanced and updated in the Rome release.

questions.question: Where is data stored?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C (Table): ServiceNow stores all data in relational database tables where records represent individual data entries across all modules and applications.
Incorrect
Option A (Record): Records are individual data rows within tables, not the storage mechanism itself.
Option B (Form): Forms provide the user interface for viewing and editing records, but data resides in underlying tables.
Option D (List): Lists display multiple records from tables in a viewable format, but actual storage occurs at the table level.

questions.question: A customer has asked for the following updates to a form:  Make Resolution code Mandatory, when state is changed to Resolved  Hide Major Incident check box, unless logged in user has Major Incident Manager role What type of rule(s) would you use to implement this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option E: UI Policy
The Logic: UI Policies are specifically designed to change the behavior of form fields in real-time based on conditions without requiring a page reload.
Requirement 1 (Mandatory Field): A UI Policy can evaluate the condition State is Resolved and set the Resolution code field to Mandatory.
Requirement 2 (Visibility based on Role): UI Policies can also include scripts (Execute if True/False) or simple conditions to evaluate roles. By checking if the user has the major_incident_manager role, the policy can set the Major Incident checkbox to Visible = true or false.
Why it’s preferred: It is a “No-Code/Low-Code” tool that provides immediate visual feedback to the user as they interact with the form.
Incorrect
Option A: Dictionary Design
Reasoning: Field settings in the Dictionary are static. You can make a field mandatory for everyone at all times, but you cannot make it conditionally mandatory based on a change in the State field or specific user roles using standard dictionary entries.
Option B: Business Rule
Reasoning: Business Rules are Server-Side. They run when a record is displayed, inserted, updated, or deleted. While a Business Rule can enforce mandatory fields upon saving (Validation), it cannot “hide” a checkbox or make a field appear mandatory while the user is typing on the form before they hit save.
Option C: Form Constraint
Reasoning: This is not a standard term or feature in ServiceNow. It is a distractor meant to sound like a technical limitation.
Option D: UI Design
Reasoning: “UI Design” is a general concept or a category, but it is not a specific “rule type” or tool within the ServiceNow platform for implementing logic. The tool used for UI design in this context is the UI Policy.

questions.question: Which mobile application is designed to interact with customer support and is not customizable?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Now Support
• Correct.
• The Now Support mobile application is specifically designed for interacting with ServiceNow customer support.
• It is not customizable, unlike other ServiceNow mobile apps that can be tailored for enterprise workflows.
• This aligns with the CSA exam expectation (2026): candidates should know that Now Support is fixed-purpose and used only for ServiceNow support interactions.
Incorrect
Option A. Now Mobile
• Incorrect.
• Now Mobile is a customizable app that allows employees to access enterprise services (HR, IT, facilities, etc.). It is not limited to customer support.
Option B. Mobile Onboarding
• Incorrect.
• Mobile Onboarding is customizable and designed for employee onboarding workflows, not customer support.
Option D. Now Onboarding
• Incorrect.
• Similar to Mobile Onboarding, this app is customizable and used for onboarding processes, not for customer support.
Option E. HI Support
• Incorrect.
• HI (Hosted Instance) Support was the older support portal, now replaced by Now Support. It is not the correct answer for the current exam context.

questions.question: The customer has asked that you change the default layout of the Task list. They would like these columns, in this order:  Number  Task Type  Parent  Short Description  Assignment Group  Assigned to  Updated
options: Right click on any column header, Context Menu > Configure > List Layout
Click List Context Menu > Configure > Columns
Click List Context Menu > Personalize List
Right click List Gear icon > Configure > Columns
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A: Right click on any column header, Context Menu > Configure > List Layout
• Correct.
• In ServiceNow, to change the default list layout (the columns shown for all users), you right-click on a column header and select Configure > List Layout.
• This opens the configuration window where you can add, remove, and reorder columns.
• This is the proper way to meet the customer’s requirement.
Incorrect
Option B: Click List Context Menu > Configure > Columns
• Incorrect.
• This option allows you to configure personalized list views for the current user, not the default layout for all users.
• It does not change the global list layout.
Option C: Click List Context Menu > Personalize List
• Incorrect.
• “Personalize List” is a user-specific customization.
• It only affects the logged-in user’s view, not the default layout for everyone.
Option D: Right click List Gear icon > Configure > Columns
• Incorrect.
• The gear icon opens personal column settings, similar to “Personalize List.”
• Again, this is user-specific and does not configure the default layout.

questions.question: What is the most common role that has access to almost all platform features, functions, and data?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. System Administrator [admin]
• The System Administrator (admin) role is the most common role with access to nearly all platform features, functions, and data in ServiceNow.
• It provides broad privileges, including configuration, customization, and management of applications and modules.
• This is the role typically referenced in CSA exam questions when asking about “full access.”
Incorrect
Option A. Base Admin [base_admin]
• This is not a standard ServiceNow role. It is a distractor and does not exist in the platform.
Option C. Admin [sn_admin]
• This is also not a standard ServiceNow role. The recognized role is System Administrator [admin], not “sn_admin.”
Option D. Security Admin [security_admin]
• This role is specific to managing security‑related features, such as access control policies and encryption.
• It does not provide full access to all platform features.
Option E. Sys Admin [sys_admin]
• This is a common mislabeling. The correct ServiceNow role is System Administrator [admin], not “sys_admin.”

questions.question: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to which of the following components?
options: Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
Order Guides, Item Variables, and flows
Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables
Order Guides, Catalog Items, and flows
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Record Producers, Order Guides, and Catalog Items
• This is correct because the baseline Service Catalog homepage in ServiceNow provides direct links to:
• Record Producers → Used to create task records (like incidents or requests) through catalog forms.
• Order Guides → Allow users to order multiple related catalog items in one request.
• Catalog Items → Standard items in the catalog that users can request.
• These three components are the foundation of the Service Catalog experience.
Incorrect
Option B. Order Guides, Item Variables, and flows
• Incorrect because item variables are part of catalog item configuration, not something directly linked on the homepage.
• Flows are automation tools (Flow Designer), not catalog homepage components.
Option C. Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables
• Incorrect because while record producers and order guides are correct, item variables are not shown as homepage links. They are embedded in catalog items.
Option D. Order Guides, Catalog Items, and flows
• Incorrect because flows are not part of the baseline catalog homepage.
• The homepage does not provide direct links to automation flows.

questions.question: What setting allows users to view a Knowledge Base article even if they are not logged in?

questions.question: Which tool is used to define relationships between fields in an import set table and a target table?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Transform Map
• Correct because a Transform Map in ServiceNow defines the relationship between fields in an import set table and fields in a target table.
• It is the key mechanism used during data imports to specify how incoming data should be mapped, transformed, and loaded into ServiceNow tables.
• Without a Transform Map, imported data cannot be properly aligned with the target table structure.
Incorrect
Option B. Field Transformer
• Incorrect because there is no tool called “Field Transformer” in ServiceNow.
• Transformation logic is handled within Transform Maps, not a separate tool.
Option C. Schema Map
• Incorrect because a Schema Map is used to visualize relationships between tables (like parent-child or reference relationships), not to define field mappings during imports.
Option D. Transform Schema
• Incorrect because “Transform Schema” is not a valid ServiceNow feature.
• The correct term is Transform Map, which handles field-level mappings.

questions.question: Where can Admins check which release is running on an ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Stats module
• This is correct. The Stats module in ServiceNow provides system information, including the current release version of the instance.
• Admins can use this to verify which release (e.g., Tokyo, Vancouver, etc.) is running.
• It is the standard and recommended way to check the release version.
Incorrect
Option B. system.upgraded table
• This is incorrect because the system.upgraded table tracks upgrade history, not the current release version.
• It shows when upgrades occurred but does not directly display the active release.
Option C. Memory Stats module
• This is incorrect because the Memory Stats module provides information about memory usage and performance metrics.
• It does not show release details.
Option D. Transactions log
• This is incorrect because the Transactions log records system transactions and performance data.
• It is useful for debugging but does not indicate the release version.

questions.question: A record is added to which table each time a knowledge article is viewed?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option B. Knowledge Use [kb_use] Correct because every time a knowledge article is viewed, a record is added to the Knowledge Use [kb_use] table. This table tracks article usage and helps administrators analyze which articles are being accessed most frequently.
Incorrect
• Option A. Knowledge Search Log [ts_query_kb] Incorrect because this table logs search queries performed in the knowledge base, not article views.
• Option C. Knowledge [kb_knowledge] Incorrect because this table stores the actual knowledge articles themselves, not the view history.
• Option D. Knowledge Feedback [kb_feedback] Incorrect because this table stores feedback records (like helpfulness ratings or comments) submitted by users, not article view counts.

questions.question: Groups are stored in what table?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option B. Group [sys_user_group] Correct because in ServiceNow, groups are stored in the sys_user_group table. This table contains records for groups that can be used to assign roles, manage access, and organize users for workflow purposes.
Incorrect
• Option A. User Group [user_groups] Incorrect because this is not a valid ServiceNow table name. It is a distractor option.
• Option C. Group [sn_sys_user_group] Incorrect because the prefix sn_ is not used for the groups table. The correct table is simply sys_user_group.
• Option D. Groups [sys_user_groups] Incorrect because the table name is singular (sys_user_group), not plural.
• Option E. User Groups [sn_user_groups] Incorrect because this is not a recognized ServiceNow table. The sn_ prefix is misleading here.

questions.question: Question A new Service Desk employee in Latin America complains that the create dates and times are incorrect on their Incident list. What would you suggest to fix this issue?
options: Have them correct the time zone on their computer.
Have them use the gear icon to set the employee‘s time zone.
Recommend they use Chrome, instead of Explorer.
Use the system properties to correct the instance‘s time zone.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Have them use the gear icon to set the employee’s time zone
• Correct because in ServiceNow, each user can configure their personal time zone via the gear icon (Preferences).
• This ensures that dates and times displayed in lists, forms, and reports are adjusted to the user’s local time zone.
• It directly resolves the issue without affecting other users or the system instance.
Incorrect
Option A. Have them correct the time zone on their computer
• Incorrect because ServiceNow does not rely on the local computer’s time zone. It uses the user’s profile settings in the instance.
Option C. Recommend they use Chrome, instead of Explorer
• Incorrect because the browser choice does not affect how ServiceNow calculates or displays time zones.
Option D. Use the system properties to correct the instance’s time zone
• Incorrect because changing the instance’s global time zone would affect all users, not just the employee in Latin America. The issue is user‑specific, not system‑wide.
Option E. Have them clear their cache
• Incorrect because clearing cache may fix display glitches, but it does not resolve incorrect time zone settings.

questions.question: On a filter condition, there is an element, which is based on the table, the user access rights, and columns on the table. What is this element called?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Field
• Correct because in ServiceNow (and similar platforms), a field is the element used in filter conditions.
• A field is tied to a table, respects user access rights, and represents a column in that table.
• When building filters, users select fields to define conditions (e.g., Incident → State = Open).
Incorrect
Option A. Attribute
• Incorrect because while attributes describe properties of fields or records, they are not the selectable elements in filter conditions.
Option B. Table
• Incorrect because a table is the overall data structure containing records and fields. Filters operate on fields within tables, not the table itself.
Option D. Column
• Incorrect because although fields correspond to columns in the database, the user interacts with fields in the filter builder, not raw columns.
Option E. Label
• Incorrect because a label is simply the display name of a field. It is not the functional element used in filter conditions.

questions.question: How are products and services in the Service Catalog organized?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Categories and Subcategories
• Correct because the Service Catalog in ServiceNow organizes products and services into categories (e.g., Hardware, Software, Access) and further into subcategories.
• This hierarchical structure makes it easier for users to browse and locate catalog items.
• It is the standard method of organizing catalog content in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option B. Incidents and Problems
• Incorrect because Incidents and Problems are part of ITSM processes, not the Service Catalog.
• They deal with issue resolution and root cause analysis, not catalog item organization.
Option C. Tickets and Requests
• Incorrect because tickets and requests are records generated after ordering catalog items, not the way catalog items themselves are organized.
Option D. Tasks and Subtasks
• Incorrect because tasks and subtasks are used in workflow execution and process management, not in catalog item organization.

questions.question: Automated Chatting agent available on the service portal is commonly referred to as?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Virtual Agent
• Correct because in ServiceNow, the automated conversational interface available on the Service Portal is officially called the Virtual Agent.
• It provides guided interactions, answers FAQs, and helps users resolve issues without needing to contact a live agent.
• This is the standard terminology used in ServiceNow CSA exam questions.
Incorrect
Option A. Alexa
• Incorrect because Alexa is Amazon’s voice assistant, not part of ServiceNow’s Service Portal.
Option B. Agentless Bot
• Incorrect because ServiceNow does not use the term “Agentless Bot” for its automated chat functionality.
Option D. Chatbot
• Incorrect because while “chatbot” is a generic term, ServiceNow specifically brands its solution as Virtual Agent.
• Using “chatbot” would not be the precise answer expected in the exam.

questions.question: Here is an example of the criteria set for a knowledge base: Companies: ACME North America Departments: HR Groups: ACME Managers Match All: Yes In this example, what users would have access to this knowledge base?
options: Employees of ACME North America, who are members of HR Department or the ACME Managers group
Members of the ACME Manager group, who are also members of HR Department and part of ACME North America
Members of the ACME Managers group, and HR department, regardless of geography
Users which are members of either ACME North America, or HR Department, or ACME Managers group
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Members of the ACME Manager group, who are also members of HR Department and part of ACME North America This is correct because the Match All = Yes setting requires that users meet all criteria simultaneously. Therefore, only users who belong to the ACME North America company, are in the HR department, and are members of the ACME Managers group will have access.
Incorrect
Option A. Employees of ACME North America, who are members of HR Department or the ACME Managers group Incorrect because this describes an OR condition, but the criteria explicitly require Match All = Yes, meaning all conditions must be met, not just one.
Option C. Members of the ACME Managers group, and HR department, regardless of geography Incorrect because geography (Company = ACME North America) is part of the criteria. Ignoring the company requirement makes this option invalid.
Option D. Users which are members of either ACME North America, or HR Department, or ACME Managers group Incorrect because this is a pure OR condition across all three criteria. With Match All = Yes, users must satisfy all three simultaneously, not just one.

questions.question: How would you distinguish between a Base Class table and a Parent Class table?
options: Extended tables can be extended from Parent tables or Base tables; but they cannot be extended from both.
Base Class tables always have tables extended from them. Parent tables do not have tables extended from them.
Extended tables are always extended from Parent tables. Extended tables are usually extended from Base tables.
Base Class table is not extended from another table, Parent class tables may be extended from another table.
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option D. Base Class table is not extended from another table, Parent class tables may be extended from another table. Correct because in ServiceNow:
• A Base Class table is the root table in the hierarchy. It is not extended from any other table (examples: task, cmdb_ci).
• A Parent Class table is a table that is extended from another table but also serves as the parent for further extensions. For example, incident extends task but can itself be extended further.
This distinction is fundamental in understanding table inheritance in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
• Option A. Extended tables can be extended from Parent tables or Base tables; but they cannot be extended from both. Incorrect because extended tables can indeed be extended from either a base or a parent table, but this statement does not clearly distinguish between base and parent tables. It is misleading rather than defining the difference.
• Option B. Base Class tables always have tables extended from them. Parent tables do not have tables extended from them. Incorrect because parent tables do have tables extended from them. For example, task (base) has incident (parent), and incident can be extended further.
• Option C. Extended tables are always extended from Parent tables. Extended tables are usually extended from Base tables. Incorrect because extended tables can be extended from either a base table or a parent table. This option is contradictory and inaccurate.

questions.question: You need to create a way for users to order a new iPhone, but only if they get two levels of approval. Approvers and users should be automatically notified at each approval level. What feature would you use to manage the approvals and notifications?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option E. Flows
• Correct because Flows (Flow Designer in ServiceNow) allow you to build automated workflows that include multi‑level approvals and notifications.
• You can configure the flow to trigger when a user orders an iPhone, then add approval steps for two different approvers.
• Notifications can be automatically sent to approvers and the requester at each stage.
• This is the modern, CSDM‑aligned way to handle approvals and notifications in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option A. Approval Criteria
• Incorrect because approval criteria define conditions for approvals, but they do not manage the full workflow or notifications.
• They are part of approval rules, not a standalone solution for multi‑level approvals.
Option B. Approval Chains
• Incorrect because while approval chains describe sequences of approvals, they are not the feature used to implement them in ServiceNow.
• Flow Designer is the actual tool to configure and automate the process.
Option C. Parent‑Child Approvers
• Incorrect because parent‑child approvers are not a ServiceNow feature.
• This option is misleading and does not exist in the CSA exam context.
Option D. Approver Delegates
• Incorrect because approver delegates are used when an approver assigns their approval responsibility to someone else.
• They do not manage multi‑level approvals or notifications.

questions.question: Access Control rules may provide access security for which of the following database objects?
options: For a specific role, group, or user
For a specific row, column, or table
For a specific CMDB Configuration item
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. For a specific row, column, or table
• Correct because ServiceNow Access Control rules (ACLs) are applied at the table level, field (column) level, and record (row) level.
• This allows fine‑grained security, ensuring only authorized users can read, write, or execute specific database objects.
• ACLs are evaluated in order and enforce security directly on the data objects themselves.
Incorrect
Option A. For a specific role, group, or user
• Incorrect because ACLs are not applied directly to roles, groups, or users.
• Instead, ACLs reference roles or conditions to determine whether a user can access a database object. The enforcement is always on the object, not the role/group itself.
Option B. For specific groups
• Incorrect because ACLs do not secure groups themselves.
• Groups may be used in conditions to grant access, but ACLs are tied to tables, fields, and records.
Option D. For a specific CMDB Configuration item
• Incorrect because ACLs are not designed to secure individual CMDB items directly.
• They secure the tables and fields that store CMDB data, not the configuration items themselves.

questions.question: What role can edit ACLs?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A) security_admin This is correct because the security_admin role is the only role in ServiceNow that has the elevated privileges required to create, modify, and edit Access Control Lists (ACLs). ACLs are critical for controlling access to data and functionality, so restricting this capability ensures proper governance and system security.
Incorrect
Option B) system_admin Incorrect because while system_admin has broad administrative rights, it does not have the elevated security permissions needed to edit ACLs. ACL editing is specifically reserved for the security_admin role.
Option C) admin Incorrect because the generic admin role is not a standard ServiceNow role. Even if considered, ACL editing requires elevated security privileges beyond typical administrative functions.
Option D) acl_admin Incorrect because acl_admin is not a standard ServiceNow role. The recognized role for ACL editing is security_admin.

questions.question: Which type of ServiceNow script runs on the web browser?

make fields read only or writable

questions.question: What are best practices regarding users/groups/roles?Select 2 answers.
options: You should assign roles to users.
You should never assign roles to groups.
You should add users to groups.
You should assign roles to groups.
questions.explanation:
The two best practices regarding users/groups/roles in ServiceNow are:
Add users to groups .
Assign roles to groups .
Here‘s why these are considered best practices:
Efficient Management: Assigning roles directly to individual users can become cumbersome and difficult to manage, especially as the number of users grows. By adding users to groups and assigning roles to groups, you can simplify administration and ensure that users inherit the necessary permissions based on their group membership.
Role-Based Access Control (RBAC): ServiceNow leverages RBAC, which grants access based on a user‘s role. By assigning roles to groups, you can effectively implement RBAC. Users within a group inherit the permissions associated with the assigned role, promoting consistency and reducing the risk of accidentally granting inappropriate access to individual users.
Here‘s why the other options are not recommended best practices:
You should assign roles to users: While technically possible, this approach is less efficient for managing user permissions in a larger environment.
You should never assign roles to groups: Assigning roles to groups is a core principle of RBAC in ServiceNow. It allows for centralized permission management and simplifies user access control.

questions.question: What type of query allows you to filter list data using normal words, instead of the condition builder?
questions.explanation: ServiceNow® NLQ translates natural language user input into glide record queries. The queries are rendered into an executable structured format, such as a JavaScript Object Notation (JSON) file or a visual definition. The output, in whichever format, is the response to the user‘s request.

questions.question: Access Control rules may be defined with which of the following permission requirements?Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation:
User Criteria can be used in Service Catalog and Knowledge Base.
Groups can‘t be used in ACLs

questions.question: When managing tags, you can adjust who is able to see it. What are the visibility options?Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation: Tags are text labels that you can associate with items like records and pages. Tags enable you to group and organize the items. Tags can be visible to any user (global), visible only to specific groups or users (shared), or visible to a single user (private).

questions.question: Which of the following statements describes how data is organized in a table?
options: A column contains data from one user and a record is one set of fields
A column is a field in the database and a record is one user
A column is one field and a record is one column
A column is one field and a record is one row
questions.explanation: A table is a collection of records in the database. Each record corresponds to a row in a table, and each field on a record corresponds to a column on that table.

questions.question: Security rules are defined to restrict the permissions of users from viewing and interacting with data. What are these security rules called?
questions.explanation: Rules for access control lists (ACLs) restrict access to data by requiring users to pass a set of requirements before they can interact with it.

questions.question: User records are stored in which table?
questions.explanation: Type sys_user.list in your PDI

questions.question: Which component of a table contains a piece of data for one record?
questions.explanation:
The individual pieces of data in a record are called fields. You enter data in fields on the form or by using the list editor. Administrators can create new or modify existing fields.
You can enter data in fields by using the list editor or by using a form. In form view, fields appear as fields in the form, and in list view they appear as columns of data in the table. Administrators can create new fields or change the type of existing fields.

questions.question: What feature do you use to specify which users are able to access a Service Catalog Item?
questions.explanation: The user criteria restriction applies only within Service Catalog for the specific item it is applied for. However, the user criteria restriction is not applied outside the Service Catalog where the user has access to the item via the table.

questions.question: Table Access Control rules are processed in the following order:
options: any table name (wildcard), parent table name, table name
table name, parent table name, any table name (wildcard)
any table name (wildcard), table name, parent table name
parent table name, table name, any table name (wildcard)
questions.explanation:
Table ACL rules are processed in the following order:
Match the table name. For example, incident.
Match the parent table name. For example, task.
Match any table name (*). For example, *.

questions.question: What is the language used for scripting in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow uses industry-standard JavaScript to extend application functionality. ServiceNow APIs (Application Programming Interfaces) provide classes and methods to do things like:
Interact with database tables: query, update, create, delete
Validate data
Write to log files
Prompt users with alerts, confirmations, or messages
Launch workflows, scheduled jobs, and events
Interact with 3rd party web services
And more…

questions.question: Where to click to always return back to Home?
questions.explanation: https://docs.servicenow.com/en-US/bundle/utah-platform-user-interface/page/administer/navigation-and-ui/concept/c_CustomizeTheBannerLogoLink.html

questions.question: The Employee On-boarding team has asked for a way for managers to order computers, monitors, business cards, and cell phones for new employees. How would you proceed to meet this requirement?
questions.explanation:
Order guide submits a single service catalog request that generates several items.
For example, a New Employee Hire order guide can contain several items that new employees commonly need, such as business cards, computer, and cell phone. After selecting this order guide, the customer can then provide information about the new employee, including location and job title. The order guide then submits an order for catalog items like business cards, based on the details provided.
Order guides determine which catalog items to order by evaluating order guide rule conditions. Information the customer enters within the order guide can be passed as cascading variables to the ordered items, allowing common information to be reused across multiple items.
Administrators and catalog administrators can create order guides for the service catalog.

questions.question: What types of entities can receive task assignments, in ServiceNow?Select 2 answers.
questions.explanation: There are 2 reference fields on the task table: assignment_group [sys_user_group], and assigned_to [sys_user]

questions.question: What automatically assigns tasks to users or groups?
questions.explanation:
The Assignment rules module allows you to automatically set a value in the assigned_to and assignment_group fields when a set of conditions occurs.
An assignment rule must also meet these additional criteria to run:
The task record has been created or updated. Assignment rules do not apply to unsaved changes on a form.
The task record must be unassigned. The record cannot have an existing value for either the assigned_to or assignment_group fields. Assignment rules cannot overwrite existing assignments (including assignments set by a default value or a previously run assignment rule).
The assignment rule is the first rule that matches the table and conditions. If more than one assignment rule matches the conditions, only the rule with the lowest order value runs.

questions.question: How would you navigate to the Schema map for a table?
options: System Dictionary > Show Schema Map; Select Table
System Definition > Tables; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map
System Definition > Dictionary; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map
System Definition > Show Schema Map; Select Table
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option B. System Definition > Tables; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map This is correct because the proper way to access the Schema Map in ServiceNow is by navigating to System Definition > Tables, selecting the desired table, and then using the Related Links section to click Show Schema Map. This provides a visual representation of relationships, extensions, and references for that table.
Incorrect
• Option A. System Dictionary > Show Schema Map; Select Table Incorrect because the Schema Map is not accessed directly from System Dictionary. The correct navigation is through System Definition > Tables.
• Option C. System Definition > Dictionary; Select Table; Go to Related links and click Show Schema Map Incorrect because while the Dictionary shows field definitions, it does not provide access to the Schema Map. The Schema Map is tied to the Tables module, not the Dictionary.
• Option D. System Definition > Show Schema Map; Select Table Incorrect because there is no direct “Show Schema Map” option under System Definition. It must be accessed via the Tables module and then through Related Links.

questions.question: What role enables someone to authorize a request, with no other permissions on the platform?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The role that enables someone to authorize a request with minimal platform permissions is:
Approver [approver_user]
Here‘s why this role is the most suitable choice:
Limited Scope: The “approver_user“ role is specifically designed for users who need to authorize requests without granting them broader access to the ServiceNow platform. This is ideal for scenarios where you want to delegate approval authority to specific individuals without giving them full-fledged ITIL functionality.
The other options provide broader permissions or are less common:
Authorize [authorize_user]: While the name suggests authorization, there isn‘t a standard “authorize_user“ role in ServiceNow. Approval functionalities are typically handled by the “approver_user“ role.
Reviewer [reviewer_user]: Reviewers might assess requests before approval, but they wouldn‘t necessarily have the final say for authorization.
Verification [verify_user]: Verifiers might confirm specific details within a request, but they wouldn‘t have the same level of authorization as an approver.
Approval Group [approval_group]: Approval groups can be used for routing approvals to a group of users, but individual users within the group would likely need an “approver_user“ role to grant final authorization.
By assigning the “approver_user“ role, you can empower users to authorize requests while minimizing the overall permissions they have within the ServiceNow platform.

questions.question: What section on a task record would you use to see the most recent update made to a record?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The most appropriate section on a task record to see the most recent update is:
Activity
Here‘s why “Activity“ is the best choice:
Real-Time Updates: The activity stream within the “Activity“ section typically displays a chronological list of changes and updates made to the task record. This includes notes added, field values modified, or any other actions performed on the task.
The other options might not show the most recent update:
Timeline: While timelines might be present in some customized interfaces, they aren‘t a universal element on task records. Additionally, timelines might require configuration to ensure they display the most recent update first.
Audit Log: Audit logs provide a detailed historical record of all changes made to a record, but they might not necessarily present the information in a user-friendly, real-time fashion for viewing the most recent update.
Journal: Similar to audit logs, journals can track changes to a record, but they might not be the most prominent location for displaying the single most recent update.
By accessing the “Activity“ section on a task record, you can quickly see the latest modifications and stay up-to-date on the task‘s progress.

questions.question: Which script runs when a record is displayed, inserted, updated, deleted, or when a table is queried?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The correct answer is: Business Rule
Here‘s why:
Business Rule: Business rules are designed to automate specific actions or enforce business logic within ServiceNow. They can be triggered by various events, including:
Record is displayed (display)
Record is inserted (insert)
Record is updated (update)
Record is deleted (delete)
Table is queried (query)
By leveraging business rules, you can achieve a wide range of functionalities, such as data validation, field population based on other fields, sending notifications, or modifying field values based on certain conditions.
The other options have different functionalities in ServiceNow:
Client Script: Client scripts execute on the user‘s browser and are typically used for actions triggered by user interactions with the user interface (UI), such as clicking a button or changing a field value.
UI Script: UI scripts are a deprecated term in ServiceNow. They were similar to client scripts but are no longer recommended for new development. Use client scripts instead.
Script Include: Script includes are reusable blocks of code that can be referenced by other scripts (business rules, client scripts, etc.) to promote code modularity and reusability.
ACL (Access Control List): ACLs define user permissions for accessing and modifying records within ServiceNow. They don‘t directly execute code but control what users can do with the data.

questions.question: What type of client script runs when a cell on a list changes value through use of the List editor?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The client script that runs when a cell on a list changes value through use of the List editor is:
onCellEdit()
Here‘s why:
Specificity: onCellEdit() is specifically designed to trigger when a cell value is modified within a list view. It‘s the most appropriate choice for capturing changes made through the List editor.
Other options have broader scopes:
onEdit(): This script isn‘t as specific as onCellEdit(). While it might run for various edit events on a form, it wouldn‘t necessarily be limited to list cell edits.
onListEdit(): There isn‘t a standard onListEdit() client script in ServiceNow. Client scripts typically focus on actions at the cell level (onCellEdit()) or the entire form (onSubmit(), onLoad(), etc.).
onChange(): onChange() is commonly used for client scripts that trigger when a field value changes on a form. While it could be used in a list view if a cell is essentially a form field, onCellEdit() is more precise for list cell edits specifically.

questions.question: What happens if you select Publish when creating articles manually or by import?
options: It triggers the publish workflow assigned to the knowledge base.
The articles are sent for review
The articles are automatically moved to a published state.
The articles are sent for approvals.
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
Selecting “Publish“ when creating or importing knowledge articles in ServiceNow triggers the publish workflow assigned to the knowledge base .
Here‘s why this is the most likely outcome:
Automated Workflow Execution: Publishing an article often initiates a predefined workflow associated with the specific knowledge base. This workflow might involve tasks like:
Automatic formatting and styling
Content approval by designated reviewers
Notification to relevant teams
Activation of the article for end-user access
The other options describe potential steps within a publish workflow, but not the direct consequence of selecting “Publish“:
Articles Sent for Review: While review might be a step within the publish workflow, publishing itself triggers the workflow execution, not just the review stage.
Articles Automatically Moved to Published State: This could be the end result after the workflow completes successfully, but publishing itself initiates the workflow, not the automatic transition.
Articles Sent for Approvals: Similar to review, approvals might be part of the workflow, but publishing starts the workflow, not just the approval stage.

questions.question: What controls the publishing and retiring process for knowledge articles?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Workflow
• Correct because in ServiceNow (and similar knowledge management systems), the publishing and retiring process for knowledge articles is controlled by workflows.
• Workflows define the sequence of approvals, reviews, and state changes that an article must go through before being published or retired.
• This ensures consistency, governance, and compliance with organizational standards.
Incorrect
Option A. Workflow Designer
• Incorrect because Workflow Designer is the tool used to build and visualize workflows, but it does not itself control the publishing/retiring process.
• The actual control is through the workflow logic, not the designer interface.
Option B. Approval Definitions
• Incorrect because approval definitions specify who must approve certain actions, but they do not control the entire publishing/retiring lifecycle.
• They are components within workflows, not the overarching control mechanism.
Option C. Approval Policies
• Incorrect because approval policies define rules for approvals (e.g., auto-approval conditions), but they do not manage the full process of publishing or retiring articles.
• Again, they are part of workflows, not the main controller.
Option E. State Lifecycle
• Incorrect because state lifecycle refers to the status progression of an article (e.g., Draft → Review → Published → Retired).
• While important, the lifecycle is enforced and managed by workflows, not by itself.

questions.question: Knowledge Base Search results can be sorted by which of the following? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Views
• Correct. Search results can be sorted by the number of views, helping users identify the most frequently accessed articles.
Option B. Relevance
• Correct. Sorting by relevance ensures that the most contextually appropriate articles appear at the top of search results.
Option D. Newest
• Correct. Sorting by newest allows users to see the most recently created or updated articles first, which is useful when looking for the latest information.
Incorrect
Option C. Popularity
• Incorrect. While views indicate usage, “popularity” is not a standard sorting option in Knowledge Base search.
Option E. My group articles
• Incorrect. This is a filter option (to restrict results to articles owned by a group), not a sorting criterion.

questions.question: What will happen if you click ‘Show Matching‘ on the ‘Software‘ category on the incident list?
options: All incidents with Software category will remain visible
It will open a new window in your browser and display all the tickets other than Software
All incidents with Software category will disappear from the list
questions.explanation:
To quickly filter a list using a value in a field, right-click in the field and select Show Matching or Filter Out. For date fields, choose from Show Before, Show After, and Filter Out.
These functions add a condition to the right in the breadcrumb of the current filter.
Quick filter
(Abbildung im Original)
In this example, right-clicking In Progress and selecting Show Matching adds the condition State = In Progress as the most specific condition of the filter. By contrast, right-clicking In Progress and selecting Filter Out adds the condition State != In Progress as the most specific condition of the filter.

questions.question: When creating a new notification, what must you define? Select 3 answers.
options: What the content of the notification
Settings for handing inactive user accounts
Under what conditions is the notification sent
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. What the content of the notification Correct because every notification requires a defined message body or content that will be delivered to recipients.
• Option B. Who receives the notification Correct because notifications must specify the audience or recipients (users, groups, or roles) to ensure the right people get the message.
• Option E. Under what conditions is the notification sent Correct because notifications are triggered by specific conditions or events (e.g., record updates, state changes). Defining these ensures the notification is sent at the right time.
Incorrect
• Option C. Settings for handling inactive user accounts Incorrect because this is not part of notification creation. Handling inactive accounts is an administrative or user management task, not a notification requirement.
• Option D. The associated knowledge base Incorrect because notifications are not tied to knowledge bases. Knowledge bases store articles, while notifications are event-driven messages.

questions.question: What will happen if you click ‘Filter Out’ on the ‘Hardware’ category on the incident list?
options: All incidents with Hardware category will disappear from the list
It will open a new window in your browser and display all the tickets other than Hardware
All incidents with Hardware category will remain visible
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. All incidents with Hardware category will disappear from the list
• Correct because the Filter Out option removes records that match the selected value from the current list view.
• In this case, incidents categorized as “Hardware” will be excluded from the displayed list, allowing the user to focus on other categories.
Incorrect
Option A. Nothing will happen
• Incorrect because clicking “Filter Out” does trigger an action—it excludes the selected category from the list.
Option C. It will open a new window in your browser and display all the tickets other than Hardware
• Incorrect because “Filter Out” does not open a new window. It simply modifies the current list view by excluding the chosen category.
Option D. All incidents with Hardware category will remain visible
• Incorrect because the purpose of “Filter Out” is to hide those records, not keep them visible.

questions.question: Which tab on the knowledge base record would you use to identify the sets of users who are able to read articles in that knowledge base?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Can Read
• Correct because the Can Read tab on a knowledge base record specifies which users, groups, or roles are allowed to read articles in that knowledge base.
• This is the tab administrators use to control knowledge article visibility.
• It ensures that only authorized users can access the content.
Incorrect
Option A. Can Access
• Incorrect because there is no “Can Access” tab in the knowledge base record. This is a distractor option.
Option B. ACL
• Incorrect because ACLs (Access Control Lists) are used at the system level to enforce security rules, but they are not a tab on the knowledge base record.
• ACLs work behind the scenes, not through a direct tab like “Can Read.”
Option D. Accessible to
• Incorrect because “Accessible to” is not the correct tab name in ServiceNow knowledge base records.
• The proper tab is Can Read, not “Accessible to.”

questions.question: Which module would you use to create a new automation of business logic such as approvals, tasks, and notifications?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option E. Process Automation > Flow Designer
• Correct because Flow Designer is the modern ServiceNow tool used to create new automations of business logic.
• It allows administrators to build flows for approvals, tasks, notifications, and integrations without writing code.
• Flow Designer is the recommended replacement for the legacy Workflow Editor, aligning with ServiceNow’s push toward low‑code automation.
Incorrect
Option A. Process Automation > Active Flows
• Incorrect because this module is used to view and manage existing flows, not to create new ones.
Option B. Process Automation > Workflow Editor
• Incorrect because Workflow Editor is the legacy tool for building workflows.
• While it can create automations, the exam emphasizes Flow Designer as the correct modern answer.
Option C. Process Automation > Flow Administration
• Incorrect because Flow Administration is for managing flow permissions and settings, not for creating new flows.
Option D. Process Automation > Process Flow
• Incorrect because Process Flow is not the module used to design automations.
• It refers to visualizing or managing processes, not building new logic.

questions.question: What sections do you need to fill in when creating a notification? Select 3 asnwers
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Who will receive
• Correct because notifications must define the recipients (users, groups, or roles).
• Without specifying recipients, the notification cannot be delivered.
Option C. When to send
• Correct because you must define the timing or conditions under which the notification is triggered.
• This ensures the notification is sent at the right moment (event-driven or scheduled).
Option E. What it will contain
• Correct because the content/message body of the notification must be specified.
• This is the actual information communicated to the recipients.
Incorrect
Option B. Who will send
• Incorrect because notifications are system-generated. The sender is implicit and not a required section.
Option D. Notes
• Incorrect because notes are optional metadata or documentation, not a required section for notification creation.

questions.question: On a form, which type of field has this icon which can be clicked, to see a preview of the associated record?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Reference
• Correct because a Reference field (also known as a lookup to another table/record) displays an icon that allows users to preview the associated record.
• This is standard behavior in form design: clicking the icon opens a quick view of the referenced record without navigating away.
• It is specifically designed to link and preview related records.
Incorrect
Option A. Choice
• Incorrect because a Choice field only allows users to select from predefined values.
• It does not provide a preview icon for associated records.
Option B. Preview
• Incorrect because “Preview” is not a field type. It describes functionality but is not a valid field type in forms.
Option D. Lookup
• Incorrect because while a lookup field is related to references, the exam context distinguishes Reference fields as the type that provides the preview icon. Lookup alone is not the precise answer.
Option E. User
• Incorrect because a User field is a specific type of reference field pointing to user records.
• However, the general answer expected is Reference, not the narrower “User” field.

questions.question: Which of the following are a type of client scripts supported in ServiceNow? Select 4 answers.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. onChange
• Correct because onChange client scripts run when a field value changes. They are commonly used to validate input or trigger dynamic updates.
Option D. onCellEdit
• Correct because onCellEdit client scripts run when a cell in a list is edited. They help enforce rules or trigger actions during inline edits.
Option E. onSubmit
• Correct because onSubmit client scripts run when a form is submitted. They are used to validate data before submission or prevent submission if conditions are not met.
Option F. onLoad
• Correct because onLoad client scripts run when a form loads. They are used to set default values, hide/show fields, or initialize UI behavior.
Incorrect
Option A. onEdit
• Incorrect because onEdit is not a valid ServiceNow client script type. Editing behavior is handled by onChange or onCellEdit, not a separate onEdit script.
Option B. onUpdate
• Incorrect because onUpdate is not a client script type. Updates are handled by Business Rules or onSubmit scripts, not a client script called onUpdate.

questions.question: Which are valid ServiceNow User Authentication Methods? (Select three correct answers)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Local Database
• Correct because ServiceNow supports authentication against its internal user table (local database).
• This is the default method where usernames and passwords are stored directly in ServiceNow.
Option D. LDAP
• Correct because ServiceNow integrates with LDAP directories (e.g., Active Directory).
• This allows centralized authentication and management of users across enterprise systems.
Option E. SSO
• Correct because ServiceNow supports Single Sign-On (SSO) using protocols like SAML, OAuth, or OpenID Connect.
• This enables seamless authentication across multiple applications with one set of credentials.
Incorrect
Option B. XML feed
• Incorrect because XML feeds are used for data integration or import/export, not authentication.
• They cannot validate user credentials.
Option C. FTP authentication
• Incorrect because FTP is a file transfer protocol, not an authentication mechanism in ServiceNow.
• ServiceNow does not support FTP for user login.

questions.question: Question: What options are available to choose from in the ‘When’ field in the Business Rule? Select 2 answers
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Before
• Correct because the ‘When’ field in a Business Rule allows you to specify execution timing.
• Choosing Before means the rule runs before the database action occurs, typically used for validation or setting values prior to saving.
Option D. After
• Correct because After is another valid option in the ‘When’ field.
• This ensures the rule executes after the database action has completed, often used for logging, notifications, or post‑processing.
Incorrect
Option B. Update
• Incorrect because Update is not a valid choice in the ‘When’ field.
• Update refers to an operation type, not execution timing.
Option C. Insert
• Incorrect because Insert is also an operation type, not a timing option.
• The ‘When’ field only supports Before and After, not CRUD operations.

questions.question: On the Form header, which element you to access form templates?
questions.explanation:
Correct:
Option A. More Options (…)
In the ServiceNow exam context, the More Options (…) menu in the form header provides access to additional form actions, including form templates.
Form templates allow users to quickly populate a form with predefined field values. The templates can be accessed through the additional actions available from the More Options menu.
Incorrect:
Option B. Stamp
Incorrect. The Stamp functionality is associated with adding or displaying predefined information on a record/form. It is not the menu used to access form templates.
Option C. Paperclip
Incorrect. The Paperclip icon is used for attachments. It allows users to add or manage files attached to the record, not access form templates.
Option D. Pages
Incorrect. Pages is not the Form header element used to access form templates. It is not the appropriate menu for applying predefined form values.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a database setting on the Application Access section of a Table?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The option that‘s not a typical database setting within the Application Access section of a table in ServiceNow:
Can write
Here‘s why:
Database Access: The Application Access section focuses on controlling user permissions for various actions within the ServiceNow application, not directly on the underlying database.
The other options are common database access settings:
Can read: This permission allows users to view records within the table.
Can update: This permission allows users to modify existing records within the table.
Can delete: This permission allows users to delete records from the table.
Can create: This permission allows users to create new records within the table.
While “Can write“ might seem like a synonym for “Can update,“ in the context of ServiceNow application access, it‘s not a standard setting. The specific permissions like “Can update“ provide more granular control over user interactions with table data.

questions.question: Which field type displays records from another table?
questions.explanation: Read more here about field types: https://docs.servicenow.com/en-US/bundle/utah-platform-administration/page/administer/reference-pages/reference/r_FieldTypes.html

questions.question: Which three Variable Types can be added to a Service Catalog Item?
options: Number List, Single Line Text, and Reference
Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The three variable types that can be added to a Service Catalog Item are:
C. Multiple Choice, Select Box, and Checkbox
Here‘s a breakdown of these variable types and why they are suitable for Service Catalog Items:
Multiple Choice: This allows users to select one option from a predefined list. Useful for capturing user preferences or selecting service options.
Select Box: Similar to Multiple Choice, but allows users to see all available options at once. Often used for presenting longer lists.
Checkbox: Enables users to select one or more options from a list. Ideal for collecting various user inputs or service configurations.
The other options are not as commonly used for Service Catalog Items:
True/False: While technically possible, True/False variables might be limiting for capturing user input or service configurations.
Number List: This could be useful in specific situations, but it‘s less common than the other options.
Ordered: Ordered variables are not typically used in Service Catalog Items. They are more suited for displaying information in a specific order.
Reference: References allow users to select existing records from other tables. This might be more appropriate for advanced use cases or selecting existing resources.

questions.question: What ServiceNow feature allows you to include data from a secondary related table on a report?
questions.explanation:
You can dotwalk to related records using Choose columns in the Configure section.
In the example below, I am starting on the incident table, and dotwalking to Assignment Group fields.
(Abbildung im Original)

questions.question: What are examples of UI Actions relating to forms? Select 3 answers.
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
Here‘s a breakdown of why these options are examples of UI Actions relating to forms in ServiceNow:
Form Context Menu: This allows users to right-click on the form header and access additional functionality defined through UI Actions. These actions can be anything from opening a related record to running a custom script.
Form Links: UI Actions can create custom links within the form itself. These links can trigger specific actions when clicked, such as navigating to another form, opening a knowledge base article, or launching a workflow.
Form Buttons: This is a common use case for UI Actions. You can create custom buttons on a form that execute specific code or workflows when clicked. This allows users to perform actions beyond the default form functionalities.
While the other options are not directly related to UI Actions:
Form Columns: These define the fields displayed on a form and are not used for triggering actions.
Form View: This determines how the form is laid out and displayed, but doesn‘t involve interactive elements like UI Actions.

questions.question: What is shown in the image below?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow® Dependency Views maps graphically display CIs that support application or business services and the relationships between the CIs.
A ServiceNow service (application service or business service) is work or goods that are supported by an IT infrastructure. For example, delivering email service to an employee can require services such as email servers, web servers, and the work to configure the user’s account.
A Dependency Views map has one starting point, called the root CI or root node of the map. The root CI is surrounded by a darker frame that repaints itself with a pulsing effect drawing the attention to the root CI. The maps can show both upstream and downstream dependencies for the root CI. By default the Dependency Views map displays 3 levels, both upstream and downstream relationships. Administrators can configure the number of levels displayed. The map collapses and expands clusters to make them easier to view. By default, clusters are collapsed.
In a Dependency Views map, map indicators indicate if a CI has any active, pending issues. You can investigate the tasks that are connected to a CI to get more details. When you return to the map from another form, the system restores the last map viewed, using the default filter and layout settings. When you click the icon (
(Abbildung im Original)
) on a CI record or on a task record that identifies a CI, the map opens.

questions.question: A knowledge article must be which of the following states to display to a user?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
A knowledge article must be in the Published state to display to a user.
Here‘s a breakdown of the different knowledge article states and their implications:
Draft: This is the initial state where the article is being created or edited. Users cannot access articles in this state.
Review: This state might be used for internal review before publishing the article. Users cannot access articles in this state either.
Published: This is the final state where the article is available for users to search and view in the knowledge base.
Pending Retirement: This state indicates that the article is scheduled to be retired (removed) in the future, but it might still be accessible to users depending on the configuration.
Retired: Articles in this state are no longer accessible to users.
Therefore, only published knowledge articles are visible and accessible to users in the ServiceNow knowledge base.

questions.question: While showing a customer their Incident form, they ask to change the Priority field title to display their internal terminology. How would you do that? Select 2 answers.

Right click on Priority and select Configure Label
Right click on Priority and select Configure Display Settings
Right click on Priority and select Configure Column

The two correct options for changing the Priority field title on an incident form to match the customer‘s internal terminology:
Right click on Priority and select Configure Label : This is the most direct approach. “Configure Label“ is often a menu option available when right-clicking on a field label in ServiceNow that allows you to modify the label displayed on the form for a specific table (incident in this case).
Right click on Priority and select Configure Dictionary : While this might seem like a broader option, “Configure Dictionary“ could potentially lead to a dictionary entry where you can modify the label associated with the “Priority“ field. Here‘s why the other options aren‘t the best choices:

questions.question: The Report Designer contains different sections for configuring your report. Which section is used to specify the name of the report, and the table or data source for the report?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The section used to specify the report name and the table or data source for the report in ServiceNow‘s Report Designer is:
D. Data
Here‘s why:
Data: This section is the starting point for defining your report. It‘s where you choose the data source that will populate the report. This can be a ServiceNow table or a pre-defined data source. You can also specify the report name here.
Design: This section focuses on the visual layout and presentation of your report. You can choose the report type (e.g., bar chart, pie chart, table), customize colors, and arrange data elements.
Configure: This section allows you to configure report-specific settings based on the chosen report type. For example, in a bar chart, you might define how data is grouped or aggregated.
Style: This section provides options for fine-tuning the appearance of your report, such as adding titles, legends, and formatting elements like font styles and colors.
Name: While the report name can be entered directly in the interface, it‘s usually specified within the “Data“ section where you configure the report‘s foundation.
Therefore, the “Data“ section serves as the starting point for your report, allowing you to define its name and data source, along with other essential parameters.

questions.question: What ServiceNow feature can be triggered by events, and is used to inform users about activities or updates in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The correct answer is:
Notifications
Here‘s why:
Notifications: Notifications are a core feature in ServiceNow that allows you to send alerts and updates to users based on various triggers or events. These events can be record changes (e.g., incident creation, update), scheduled times, or workflow actions. Notifications can be sent via email, SMS, or internal messaging within ServiceNow.
Events: Events themselves are occurrences within ServiceNow that trigger actions or workflows. Notifications are one way to respond to events and inform users.
Business Rules: Business rules define logic that executes based on events. While business rules can trigger actions like sending notifications, they are not the notifications themselves.
Alerts: Alerts can be a type of notification, but they often refer to more critical or urgent situations.
Texts: Text messages (SMS) can be a delivery channel for notifications, but notifications encompass a broader range of delivery methods (email, internal messaging).
Therefore, Notifications are the ServiceNow feature specifically designed to inform users about activities and updates based on event triggers.

questions.question: When impersonating a user for testing purposes, what is the best way to return to your account?
options: Turn your computer off and on again
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The most efficient way to return to your account after impersonating a user for testing purposes in ServiceNow is:
End Impersonation
Here‘s why:
End Impersonation: ServiceNow typically provides a dedicated “End Impersonation“ option within the user menu or banner. Selecting this option immediately switches you back to your own account without requiring additional steps like logging out or restarting your computer.
Clear browser cache: Clearing the browser cache might not necessarily affect the impersonation session within ServiceNow. It‘s designed to remove temporary internet files, not necessarily user authentication details.
Turn your computer off and on again: This is an extreme and unnecessary step. ServiceNow impersonation is managed within the application itself, and restarting your computer wouldn‘t affect the session.
Log out and back in: While logging out and logging back in would eventually get you back to your account, it‘s a less efficient approach compared to the readily available “End Impersonation“ option.
By using “End Impersonation,“ you can seamlessly switch back to your administrator account and continue working without interrupting your workflow.

questions.question: Which section of the ServiceNow UI allows you to perform a global search?
questions.explanation:
(Abbildung im Original)
The correct answer is: Banner frame

Banner frame: The banner frame typically sits at the top of most ServiceNow pages and includes a global search bar. This allows you to search across various modules and data sources in ServiceNow using keywords.
Content frame: The content frame displays the specific content of the module or record you‘re currently working on. It wouldn‘t contain a global search bar for searching across the entire platform.
Application Navigator: The application navigator provides a menu structure for accessing different modules and functionalities within ServiceNow. While it can help you navigate to specific areas for searching within those modules, it wouldn‘t be used for a general platform-wide search.
Record form: Record forms are used to create or edit individual records within ServiceNow. They might have search functionalities specific to the data within that record, but not for global searches across the entire system.
Therefore, the banner frame with its global search bar is the designated section of the ServiceNow UI for performing a search that encompasses various modules and data sources.

questions.question: A task worker asks how they can monitor any updates occurring to records assigned to him, like responses from customers. What do you suggest?

Open an Agent workspace tab for each record he wants to monitor

Select Service Desk > My Work Dashboard

The best option for the task worker to monitor updates on assigned records, including customer responses, is:
C. On My Work list, select the Activity Stream icon to show a frame with live updates
Here‘s why this is the most suitable solution:
Activity Stream: The activity stream provides a real-time feed of updates and changes made to records assigned to the user. This includes customer replies, notes added by other agents, or any modifications to the record itself.
The other options are less effective for live monitoring:
A. Click on the eyeglass icon to expand the Monitor frame: While the monitor frame might display information about specific records, it wouldn‘t necessarily offer a live feed of updates unless specifically configured for that purpose.
B. Open an Agent workspace tab for each record he wants to monitor: This approach can be very cumbersome and impractical, especially if the task worker has many assigned records.
D. Select Service Desk > My Work Dashboard: Dashboards typically provide an overview of assigned tasks and metrics, but they might not offer real-time updates on individual records unless specifically designed with that functionality.
By using the activity stream within “My Work“ list, the task worker can efficiently monitor all updates on their assigned records in a centralized location.

Categories provide a hierarchical structure for organizing knowledge articles based on a specific topic or area. This allows users to efficiently locate relevant articles by browsing through categories that align with their needs.
