questions.question: What do client request + server response =?
questions.explanation:
The equation client request + server response = round trip accurately represents communication between a client and a server.
Here’s the breakdown:
• Client request: The initial action initiated by a client (like a web browser) sending data or instructions to the server.
• Server response: The server processes the request, performs the necessary actions, and sends data or a response back to the client.
This exchange between client and server constitutes a single round trip. The client waits for the server’s response before proceeding further.
Here’s why the other options are not as fitting:
• Single trip: While a single request-response pair is involved, it’s not a “trip” in the communication sense since the client expects a response.
• Multiple trip: This might imply multiple back-and-forth exchanges beyond a single request-response cycle.
• None of the above: A round trip is the most appropriate term for this fundamental client-server interaction.

questions.question: In Service Catalog, when a user orders several Items, following records are created: (Select three that Apply)
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. SCTASK Correct because Service Catalog Tasks (SCTASK) are created to track the fulfillment steps required for catalog items. Each item ordered can generate one or more tasks depending on the workflow.
• Option C. REQ Correct because a Request (REQ) record is created to represent the overall service catalog request submitted by the user. It acts as the parent record for all requested items.
• Option E. RITM Correct because a Requested Item (RITM) record is created for each catalog item ordered. It is linked to the parent request (REQ) and may generate associated tasks (SCTASK).
Incorrect
• Option B. CHG Incorrect because Change (CHG) records are not automatically created when ordering catalog items. They are part of Change Management, not Service Catalog fulfillment.
• Option D. INC Incorrect because Incident (INC) records are not created by default when ordering catalog items. Incidents are part of ITSM processes for issue tracking, not catalog requests.

questions.question: When you open a service catalog and click the order button what gets created?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. REQ > RITM > TASK Correct because in ServiceNow, when a user places an order through the Service Catalog, the system generates a Request (REQ), which contains one or more Requested Items (RITM), and each RITM can generate one or more Tasks. This hierarchy ensures proper tracking and fulfillment of catalog requests.
Incorrect
• Option B. Task Incorrect because while tasks are created as part of the fulfillment process, they are not the first or only record created. Tasks are generated under RITMs, which are part of the REQ structure.
• Option C. Item Incorrect because the catalog item is what the user selects, but the system does not create a record simply called “Item.” Instead, it creates the structured hierarchy of REQ > RITM > TASK.

questions.question: What does specifying a coalesce mean?
options: It's a special data set brought over using a different module
Make the report that will feed the gauge
The field or fields you specify will be used as a unique key
questions.explanation:
In ServiceNow, specifying a coalesce means the field or fields you specify will be used as a unique key when importing data.
Here’s a breakdown of what coalescing does:
• Unique Key: When you set a field as a coalesce field during data import, it acts like a unique identifier for that record. ServiceNow uses this field (or combination of fields) to determine if an existing record exists in the target table.
• Matching: During the import process, ServiceNow compares the values in the coalesce field(s) of the import set record with the corresponding field(s) in existing records of the target table.
• Update or Create: If a matching record is found based on the coalesce field values, the existing record in the target table is updated with the new data from the import set. However, if no match is found, a new record is created in the target table using the data from the import set.
This approach helps ensure data integrity and avoids creating duplicate records during data imports.
Here’s why the other options are not relevant to coalescing:
• Special data set brought over using a different module: Coalescing is a functionality within the import process itself, not involving separate modules.
• Make the report that will feed the gauge: Coalescing is specifically for data import and record matching, not report generation for gauges.
• None of the above: While the other options aren’t directly related to coalescing, specifying a coalesce field does play a crucial role in establishing record uniqueness during data imports.

questions.question: A role does not inherit all the permissions of any other roles it includes.
questions.explanation:
The statement is FALSE. In ServiceNow, a role can inherit permissions from other roles it includes. This is a key feature for managing user access efficiently.
Here’s why the other option is incorrect:
• TRUE: Roles can inherit permissions from other roles included in their definition. This allows you to build more complex access controls by combining permissions from various roles.
By inheriting permissions, you can create a hierarchy of roles, where higher-level roles have all the permissions of lower-level roles they include, plus any additional permissions specific to the higher role.

questions.question: What is contextual security?

It's a group of customizations that can be packaged and moved from one instance to another

C. It’s a system security type, which Controls every level in the ServiceNow object hierarchy. You can control specific tables and fields.
Contextual security in ServiceNow provides granular access control over data within the platform.
It allows you to define permissions based on specific conditions, giving you more control over who can see and modify data.
Here’s a breakdown of why the other options are incorrect:
• A. Means the field has been modified: This describes a field state, not a security concept.
• B. Display information from a record: While contextual security can affect what information is displayed, its primary purpose is access control.
• D. It’s a group of customizations that can be packaged and moved from one instance to another: This describes an Update Set, a different feature for managing customizations.

questions.question: Client Script on the Task table will be applied to Problem table as well
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is Only if inherit is true.
Here’s why:
• Client scripts are defined on specific tables. By default, they only apply to the table they are defined on.
• The “Inherit” checkbox on a client script allows it to be inherited by child tables. When checked, the script will run on the parent table (where it’s defined) and any child tables that extend it.
• Task is a parent table to many others, including Problem.
Therefore, for a client script defined on the Task table to apply to the Problem table as well, the “Inherit” checkbox on the script must be marked.

questions.question: What module in the Service Catalog application does an Administrator access to begin creating a new item?
questions.explanation:

To create a new catalog item in ServiceNow, an administrator would typically access the Maintain Items module within the Service Catalog application. This module provides the necessary tools and options to define the attributes, variables, and workflows associated with a catalog item.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• B. Maintain Categories: This module is used to manage categories within the Service Catalog, helping to organize and classify catalog items.
• C. Content Items: This module is not directly related to creating catalog items. It might be used for managing knowledge articles or other content within the Service Catalog.

questions.question: Which is true regarding Knowledge Base?
options: In a Knowledge base, articles are grouped according to categories.

• Product: Grouping articles by specific products or services
• Process: Grouping articles related to specific business processes

questions.question: Which of the following statement is TRUE about sys_dictionary?
options: sys_dictionary is a table where all the details about the fields are stored
sys_dictionary is a field and used for make field mandatory
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. sys_dictionary is a table where all the details about the fields are stored
The sys_dictionary table in ServiceNow is a crucial system table that stores metadata about all fields in the platform. This includes information such as:
• Field name: The unique identifier of the field.
• Data type: The type of data the field can store (e.g., string, integer, date).
• Mandatory flag: Whether the field is mandatory or optional.
• Display name: The label displayed for the field on forms and lists.
• Help text: Additional information or instructions for the field.
• Reference field: If the field references another table, the target table is specified.
• Validation rules: Any validation rules or constraints applied to the field.
By understanding the structure of the sys_dictionary table, administrators can customize and extend the functionality of ServiceNow. However, it’s important to exercise caution when making direct modifications to this table, as it can have unintended consequences.

questions.question: To generate task based records through service request which is the correct option below?
questions.explanation:
A Record Producer is correct because it allows users to create task-based records through a service request. A Record Producer is essentially a form within ServiceNow that offers an alternative way to create records for a specific table. Users can complete the form to generate incident records, change requests, and so on, directly from the service catalog.
Let’s briefly touch on why the other options are incorrect:
A. UI Action: UI Actions are buttons, links, or context menu items that execute actions, but they don’t directly generate task-based records from service requests.
C. Service Catalog: While it contains Record Producers, the Service Catalog itself is not the mechanism for generating records. It is more of a container or organizer for these types of functionalities.
D. UI Policy: UI Policies manage the behavior and appearance of fields on forms, but they do not generate task-based records through service requests.
E. Business Rule: Business Rules are server-side scripts that run when records are inserted, updated, or deleted. They are more about automation and logic execution rather than direct record creation through service requests.

questions.question: Which of the following are a type of client scripts supported in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct Options
A. onLoad:
• Explanation: This type of client script runs when a form is loaded. It is used to perform actions or validations when a form is initially displayed to the user.
B. onSubmit:
• Explanation: This client script runs when a form is submitted. It is used to validate the data or perform actions right before the form data is sent to the server.
C. onCellEdit:
• Explanation: This type of client script is executed when a cell in a list is edited. It is specifically for list-based actions rather than form-based ones.
E. onChange:
• Explanation: This client script runs when a particular field’s value changes on a form. It is used to perform actions or validations based on the new value of the field.
Incorrect Options
D. onUpdate:
• Explanation: This is not a type of client script. “onUpdate” is commonly used in business rules and it runs when a record is updated in the database.
F. onSave:
• Explanation: This is not a recognized client script type in ServiceNow. “onSave” is not a valid event for client scripts.
Client scripts are a powerful tool in ServiceNow for enhancing user experience and ensuring data integrity on the client side. Each type serves a specific purpose and allows for various interactions and validations on forms and lists.

questions.question: Which of the following is true?
options: When moved from left to right slush bucket, referance fields get deleted
Deleted system tables will be created again during an instance upgrade

System tables are core tables that are essential for the functioning of ServiceNow. These tables cannot be deleted, as they are integral to the platform’s operations.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• B. When moved from left to right slush bucket, referance fields get deleted: Moving a field from the left to the right slush bucket during table customization hides the field, but it doesn’t delete it. The field still exists in the database and can be made visible again.
• C. Deleted system tables will be created again during an instance upgrade: While ServiceNow upgrades can restore certain system configurations, it’s not guaranteed that deleted system tables will be recreated. Deleting system tables can lead to significant issues and instability in the instance.

questions.question: If the system administrator wants to modify the homepage, which of the following links on the page indicates that this can be done?

• C. Make Gauge: This option is specific to creating performance analytics gauges and is not relevant to customizing the homepage layout.

questions.question: Out of the below listed applications, which will not run natively on smartphones?

questions.question: The baseline Service Catalog homepage contains links to which of the following components?

Record Producers, Order Guides, and Item Variables

questions.question: In a workflow, what is the workflow timeline?
options: Defines unique key for record. If record found, import will update the record. If not found, import will create a new record.
Shows the progress of a workflow. It provides a complete time-based display of activities associated with workflow context.
An automation block such as approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers and utilities
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. Shows the progress of a workflow. It provides a complete time-based display of activities associated with workflow context.
A workflow timeline in ServiceNow provides a visual representation of the progress of a workflow instance. It shows the sequence of activities, the time taken for each activity, and any delays or bottlenecks. This helps in understanding the overall workflow execution and identifying areas for improvement.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. Defines unique key for record. If record found, import will update the record. If not found, import will create a new record: This describes the concept of a unique identifier and data import process, which is not directly related to workflow timelines.
• C. An automation block such as approvals, conditions, notifications, tasks, timers and utilities: This describes the various elements that can be used to build a workflow, but it’s not specifically the workflow timeline.

questions.question: What does a request number in Service Catalog represent?
options: It represents the individual item in the order.
It represents the task to complete.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. It represents the order number
• Correct because the request number (REQ) in ServiceNow Service Catalog represents the overall order placed by a user.
• It is the unique identifier for the entire request, which may contain multiple items.
• Example: If a user orders a laptop and software, both items are tied to the same request number, showing they belong to one order.
Incorrect
Option B. It represents the individual item in the order.
• Incorrect because individual items in a request are tracked by Request Item numbers (RITM), not the request number itself.
• The REQ groups all items together, while RITMs represent each catalog item separately.
Option C. It represents the task to complete.
• Incorrect because tasks generated from catalog items are tracked as TASK numbers, not request numbers.
• Tasks are linked to RITMs, which in turn roll up to the REQ.

questions.question: What defines conditions that are evaluated against users to determine which users can access Service Catalog items?
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. User Criteria
User Criteria is a feature within ServiceNow that allows you to define specific conditions to determine which users can access particular Service Catalog items. By setting up user criteria, you can control visibility and eligibility for items based on various factors, such as:
• User Roles: Restricting access to specific roles or groups of users.
• User Groups: Limiting access to members of particular user groups.
• User Attributes: Filtering access based on user attributes like department, location, or job title.
This provides a flexible and granular way to manage access to Service Catalog items, ensuring that only authorized users can view and request specific services.

questions.question: An outbound SOAP message is defined. Which function can invoke the SOAP message?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. UI Action
UI Actions can be configured to trigger various actions, including sending outbound SOAP messages. By defining specific conditions and scripts within a UI Action, you can initiate SOAP calls to external systems when certain events occur, such as:
• A record being created or updated
• A button being clicked on a form or list
• A specific condition being met
This allows for integration with other systems and automation of tasks based on data exchange.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. UI Policy: UI Policies are used to control the visibility and behavior of UI elements on forms and lists. They are not directly used to trigger outbound SOAP messages.
• B. Data Policy: Data Policies are used to enforce data integrity and security rules. They are not designed to initiate outbound communication.

questions.question: Which table defines what conditions trigger an SLA?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. contract_sla
• Correct because the contract_sla table defines the conditions that trigger an SLA in ServiceNow.
• This table stores the SLA definitions, including rules such as when an SLA should start, pause, stop, or reset.
• It is the central configuration point for SLA policies and conditions.
Incorrect
Option B. task_sla
• Incorrect because the task_sla table tracks the actual SLA records applied to tasks (like incidents or requests).
• It does not define the conditions; instead, it records SLA progress and compliance once triggered.
Option C. sla_condition_class_list
• Incorrect because this is not the table used to define SLA conditions. It is a distractor option and not part of the standard SLA configuration in ServiceNow.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to initiate a flow?
questions.explanation:
A. An Event
Incorrect Option: While events can be used in ServiceNow to trigger flows, they are not the primary method for initiating a flow. Events are more about signaling that something has occurred within the system, and while they can be part of a flow’s design, they do not directly initiate a flow on their own.
B. A spoke
Incorrect Option: A spoke refers to a set of actions or integrations that are packaged together for use in Flow Designer, particularly for integration with third-party applications or services. Spokes provide reusable components but do not initiate flows themselves.
C. Trigger
Correct Option: A trigger is the primary mechanism used to initiate a flow in ServiceNow. Triggers define the conditions under which a flow should start executing, such as when a record is created, updated, or deleted, or when an event occurs. This makes “Trigger” the correct answer as it directly relates to starting flows.
D. Core Action
Incorrect Option: Core actions are operations that can be performed within a flow once it has been initiated (such as sending notifications or updating records) but do not serve as initiation points for flows themselves. They are part of the flow’s execution rather than its initiation.

questions.question: On any ServiceNow instance, which of the following allows a user to edit field values in a list without opening the form?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. List Editor
• Correct because the List Editor feature in ServiceNow allows inline editing of field values directly within a list view.
• Users can update multiple records quickly without opening each record’s form individually.
• This is the intended functionality for efficient bulk editing in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option B. Data Editor
• Incorrect because there is no feature called “Data Editor” in ServiceNow.
• This is a distractor option and not part of the CSA exam’s valid terminology.
Option C. Form Designer
• Incorrect because Form Designer is used to design and configure forms (adding/removing fields, sections, layout changes).
• It does not allow inline editing of list values.
Option D. Edit Menu
• Incorrect because the Edit Menu provides options for editing or configuring lists/forms but does not enable inline editing of field values.
• Inline editing is specifically handled by the List Editor.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements describes the contents of the Configuration Management Database (CMDB)? A. The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets B. The CMDB contains the Business Rules that direct the intangible, configurable assets used by a company C. The CMDB archives all Service Management PaaS equipment metadata and usage statistics D. The CMDB contains ITIL process data pertaining to configuration items
questions.explanation:
A. The CMDB contains data about tangible and intangible business assets
A Configuration Management Database (CMDB) is a repository of information about all the IT assets within an organization. This includes both tangible assets like hardware (servers, routers, switches) and intangible assets like software (applications, databases) and services. By maintaining accurate and up-to-date information about these assets, organizations can better manage their IT infrastructure, improve service delivery, and reduce downtime.

questions.question: Which of the following can be performed by inbound email action?
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Create or update task record
Inbound Actions in ServiceNow are designed to process incoming emails and trigger specific actions within the platform. One of the most common use cases is creating or updating records, such as incidents or tasks.
By defining rules and conditions in the Inbound Action, you can:
• Create new records: Extract relevant information from the email and create a new record, such as an incident or task.
• Update existing records: Identify existing records based on specific criteria (e.g., reference numbers) and update them with information from the email.
Here’s why the other option is incorrect:
• B. Validate a form: While Inbound Actions can be used to trigger workflows and business rules that may include form validation, they are not directly designed to validate forms themselves. Form validation is typically handled by client-side scripts, server-side scripts, or UI policies.

questions.question: Which of the following statement describes the purpose of an Order Guide in ServiceNow platform?
options: Order Guide provide the ability to order multiple, related items as one request
Order Guide provide a list of guidelines for Administrators on how to set up item variables
Order Guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Order Guide provide the ability to order multiple, related items as one request
An Order Guide in ServiceNow is a powerful tool that enables users to order multiple related items as part of a single request. It provides a structured and guided process for placing complex orders, streamlining the request fulfillment process.
Here’s a breakdown of why the other options are incorrect:
• B. Order Guide provide a list of guidelines for Administrators on how to set up item variables: While Order Guides can involve item variables, their primary purpose is not to provide guidelines for administrators. They are designed to guide end-users through the ordering process.
• C. Order Guides restrict the number of items in an order to only one item per request: Order Guides are specifically designed to handle multiple items within a single order. They allow for complex configurations and dependencies between items.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true characteristics for workflows in service catalog?
options: The start & end activities in workflows can be changed.
Workflows can have a maximum of five rounds of approval actions.
Only one rollback activities is allowed in a workflow
Workflows can have a multiple rounds of approval actions.
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Workflows can have a multiple rounds of approval actions.
ServiceNow workflows are highly flexible and can accommodate multiple rounds of approvals, allowing for complex decision-making processes. You can configure workflows with multiple approval stages, each with its own set of conditions and approvers.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. The start & end activities in workflows can be changed: While you can modify the workflow design, changing the start and end activities is not typically recommended as it can disrupt the overall flow.
• B. Workflows can have a maximum of five rounds of approval actions: There’s no strict limit on the number of approval rounds in a workflow. You can configure as many rounds as needed based on your specific business requirements.
• C. Only one rollback activities is allowed in a workflow: You can include multiple rollback activities in a workflow to handle different scenarios and error conditions.

questions.question: What are the UI components of a homepage?
options: Banner, Content pane and Application Navigator
Banner, Content pane, Header and Application Navigator
Banner, Content pane, Header, Footer and Application Navigator
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A: Banner, Content pane and Application Navigator
The Logic: These are the three fundamental pillars of the ServiceNow classic UI.
Banner Frame: Located at the top, it contains the logo, user profile, global search, and system settings.
Application Navigator (Left Nav): Provides links to all applications and modules available to the user.
Content Pane: The central area where data, forms, lists, and dashboards (or homepages) are displayed.
Incorrect
Option B: Banner, Content pane, Header and Application Navigator
Reasoning: In ServiceNow terminology, the “Header” is functionally part of the Banner Frame. Listing it as a separate standalone UI component alongside the Banner is redundant and technically inaccurate within the context of the platform’s core architecture.
Option C: Banner, Content pane, Header, Footer and Application Navigator
Reasoning: While some web applications utilize a “Footer,” the standard ServiceNow interface is designed as a workspace that maximizes vertical space. There is no official “Footer” component recognized as a primary UI framework element in the CSA curriculum.

questions.question: Button, Related Links and Context Menu are part of?
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. UI Action
UI Actions are used to create buttons, links, and context menu items that trigger specific actions within ServiceNow. They can be displayed in various locations on forms, lists, and records.
Here’s a breakdown of why the other options are incorrect:
• A. Form: A form is the visual layout of a record, but it doesn’t directly define the actions that can be performed on the record.
• C. Client Script: Client scripts are used to manipulate the client-side behavior of ServiceNow forms and lists. They can be used to dynamically modify the UI, but they don’t directly create buttons or links.
• D. UI Page: UI Pages are used to create custom web pages within ServiceNow, but they are not used to create buttons or links in the context of forms and lists.

questions.question: Is it true that all users can manage and setup import sets?
questions.explanation:
FALSE
Not all users can manage and set up import sets in ServiceNow. This is typically a task for administrators or users with specific permissions. The ability to create, modify, and run import sets is controlled by role-based access control.
Only users with appropriate roles, such as the admin role or custom roles with the necessary permissions, can perform these actions. This restriction helps to maintain data integrity and security within the ServiceNow instance.

questions.question: Variable sets can be used in which of the below options? Choose all that apply.
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Record Producer, B. Order Guides, and C. Catalog Items
Variable sets are reusable collections of variables that can be added to various ServiceNow records, including:
• Record Producers: To streamline the creation of records by providing a consistent set of fields.
• Order Guides: To guide users through a series of steps and collect necessary information for fulfilling requests.
• Catalog Items: To define the attributes and options for items offered in the Service Catalog.
Incidents are typically created through incident forms, which may include variables but are not directly associated with variable sets.

questions.question: How to differentiate SLA, OLA and underpinning contracts based on which options below?
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Type
The Type field is used to differentiate between SLAs, OLAs, and Underpinning Contracts (UCs) in ServiceNow. By specifying the appropriate type, you can define the specific terms, metrics, and conditions associated with each type of agreement.
Here’s a breakdown of why the other options are incorrect:
• A. sys_id: This is a unique identifier for each record in ServiceNow, but it doesn’t differentiate between SLA, OLA, and UC types.
• B. configuration item: Configuration items are assets or services that are managed in the CMDB. While SLAs, OLAs, and UCs may be associated with CIs, the type field is the primary differentiator.
• C. meta-type: This is a technical field used to categorize different types of records in ServiceNow. It’s not directly used to differentiate between SLAs, OLAs, and UCs.

questions.question: In SLA, a “retroactive start” allows setting the start time to a time from an earlier event?
questions.explanation:
TRUE
A retroactive start in ServiceNow SLAs allows you to set the start time of an SLA to a time prior to the actual creation of the record. This is useful in scenarios where the SLA should start counting from a specific event or time, such as:
• Incident creation time: The SLA can start when the incident is first reported, even if the record is created later in the system.
• Email receipt time: The SLA can start when an email is received, regardless of when the incident record is created.
• Other specific events: You can define custom conditions to trigger the start of the SLA based on various events within your workflow.

questions.question: What details does a knowledge article hold? (Select three that apply)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Troubleshooting tips
• Correct because knowledge articles provide step‑by‑step troubleshooting guidance to resolve issues.
Option B. Known errors
• Correct because knowledge articles document known errors to help users identify recurring problems.
Option C. User Solutions
• Correct because knowledge articles capture solutions contributed by users or support teams to resolve specific issues.
Incorrect
Option D. All of the above
• Incorrect because not all listed options are valid. “User information” is not part of a knowledge article’s details, so “All of the above” cannot be correct.
Option E. User information
• Incorrect because knowledge articles do not store personal user information. They are focused on technical content such as errors, solutions, and troubleshooting steps.

questions.question: What are the 3 components of the Now Platform User Interface?
questions.explanation:
The 3 main components of the Now Platform User Interface are:
• Application Navigator: This is the left-hand sidebar that provides a hierarchical view of all applications and modules available to the user.
• Banner: This is the topmost section that displays the ServiceNow logo, company name, and other branding elements.
• Content Frame: This is the main area where the actual content of the application is displayed.

questions.question: Which of the following belongs to Service Catalog
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. Variables Correct. Variables are part of the Service Catalog. They allow customization of catalog items by capturing user input (e.g., text fields, checkboxes, dropdowns) when submitting a request.
• Option B. Catalog Items Correct. Catalog Items are the core of the Service Catalog. They represent the goods or services offered to users (e.g., request a laptop, software installation).
• Option D. Record Producers Correct. Record Producers are also part of the Service Catalog. They provide a way to create records in tables (like incidents or change requests) through a simplified catalog interface.
Incorrect
• Option C. Change tasks Incorrect. Change tasks belong to the Change Management application, not the Service Catalog. They are used to track work related to change requests, not catalog requests.

questions.question: A variable set can be used in multiple catalog Items
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. TRUE
Yes, a variable set can be used in multiple catalog items. This is one of the key benefits of using variable sets. By creating and maintaining a single variable set, you can reuse the same set of variables across multiple catalog items. This promotes consistency, reduces redundancy, and simplifies maintenance.
When you add a variable set to a catalog item, the variables within that set become available for use on the catalog item form. This allows you to quickly and easily add complex forms to your catalog items without having to create each variable individually.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is TRUE for a field on an audited table?
options: Add "no_audit = true" to attribute for exclude from auditing
Add "no_audit = 0" to attribute for exclude from auditing
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Add “no_audit = true” to attribute for exclude from auditing
To exclude a field from being audited in ServiceNow, you need to add the attribute no_audit = true to the field definition. This tells the system to not track changes to that specific field.
Here’s why the other option is incorrect:
• B. Add “no_audit = 0” to attribute for exclude from auditing: This is not a valid syntax for excluding a field from auditing. The correct syntax is no_audit = true.
By using the no_audit attribute, you can selectively control which fields are audited, helping to optimize performance and reduce storage requirements.

questions.question: How to make a field mandatory at data base level, before updating or inserting?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Data Policy
Data Policies are used to enforce data integrity and security rules at the database level. By creating a data policy, you can ensure that certain fields are always populated with valid data before a record is created or updated.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. UI Policy: UI Policies are used to control the behavior of UI elements on forms and lists. While they can be used to make fields mandatory on a form, they don’t enforce mandatory fields at the database level.
• B. Client Scripts: Client Scripts are used to manipulate the client-side behavior of ServiceNow forms and lists. They can validate input and display error messages, but they cannot prevent invalid data from being saved to the database.

questions.question: SLA, OLA and UC are related to?
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Service Level Management
SLAs (Service Level Agreements), OLAs (Operational Level Agreements), and UCs (Underpinning Contracts) are all key concepts within Service Level Management. They are used to define, measure, and manage the quality of IT services.
• SLA: An agreement between a service provider and a customer that defines the expected level of service.
• OLA: An agreement between internal teams within an organization that outlines how they will collaborate to deliver services.
• UC: A contract between a service provider and a third-party supplier.
These agreements help ensure that services are delivered efficiently, effectively, and in accordance with agreed-upon standards.

questions.question: _ application menu has the details about the upgrades in the system
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. Upgrade History
The Upgrade History application menu in ServiceNow provides detailed information about the upgrade history of your instance. This includes:
• Upgrade versions: A list of previous and current versions of ServiceNow installed on your instance.
• Upgrade dates: The dates when each upgrade was performed.
• Upgrade notes: Important information and instructions related to each upgrade.
• Patch information: Details about any patches or hotfixes applied to the instance.
By reviewing the Upgrade History, you can track the evolution of your ServiceNow instance, identify potential issues, and plan for future upgrades.
The other options are not directly related to upgrade history:
• B. Documentation: This menu typically provides access to general documentation and help resources for ServiceNow.
• C. Upgrades: This menu might be used to initiate or manage upgrades, but it doesn’t provide a detailed history of past upgrades.
• D. History: This could refer to various types of history, such as change history or audit logs, but it’s not specifically related to upgrade history.

questions.question: By default in ServiceNow, what customization’s are added to Update Sets?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Changes made to a form.
By default, ServiceNow automatically captures changes made to forms in update sets. This includes modifications to form layouts, field configurations, UI policies, and client scripts.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. Changes made to a schedule: Changes to schedules are not automatically captured in update sets. You need to manually add them to the update set.
• B. Changes made to data: Changes to individual records (data) are not captured in update sets. Update sets are primarily for configuration changes.
• D. Changes made to a homepage: Changes to homepage layouts and content are not automatically captured. You need to manually add them to the update set.

questions.question: What are the ways to Create CMDB data
questions.explanation:
The correct options for creating CMDB data are:
A. Discovery C. Import Set D. Manual
Here’s a breakdown of each option:
• Discovery: ServiceNow Discovery is an automated tool that can scan your IT infrastructure and automatically populate the CMDB with information about devices, software, and network configurations.
• Import Set: You can import data from external sources, such as CSV files or other systems, into the CMDB using Import Sets.
• Manual: You can manually create and update CMDB records through the ServiceNow user interface. This is typically used for one-off records or for data that cannot be automated.
B. Help the Help Desk: While Help Desk can provide information about IT assets, it’s not a direct method for creating CMDB data.

questions.question: Which of the following are captured in update set
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Table Creation and D. Field Creation
Update Sets in ServiceNow are used to package and transport configuration changes between instances. They capture changes to various aspects of the ServiceNow configuration, including:
• Tables: Changes to table structures, fields, and ACLs are included.
• Fields: Creation, modification, and deletion of fields are captured.
Why not A and B?
• A. Group Creation: Changes to groups and users are typically managed through the user interface and are not directly captured in update sets.
• B. Incident Creation: Changes to individual records, like incidents, are not captured in update sets. Update sets primarily focus on configuration changes, not data changes.

questions.question: Server side scripting is used in which of the following? (Select all that Apply)
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. Script include Correct. Script Includes are reusable server‑side scripts that can be called from other server‑side code (like Business Rules) or even from client‑side code via GlideAjax. They run on the server and are a key part of server‑side scripting in ServiceNow.
• Option D. Business rule Correct. Business Rules are server‑side scripts that execute when records are inserted, updated, deleted, or queried. They enforce business logic and data consistency, making them a core example of server‑side scripting.
Incorrect
• Option B. UI Policy Incorrect because UI Policies are primarily client‑side. They dynamically change form behavior (like making fields mandatory or visible) in the browser, not on the server.
• Option C. Client script Incorrect because Client Scripts run in the user’s browser. They handle form field validation, dynamic field changes, and user interactions, but they are not server‑side.

questions.question: Which would NOT appear in the History section of the Application navigator?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. UI Pages
The History section of the Application Navigator displays a list of recently accessed records, lists, and forms. It’s a quick way to navigate back to previously viewed items.
UI Pages are not directly associated with records or lists. They are underlying web pages that provide the structure and content for forms and other UI elements. Therefore, they wouldn’t appear in the History section.

questions.question: Personlizing a list for an individual user will not affect other users list layout
questions.explanation:
TRUE
Personalizing a list view in ServiceNow is a user-specific setting. When a user personalizes a list view, it only affects their own view of the list. Other users will continue to see the default list view or any other personalized view that they have saved.
This ensures that individual users can tailor their ServiceNow experience to their specific needs and preferences without impacting other users.

questions.question: Where will a user find option to edit a list in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. List control
The List control is the primary mechanism for customizing list views in ServiceNow. By accessing the list control, users can:
• Choose which fields to display: Select the most relevant fields to show in the list view.
• Reorder columns: Rearrange the order of columns to prioritize the information needed.
• Resize columns: Adjust the width of columns to fit the screen size and viewing preferences.
• Save custom views: Save personalized views for future use.
The Grid control is a visual representation of the data in a list view. While it allows for basic interactions like sorting and filtering, it doesn’t provide the same level of customization as the list control.

questions.question: Groups are stored in which table
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
B. sys_user_group:
• sys_user_group: In ServiceNow, groups are stored in the sys_user_group table. This table contains all the information related to user groups, including their names, descriptions, and members. User groups are essential for managing permissions, roles, and access control within the platform.
Incorrect Options:
A. user_group:
• Incorrect. There is no table named user_group in ServiceNow for storing groups. The correct table is sys_user_group.
C. group:
• Incorrect. The table group does not exist in ServiceNow for storing group information. The correct table is sys_user_group.
D. sys_group:
• Incorrect. The table sys_group does not exist in ServiceNow for storing group information. The correct table is sys_user_group.

questions.question: Which one statement correctly describes Access Control rule evaluation?
options: If more than one rule applies to a row, the older rule is evaluated first
Rules are evaluated using roles. The role with the most permissions evaluates the rules first
If a row level rule and a field level rule exist, both rules must be true before an operation is allowed
Rules are evaluated from the general to the specific, so a table rule must be active to continue
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. If a row level rule and a field level rule exist, both rules must be true before an operation is allowed
In ServiceNow, Access Control Rules (ACLs) are evaluated in a hierarchical manner. If multiple rules apply to a specific record or field, the following logic is used:
• Row-level rules: These rules apply to the entire record and are evaluated first.
• Field-level rules: These rules apply to specific fields within a record.
Both row-level and field-level rules must be satisfied for an operation (like viewing, editing, or deleting) to be allowed. If either rule is not met, the operation will be denied.
Here’s why the other options are incorrect:
• A. If more than one rule applies to a row, the older rule is evaluated first: The order of evaluation is based on the specificity of the rule, not the creation date.
• B. Rules are evaluated using roles. The role with the most permissions evaluates the rules first: While roles play a role in determining access, the evaluation of ACLs is based on the specific conditions defined in the rules themselves.
• D. Rules are evaluated from the general to the specific, so a table rule must be active to continue: This is partially correct, but it’s important to note that both row-level and field-level rules must be satisfied, regardless of their order.

questions.question: Knowledge process consists of which of the below components?
options: document creation, approval and review from SMEs and publishing
document creation, approval and review from SMEs
questions.explanation:
Answer: A. document creation, approval and review from SMEs and publishing
A comprehensive knowledge process in ServiceNow typically involves the following key steps:
• Document Creation: Authoring new knowledge articles or updating existing ones.
• Approval and Review: Submitting articles for review and approval by subject matter experts (SMEs).
• Publishing: Making approved articles accessible to end-users through various channels, such as the Service Portal or knowledge search.

questions.question: How is the knowledge base populated? Choose the right answer.
options: The problem application plugin has a workaround feature.
You can develop a business rule that generates a news item.
questions.explanation:
Correct:
Option C. Importing existing articles
The ServiceNow Knowledge Base can be populated by importing existing knowledge articles using import sets or migration tools. This is a standard and supported method to bring pre-existing documentation into the Knowledge Management module, making it available for users to search and consume.
Incorrect:
Option A. Using update sets
Update sets are used to migrate configuration changes between instances, not to populate or manage knowledge article content.
Option B. The problem application plugin has a workaround feature
While problems can have workarounds, this feature does not automatically populate the Knowledge Base. Knowledge articles must be created or imported explicitly.
Option D. You can develop a business rule that generates a news item
News items are separate from Knowledge Management and do not populate the Knowledge Base.
Option E. From an existing problem record
Although a knowledge article can be manually created based on a problem record, a problem record by itself does not automatically populate the Knowledge Base.

questions.question: Links, buttons, context menu action belongs to?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. UI action
• Correct because UI Actions in ServiceNow are used to add links, buttons, and context menu items to forms and lists.
• They allow administrators to trigger scripts or redirect users to perform specific actions.
• This is the right answer since the question explicitly mentions links, buttons, and context menu actions.
Incorrect
Option A. Form
• Incorrect because a form is the structure used to display and edit records.
• While forms can contain buttons or links, those elements are created through UI Actions, not the form itself.
Option B. Client script
• Incorrect because client scripts are used to run JavaScript in the browser to manipulate form fields, validate data, or respond to user input.
• They do not directly create links, buttons, or context menu actions.

questions.question: LDAP comes auto configured with company ServiceNow vendor instance
questions.explanation:
FALSE.
LDAP (Lightweight Directory Access Protocol) integration is not automatically configured with a ServiceNow instance. It requires manual configuration, including setting up connection parameters, user synchronization rules, and authentication settings.

questions.question: Which is true regarding Knowledge Base?
options: In a Knowledge base, articles are grouped according to categories.
In a Knowledge base, articles are grouped according to users.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A. In a Knowledge base, articles are grouped according to categories.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Correct: Knowledge base articles are typically organized into categories based on topics or subjects. This helps users find relevant information more easily.
B. Incorrect: Articles are not grouped according to users. They are grouped based on their content and relevance.

questions.question: Can we draw multiple transitions from a single activity in workflow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option B. TRUE Correct. In ServiceNow workflows, you can draw multiple transitions from a single activity. This is especially useful when defining different paths based on conditions or approvals. For example, from an approval activity, you can have one transition for “Approved” and another for “Rejected,” allowing the workflow to branch accordingly.
Incorrect
• Option A. No Incorrect because ServiceNow workflow activities are designed to support multiple transitions. Restricting to only one transition would prevent workflows from handling branching logic, which is a core capability of the workflow engine.

questions.question: Fill in the blank: _____ is any content created using the ServiceNow knowledge base.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is D. Article.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: While blogs can be created on ServiceNow, they are typically not considered part of the Knowledge Base.
B. Incorrect: News items are used for time-sensitive announcements and notifications. They are not the same as Knowledge Base articles.
C. Incorrect: Posts are not a specific term used for Knowledge Base content.
D. Correct: Knowledge Base articles are the primary content type within the Knowledge Base. They contain information, solutions, and best practices that can be shared with users.

questions.question: Choose the table name where business rule information is stored in a ServiceNow instance.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. “sys_script” table
• Correct because all Business Rules in ServiceNow are stored in the sys_script table.
• This table contains the logic for automation that runs on records when they are inserted, updated, deleted, or queried.
• It is the authoritative source for business rule definitions in a ServiceNow instance.
Incorrect
Option A. “sys_include” table
• Incorrect because sys_include is not related to business rules.
• It is not used for storing automation logic; instead, business rules are exclusively stored in sys_script.
Option C. “sys_script_include” table
• Incorrect because sys_script_include stores Script Includes, which are reusable server‑side functions written in JavaScript.
• Script Includes can be called from Business Rules, but they are not the same as Business Rules themselves.

questions.question: List the different type of table relationships
questions.explanation:
The correct options are:
B. Many to Many C. Extensions D. One to many
Here’s a breakdown of each option:
A. Multiple Inheritance: ServiceNow does not support true multiple inheritance like object-oriented programming languages. While there are ways to simulate multiple inheritance using extensions and reference fields, it’s not a direct implementation.
B. Many to Many: This is a common relationship type in ServiceNow. It’s implemented using a junction table, which connects two tables with a many-to-many relationship. For example, a task can be related to multiple incidents, and an incident can be related to multiple tasks.
C. Extensions: This is a unique type of relationship in ServiceNow where one table extends another. The child table inherits all fields and behaviors of the parent table and can add additional fields and behaviors. This is a powerful way to create specialized tables based on a common parent table.
D. One to many: This is another common relationship type. In this relationship, one record in one table can be related to multiple records in another table. For example, a change request can have multiple tasks.

questions.question: Applications and modules are loaded based on?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Roles
• Correct because in ServiceNow, applications and modules are loaded based on user roles.
• Roles determine what a user can see and access in the application navigator.
• For example, a user with the admin role will see all applications and modules, while a user with limited roles will only see those relevant to their permissions.
• This aligns with the principle of least privilege, ensuring users only access what they need.
Incorrect
Option A. ServiceNow version
• Incorrect because the version of ServiceNow does not determine which applications or modules are loaded.
• While newer versions may introduce additional features, access is still controlled by roles, not version.
Option C. Group membership
• Incorrect because group membership affects assignment and workflow routing, not application/module visibility.
• Groups are used for task assignment, but they do not control what appears in the application navigator.
Option D. Business rules
• Incorrect because business rules are server-side logic that run when records are displayed, inserted, updated, or deleted.
• They do not control application/module loading; they enforce process logic instead.

questions.question: Which of the following is true while solving incidents as per ITIL framework?
options: Incident Priority is filled by the user.
Incident Impact is calculated on the basis of Urgency & Priority.
Incident Priority is calculated on the basis of Impact & Urgency.
Incident Urgency is based on Impact & Priority.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is C. Incident Priority is calculated on the basis of Impact & Urgency.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: Incident Priority is typically determined by the IT support team based on the impact and urgency of the incident, not solely by the user’s input.
B. Incorrect: Incident Impact is assessed based on the severity of the incident and its potential consequences. It’s not calculated based on urgency and priority.
C. Correct: Incident Priority is a calculated value that considers both the Impact and Urgency of an incident. A higher impact and higher urgency typically result in a higher priority.
D. Incorrect: Incident Urgency is assessed based on how quickly the incident needs to be resolved. It’s not calculated based on impact and priority.

questions.question: Choose any 3 ways from the below to update CMDB in a ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
A. Correct: CMDB data can be manually entered into the ServiceNow instance by authorized users.
B. Correct: External integrations with tools like SCCM, AD, or other IT asset management systems can automatically populate CMDB data.
C. Incorrect: UI Macros are used to create reusable UI components, not for updating CMDB data.
D. Correct: Import sets can be used to import large amounts of CMDB data from external sources, such as CSV files or databases.
E. Incorrect: UI Policies are used to control the visibility and behavior of UI elements on forms. They are not used to update CMDB data.

questions.question: Knowledge process consists of which of the following?
options: document creation, approval and review from SMEs and publishing
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is B. document creation, approval and review from SMEs and publishing.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: Publishing is just one step in the knowledge process. It’s the final step after creation, approval, and review.
B. Correct: This option accurately describes the key steps in the knowledge process:
• Document creation: Authoring new knowledge articles.
• Approval and review from SMEs: Subject matter experts review and approve the content.
• Publishing: Making the articles accessible to end-users.
C. Incorrect: Document creation is only the first step. It needs to be followed by review, approval, and publishing.
D. Incorrect: UI pages are not directly related to the knowledge process. They are used to create custom user interfaces in ServiceNow.

questions.question: SLA, OLA and UC are configured in which module?
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
C. SLM (Service Level Management):
• Explanation: SLA (Service Level Agreement), OLA (Operational Level Agreement), and UC (Underpinning Contract) are all configured within the Service Level Management (SLM) module in ServiceNow. This module is specifically designed to manage and monitor the performance of various service level agreements, ensuring that the agreed-upon service levels are met. SLM provides tools to define, track, and report on SLAs, OLAs, and UCs.
Incorrect Options:
A. Service Catalog:
• Explanation: The Service Catalog module is used to create and manage service offerings that users can request, such as hardware, software, and services. It is not designed for managing SLAs, OLAs, or UCs.
B. ITSM (IT Service Management):
• Explanation: While ITSM encompasses a range of processes and modules, including incident, problem, and change management, it does not specifically refer to the module where SLAs, OLAs, and UCs are configured. The SLM module is the correct place for these configurations.

questions.question: Update set can be moved from one instance to another only if state is marked Completed?
questions.explanation:
TRUE.
An update set can only be moved from one instance to another if its state is marked as “Completed”. This indicates that the update set is ready to be deployed and contains a stable set of changes.

questions.question: Use ______ to create a story with data that can be shared.
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is D. Dashboards.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: Formatters are used to format data within a field, such as currency or dates. They don’t create stories or visualizations.
B. Incorrect: Field values are the actual data stored in a field. They don’t provide a way to create stories or visualizations.
C. Incorrect: Task tables are used to track tasks and work items. They are not directly used for creating stories or visualizations.
D. Correct: Dashboards allow you to create visualizations, such as charts and graphs, to present data in a meaningful way. You can use dashboards to tell stories about data trends, patterns, and insights.

questions.question: When you open a service catalog and click the Order button what gets created first?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is D. REQ.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: An RITM (Request Item) is created after a request is approved and ready to be fulfilled.
B. Incorrect: Tasks are created within an RITM to break down the work into smaller steps.
C. Incorrect: An incident is created to report and resolve problems or service disruptions. It’s not directly related to ordering items from the Service Catalog.
D. Correct: When you click the “Order” button in a Service Catalog, a Request (REQ) is created to initiate the ordering process. This request is then evaluated and approved before being converted into an RITM.

questions.question: Which one of the below is used to group related fields together?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A. Sections.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Correct: Sections are used to group related fields together on a form. This improves the visual organization and readability of the form.
B. Incorrect: Form Layout is used to define the overall layout of a form, including the placement of sections and fields.
C. Incorrect: Views are used to define different ways to display records in a list. They don’t group fields together on a form.
D. Incorrect: List Layouts are used to define the columns and filters displayed in a list view. They don’t group fields together on a form.

questions.question: Incident extends which table?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A. task table.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Correct: The Incident table extends the Task table. This means that Incident records inherit fields and behaviors from the Task table, such as assignment groups, due dates, and state transitions.
B. Incorrect: The CMDB_CI table is used to store information about Configuration Items, such as servers, networks, and applications. It’s not related to the Incident table.

questions.question: The MID Server initiates all communications with the ServiceNow instance. This communication is saved as records in ____. FIll in the blank with the correct option.
questions.explanation:
Correct
option D. ECC Queue
Holds communication records.
Incorrect
option A. Transactions
Session logs.
option B. Import Queue
Data imports.
option C. Staging Table
Import staging.

questions.question: Only predefined roles can be migrated from one instance to another?
questions.explanation:
FALSE.
While predefined roles can be migrated, you can also create custom roles and migrate them between instances. This allows you to maintain consistent role-based access control across different ServiceNow environments.

questions.question: When searching using the App Navigator search field, what can be returned? (Choose four)
options: A. Names of Applications and Modules
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Names of Applications and Modules
• Correct because the App Navigator search field can return both application names and module names when searched.
• This helps users quickly locate functionality without manually browsing the navigation pane.
Option B. Names of Modules
• Correct since modules are searchable directly.
• For example, typing “Incident” will return the Incident module if it exists.
Option C. Names of Applications
• Correct because applications themselves (like “Change” or “Service Catalog”) are searchable.
• This allows users to jump directly to the application container.
Option D. Favorites
• Correct because the App Navigator also searches through Favorites that users have pinned.
• This makes it easier to access frequently used modules or applications.
Incorrect
Option E. History Records
• Incorrect because the App Navigator does not search through history records.
• History is tracked separately in the history tab, not in the App Navigator search.
Option F. Titles of Dashboard Gauges
• Incorrect because dashboard gauges are not part of the App Navigator search scope.
• Gauges are visual elements within dashboards, not applications or modules.

questions.question: Which tables are not part of base ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is B. custom tables.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: Base tables are part of the core ServiceNow platform and are included in every instance.
B. Correct: Custom tables are created by administrators to store specific data that is not part of the standard ServiceNow schema. They are not part of the base instance.
C. Incorrect: Extended tables are created by extending existing base tables. They are part of the ServiceNow instance, but they are not considered base tables themselves.

questions.question: On ServiceNow instance, where can you view information about the system activity?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A. System logs.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Correct: System logs provide detailed information about system activities, including errors, warnings, and other events. This is the primary source for troubleshooting issues and understanding system behavior.
B. Incorrect: Stats provide information about system performance and resource usage, but they don’t provide detailed activity logs.
C. Incorrect: Upgrade History records the history of upgrades performed on the instance, but it doesn’t provide real-time system activity information.
D. Incorrect: System Diagnostics provides tools to diagnose specific issues, but it doesn’t provide a comprehensive view of system activity.

questions.question: Choose all the possible way by which events can be created on a ServiceNow instance.
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A (Business rules): Business rules can fire gs.event() to trigger events on record operations (insert/update/delete).
Option B (Workflow): Workflow activities include “Event” action to create events during workflow execution.
Incorrect
Option C (UI Macro): UI Macros render HTML/Jelly server-side but cannot create events (client-side only).
Option D (Client scripts): Client scripts run in browser (client-side) and cannot directly create server-side events.

questions.question: Can you change the number prefix from “INC” to “IN” for incident table?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. System definition > Number maintenance table (sys_number)
• Correct because ServiceNow allows administrators to configure and change the number prefix for tables (like Incident, Problem, Change) through the Number Maintenance (sys_number) table.
• By navigating to System Definition → Number Maintenance, you can locate the entry for the Incident table and update the prefix from INC to IN.
• This is the supported and proper way to change prefixes in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option B. No
• Incorrect because ServiceNow does allow changing prefixes.
• The prefix is not hardcoded; it is configurable via the Number Maintenance table.
• Saying “No” ignores the platform’s flexibility and the administrator’s ability to customize numbering schemes.

questions.question: What setting allows users to view a knowledge base article even if they are not logged in?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is C. The Public setting.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: The “ESS_user” role is for end-users to access self-service portals and submit requests. It doesn’t directly control the visibility of knowledge base articles.
B. Incorrect: There’s no predefined role called “Allow All.” Roles in ServiceNow are used to control access to specific records and functions, not to make all knowledge base articles public.
C. Correct: The “Public” setting on a knowledge article makes it accessible to anyone, regardless of whether they are logged into ServiceNow. This is the primary way to make knowledge articles publicly available.

questions.question: Task related records extend task table. Can a task refer one or more configuration items?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. TRUE
• This is correct because in ServiceNow, the task table (which is a base table) includes a Configuration Item (CI) reference field.
• This allows tasks such as incidents, problems, and changes (all of which extend the task table) to be associated with one or more configuration items.
• Linking tasks to CIs is essential for ITSM processes like impact analysis, root cause analysis, and change management.
Incorrect
Option B. FALSE
• Incorrect because it ignores the fact that the task table schema already includes the CI reference field.
• If this were true, ServiceNow would not be able to support core ITIL practices that depend on associating tasks with configuration items.

questions.question: Which one is not part of filter conditions?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is D. Type Field.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: Operators are used to specify the comparison between the field value and the specified value. Examples of operators include “equals,” “not equals,” “contains,” “starts with,” and “ends with.”
B. Incorrect: The Field is the specific field in the table that you want to filter on.
C. Incorrect: The Value is the specific value you want to filter for.
D. Correct: There is no concept of a “Type Field” in filter conditions. Filter conditions are defined by the field, operator, and value.

questions.question: Which of the below actions can a user perform in Knowledge management?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. View articles
• End users and knowledge workers can search and view published knowledge articles.
• This is the most basic function of Knowledge Management, ensuring information is accessible to those who need it.
• Correct.
Option B. Edit articles
• Users with appropriate roles (e.g., knowledge_admin, knowledge_manager, or assigned contributors) can edit existing knowledge articles.
• Editing ensures articles remain accurate and up to date.
• Correct.
Option D. Create articles
• Authorized users can create new knowledge articles to capture solutions, troubleshooting steps, or best practices.
• This supports the continual improvement cycle of Knowledge Management.
• Correct.
Incorrect
Option C. Hide articles
• Hiding articles is not a standard user action in ServiceNow Knowledge Management.
• Articles can be retired, unpublished, or restricted by permissions, but “hide” is not a defined action available to users.
• Incorrect.

questions.question: Choose the stages for publishing a basic Knowledge publishing workflow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Draft > Review > Published > Retire
• Correct. In ServiceNow’s Knowledge Management workflow, the standard stages are:
• Draft – Article is created.
• Review – Article is reviewed/approved.
• Published – Article is available to users.
• Retire – Article is withdrawn when outdated.
• This is the proper sequence for a basic knowledge publishing workflow.
Incorrect
Option A. Created > Reviewed > Deployed
• Incorrect. This resembles a software deployment lifecycle, not the ServiceNow Knowledge workflow. ServiceNow uses “Published” and “Retire,” not “Deployed.”
Option C. Start > Process > End
• Incorrect. Too generic. These are not actual ServiceNow Knowledge workflow stages.
Option D. None
• Incorrect. ServiceNow does have a defined workflow for Knowledge publishing, so “None” is not valid.

questions.question: Which table stores information about groups in ServiceNow instance?
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
A. sys_user_group:
• Explanation: The sys_user_group table is the correct table in ServiceNow that stores information about user groups. This table includes details such as group name, description, and the users that are part of each group. It is used for managing user groups, which are essential for assigning roles and permissions within the ServiceNow instance.
Incorrect Options:
B. sys_group:
• Explanation: This is not a recognized table in ServiceNow for storing group information. The correct table is sys_user_group.
C. sys_grp:
• Explanation: This is also not a recognized table in ServiceNow. The correct table is sys_user_group.
D. sys_groups:
• Explanation: Similar to the above, sys_groups is not a valid table in ServiceNow for storing group information. The correct table is sys_user_group.
E. sys_user_grp:
• Explanation: This table name is incorrect. The correct table for storing information about groups is sys_user_group.

questions.question: How can Banner Color on ServiceNow instance be personalized?
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
B. Themes section:
• Explanation: The banner color on a ServiceNow instance can be personalized through the Themes section. This allows administrators to customize the look and feel of the instance, including the banner color, to match the organization’s branding and visual identity.
Incorrect Options:
A. Not Possible:
• Explanation: This is incorrect because it is indeed possible to personalize the banner color in ServiceNow through the Themes section.
C. Navigation Pane:
• Explanation: The Navigation Pane is used to manage the navigation and layout of the ServiceNow instance, but it does not provide options to personalize the banner color.
D. Developer Sections:
• Explanation: Developer Sections are used for managing development-related settings and customizations, but they do not offer options to personalize the banner color.

questions.question: What related tables does the schema map show?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Class extension or reference
• Correct because the schema map in ServiceNow visually shows relationships between tables, specifically:
• Class extensions (inheritance relationships, e.g., Task → Incident).
• Reference fields (links between tables, e.g., Incident referencing sys_user).
• This is the intended purpose of the schema map: to help administrators understand how tables are related structurally and via references.
Incorrect
Option B. Sys_user
• Incorrect because while sys_user is a table that may appear in the schema map if referenced, the schema map does not specifically show only this table.
• The schema map is about relationships, not individual tables by name.
Option C. Cmdb_ci_computers
• Incorrect because cmdb_ci_computers is just one CMDB table.
• Like sys_user, it may appear if referenced, but the schema map does not inherently show this table by default.
Option D. All the options
• Incorrect because not all listed options are correct.
• The schema map does not automatically show every table (like sys_user or cmdb_ci_computers) unless they are part of a relationship.

questions.question: How are local flow variables accessed in flow designer data panel?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is D. Data pills.
Data pills are visual representations of variables in Flow Designer. They are used to access and manipulate variable values within the flow. Local flow variables, which are variables defined within a specific flow, are displayed as data pills in the Data panel.
Here’s a breakdown of the incorrect options:
• A. Scratchpad variables: Scratchpad variables are temporary variables used for quick calculations or temporary storage within a script. They are not directly accessible in the Flow Designer data panel.
• B. New generated items: This is not a relevant term in the context of Flow Designer data access.
• C. New tabs: New tabs are used to organize different parts of a flow, but they don’t directly relate to accessing variables.

questions.question: Which of the following gets automatically captured in an update set?
questions.explanation:
Correct Options (Automatically Captured)
• Table (Option B):
• Explanation: Changes made to tables, including the creation and modification of table structures, are automatically captured in update sets. This includes new fields added to a table and other structural changes, making this option correct.
• Forms (Option C):
• Explanation: Customizations to forms, such as layout changes or the addition of fields, are also automatically captured in update sets. When a form is modified, the entire form layout and its components are included in the update set, confirming that this option is correct.
• Views (Option D):
• Explanation: Changes to views, which define how records are displayed in lists and forms, are typically captured in update sets as well. This includes any modifications made to existing views or the creation of new views, making this option correct.
Incorrect Option (Not Automatically Captured)
• Users (Option A):
• Explanation: User records and their configurations are not captured in update sets by default. Update sets focus on configuration changes rather than transactional data such as user records or group memberships. Therefore, this option is incorrect.

questions.question: In SLA, what attribute controls what is calculated as hours in a work day, # of work week days?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A. Schedule.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Correct: The “Schedule” attribute in an SLA defines the working hours, days, and holidays. This information is used to calculate the duration of incidents and tasks, taking into account business hours and non-working time.
B. Incorrect: The “Type” attribute specifies the type of SLA, such as incident or task SLA. It doesn’t control the calculation of working hours.
C. Incorrect: The “Duration” attribute specifies the target time for resolving an incident or task. It’s not directly related to the calculation of working hours.

questions.question: What table is used to store customisation of an update set in ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is B. sys_update_xml.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Incorrect: The incident table is used to track and manage incidents in ServiceNow. It’s not related to update sets.
B. Correct: The sys_update_xml table stores the XML representation of the customizations that are included in an update set. This table is crucial for tracking and managing changes made to the ServiceNow instance.
C. Incorrect: While the update_set table exists, it primarily stores metadata about update sets, such as their name, description, and state. It doesn’t store the actual customizations.

questions.question: What enables you to track and aggregate data over time through elements called scorecards and indicators?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is A. Performance Analytics.
Here’s a breakdown of the options:
A. Correct: Performance Analytics is a powerful tool in ServiceNow that allows you to track and analyze key performance indicators (KPIs) over time. It uses scorecards and indicators to visualize data and identify trends.
B. Incorrect: Workflow versions are used to manage different versions of a workflow, but they are not directly related to tracking and aggregating data over time.
C. Incorrect: Update sets are used to manage and transport customizations between ServiceNow instances. They are not designed for data tracking and analysis.
D. Incorrect: Task SLAs are used to track the performance of tasks and measure service level adherence. While they can provide data on task completion times, they are not specifically designed for long-term data tracking and aggregation.

questions.question: A Schema Map displays which of the following?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Extended Tables
• Correct because the Schema Map shows extended tables that inherit from a parent table.
• This helps administrators visualize how tables are related through extensions, making it easier to understand the hierarchy.
Option D. Reference Table
• Correct because the Schema Map also displays reference tables that are linked through reference fields.
• This allows admins to see relationships between tables and how data is connected.
Option E. Extending Tables
