• Correct because the Schema Map highlights tables that extend the current table, showing inheritance and dependencies.
• This is critical for understanding how customizations or extensions affect the data model.
Incorrect
Option A. Task Table
• Incorrect because while the Task table is a common parent table in ServiceNow, the Schema Map does not specifically display only the Task table.
• It displays relationships relevant to the selected table.
Option C. Workflows
• Incorrect because workflows are process automation tools, not part of the Schema Map visualization.
• Schema Map focuses on table relationships, not workflow logic.
Option F. Incidents
• Incorrect because Incidents are a specific record type.
• The Schema Map does not display individual records; it shows table structures and relationships.

questions.question: What details does a knowledge article hold?
options: Known errors , User Solutions , Troubleshooting tips
Known errors , User Solutions , Troubleshooting tips , User information
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Known errors, User Solutions, Troubleshooting tips
• Correct because knowledge articles in ServiceNow are designed to capture technical resolutions and troubleshooting guidance.
• They typically include known errors, solutions/workarounds, and troubleshooting steps to help users resolve issues quickly.
• This aligns with the purpose of the Knowledge Management application: providing reusable solutions to common problems.
Incorrect
Option B. Known errors, User Solutions, Troubleshooting tips, User information
• Incorrect because knowledge articles do not store user information.
• User information is managed in the User [sys_user] table, not within knowledge articles.
• Adding user information here would be a security and data governance issue, and it is not part of the knowledge article structure.

questions.question: When can a knowledge article be viewed?
options: After it is set to public
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. After it is published Correct. In ServiceNow, a knowledge article becomes available for viewing only after it is published. Draft or created articles remain in the authoring stage and are not visible to end users until they are formally published. Publishing ensures the article is reviewed, approved, and ready for consumption in the Knowledge Base.
Incorrect
• Option B. After it is set to public Incorrect because simply setting an article to “public” does not make it viewable unless it is also published. Visibility settings control who can access the article, but publication status determines whether it is accessible at all.
• Option C. After it is created Incorrect because newly created articles are in draft status. They cannot be viewed by end users until they are published. Creation alone does not make them available in the Knowledge Base.

questions.question: From the below, choose all the possible ways by which a Service Catalog workflow be attached?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Automatically on condition
• Correct because workflows can be attached to catalog items automatically based on conditions defined in the workflow or catalog item configuration.
• This ensures that when a user requests a catalog item, the workflow is triggered without manual intervention.
Option C. Manually on catalog item form
• Correct because administrators can manually attach a workflow to a catalog item through the catalog item form.
• This is a direct way to ensure the workflow is linked to the item for request fulfillment.
Incorrect
Option A. Through Transform map
• Incorrect because Transform Maps are used in Import Sets to move data into ServiceNow tables.
• They are not related to attaching workflows to Service Catalog items.

questions.question: Which of the below rightly explains the relation between RITM, task and request?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. REQ → RITM → tasks
• Correct because in ServiceNow, when a user submits a catalog request:
• A Request (REQ) record is created.
• Each item in the request generates a Requested Item (RITM).
• Each RITM can then generate one or more Tasks for fulfillment.
• This hierarchy ensures proper tracking and fulfillment of catalog requests.
Incorrect
Option A. REQ → tasks → RITM
• Incorrect because tasks are not created directly under the request. They are created under RITMs.
• This misrepresents the hierarchy.
Option B. RITM → REQ → tasks
• Incorrect because the request (REQ) is the parent record. RITMs are children of the request, not the other way around.
• Tasks are further children of RITMs, not directly tied to REQ.

questions.question: Different views can be created for a list to show different columns and records
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B: TRUE
• Correct because in systems like SharePoint or similar list-based applications, you can create multiple views of a list.
• Each view can display different columns and filter different records, allowing customization for reporting, analysis, or user-specific needs.
• This flexibility is a key feature of list management tools.
Incorrect
Option A: FALSE
• Incorrect because lists are not restricted to a single view.
• Saying “False” would ignore the ability to create customized views that show different subsets of data.
• The statement in the question is true, so marking it as false would be wrong.

questions.question: Which application is used primarily to load data into ServiceNow?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. System Import Sets
• Correct because System Import Sets is the primary ServiceNow application used to load data into the platform.
• It allows administrators to import data from external sources (CSV, Excel, JDBC, etc.), stage it in temporary tables, and then transform it into target tables.
• This is the standard and recommended way to bring external data into ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option A. Import Hub
• Incorrect because there is no native ServiceNow application called “Import Hub.”
• This option is a distractor and does not exist in the ServiceNow ecosystem.
Option B. Import Management
• Incorrect because while ServiceNow has Data Management and Integration capabilities, “Import Management” is not the formal application name used for loading data.
• The correct terminology is System Import Sets.
Option D. Import Set
• Incorrect because “Import Set” refers to the tables created during the import process, not the application itself.
• Import Sets are part of the process, but the application used is System Import Sets.

questions.question: Which field type displays as a checkbox on the Form? (Select two that apply)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. True/False
• Reasoning: A True/False field type is represented as a checkbox on a form. Checking the box = True, unchecking = False.
• Exam Focus: This is a standard way ServiceNow represents boolean values.
Option D. Checkbox
• Reasoning: A Checkbox field type directly displays as a checkbox on the form.
• Exam Focus: This is the most obvious checkbox field type in ServiceNow.
Incorrect
Option A. Multiselect Choice
• Displays as a list or dropdown where multiple values can be selected, not as a single checkbox.
Option B. Choice
• Displays as a dropdown or radio buttons depending on configuration, not a checkbox.
Option E. Checkbox list
• Displays multiple checkboxes for multiple options, but this is not the same as a single checkbox field type. The exam specifically refers to the field type that displays as a checkbox, not a list of them.

questions.question: Tables that exist in the base system are called ……….
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. core tables
• Correct because in ServiceNow and similar exam contexts, core tables are those that exist in the base system by default.
• These tables are part of the platform’s foundational data model and cannot be deleted.
• Examples include task, cmdb_ci, and sys_user.
Incorrect
Option B. custom tables
• Incorrect because custom tables are created by developers or administrators to extend functionality.
• They do not exist in the base system by default.
Option C. parent tables
• Incorrect because parent tables are those from which other tables extend.
• While some parent tables may be core, the term “parent tables” does not specifically mean “tables that exist in the base system.”
Option D. default tables
• Incorrect because “default tables” is not a recognized term in ServiceNow exam contexts.
• The correct terminology is core tables.
Option E. fixed tables
• Incorrect because “fixed tables” is not a valid concept in ServiceNow.
• The platform does not use this terminology.
Option F. base tables
• Incorrect because while “base table” refers to a table that is not extended from another, it is not the same as “tables that exist in the base system.”
• The exam specifically expects core tables as the answer.

questions.question: Which tool is used for creating dependencies between configuration items in the CMDB?
questions.explanation:
CI Relationship Editor is the tool typically used for creating dependencies between Configuration Items (CIs) in a CMDB (Configuration Management Database).
This tool allows you to:
• Define relationships: Establish connections between different CIs, such as a server and its applications, or a network device and its interfaces.
• Specify relationship types: Indicate the nature of the relationship, such as “depends on,” “is part of,” or “is used by.”
• Visualize dependencies: Create diagrams to visualize the complex relationships between CIs.
• Manage dependency changes: Update and modify relationships as the IT infrastructure evolves.
By effectively managing CI relationships, you can gain a better understanding of your IT environment, identify potential impact points, and streamline change management processes.
Read more here: https://docs.servicenow.com/bundle/utah-servicenow-platform/page/product/configuration-management/reference/ci-class-manager-landing-page.html

questions.question: What are examples of Core tables in the ServiceNow platform?
questions.explanation: Watch a quick video to get familiar with tables: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=a7Nrz0OU8XM

questions.question: The Employee On-boarding team has asked for a way for managers to order computers, monitors, business cards, and cell phones for new employees. How would you proceed to meet the requirement?
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
A. Create Order Guide:
• Explanation: An Order Guide in ServiceNow allows you to bundle multiple related items into a single request, making it easier for managers to order all necessary items (computers, monitors, business cards, cell phones) for new employees at once. Order Guides provide a streamlined and user-friendly way to handle complex ordering processes, ensuring that all required items are included in the request and that the process is efficient.
Incorrect Options:
B. Create Requested Item:
• Explanation: A Requested Item represents a single item within a catalog request. While you can create individual requested items for each piece of equipment, this does not provide the bundled ordering experience that an Order Guide offers.
C. Create Record Producer:
• Explanation: A Record Producer is used to create records in a table through a service catalog. It is useful for creating new records but does not facilitate the ordering of multiple related items in a bundled, streamlined manner like an Order Guide.
D. Create On-boarding Bot:
• Explanation: While an on-boarding bot could assist with the on-boarding process by guiding users through various steps, it is not specifically designed for creating and managing bundled catalog requests. The primary focus here is on automating and simplifying the ordering process, which is best achieved with an Order Guide.

questions.question: On Access Control Definitions, what are ways you can set the permissions on a Table? Select 3 answers.
options: Script that sets the answer variable to true or false
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. Groups Correct because permissions can be assigned to specific groups of users. This allows collective access management, ensuring all members of a group inherit the same access rights.
Option C. Roles Correct because roles are the primary mechanism for controlling access in ServiceNow. Access Control Lists (ACLs) often check for roles to determine whether a user can perform an action on a table or field.
Option E. Conditional Expressions Correct because ACLs can include conditions that must evaluate to true for access to be granted. These conditions allow fine‑grained control beyond just roles or groups, such as restricting access based on field values.
Incorrect
Option B. Script that sets the answer variable to true or false Incorrect because while ACLs can include scripts, they are not considered a primary way to set table permissions. Scripts are used for advanced logic, but the main mechanisms are roles, groups, and conditions.
Option D. CRUD Incorrect because CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) defines types of access, not the mechanism for setting permissions. Permissions are enforced through ACLs using roles, groups, and conditions, not directly by CRUD itself.

questions.question: Scenario: You are asked: What happens when you change the order of columns using the Column Context Menu > Configure > List Layout?
options: The order of columns for this list changes for all users
The order of columns for this list changes only for the logged-in user
The order of columns for this list changes for all users except the users who personalized the list
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. The order of columns for this list changes for all users
• Correct because when the Column Context Menu > Configure > List Layout option is used, the change is applied globally.
• This means the updated column order is enforced across the organization for all users who access the list.
• It is not a personalization setting; it is a configuration change that overrides individual views.
Incorrect
• Option B. The order of columns for this list changes only for the logged‑in user
• Incorrect because personal customization is done through personalization settings, not the Configure > List Layout option.
• The configuration menu applies universally, not just to the current user.
• Option C. The order of columns for this list changes for all users except the users who personalized the list
• Incorrect because personalization does not override administrator‑configured list layouts.
• Once the layout is changed via configuration, it applies to everyone.
• Option D. None of the listed answers
• Incorrect because Option A is indeed the correct answer.
• Therefore, this option is invalid.

questions.question: When designing a relationship between 2 configuration items, which of the following roles will the base CI take?
options: The base CI can be the parent or child CI depending on the relationship nature
The relationship doesn‘t involve parent-child roles
The base CI will be the parent CI
The base CI will be the child CI
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. The base CI will be the child CI
• Correct because in CMDB relationship modeling, the base CI is always designated as the child CI.
• The related CI becomes the parent, ensuring consistency in how dependencies and hierarchies are defined.
• This rule avoids ambiguity and enforces a clear governance model when mapping relationships between configuration items.
Incorrect
Option A. The base CI can be the parent or child CI depending on the relationship nature
• Incorrect because the role of the base CI is fixed as the child, not variable.
• Allowing it to switch roles would create inconsistency in CMDB design.
Option B. The relationship doesn’t involve parent‑child roles
• Incorrect because CI relationships explicitly use parent‑child structures to represent dependencies (e.g., hosting, connected‑to, depends‑on).
Option C. The base CI will be the parent CI
• Incorrect because the base CI is never the parent; it is always the child in relationship definitions.

questions.question: User records are stored in which table
questions.explanation:
sys_user
The sys_user table is the primary table in ServiceNow where all user information is stored. This includes:
• User credentials (username, password)
• User roles and permissions
• Contact information
• And other relevant user attributes.
This table is fundamental to the ServiceNow platform and is used for managing all users, including administrators, agents, and self-service users.

questions.question: What do you click when you have made modifications to your report, and you want to see the results without saving?
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
A. Run:
• Explanation: In ServiceNow, after making modifications to a report, you can click the “Run” button to execute the report and see the results of your changes without saving them. This allows you to verify that your modifications produce the desired outcome before committing the changes.
Incorrect Options:
B. Execute:
• Explanation: “Execute” is not the standard terminology used in ServiceNow for running reports. The correct term is “Run.”
C. Test:
• Explanation: “Test” is not used in the context of running reports in ServiceNow. It is more commonly associated with testing scripts or configurations.
D. Preview:
• Explanation: While “Preview” might seem like a reasonable option, it is not the term used in ServiceNow for running reports to see the results. “Run” is the correct action to see the report output without saving.
E. Try it:
• Explanation: “Try it” is not a recognized option in ServiceNow for running reports. It is not the correct terminology used for this action.

questions.question: Your customer wants to update a notification, so it is sent to the Caller, and also to the Manager of the Caller. How would you approach this requirement?
options: Set Who will receive to Subscribable
On the Send to tab, add Caller field, dot walk to Caller’s Manager to add Manager
Create workflow and include a notification in the workflow
On Who will receive tab, select Copy Manager check box
On Who will receive tab, add Caller field, dot walk to Caller’s Manager to add Manager
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
• E. On Who will receive tab, add Caller field, dot walk to Caller’s Manager to add Manager: This option allows you to directly specify the recipients of the notification, including the Caller and their Manager. By using dot-walking, you can dynamically determine the Manager’s email address based on the Caller’s record.
Incorrect Options:
• A. Set Who will receive to Subscribable: This option allows users to subscribe to notifications, but it doesn’t automatically send notifications to the Manager.
• B. On the Send to tab, add Caller field, dot walk to Caller’s Manager to add Manager: The Send to tab is typically used for email notifications, not general notifications.
• C. Create workflow and include a notification in the workflow: While this approach can be used for complex notification scenarios, it’s overkill for this simple requirement.
• D. On Who will receive tab, select Copy Manager check box: This option is not available in ServiceNow notifications.

questions.question: What type of rule specifies which user or groups are responsible to work on different types of tasks?
questions.explanation:
Answer: B. Assignment
• This type of rule is specifically designed to determine which user or group should be assigned to a task or incident based on various criteria, such as the task type, priority, or other relevant factors.
• Other Options:
• On-call Schedule: This rule defines schedules for on-call rotations, but it doesn’t directly assign tasks to specific users.
• Routing Rule: This rule determines the workflow path for a record, but it doesn’t necessarily assign tasks to specific users.
• Calendar: Calendars are used for scheduling events and appointments, not for task assignments.
• Escalation Rule: This rule defines escalation policies, but it doesn’t directly assign tasks to specific users.

questions.question: When looking at a long list of records, you want to quickly filter to show only those which have Category = Hardware. How might you do that?
options: On Breadcrumb, click > icon, type Hardware and click enter
Right click on magnifier, type Hardware and click enter
Click Funnel icon, type Hardware and click enter
On the list, locate and right click on the value Hardware, select Show Matching
On the Category column header, right click and select Show > Hardware
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. On the list, locate and right click on the value Hardware, select Show Matching
• This is the correct answer.
• In ServiceNow lists, you can right-click directly on a field value (like “Hardware”) and choose Show Matching.
• This filters the list instantly to only show records with that same value in the column.
• It’s the fastest way to filter without building a condition manually.
Incorrect
Option A. On Breadcrumb, click > icon, type Hardware and click enter
• Incorrect because breadcrumbs are used to refine filters already applied, not to type values directly.
• You cannot simply type “Hardware” into a breadcrumb.
Option B. Right click on magnifier, type Hardware and click enter
• Incorrect because the magnifier icon is used for searching, not filtering by exact field values.
• It won’t filter the list to only “Hardware” records.
Option C. Click Funnel icon, type Hardware and click enter
• Incorrect because the funnel icon opens the filter condition builder.
• You would need to specify the field (Category) and value (Hardware). Simply typing “Hardware” is not valid.
Option E. On the Category column header, right click and select Show > Hardware
• Incorrect because right-clicking the column header allows sorting or configuring the list, not filtering by a specific value.
• The “Show Matching” option is only available when right-clicking on an actual field value, not the header.

questions.question: Which resource would you use to determine if a specific user could contribute to a particular knowledge base?
questions.explanation:
To determine which resource can be used to check if a specific user can contribute to a particular knowledge base in ServiceNow, let’s analyze each option provided in the question:
A. User Criteria Diagnostics
Correct: User Criteria Diagnostics is a tool in ServiceNow that allows administrators to analyze user criteria settings. It provides insights into which users meet the criteria set for accessing specific knowledge bases. This resource can effectively help determine if a user has the necessary permissions to contribute to a particular knowledge base.
Definition and Purpose:
• The User Criteria Diagnostics feature in ServiceNow is a tool that provides administrators with insights into how user criteria are evaluated against specific users and their roles. It is particularly useful for troubleshooting and verifying access permissions related to various modules, including knowledge bases.
How It Works:
• When a knowledge base is created, administrators can set up User Criteria to control who can read, write, or contribute to that knowledge base. These criteria can include conditions based on user roles, groups, or specific attributes (like department or location).
• The User Criteria Diagnostics tool allows administrators to input a specific user and see how that user matches against the defined criteria for different knowledge bases.
Why It’s Useful:
• Verification of Access: By using this tool, an administrator can quickly verify whether a user meets the necessary conditions to contribute to a knowledge base. This is crucial when a user claims they cannot access or contribute to a knowledge base, as it helps pinpoint the exact reason.
• Detailed Output: The diagnostics provide a detailed output that includes which user criteria are applied and whether the user meets or fails each one. This makes it easy to identify misconfigurations or oversights in user access settings.
• Troubleshooting: If a user is unable to access a knowledge base they believe they should be able to contribute to, the User Criteria Diagnostics can help troubleshoot the issue by showing exactly where the criteria are not being met.
Example Scenario:
• Suppose you have a knowledge base that is set to allow contributions only from users in the “Knowledge Authors” group. If a user who is not in that group tries to contribute, using User Criteria Diagnostics would reveal that the user does not meet the criteria for that knowledge base due to group membership.
B. sn_kb_author role
Incorrect: The sn_kb_author role is specifically assigned to users who are allowed to create and manage knowledge articles. While having this role is essential for contributing to knowledge bases, it does not provide a diagnostic capability or assessment tool to check if a specific user can contribute. It simply indicates that users with this role have the necessary permissions.
C. User Criteria Job Log
Incorrect: The User Criteria Job Log tracks the execution of user criteria jobs but does not specifically assess whether a user can contribute to a knowledge base. It may provide information about past evaluations but does not serve as a direct resource for determining current access rights related to knowledge bases.
D. Knowledge Author Group
Incorrect: The Knowledge Author Group is a group of users who have been granted permissions to author knowledge articles. While being part of this group allows users to contribute, it does not serve as a diagnostic tool to check if an individual user can contribute. Membership in this group is more about granting access than evaluating it.
• Role vs. Specific Knowledge Base Access:
• Being part of a Knowledge Author Group indicates that a user has the general authority to author knowledge articles. However, it does not necessarily confirm that they have access to contribute to a specific knowledge base. The ability to contribute can be further restricted by user criteria set for that particular knowledge base.
• User Criteria Considerations:
• Each knowledge base can have its own set of user criteria that dictate who can contribute. For example, a knowledge base may allow contributions only from users in a specific role or group that is not the same as the Knowledge Author Group. Thus, knowing that a user is in a Knowledge Author Group does not automatically grant access to all knowledge bases.
• Access Configuration Complexity:
• Access control in ServiceNow can be complex, where multiple factors (such as roles, groups, and user attributes) can influence a user’s ability to contribute to a knowledge base. The Knowledge Author Group does not account for these specific configurations and conditions.
• No Direct Evaluation Mechanism:
• The Knowledge Author Group serves as a membership designation but does not provide a mechanism to evaluate against the specific user criteria set for each knowledge base. Therefore, it lacks the diagnostic capabilities that the User Criteria Diagnostics tool offers.
Example Scenario:
• Imagine a scenario where a user is part of the Knowledge Author Group but the knowledge base has user criteria that restrict contributions to only those in a specific department. In this case, even though the user is in the Knowledge Author Group, they would not be able to contribute to that knowledge base due to the department restriction, highlighting the limitation of relying solely on group membership.
E. KB Author Checker
Incorrect: While the KB Author Checker sounds like it could be a tool for checking author permissions, it is not an officially recognized resource in ServiceNow for determining if a specific user can contribute to a knowledge base. The proper tools for this purpose are the User Criteria Diagnostics and understanding role assignments like sn_kb_author.

questions.question: Business rules are real time
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. FALSE
• Reasoning: Business Rules in ServiceNow are not real‑time. They run on the server side when records are inserted, updated, deleted, or queried. They execute before or after database operations, but they do not run instantly in the client’s browser like UI Policies or Client Scripts.
• Exam Focus: The CSA exam expects you to distinguish between server‑side logic (Business Rules) and client‑side logic (UI Policies, Client Scripts). Business Rules are powerful but not real‑time.
Incorrect
Option A. TRUE
• Reasoning: This is a common misconception. While Business Rules can feel immediate because they run during database transactions, they are not real‑time client‑side events. They depend on server execution and database triggers, so they cannot be classified as real‑time.
• Exam Trap: The exam tests whether you understand that Business Rules ≠ real‑time. Real‑time behavior is handled by Client Scripts/UI Policies.

questions.question: What is an ACL defined and applied to?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option D. Specific Role or user
• Correct because Access Control Lists (ACLs) in ServiceNow are defined and applied to roles or users.
• ACLs determine whether a user with a given role can access a specific table, record, or field.
• This ensures contextual security by controlling access based on role assignments or user identity.
Incorrect
Option A. Specific Table User
• Incorrect because ACLs are not defined for individual table users; they are applied at the role/user level.
Option B. Specific user on a CI
• Incorrect because ACLs are not tied to configuration items (CIs) directly; they govern access to tables, records, and fields.
Option C. Specific group of users
• Incorrect because ACLs do not apply to groups directly. Instead, ACLs apply to roles, and users in those groups may inherit roles, but ACLs themselves are not defined at the group level.

questions.question: Production, Development and Test/QA are the only types of environments in remote instances ServiceNow.
questions.explanation:
FALSE
While Production, Development, and Test/QA are common environment types in ServiceNow, they are not the only ones. Organizations often implement additional environments for specific purposes, such as:
• Pre-Production: A staging environment to test final configurations and integrations before deployment to production.
• User Acceptance Testing (UAT): An environment for end-users to test the system and provide feedback.
• Disaster Recovery (DR): A dedicated environment for testing disaster recovery procedures and ensuring business continuity.
The specific number and types of environments can vary depending on the organization’s needs and complexity.

questions.question: ServiceNow provides customers with a dedicated database, application and data isolation using which one of the following models?
questions.explanation:
ServiceNow provides customers with a dedicated database, application, and data isolation using a single-tenant model.
• Single-tenant architecture means each customer gets their own dedicated instance of the ServiceNow platform. This provides the highest level of security and isolation for each customer’s data.
While ServiceNow operates on a cloud infrastructure, the single-tenant model ensures that each customer’s data remains separate and secure from other customers.
https://community.servicenow.com/community?id=community_question&sys_id=aa81136ddbdcdbc01dcaf3231f961984

questions.question: When importing data from a spreadsheet, which step defines where the incoming data columns will be written in the receiving table?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option E. Create Transform Map
• Correct because a Transform Map in ServiceNow defines the mapping between source data (spreadsheet columns) and the target table fields.
• It specifies exactly where each incoming column will be written in the receiving table.
• Without a Transform Map, ServiceNow cannot know how to align spreadsheet data with the destination table schema.
Incorrect
Option A. Schedule Transform
• Incorrect because scheduling a transform only determines when the data import runs, not how the data columns map to the table fields.
Option B. Select Data Source
• Incorrect because selecting a data source identifies where the data is coming from (e.g., spreadsheet, JDBC, etc.), but it does not define the mapping of columns to fields.
Option C. Field Mapping
• Incorrect because while field mapping is part of the transform map, the step itself is not standalone. The correct terminology in ServiceNow is Transform Map, which encompasses field mapping.
Option D. Load Data
• Incorrect because loading data simply imports the spreadsheet into a staging table. It does not define how the data will be written into the target table.

questions.question: Which plugin needs to be activated in order to translate the content of catalog item to multiple languages?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is B. Localization framework plugin (com.glide.localization_framework).
This plugin enables the translation of Service Catalog items into multiple languages. It allows you to configure localization settings, request translations, and manage the translation process for your Service Catalog items.
Here’s a breakdown of why the other options are incorrect:
• A. Multiple Language framework plugin: This plugin is not specifically designed for translating Service Catalog items.
• C. Translation framework plugin: While this plugin might be involved in some translation processes within ServiceNow, it’s not the primary plugin used for translating Service Catalog items.

questions.question: How can administrators utilise the same content for different notification channels?
questions.explanation:
Answer: D. Provide common notification content
• This option allows administrators to create a single, centralized content block that can be reused across various notification channels. This promotes consistency and reduces the need for duplicate content management.
Incorrect Options:
• Provide default notification content: This option typically refers to pre-configured notification messages that are applied by default to specific events or incidents. While it can be useful for basic notifications, it doesn’t directly address the requirement of using the same content for different channels.
• Enable actionable notification content: This feature allows users to take actions directly from within a notification, such as approving a request or resolving an incident. It’s helpful for user interaction but doesn’t directly relate to content reuse across channels.
• Set up related notification content: This option might be used to create relationships between different notification templates, but it doesn’t necessarily ensure that the same content is used across multiple channels.

questions.question: Which fields can be configured in reporting to perform arithmetic, coalesce, concatenation and length?
questions.explanation:
Answer: C. Function fields
• These fields allow you to perform various calculations, manipulations, and transformations on data, including arithmetic operations, coalescing, concatenation, and length calculations. They are specifically designed for data manipulation and reporting purposes.
Incorrect Options:
• Calculation fields: While calculation fields can perform basic arithmetic operations, they are typically used to calculate values based on other fields within a record. They are not as flexible as function fields for advanced data manipulation.
• Sourcing fields: Sourcing fields are used to retrieve values from other tables or records. They do not provide any built-in functions for arithmetic, coalescing, concatenation, or length calculations.

questions.question: How can administrators personalize access to applications and modules for users and groups in the Platform to complete their work more efficiently? (Select 3)
options: Create homepages and dashboards and assign specific work to users and groups
Create a workspace with links to access the applications and modules
Configure sidebars with links, specific to users and groups
Enable the user preference to specify the page that appears when they log in to the Next Experience user interface
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. Create homepages and dashboards and assign specific work to users and groups → Correct because admins can design homepages and dashboards tailored to roles or groups, ensuring users immediately see relevant tasks, KPIs, and modules.
• Option B. Create a workspace with links to access the applications and modules → Correct because workspaces provide a consolidated, role‑based view with navigation links, streamlining access to applications and modules for specific groups.
• Option C. Configure a custom menu → Correct because custom menus allow administrators to personalize navigation, grouping applications and modules in ways that match user workflows, improving efficiency.
Incorrect
• Option D. Configure sidebars with links, specific to users and groups → Incorrect because ServiceNow does not support configuring sidebars as a personalization method for access. Navigation is managed through menus, dashboards, and workspaces instead.
• Option E. Enable the user preference to specify the page that appears when they log in to the Next Experience UI → Incorrect because this is a user‑driven preference, not an administrator‑controlled personalization method for groups or roles. It does not provide centralized control for admins.

questions.question: If we make the short description field on the incident table as mandatory at the dictionary level, what happens?
options: Short description will be mandated on incident table only
Short description will be mandated on all the tables which are extending task table
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option C. Short description will be mandated on all the tables which are extending task table
• Correct because the incident table extends the task table.
• When a field is made mandatory at the dictionary level, the requirement propagates to all child tables that inherit from the parent (task).
• Therefore, the short description field becomes mandatory not only on the incident table but also on all tables extending task.
Incorrect
Option A. Nothing happens
• Incorrect because making a field mandatory at the dictionary level does have an effect.
• It enforces the requirement across the parent table and all extending tables.
Option B. Short description will be mandated on incident table only
• Incorrect because the mandatory setting applies at the dictionary level, not just the incident table.
• Since incident extends task, the requirement cascades to all task‑derived tables, not just incident.

questions.question: Users with the following role will have full view/edit/delete and share privileges of all dashboard on given ServiceNow instance.
questions.explanation:
Correct Option:
dashboard_admin: This role provides the highest level of permissions for dashboards, granting full control over their creation, modification, deletion, and sharing.
Incorrect Options:
homepage_admin: This role is primarily concerned with managing the ServiceNow homepage, including its layout and content. It doesn’t provide specific permissions for dashboards.
report_admin: This role is focused on managing reports, not dashboards.
dashboard_manager: While this role provides some level of control over dashboards, it doesn’t grant full permissions, including delete and share privileges.

questions.question: Following types of reports are available in ServiceNow: (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation:
Correct
• Option A. Pareto
• Correct: ServiceNow supports Pareto charts (80/20 rule visualization) to highlight the most significant factors in a dataset.
• Option B. Line Chart
• Correct: Line charts are available for trend analysis over time, commonly used in performance and operational reporting.
• Option C. Donut
• Correct: Donut charts are supported as a variation of pie charts, useful for showing proportions with a central empty space.
• Option D. List
• Correct: List reports are one of the most common report types in ServiceNow, displaying tabular data directly from tables.

questions.question: What are examples of UI Actions, relating to Lists? (Select four responses)
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option A. List Buttons
• Correct because list buttons are UI Actions that appear above a list and allow users to perform actions on selected records (e.g., “Delete,” “Update”).
Option B. List Context menu
• Correct because the list context menu provides right‑click options on list rows, enabling quick actions like “Edit,” “Copy,” or “Delete.”
Option C. List Links
• Correct because list links are clickable UI Actions that appear in lists, often used to navigate or trigger specific actions.
Option D. List Choices
• Correct because list choices are UI Actions that allow users to select from predefined options when interacting with lists.
Incorrect
Option E. List Control
• Incorrect because list control is not a UI Action type. It refers to list configuration or display settings, not an actionable UI element.
Option F. List Override
• Incorrect because list override is not a recognized UI Action type in ServiceNow. Overrides are related to customizing behavior, not UI Actions.

questions.question: What table is used to track all changes in an update Set?
questions.explanation:
The correct answer is sys_update_xml.
Here’s why:
• sys_update_xml: This table stores all the individual changes (records, configurations, scripts, etc.) that are captured within an Update Set. Every modification made within the scope of an Update Set is recorded as a row in this table.
Let’s look at why the other options are incorrect:
• update_set: This table stores the Update Set records themselves (name, description, state, etc.), but not the individual changes contained within them.
• Incident: This table is for tracking incident records, not Update Set changes.
• sys_update_set: This is a synonym for update_set, and as stated above, it does not store the individual changes.

questions.question: What are events caused by?
questions.explanation:
Correct
Option B. Workflow Scripts and Business Rules
• Reason: In ServiceNow, events are generated primarily by Business Rules and Workflow scripts.
• These events are then placed into the event queue and can trigger Notifications or other automated actions.
• This is the official mechanism for event generation in the ServiceNow platform.
Incorrect
Option A. User action and scripts
• Incorrect because while user actions (like form submissions) may indirectly lead to events, they do so only through Business Rules or Workflows.
• User actions alone do not directly generate events.
Option C. Class extension or reference
• Incorrect because extending classes or referencing them does not generate events.
• This is related to object‑oriented design, not ServiceNow’s event framework.
Option D. None of the above
• Incorrect because there is a valid answer: events are caused by Workflow Scripts and Business Rules.
